proposals.latency_budget: Generate the approval card in under 2 seconds; spoken approval round trip under 4 seconds; expire unanswered approvals after a configurable window and leave the task paused.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: one compact summarization call for complex changes; simple structured actions need no model. Network/audio transport dominates latency, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Approval must be bound to a single job, exact action hash, target tab/app, and short expiry; replayed or altered approvals must fail closed. Redact secrets and unrelated page text. Never treat ambient speech or an unpaired pendant as approval. Owner policy requires confirmation for sending mail, deleting files, and buying.
missing: A cryptographically bound approval token generated by the pendant/relay and verified by the Mac executor
A structured before/after diff format for browser, file, mail, and purchase actions
A real approval gate in the FULL_CONTROL execution path (currently action-risk classification is dead code)
A pendant audio/UI protocol for clear affirmative, rejection, and correction responses
Receipt evidence linking the approved hash to the exact executed action

proposals.user_asks: “I’m focusing now.” (press pendant button) — silence routine browser/calendar noise until I press again, but interrupt me for genuinely urgent items; when focus ends, give me one short catch-up.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is the only always-present, low-friction intent signal; the relay is always awake; the Mac knows its actual Focus state and local notifications; the browser knows which authenticated page changes matter. Together they provide a reliable interruption boundary instead of another calendar-only meeting mode. It must restore the exact prior Mac state after expiry or a dropped link.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the button acknowledgement and urgent interrupt decision; a cheap background model ranks queued changes and writes the catch-up. Deterministic rules handle TTL, deduplication, and restoring state.
proposals.latency_budget: Button acknowledgement under 300 ms; Focus application/restore under 2 s; urgent interrupt under 5 s; catch-up can arrive asynchronously when focus ends.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per focus window, dominated by background summarization; routine state transitions and deduplication are local/server compute.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not transmit page bodies by default—send only source, timestamp, severity, and a short redacted snippet. Never auto-send or submit browser actions. Store the prior Focus configuration and lease expiry, encrypt it, and expire it. Require explicit button press to end early; on relay/Mac failure fail open to the owner's prior notification state, not a permanently muted state.
missing: A pendant-side focus-window button/LED skill with offline acknowledgement and a pending-event bit
A relay focus-lease state machine with TTL, idempotent start/stop, reconnect reconciliation, and urgent-event policy
Mac integration that snapshots and restores the exact Focus/notification state without Accessibility
Browser page-watch results normalized into urgent-vs-queued signals
A small dashboard showing active lease, expiry, queued count, and restoration receipt

proposals.user_asks: “Continue this on my Mac.” — hand the current pendant conversation to the Mac as a private, one-time continuation: open the relevant app or authenticated browser tab, place a concise task capsule where I can see it, and let me say “back” to return the result to the pendant.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must repeat the task, find the right app or tab, and reconstruct context when moving from voice to desktop. This creates a secure handoff between the device that heard the intent and the machine that can show and edit the work, without dumping the entire conversation into a document or exposing unrelated private context.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short handoff acknowledgement and return command. A cheaper background model compiles the minimal task capsule and extracts the final result; deterministic code handles token expiry, app/tab targeting, and receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff within 500 ms; Mac opens the target within 3 seconds; return a result within 2 seconds after the owner says “back,” excluding long-running work.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.002–$0.02 per handoff, dominated by capsule compilation and result summarization; transport, routing, and local file/UI actions are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: Use a single-use, short-lived handoff token bound to the paired pendant and Mac session. Send only the selected task capsule, never the raw transcript by default. Do not copy secrets into clipboard or files; redact sensitive entities and show the capsule destination. Browser actions remain read/draft-only unless separately requested, and the handoff expires if the Mac does not accept it.
missing: A relay handoff protocol that issues one-time capability tokens and tracks accepted/completed/expired states
A compact context-capsule compiler with explicit source references and redaction
A Mac receiver that resolves the capsule into an app, file, or authenticated browser tab and reports a typed receipt
A pendant return event that fetches the result without reopening the microphone
A dashboard view showing active handoffs and allowing revocation

proposals.user_asks: “Let me know silently when it’s done.” — after I hand a long Mac or browser task to you, give the pendant a distinct haptic pattern for completed, needs-attention, or failed, and let a button press replay a one-sentence status.
proposals.why_useful: The owner should not need to keep checking the Mac or open the microphone while walking, in a meeting, or listening to something else. A tactile receipt turns asynchronous work into an ambient signal, while keeping potentially sensitive content off the pendant speaker until explicitly requested.
proposals.model_tier: No realtime model is needed for completion classification. Deterministic receipt mapping handles completed/attention/failed; a cheaper background model produces the optional one-sentence spoken status.
proposals.latency_budget: Haptic notification within 2 seconds of a terminal receipt; button status replay begins within 500 ms.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.001 per event; almost entirely device and relay computation, with optional status summarization costing a fraction of a cent.
proposals.security_concerns: Haptics reveal only a coarse state, not task content. Do not speak sensitive details without the explicit replay press. Bind notifications to the paired device, deduplicate receipt IDs, and expire stale notifications so a later owner does not receive misleading signals.
missing: Pendant firmware haptic pattern queue with persistence across link loss and bounded flash use
Relay subscription that converts Mac/browser terminal receipts into device notifications
A stable receipt taxonomy shared by /jobs receipts, browser results, and failures
A button event to request the latest status and a delivery acknowledgement

proposals.user_asks: When I ask “what am I on the hook for today?”, gather my Calendar and Mail plus the logged-in pages I have open, identify commitments, deadlines, and conflicts, and leave me a sourced review board with a short spoken summary and suggested next actions—never send, submit, or reschedule anything.
proposals.why_useful: This turns scattered obligations into one actionable view: a meeting promise in Mail, a due date in a private portal, and a calendar collision are linked as one item rather than three separate alerts. The Mac leaves an auditable board the owner can review later, while the pendant gives only the highest-priority exceptions.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for extraction, deduplication, deadline/conflict reasoning, and board generation; reserve realtime only for the spoken request and a brief answer. Use no realtime context replay for the overnight/background work.
proposals.latency_budget: Spoken acknowledgement under 1 second; initial answer in 10–20 seconds when browser is healthy. If private tabs are unavailable, say so immediately and complete Calendar/Mail-only results rather than hanging. Background board can finish asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: One background text invocation per request plus bounded authenticated-page extraction; dominant cost is browser page reads and context, not the short realtime acknowledgement. TTS is a few seconds of generated PCM and should be cached with the board.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar/Mail and logged-in page contents leave the Mac only as scoped extracts; redact message bodies by default and retain source URLs, timestamps, and snippets rather than whole pages. Never submit forms or send mail. Browser session IDs and tab URLs must be kept out of the pendant transcript; require explicit owner action later for any mutation.
missing: A durable cross-source commitment schema (source, evidence snippet, due timestamp, owner, confidence, status, conflict links) and deduplication pass
The durable browser job runner and resumable result stream for private-page reads; current router/backends exist but jobs do not survive restart
A review-board writer that atomically creates/updates one dated folder with a brief, evidence manifest, and draft suggestions
A healthy authenticated browser tab/heartbeat; current browser status is online but has no active tab and nine pending commands

proposals.user_asks: When I miss or am about to miss a commitment, tell me what is at risk, find the smallest set of recovery options across my Calendar, Mail, and logged-in work pages, and prepare a choice card on my Mac with draft messages and proposed times—then let me choose one from the pendant. Never send, submit, or reschedule without my explicit choice.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can summarize sources, but it cannot connect a slipping commitment to concrete, evidence-backed recovery choices. This would turn “I’m late” into a calm decision: what can be moved, who needs a draft notice, what deadline is hard, and which option causes the least downstream damage.
proposals.model_tier: Use a background model for monitoring, commitment extraction, dependency analysis, and generating alternatives. Use the realtime tier only for the pendant’s brief alert and the owner’s selection. Use a cheap deterministic rules layer for time arithmetic, conflict checks, and redaction.
proposals.latency_budget: A risk alert should reach the pendant within 30 seconds of a detected change or missed start. A choice card should appear on the Mac within 1–2 minutes; selecting an option should acknowledge in under 1 second and queue the selected plan for explicit execution.
proposals.cost_estimate: Periodic checks are mostly deterministic and low-cost; one background model call only when a commitment changes or crosses a risk threshold. Browser extraction and authenticated session availability dominate cost and latency; spoken alerts are short cached audio.
proposals.security_concerns: Private calendar, mail, and portal evidence must remain scoped to the relevant commitment, with source snippets and timestamps rather than whole-page retention. Drafts must be visibly marked unsent. No browser form submission, email send, or calendar mutation may happen from the alert alone; the chosen option must produce a human-readable before/after plan and a second explicit execution request.
missing: A commitment lifecycle model with planned, at-risk, missed, recovered, and dismissed states, including evidence and dependency edges
A cross-surface change detector that compares Calendar/Mail/browser observations over time instead of only answering on demand
A choice-card renderer and pendant selection protocol that carries an opaque option ID back to the Mac without replaying private content
A transactional action bundle that can execute a selected multi-app recovery plan and return per-step receipts or restore the prior draft state

proposals.user_asks: “Start meeting mode.”
proposals.why_useful: With one pendant press or spoken command, the hive should recognize the current/next meeting, quietly assemble the agenda and relevant mail/calendar context, keep a live 24 kHz audio sidecar while the owner talks, and after the meeting leave a cited recap with decisions, open questions, and draft follow-ups—never sending anything automatically. The pendant supplies an immediate, hands-free trigger and audio; the Mac knows which meeting app/window is active and can read Calendar/Mail; the browser bridge can inspect the authenticated agenda or project tab; the relay keeps the session alive and delivers the recap when the Mac or pendant link briefly drops.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only for the live turn-taking/audio control; use a cheaper background model for agenda extraction, transcript cleanup, decision/action-item synthesis, and draft generation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pendant trigger in under 300 ms, select the meeting context in under 2 s, and keep audio playout below 250 ms end-to-end. Post-meeting recap can take 1–3 minutes and should be resumable.
proposals.cost_estimate: One realtime session plus roughly 2–5 minutes of background transcription/synthesis; dominant cost is live audio tokens, so only the meeting interval should use realtime and the recap should use the slower tier.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar/Mail and authenticated browser content leave the Mac only as redacted, cited excerpts; raw audio/transcript needs explicit retention (default delete after recap). Never submit/send a draft. Starting capture must be an explicit button or spoken command with a clear LED/audio acknowledgment; meeting mode must show an obvious active indicator.
missing: A meeting-context correlator joining the next Calendar event to the foreground Mac app and optionally an authenticated browser tab
A session-scoped audio/transcript capsule that survives a dropped Mac link and supports resumable post-meeting processing
A citation-preserving recap/draft artifact written to the owner's AI-Pendant-Workspace with a dashboard review state
A true 24 kHz capture/uplink path: current pendant capture is 15,625 Hz and 16 kHz Opus uplink even though playback decodes 24 kHz

proposals.user_asks: “Move this conversation to my Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner should be able to begin a thought hands-free on the pendant and continue it at the desk without repeating the request or losing the assistant's working context. The pendant marks the exact turn and provides a short spoken acknowledgment; the relay seals a resumable conversation capsule; the Mac opens the relevant workspace, browser tab, or draft and presents the same pending decision; the owner can then type, inspect sources, or continue by voice. When they leave the desk, a single pendant press should hand the unfinished state back, including what was already done and what remains.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the handoff acknowledgment and any continuing live speech. Use a cheaper background model to compress the conversation capsule, select relevant files/tabs, and generate the Mac-side continuation view.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 300 ms, persist the capsule before replying, and have the Mac workspace ready within 3 seconds. Returning to the pendant should require only a short state summary, not a full replay.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small realtime turn per handoff; background compression and workspace selection should be a low-cost model. Storage is a small encrypted capsule plus references, so the dominant cost is not storage but repeated context if the capsule is not compact.
proposals.security_concerns: The capsule may contain private speech, authenticated URLs, and draft text. Encrypt it, retain it only until the task is completed or for a user-configurable short TTL, and redact secrets from dashboard previews. Opening a file or tab is reversible; sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting must remain an explicit separate action. The owner must see which Mac surfaces will be opened before the handoff executes.
missing: A versioned, encrypted handoff-capsule format with turn boundary, task state, completed actions, pending decisions, source references, and expiry
A relay-to-Mac handoff route with idempotency and acknowledgement, plus a Mac-to-pendant resume route
A workspace resolver that maps capsule references to an existing Mac file/tab without leaking authenticated page contents into the relay log
A dashboard/menubar continuation card showing capsule provenance and allowing discard or resume

proposals.user_asks: “Save where I am and remind me at 3—or when I get back to my Mac—then put me back exactly where I left off and give me the short version.”
proposals.why_useful: Interruptions currently lose the relationship between the pendant request, the Mac's active work, and authenticated browser state. A resume capsule would let the owner safely switch contexts without re-finding tabs, files, or the last unfinished step. It is genuinely multi-surface: the pendant supplies intent and timing, the always-on relay persists a compact capsule, the Mac observes and restores desktop state, and the browser reattaches private tabs.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to parse the spoken save/resume intent and answer the immediate acknowledgment. Use a cheaper background model to compress the snapshot into a structured capsule, classify stale/unsafe restoration steps, and generate the short spoken brief. The relay scheduler delivers the reminder without an LLM call unless the capsule needs summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; capture in 3 seconds. At the scheduled time, deliver the reminder immediately, then restore reversible app/tab state in under 10 seconds and speak a 20–30 second summary. If the Mac or browser is offline, retain the reminder and report the missing surface rather than silently pretending to restore it.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per save/resume, dominated by one small background summarization call; scheduled reminders and deterministic state capture cost no model tokens. A long or noisy snapshot should be truncated before model use.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules can contain private URLs, window titles, document names, and snippets from logged-in tabs. Store only an owner-selected allowlist (active app, tab titles/URLs, file path, explicit note), redact page bodies and secrets by default, encrypt at rest, attach an expiry, and show provenance on the Mac. Never replay clicks, submits, sends, purchases, or destructive actions during restore; reopen/read only and ask the owner separately. The pendant should support a physical privacy cancel before saving a sensitive capsule.
missing: A durable resume-capsule schema with redaction, sensitivity, expiry, and provenance fields
A trigger that combines a one-shot schedule with Mac-return/foreground-online presence
Read-only capture of active window, caret/selection, workspace, and authenticated browser tab metadata in one atomic snapshot
Browser session/tab reattachment by stable session and tab identifiers, with stale-tab detection
A deterministic restore plan that opens apps/files/URLs but never performs consequential UI mutations
A pendant delivery path for capsule reminder plus a concise audio summary and a dashboard listing/expiry control
built_from: mac_read_sources (calendar_today/calendar_range for choosing a safe resume time)

proposals.user_asks: “Protect my focus: interrupt me on the pendant only for something genuinely urgent; queue everything else and give me one concise catch-up when I’m free.”
proposals.why_useful: The system can already produce briefs, watch pages, and finish Mac jobs, but it lacks a shared attention policy. Today each surface can alert independently, causing duplicate or badly timed interruptions. This capability turns the pendant into one attention gate: browser changes, mail/calendar signals, and Mac job receipts are deduplicated, ranked against the owner's current focus and calendar, then either delivered now or batched for a quiet window.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic rules for urgency, duplicate suppression, quiet hours, and calendar conflict. Use the cheaper background model to rank ambiguous changes and write the batch digest. Reserve realtime for an explicit spoken override such as “what am I missing?” or “interrupt me now.”
proposals.latency_budget: Ingest events within 30 seconds and make the interrupt/batch decision in under 2 seconds without an LLM. Urgent delivery should reach the pendant within 5 seconds. A batched digest can be generated at the next quiet window in under 30 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-based event routing; roughly $0.002–$0.02 per digest depending on queued item count. Cost is dominated by one compact summarization call, not by every event.
proposals.security_concerns: The policy engine sees sensitive mail subjects, private browser changes, calendar titles, and Mac job details. Keep raw content on the originating surface, pass only minimal typed event facts to the relay, encrypt queues, set per-source sensitivity and retention, and make high-sensitivity events opt-in. Never infer urgency from message content without retaining source/provenance. A physical pendant gesture must pause all delivery immediately; dashboard must expose why each item was interrupted or deferred.
missing: A shared attention-policy object with urgency thresholds, source sensitivity, quiet windows, batching limits, and a physical pause state
An event envelope and idempotent deduplication key shared by browser watches, Mac receipts, calendar/mail readers, and relay jobs
A relay-side policy evaluator that can fan out one event to pendant audio/haptics, Mac notification, or a deferred queue
A cross-surface urgency classifier with provenance and an explainable 'why now' result
A durable queue with expiry and a one-tap spoken review/acknowledge flow
Dashboard controls for previewing, editing, and temporarily overriding the policy

proposals.user_asks: “Use what I’m looking at on my Mac: read the selected text or page, answer my question about it on the pendant, and—when I say so—put the result back into the right document or browser field.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must manually copy context from the Mac into the pendant conversation and then manually carry the answer back. This would make the wearable a hands-free companion to the exact desktop focus: a selected paragraph, spreadsheet cell, document, or authenticated page. It is not a generic Mac command or a browser watcher; it is a secure, ephemeral semantic bridge from current desktop context to pendant conversation and back.
proposals.model_tier: Use a small background/text model for extraction cleanup and question answering; use realtime only for the live spoken exchange. Deterministic routing should decide whether the source is selected text, current document, or active browser tab. Do not send screenshots or full page bodies unless explicitly requested.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture the focused context in under 2 seconds, answer a short question in under 4 seconds, and stage a requested insertion in under 3 seconds. If context capture fails, say exactly which surface is unavailable rather than guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.02 per interaction, dominated by text understanding and answer generation. Most short selections fit in one inexpensive request; no model call is needed for capture, hashing, or insertion staging.
proposals.security_concerns: Selected text and authenticated pages may contain passwords, health data, or confidential work. Keep the payload ephemeral, encrypt transport and relay storage, redact secrets/credentials, attach source app/URL and timestamp, and delete it after the response unless the owner explicitly saves it. Never submit, send, or overwrite on a spoken 'answer' alone: insertion must be a separate explicit command and show the target app/field plus a before/after preview. Disable capture while the pendant privacy pause is active.
missing: A Mac bridge operation that reads the current selection and focused target without requiring a screenshot, with app/URL/title provenance
A browser operation that returns the active tab's selected text and a stable editable-target descriptor
An ephemeral context envelope shared between Mac, relay, pendant, and browser, with redaction, TTL, and size limits
A staging API that proposes an insertion and returns a diff/target preview before any write
Pendant protocol messages for context-ready, answer-ready, and insertion-preview audio/haptic states
A dashboard view showing the source, payload expiry, and exact target of any staged insertion

proposals.user_asks: “If one part of the system is unavailable, keep the useful part moving and tell me exactly what is waiting—then finish the private step automatically when that device comes back.”
proposals.why_useful: A disconnected browser currently strands an entire request even when the relay, pendant, and Mac are healthy. The owner should get graceful partial completion: public research, local drafting, and a clear pending private step can proceed now; authenticated reads or writes wait without being retried blindly, then resume only after the original session and target are verified. This is a fault-tolerant cross-surface workflow, not another watcher or daily brief.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic dependency analysis and health checks to split work. Use a cheap background model to summarize completed portions and explain the blocked portion. Use realtime only to answer the owner's immediate question or accept a change to the fallback plan.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect a missing surface within 5 seconds, produce a partial result within the normal task budget, and notify the owner once. On reconnection, validate state in under 10 seconds before proposing continuation; never silently execute a stale private mutation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually $0.001–$0.01 extra for a partial-result explanation; health checks, dependency tracking, and continuation validation are deterministic. This reduces wasted model and browser retries.
proposals.security_concerns: Private steps must retain only opaque session/tab references and a redacted intent until the browser returns. Public fallback must never receive authenticated page content. Continuation must compare origin, URL, title, session binding, and a page fingerprint; any mismatch becomes a review item. Mutations always require a newly rendered preview, even if the original request was approved.
missing: A typed task dependency graph that can mark steps complete, blocked, substituted, or awaiting a surface
A policy-controlled fallback planner distinguishing public data, local files, authenticated reads, and irreversible writes
A durable continuation record with session/tab binding, page fingerprint, expiry, and stale-state detection
A single partial-result protocol for pendant speech, Mac receipts, and dashboard status
A reconnect validator that re-plans only the blocked steps and emits a clear diff before continuing

proposals.user_asks: “Play my queued briefings on the pendant, and keep going from where I left off if the connection drops.”
proposals.why_useful: The current pipeline can render 24 kHz mono PCM and mark it waiting, but the wearable's actual decoder is Opus at 24 kHz in 60 ms frames. An interrupted download or format mismatch can strand an otherwise completed briefing. This would make long briefings and scheduled audio dependable: the owner hears each item once, can pause/resume, and does not need to repeat the request after LTE or bridge loss.
proposals.model_tier: Background/scheduled work uses a cheaper model only to rank and label queued audio; no expensive realtime reasoning is needed during playback. Realtime is used only when the owner interrupts or asks a follow-up. The pendant firmware handles packet timing locally.
proposals.latency_budget: Start playback within 2 seconds when a complete object is available; resume within 1 second after link recovery. Upload/render can remain asynchronous. A 60 ms jitter buffer and at least 3 acknowledged frames should mask normal LTE variability.
proposals.cost_estimate: Small per-briefing relay/storage cost; roughly one TTS render plus Opus transcode, dominated by audio duration and R2 egress. No extra LLM call for ordinary playback. Receipts and resume metadata are tiny D1 records.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio may contain private calendar/mail content. Bind each manifest and frame request to the owner's authenticated device/session, use short-lived signed URLs, encrypt in transit, and delete audio plus manifests according to the existing retention policy. Never synthesize or enqueue a new spoken response from a stale or unverified job. Playback is safe without confirmation; generating a briefing that reads private sources still follows their source permissions.
missing: A canonical Opus 24 kHz/60 ms object format and manifest (codec, sequence count, duration, hash, loudness metadata) instead of accepting ambiguous PCM at relay_result
Resumable range/frame fetch with per-frame acknowledgements, idempotency keys, and a durable pendant playback cursor that survives reboot
A relay-side transcode/validation step that rejects mismatched sample rate/codec before advertising 'waiting for the pendant'
A Mac/relay fallback policy: if the pendant is offline, retain the item and expose queued/started/paused/completed state rather than replaying it
Firmware implementation within the nRF9160 CPU/RAM budget, including jitter buffer, cursor persistence, and an explicit cancel/skip gesture

proposals.user_asks: “When I say ‘put this in front of me,’ use the pendant to hand the conversation to my Mac: open the relevant document or logged-in page, place the exact cited passage and next action in a review note, and tell me when the handoff is ready.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the pendant can converse and the Mac can act, but the owner must manually explain the handoff, find the source again, and reconstruct what was decided. This creates a physical-to-desktop continuation: a short spoken request becomes a bounded, source-linked workspace waiting on the Mac without losing the conversational context or silently submitting anything.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to recognize the handoff intent and capture the owner's short clarification. Use a cheaper background model to resolve citations, select the target app/page, and format the review note. The Mac executor performs deterministic opening and note-writing actions.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 500 ms, create a handoff capsule within 3 seconds, and stage the Mac workspace within 8 seconds when the required app/session is available. If a private browser session is unavailable, leave a clearly marked pending capsule rather than guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small background-model call per handoff, plus negligible relay/D1 storage and normal Mac/browser operations. No vision call is needed when an existing URL, file path, or cited source locator is available; vision is an optional fallback only.
proposals.security_concerns: The capsule may contain private mail, calendar, or logged-in webpage content. Encrypt it in transit, bind it to the paired pendant and Mac session, redact secrets by default, and retain it briefly. Opening a page and creating a note are reversible; sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting anything must remain outside the handoff and require the owner's existing confirmation policy. Show source URL/path, timestamp, and quoted hash in the note so stale content is visible.
missing: A cross-surface handoff capsule schema carrying conversation ID, source citations, quoted text hash, target surface, requested next action, freshness deadline, and sensitivity
A relay-to-Mac delivery/acknowledgement channel with idempotency and expiry, distinct from ordinary action jobs
A provenance-aware Mac staging operation that can open a file/page and create a review note without treating the note as an instruction to submit
Browser-session reattachment and freshness verification before placing authenticated content in the capsule
Pendant feedback states for accepted, waiting-for-Mac, ready, stale, and failed handoffs

proposals.user_asks: “When I walk away from my Mac, pause anything private and put my browser work into a safe state; when I come back wearing the pendant, restore only what I was actively using.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is continuously with the owner and can provide a stronger presence signal than a Mac timer. This would prevent private mail, account pages, or spoken audio from remaining exposed during an unexpected interruption, while preserving the exact working state instead of forcing a full restart. It is a coordinated physical-presence feature that neither the pendant nor Mac can safely provide alone.
proposals.model_tier: No LLM is needed for presence transitions. Use deterministic firmware/relay state machines; a cheap background model may classify which open work is resumable after return. Realtime is reserved for an explicit spoken override.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause or mute within 2 seconds of confirmed departure and secure browser state within 5 seconds. Resume only after a stable return signal for 3–5 seconds, avoiding flapping at the edge of radio range.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; small relay state and event traffic. Hardware cost depends on presence signal: approximately $2–5 for a BLE-capable companion/proximity design if the current radio cannot provide sufficiently reliable proximity, with modest battery impact.
proposals.security_concerns: A proximity token must not become an unlock credential by itself. Use encrypted rotating challenge-response, require the already-paired pendant and Mac identity, and let the owner choose whether return restores tabs, unmutes audio, or only displays a summary. Never auto-submit or send anything. Departure should redact or lock sensitive content, not delete it.
missing: A signed, debounced pendant-presence signal with explicit departed/returned confidence and replay protection
Mac privacy actions that can mute pendant playback, lock or blur selected windows, and snapshot browser session state without destructive mutation
Browser extension support for freezing authenticated tabs and restoring only the owner-approved active set
A durable cross-surface state machine with crash recovery and an owner-visible audit trail
A first-run policy UI defining which apps/pages/audio may pause, hide, or restore

proposals.user_asks: “Make sure that actually happened everywhere I asked, and tell me if anything is out of sync.” After an action spanning my Mac and a logged-in browser, reconcile the intended end state against independent observations, identify partial completion or conflicting state, and prepare the smallest repair plan without silently retrying.
proposals.why_useful: Today a receipt can say an action completed even when Mac input never reached the screen, while browser commands can remain queued against a private session. The owner needs an end-state guarantee, not merely an execution log: one answer showing which surfaces agree, which do not, and what repair would change.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the owner's live request and concise spoken status; use a cheaper background model for reconciliation, evidence comparison, and repair-plan generation. Use deterministic checks before any model interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the request within 1 second; perform quick local checks within 5 seconds. Allow background reconciliation to continue after the conversation and notify the pendant when evidence converges or a repair decision is needed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one low-cost background text-model invocation plus deterministic Mac/browser reads; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per reconciliation depending on page evidence size. Realtime cost is limited to the initial request and final short status.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and local application state must stay scoped to the requested job and be minimized in relay events. Never replay a stale browser mutation merely because the intended state is absent; distinguish unknown from false and require explicit owner confirmation for a repair that could duplicate an external side effect. Store hashes and provenance rather than full sensitive content where possible.
missing: A cross-surface end-state assertion schema that describes the intended result independently of the action list
Independent postcondition readers for Mac files/apps and browser DOM/session state
Receipt-to-observation reconciliation with confidence, freshness, and conflict states
A repair planner that understands non-idempotent external effects and produces a reviewable diff
Relay and pendant notification support for partial, conflicting, and finally-verified outcomes

proposals.user_asks: Don't interrupt me at the wrong time. Collect anything urgent from my pendant, Mac, calendar/mail, and logged-in browser, decide whether it can wait, and deliver it through the right surface when I'm actually available. If I miss it, leave one sourced, expiring queue item I can acknowledge later.
proposals.why_useful: Current briefs and page watches can find information but cannot arbitrate attention across surfaces. This would prevent stale browser alerts during meetings, avoid repeated spoken interruptions, and preserve one auditable handoff from discovery to delivery and acknowledgment.
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model for event normalization, deduplication, urgency scoring, and capsule composition; realtime tier only for the brief spoken handoff or a live follow-up question.
proposals.latency_budget: Event ingestion under 5 seconds; quiet-mode decisions under 1 second; spoken handoff under 2 seconds after an availability event; background reconciliation can take minutes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per event batch using a cheap model; realtime cost only when the owner answers or requests explanation. Dominant cost is browser extraction and repeated context, reduced by hashes and compact citations.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar/mail/browser content is private and should remain local or authenticated relay paths; capsules must carry source URLs/snippet hashes, sensitivity labels, expiry, and delivery audit. Never infer urgency from an offline or unauthenticated browser. Require explicit owner action for any send/submit; acknowledgment is not approval to mutate external systems.
missing: A shared attention-state event schema (pendant availability, quiet hours, meeting/foreground state, browser health, urgency, expiry).
A relay-side durable attention queue with deduplication, leases, acknowledgment/snooze/expire, and exactly-once delivery receipts.
Pendant availability/quiet-mode events and a low-friction acknowledge/snooze gesture.
Mac read-only implementations (the granted mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources currently return schema-only errors) plus a foreground/meeting signal.
Browser liveness envelope and command epoch integration so stale/offline tabs cannot generate current alerts.
A dashboard view showing queued capsules, provenance, expiry, and delivery history.

proposals.user_asks: When I'm in a meeting or around other people, keep private browser, mail, and calendar details out of spoken responses. Tell me only that something needs attention, and put the details in a local Mac review panel until I explicitly unlock them.
proposals.why_useful: Timing/quiet-mode alone does not prevent accidental disclosure: a perfectly timed voice alert can still speak a subject line or account detail aloud. This creates a cross-surface privacy boundary while retaining useful awareness.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap/background classifier for sensitivity labels and meeting-state reconciliation; realtime model only produces a generic redacted sentence. No model should receive full content when a local rule can redact it.
proposals.latency_budget: Privacy decision must complete before any spoken payload (<100 ms after an event); local review panel can update within 2 seconds; unlock and detail retrieval may take 1–3 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-based redaction; <$0.005 only for ambiguous sensitivity classification. Main cost is local/browser extraction, not generation.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitive payloads remain on the Mac or authenticated browser session; relay receives opaque item IDs, urgency, and redacted text by default. Meeting detection should use Calendar/foreground signals, not microphone capture. Explicit unlock is scoped, time-limited, and logged; never read full content aloud while privacy lock is active.
missing: A privacy-state contract shared by pendant, relay, and Mac (public, private, meeting, unlocked-until).
Local Mac review panel/API that can hold encrypted detail payloads and release them only after a deliberate unlock gesture.
Browser/Mail/Calendar sensitivity metadata and redaction before relay serialization.
A pendant privacy-lock and scoped unlock gesture that works offline and survives reconnect.

proposals.user_asks: "When a browser-dependent task is waiting, keep it safely queued and tell me on the pendant exactly whether it is queued, stale, blocked, or completed; when Chrome reconnects, resume only still-valid steps and give me one completion receipt instead of replaying old commands."
proposals.why_useful: The live system currently has Chrome offline with 10 pending commands, while the Mac journal shows browser_navigate failed 9/9 times and 112/120 jobs lack tier attribution. Today the owner cannot distinguish a command that never reached Chrome from one that ran against an old tab, and reconnecting risks duplicate or stale actions. This makes the wearable/Mac/browser/relay combination dependable rather than silently accumulating work.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic state machine and background model only for summarizing receipts; never spend the realtime tier on queue bookkeeping. Use the planner only if a resumed multi-step goal needs replanning after a tab or auth state changed.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 300 ms from relay state; reconnect reconciliation under 2 s for command metadata; browser execution remains bounded by the extension's normal response time. If offline, speak one short queued/stale sentence and do not pretend completion.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for state transitions and receipts; roughly 1–2k background tokens only when generating a human summary after a batch. Main cost is small durable metadata (command hash, tab/session binding, expiry, result cursor), under 10 KB per queued task.
proposals.security_concerns: Never persist page contents or cookies in the relay; persist only opaque session/tab ids, action hashes, timestamps, and typed outcome codes. Auth pages, CAPTCHA, changed origin, and missing tabs become blocked/stale and require a fresh owner request; do not auto-replay clicks or form submissions. Browser reads may proceed under the owner's existing preference, but sending/deleting/purchasing stays confirmation-required. The pendant should announce only status, not sensitive page text.
missing: A durable browser command state machine with leases, TTL, idempotency hash, tab/session fingerprint, and explicit queued/running/stale/blocked/completed outcomes
A reconnect handshake in the browser extension that reports current tabs and accepts only unexpired commands whose fingerprint still matches
Relay-to-pendant compact status events and a single cited completion receipt correlating browser result, Mac job, and relay job
A read-only reconciliation endpoint that can mark pending commands stale without executing them

proposals.user_asks: "When I'm in a meeting or presenting, keep the pendant and Mac quiet unless something is genuinely urgent; hold everything else, then give me one short catch-up when the meeting ends—without recording the meeting unless I explicitly press the button."
proposals.why_useful: Today Calendar, the Mac foreground state, relay delivery, and pendant output do not share a single interruptibility decision. The owner can be interrupted by routine mail/browser/job results at exactly the wrong moment, or miss them because each surface queues independently. This creates a real capability no one node can provide: calendar-aware, device-wide attention arbitration with a privacy-preserving meeting boundary.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic policy for meeting boundaries, urgency, quiet delivery, and queue coalescing; background model only to produce the post-meeting three-item digest. Realtime is reserved for an explicit spoken interruption or emergency alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Calendar/foreground changes reflected across surfaces within 1 second. Emergency alerts bypass within 300 ms; routine events are held. Post-meeting digest is ready within 5 seconds of the boundary, with no waiting on a large model call for the mode switch.
proposals.cost_estimate: Almost no model cost during meetings; one short background summarization call per meeting digest, typically 500–1,500 input tokens. Durable queue metadata is under 1 KB per event; audio recording remains zero unless the owner explicitly activates capture.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar event titles and foreground-app names should be reduced to a local sensitivity class (meeting, presenting, private, free) before leaving the Mac. Never infer or transmit meeting audio; the relay receives only mode, urgency class, and opaque event ids. Emergency bypass must be configurable and auditable. Digest sources remain redacted by default and sending/deleting actions remain separate from notification.
missing: A shared interruptibility lease issued by the Mac/relay with start, end, reason class, and expiry, consumed by both pendant delivery and Mac/browser notifications
A deterministic urgency taxonomy and coalescer that turns held events into one bounded digest without silently dropping them
Calendar boundary and presentation detection using the already-authorized Calendar automation plus explicit owner button override; no microphone-based detection
A durable audit trail showing why an item was held, bypassed, delivered, or expired, and a recovery path for missed boundaries

proposals.user_asks: "For any answer or action, let me ask ‘what did you rely on?’ and hear a short source trail—what came from my Mac, browser, pendant, or the cloud, when it was observed, and what was inferred—without exposing page contents or secrets."
proposals.why_useful: The current system can execute across surfaces and produce receipts, but the owner cannot distinguish a fresh Calendar/Mail fact from a stale browser observation, a planner inference, or a relay-generated claim. A compact provenance trail would let them trust, correct, or retract an answer without reading raw logs or sending private page text to the cloud. This is a new epistemic capability, not another action gate or job-status screen.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic provenance graph and freshness/confidence calculations; use a cheap background model only to verbalize the already-structured trail into one sentence. Never use the realtime tier merely to build provenance.
proposals.latency_budget: Attach provenance identifiers during execution with under 20 ms local overhead; answer a spoken ‘what did you rely on?’ query in under 500 ms from the durable graph. Raw evidence stays on the originating device; only the compact trail crosses surfaces.
proposals.cost_estimate: No per-turn model cost for capture or graph updates; roughly 200–600 tokens for an optional natural-language explanation. Storage is small: source id, timestamp, freshness, transform labels, and redacted hashes, under 2 KB per claim.
proposals.security_concerns: Store source classes, timestamps, redacted field names, and content hashes—not mail bodies, cookies, URLs with query secrets, or page text. Use per-owner encryption and expiry for sensitive provenance. The owner can delete a trail without deleting the underlying source. Clearly label inference and stale evidence; never claim a source was consulted when it was not.
missing: A claim-level provenance envelope propagated from Calendar/Mail/source reads and browser observations through planner, relay, TTS, and Mac action receipts
A privacy-preserving evidence registry with freshness/expiry, redacted hashes, and source-local retention
A compact pendant query/response protocol for ‘why do you think that?’ and ‘forget this evidence’
Dashboard visualization that joins claim ids to job/action/pipeline ids without revealing protected content

proposals.user_asks: “Read the key number or sentence from the private page I’m looking at, say it to me once through the pendant, and forget it afterward.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the browser can hold an authenticated page and the pendant can speak, but there is no deliberate one-shot private handoff: the owner must expose the page to another surface, risk leaving sensitive text in durable research/session history, or read it themselves. This would let them retrieve a balance, deadline, tracking number, or short instruction hands-free while preserving a clear ephemeral boundary.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background/text extraction model for selecting the requested field and redacting surrounding content; use realtime only for the owner’s live request and one short spoken response. No model should summarize beyond the requested field.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds after the browser bridge responds; one browser read and one short TTS/audio delivery. If the bridge is unavailable, say so immediately rather than substituting a public or stale page.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically a few cents or less per invocation; browser extraction and a short realtime/TTS turn dominate, with no need for a long context resend.
proposals.security_concerns: The browser extension must return only the requested semantic field, not a full page. Redact secrets by default, display the source tab/domain and capture time in the response metadata, keep the spoken payload in volatile memory/audio buffers only, and delete the associated capsule/session transcript immediately after successful delivery. Require an explicit spoken confirmation for values classified as authentication secrets, payment credentials, or one-time codes; never read those automatically. If audio is routed through the relay, the selected phrase leaves the Mac briefly, so the owner needs a privacy setting that permits or forbids relay transit.
missing: An ephemeral, non-persisting browser extraction contract with a field-size limit and source-domain receipt.
A relay audio delivery mode that acknowledges playback and then cryptographically/transactionally purges text, audio, and trace payloads.
A cross-surface privacy classification/redaction service that distinguishes ordinary private facts from credentials and one-time secrets.
A pendant response primitive for one-shot playback with no replay/history affordance.
A durable deletion receipt proving the handoff payload and derived audio were purged without retaining the sensitive value.

proposals.user_asks: “Pause here; when I say resume, put me back exactly where I was and remind me what I was doing.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant becomes a reliable interruption buffer: it records the Mac's foreground app, open work files, authenticated browser tabs, and the next calendar item, then later restores only the reversible parts and speaks a one-sentence orientation. No single node can do this: the pendant supplies the interruption trigger, the relay keeps the capsule while the owner is away, the Mac observes and restores desktop state, and the browser bridge preserves private tab/session context.
proposals.model_tier: Use Realtime only for the short pause/resume utterance and spoken confirmation; use a cheaper background model to label the captured context and rank the likely next action. Deterministic code should capture, diff, and restore state; no model should invent paths or URLs.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause acknowledgement under 1 second with a local/relay receipt; capsule completion within 3 seconds when Mac and browser are online. Resume should speak immediately from the stored capsule, then restore app/file/tab state in under 8 seconds. If the browser is offline, say so and restore the Mac portion instead of waiting 45 seconds for browser timeout.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per pause/resume, dominated by the small background labeling call; routine pauses can be zero-model deterministic records. Storage is a few KB of redacted metadata per capsule plus optional short note, with configurable expiry.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules contain private app names, file paths, calendar titles, and authenticated tab URLs, so encrypt at rest, redact query parameters and page text by default, and expire after 7 days. Never capture passwords, form fields, clipboard contents, screenshots, or microphone audio. Restoring an app, file, or browser tab is reversible and can be automatic; sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting anything remains outside restore and requires the owner's existing confirmation policy. Clearly label stale/offline browser state.
missing: A durable capsule schema with provenance, TTL, redaction, and per-surface freshness
A pendant pause/resume event that survives a dropped link and queues a capsule identifier offline
A fast preflight that skips offline browser commands instead of waiting for their timeout
An implementation (not just schema) for read-only Mac inspection; until then, use the existing /observe route as the fallback

proposals.user_asks: “Why didn’t that work? Diagnose the Mac and browser connection, tell me the one thing I need to fix, and keep trying once it’s fixed.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner sees long browser timeouts, fake-success UI receipts, and opaque “failed” jobs. A spoken repair flight recorder would correlate the pendant request, relay pipeline, Mac reachability/TCC state, browser heartbeat, and job receipts; give one actionable diagnosis instead of a vague error; then automatically retry only the failed, non-destructive step after the relevant surface returns.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic rules for diagnosis and retry eligibility; use a cheap background model only to turn the evidence into one short spoken explanation. Realtime handles the owner's question and acknowledgement, not the investigation.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial diagnosis under 2 seconds from cached health state, with active probes capped at 3 seconds. Never wait on a browser command's 45-second timeout when /browser/status already says offline. After heartbeat recovery, retry within 5 seconds and report the original receipt plus the new receipt.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually zero model calls for rules; under $0.005 when narration needs summarization. Small durable records (health snapshots, job IDs, and error classes) can expire after 24 hours.
proposals.security_concerns: Diagnostics may include app names, tab URLs, file paths, and TCC state. Keep raw details local and send the relay only an error class, timestamps, and redacted labels unless the owner asks for detail. Never retry send/delete/buy/submit actions; retry only idempotent reads and explicitly reversible opens. Do not attempt to grant Accessibility or Screen Recording—tell the owner the exact manual System Settings action required.
missing: A correlation ID shared across pendant request, pipeline, browser command, and Mac job receipts
A failure classifier that distinguishes offline, timeout, TCC-untrusted UI, permission denial, and malformed plans
A retry ledger with idempotency keys and an explicit allowlist of safe retry types
A browser heartbeat recovery event and a Mac-side TCC remediation hint

proposals.user_asks: “Finish this when I come back, but only if nothing important changed; otherwise tell me exactly what changed before touching anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets safe continuity across interruptions without having to remember whether a draft, tab, or file changed. The system captures a proof of the relevant Mac file, foreground app, browser tab, and task intent; later the relay and pendant can detect a mismatch and explain it instead of blindly replaying stale actions. This is different from a durable job queue: it is state-conditional continuation with an explicit before/after explanation.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic hashes, timestamps, tab identity, and file metadata for the state proof. Use a cheap background model only to summarize the differences. Realtime is reserved for the brief spoken confirmation or alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture under 1 second. Resume validation under 2 seconds from Mac and browser health/state, with a hard 3-second timeout per surface. If a surface is offline, preserve the continuation and tell the owner which proof is unavailable rather than executing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost for metadata and hashes; under $0.005 only when a model summarizes meaningful differences. Each continuation proof should be under 10 KB and expire after an owner-selected period.
proposals.security_concerns: Never hash or upload raw passwords, clipboard contents, form values, or page bodies by default. Keep file hashes and private URLs local; relay receives only opaque capsule IDs and redacted difference summaries. A mismatch must block continuation, not be treated as approval. Sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting remains excluded and requires the existing owner confirmation policy.
missing: A durable continuation record containing task intent, per-surface state proofs, expiry, and an idempotency key
Mac file/app proofs and browser DOM-region or semantic proofs that can be compared without exporting private content
A validator that atomically compares all proofs immediately before execution and emits structured diffs
A resume protocol from pendant to relay that can survive offline periods and distinguish stale, changed, and unavailable state

proposals.user_asks: When my browser extension is disconnected, still tell me what you can verify from the Mac, and queue the private-page part to finish automatically when the browser reconnects.
proposals.why_useful: Today a browser request either blocks for 45 seconds or fails even though Calendar/Mail and local Mac state may still be available. This gives the owner a useful partial answer now, a clear missing-data notice, and an automatic continuation later without pretending the private page was read.
proposals.model_tier: Use no model for connectivity, source reads, queueing, or reconciliation; use the cheap background text tier only to merge verified snippets into a short brief. Reserve realtime for the owner's follow-up question.
proposals.latency_budget: Return local verified findings and a queued receipt within 1 second; browser continuation runs in the background after heartbeat and should not block the voice turn.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost; metadata and one short background summary dominate. No page body leaves the Mac unless the owner requested that source.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep authenticated page bodies on the Mac/relay boundary, redact secrets from the partial brief, bind queued work to the original tab/session, and never submit forms or send messages as part of recovery. Report stale or unverified data explicitly.
missing: A durable reconnect/resume worker rather than the current single blocking browser wait
An implemented read-only Mac source/inspection tool (the newly granted schemas currently return no implementation)
The reachability/truth envelope proposed this round
Browser heartbeat-triggered delivery to pendant speech and dashboard

proposals.user_asks: If I leave my Mac halfway through a task, let me resume it from the pendant later—'continue the draft' or 'finish the research'—with the exact open tabs, files, findings, and next safe step restored.
proposals.why_useful: Today a long task is tied to one live Mac session; leaving the machine loses the working set or forces a restart. A portable continuation capsule would make the pendant a genuine always-present control surface for work that began on the Mac, without replaying completed actions or exposing unrelated desktop context.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to summarize and compact the task capsule; use realtime only to interpret the pendant's short resume command and answer immediate status questions.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture a capsule in under 2 seconds when the task pauses; restore the working set and return a spoken status in under 3 seconds when the owner resumes. Long research or browser work continues asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small background summarization call per pause/resume, typically well below a cent; storage is a few KB per capsule. The dominant cost is only if the owner asks for a fresh synthesis of the preserved sources.
proposals.security_concerns: Capsules may contain authenticated URLs, draft text, filenames, and private findings. Encrypt them at rest, bind them to the owner's paired pendant and Mac session, apply per-source sensitivity and expiry, and omit page bodies/secrets unless explicitly requested. Resuming must never send, submit, delete, purchase, or overwrite without the existing owner policy for that action.
missing: A portable, encrypted continuation-capsule format with source references, completed action IDs, pending steps, and expiry
A relay endpoint and pendant command for listing, selecting, expiring, and resuming capsules
Mac and browser adapters that can reattach to the saved session/tab/file identifiers and report which references are stale
A reconciliation layer that refuses to replay completed actions and explains when a saved tab or file no longer exists

proposals.user_asks: If my private browser connection breaks, tell me immediately, pause and preserve any queued work, then reconnect and resume only the safe steps without duplicating anything; give me a concise recovery report.
proposals.why_useful: Today the bridge reports contradictory online states and has 11 stale commands, including one processing for 19 attempts. Browser tasks silently time out or can be retried into duplicates. A cross-surface circuit breaker would protect authenticated work, let the pendant report the outage, and recover automatically when Chrome/Safari returns.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic relay/Mac state machines for heartbeats, lease expiry, idempotency, queue quarantine, and replay; use the realtime model only to explain the incident to the wearer and classify ambiguous recovery, never to decide whether a mutation is safe.
proposals.latency_budget: Heartbeat detection within 15 seconds; pendant alert under 2 seconds after relay receives the fault; reconnect probe within 30 seconds; replay only after three healthy heartbeats. Recovery report under 5 seconds after replay completes.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for normal operation; roughly $0.001–$0.01 only when the realtime model summarizes a failure or asks the owner to resolve an ambiguous step. Dominant cost is durable queue/state storage and heartbeat traffic.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated URLs and extracted page data must stay local to the Mac/extension and be referenced by opaque job IDs in relay telemetry. Never replay submit/send/purchase/delete steps automatically; quarantine them with before-state evidence and require the existing owner-controlled review path. Expire leases and wipe quarantined payloads according to retention settings.
missing: A browser queue circuit breaker that distinguishes stale/offline/processing leases from healthy commands
An idempotency-aware replay ledger shared by relay and Mac/browser bridge
A pendant-visible outage/recovery event and concise receipt format
A health handshake that verifies the actual tab/session, not only extension lastSeenAt

proposals.user_asks: When I say “pause this and pick it up when I’m free,” freeze the work across my pendant, Mac, and private browser exactly where it is, save a private resume capsule, and restart it at the next suitable calendar window with a one-sentence reminder of what was waiting.
proposals.why_useful: Today an interruption strands multi-step work: the browser may lose its tab, the Mac may leave half-written artifacts, and the pendant has no reliable way to resume the same intent later. This would let the owner defer difficult work without re-explaining it or risking duplicate actions, while respecting meetings and focus time.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic state capture, calendar-window selection, leases, and idempotency for the mechanics; use a cheaper background model to compress the resume capsule and rank suitable windows. Reserve realtime only for the spoken pause/resume exchange.
proposals.latency_budget: A pause acknowledgement within 2 seconds, capsule persistence within 5 seconds, and resume scheduling immediately after calendar synchronization. On resume, restore state before speaking; the spoken reminder should take under 10 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per pause/resume, dominated by one small background summarization call; calendar reads, local snapshots, and durable capsule storage are the main non-model costs.
proposals.security_concerns: Resume capsules may contain authenticated URLs, drafts, and local filenames. Keep raw contents on the Mac/browser session, store only encrypted references and hashes on the relay, apply owner-configured retention, and never auto-submit/send/purchase after resumption. If a page or file changed, stop and report the conflict instead of guessing.
missing: A first-class resumable-work capsule spanning relay jobs, Mac receipts, and browser tab/session state
Atomic pause semantics that stop new mutations while allowing the current reversible step to finish
Calendar-aware resume scheduler with quiet hours and conflict detection
Conflict UI/voice flow showing what changed since pause and offering resume, revise, or discard

proposals.user_asks: When my browser is offline, queue this request safely, do whatever can be completed on my Mac without the browser, and resume the authenticated browser steps when the bridge returns; tell me on the pendant exactly what completed, what is waiting, and what still needs my approval.
proposals.why_useful: The current browser can be offline with orphaned tabs and pending commands. Today a request either fails or leaves the owner wondering whether retrying will duplicate work. This makes the hive resilient: the pendant remains the control surface, the relay owns durable intent, the Mac performs independent reversible preparation, and the browser resumes only the missing authenticated steps with a clear receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the short spoken status and ambiguity resolution; use a cheaper background model for intent decomposition, dependency analysis, retry scheduling, and receipt summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant in under 1 second; decompose and persist the plan in under 3 seconds; resume automatically within one heartbeat after browser recovery. Do not block local Mac work on browser availability.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per queued request depending on decomposition and final summary; most retries, heartbeat checks, and receipt generation are deterministic and should not invoke the expensive model.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist intent and step state, not browser cookies or page bodies, in the relay. Keep authenticated extraction on the existing browser bridge; redact secrets from receipts. Never send or submit a browser mutation automatically after recovery: preserve the owner's existing destructive confirmation policy and show before/after evidence. Quarantine stale leases and require idempotency keys so reconnects cannot duplicate a form submission.
missing: A durable dependency-aware intent record that can split Mac-local and browser-only steps and survive reconnects
Lease expiry/quarantine for stale browser commands plus resumable checkpoints keyed by request and step id
A typed handoff receipt that joins Mac job receipts, browser results, and pendant audio/status events
A browser recovery event or heartbeat contract that distinguishes a fresh bridge from an old session

proposals.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” on the pendant, capture the thought, identify what I was looking at in the browser and what meeting or project it relates to, then create one private, cited Markdown note in my AI-Pendant-Workspace and tell me where it was saved. If the browser or Mac is temporarily unavailable, hold the capsule and finish it automatically when they return.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can speak an idea while walking away from the computer and later recover not just the words, but the page, project, and time context that make the idea useful. No single surface can do this: the pendant has the moment of capture, the relay can retain the intent, the browser has private page context, and the Mac has the durable workspace and local calendar/project data.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to detect the short capture command and acknowledge it. Use a cheaper background model to transcribe, resolve page/project context, generate the Markdown note, and produce the final receipt.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 1 second and persist the raw capsule immediately. Finalize within 10 seconds when all surfaces are online; otherwise tell the owner it is held and complete it within one browser/Mac heartbeat after recovery.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per capsule; transcription and context resolution dominate. Deterministic storage, file creation, retries, and receipts should not invoke a model.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio should be discarded after transcription unless the owner explicitly chooses retention. Browser content may contain secrets, so store only the minimum cited excerpt and URL, redact credentials and tokens, and never include private page text in spoken acknowledgements. Writing a note is permitted by the owner's current policy, but the file path and sources must be shown in the receipt.
missing: A first-class offline capture capsule with durable id, transcript, source timestamp, and retry state
A browser-context snapshot API that returns the active tab's URL/title plus a bounded cited excerpt without requiring a live UI scrape
A context joiner that can associate the capsule with Calendar/project entities while preserving provenance and freshness
An idempotent Mac note writer that creates one Markdown artifact and updates it rather than duplicating it after retries
A pendant acknowledgement and later-completion event contract for held capsules

proposals.user_asks: If the pendant loses signal or I interrupt you halfway through a task, keep my place and resume it later without losing my words or repeating any Mac/browser actions.
proposals.why_useful: Today an LTE-M drop can lose seconds of speech while the Mac job may still be running, leaving the owner unsure whether to repeat the request and risking duplicate clicks or submissions. A resumable handoff would preserve the unsent audio locally, reconcile it with relay/job receipts, and continue only from the last acknowledged step.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to acknowledge the interruption and classify the handoff; use a cheaper background model to transcribe/reconcile queued audio and summarize the resume state. The Mac and browser agents execute no step twice: they consume idempotency keys and receipts.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local interruption marker and one short spoken acknowledgement under 1 s; reconnect upload in the background. Resume summary within 10 s of link recovery, bounded by the existing job/browser polling cadence.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per interruption, dominated by background transcription/reconciliation; negligible when no interruption occurs. SD buffering and receipt reconciliation are local/server metadata, not model-heavy.
proposals.security_concerns: Unsent audio temporarily resides on the pendant SD and transcript/job metadata on the relay; encrypt SD files, bind them to an authenticated session, expire them after successful acknowledgement, and expose a delete-now gesture. Never auto-resume an irreversible browser or Mac mutation without a durable pre-action receipt and explicit owner instruction; private page content stays in the authenticated browser session.
missing: Pendant firmware interruption journal with encrypted sequence-numbered audio chunks and a local 'resume pending' state
Relay reconciliation service joining audio sequence ACKs to Mac/browser job receipts and issuing a resumable capsule
Mac/browser executors must persist idempotency keys and last-completed step before each action
Owner-facing resume capsule/notification and dashboard view of pending, resumed, and discarded work
A real packet-loss/half-duplex test fixture across LTE-M, relay, Mac bridge, and browser session

proposals.user_asks: “Make my browser available, then handle the thing I just asked about.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a stopped extension leaves commands queued and the Mac reports misleading validation failures. This gives the owner one reliable spoken recovery path: the pendant starts the recovery, the relay coordinates it, the Mac verifies the bridge, and only then does the browser agent continue with evidence and a final receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to understand the short spoken request and report status; use a cheap background planner for action normalization, heartbeat polling, and queue reconciliation. Browser extraction can use the existing slower research tier.
proposals.latency_budget: A healthy bridge should continue in under 2 seconds. If offline, allow one launch and a 15-second bounded heartbeat wait, then tell the owner it could not recover rather than looping.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental model cost for healthy requests; one short realtime turn plus inexpensive background orchestration. Dominant cost is any subsequent authenticated-page extraction, not recovery.
proposals.security_concerns: The browser may hold private authenticated tabs. Relay receives only bridge state, request IDs, and summarized receipts; page contents remain on the Mac/browser path. Never auto-submit or auto-replay stale queued mutations; show the owner which queued reads are safe and require an explicit continuation for writes.
missing: Shared action-contract normalization at the /execute/computerControl boundary
A launch-and-heartbeat recovery endpoint/state machine
Queue reconciliation that classifies pending commands by idempotency and read/write effect
Extension reconnect UX that surfaces the recovered tab/session in the dashboard and pendant status

proposals.user_asks: “My browser was disconnected. Tell me exactly what was attempted, what never ran, and let me resume only the safe items.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can be left with queued browser commands and failed Mac receipts, but no single cross-device explanation of whether a request was attempted, duplicated, or merely waiting. They need a trustworthy reconnect report before continuing private browser work.
proposals.model_tier: Use a deterministic background reconciliation service for request/receipt comparison; use the realtime model only to turn the resulting structured report into a short spoken explanation and to interpret the owner's choice of items to resume.
proposals.latency_budget: Generate the report within 3 seconds of reconnection; resume selected read-only items immediately and keep writes staged for a later explicit spoken choice.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal model cost: normally one short realtime response, with deterministic reconciliation dominating compute. No page re-reading unless the owner selects an item whose evidence has expired.
proposals.security_concerns: The report must distinguish attempted versus completed without exposing page contents to the relay. Store hashes, request IDs, timestamps, tab/session IDs, and effect classes; redact URLs and snippets by default. Never resume a mutation solely because it was previously queued. Require an unambiguous item selection and preserve an append-only audit record.
missing: A cross-surface intent ledger linking pendant request IDs to Mac jobs, browser command IDs, and receipts
A disconnect epoch and reconnect watermark so queued work can be classified as pre-disconnect, in-flight, or post-reconnect
A read-only reconciliation endpoint returning item-level resume eligibility and evidence freshness
A dashboard and pendant interaction for selecting individual safe items rather than replaying the whole queue

proposals.user_asks: If I ask you to do something on a logged-in website while my browser is disconnected, park the request, reconnect the bridge, and continue exactly once when it is safe—then tell me what ran, what was skipped, and why. Never blindly replay the 12 commands already waiting.
proposals.why_useful: Today the Mac bridge is online but the browser is offline with 12 pending commands, leaving the owner unable to know whether a request is lost, delayed, or about to be duplicated. This makes the pendant/relay, Mac, and private browser act as one reliable system without risking stale or duplicate clicks.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for queue classification and retry/reconciliation; use realtime only to acknowledge the owner and report completion. Use the Mac planner for launching/observing the bridge, and the browser harness for authenticated-page work.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate spoken acknowledgment under 1 second; reconnect polling every 5–10 seconds while the Mac is awake; resume within roughly 30 seconds after a verified heartbeat. No work should be lost across a relay or Mac restart.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: mostly D1/R2 state transitions and heartbeat polling. One model call only when reconciling an ambiguous result or summarizing evidence; browser minutes dominate public-page fallback, which must not be used for private sessions.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, tab IDs, and extracted content stay on the authenticated Safari bridge and relay only receives typed status/evidence. The bridge must quarantine existing pending commands, assign request/action idempotency keys, verify tab/session affinity and a fresh heartbeat, and classify each result as not-started, started/unknown, succeeded, or skipped. No automatic replay of an unknown mutation; preserve the receipt for the owner. No approval gate is added—the owner policy is maximum access—but destructive actions still need explicit intent at the originating request.
