Shared temporal/entity normalization library
Durable reconciliation job and evidence-bundle storage
Dashboard and pendant rendering for competing claims

changes.change: Implement a redacted cross-surface handoff coordinator as a durable job type. It should fan out bounded Calendar/Mail reads, an authenticated browser extraction request, and a read-only Mac workspace inspection; normalize each result into {source, observedAt, sensitivity, citation, confidence, expiry}; redact before relay storage; produce a Markdown/JSON packet and an audio item; attach both to one jobId with receipts, partial-failure states, retry limits, and DELETE-by-job retention cleanup. A pendant request should create the job and receive progress events, not resend raw source context on every turn.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask once, hands-free, and get a trustworthy current state even when one source is unavailable. They see exactly where each fact came from, can review the packet on the Mac, and do not get stale or silently fabricated answers when the browser is offline.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a relay fan-out state machine, redaction/provenance schema, Mac adapter, browser timeout/reconnect handling, packet/audio writers, and dashboard/pendant progress UI. Start with read-only sources and a 10-second deadline.
changes.risk: Partial results could be mistaken for complete results; prevent this with a prominent completeness banner and per-source status. Browser page content may contain secrets or prompt injection; isolate extraction, strip instructions, and never execute page-provided actions. Crashes could leave artifacts; use idempotency keys and TTL cleanup. Recovery is retrying only failed source branches or deleting the job.
changes.cost_impact: Low per invocation beyond existing reads; background summarization and TTS dominate, roughly $0.01–$0.04. Storage is small (typically <100 KB packet plus audio) and should expire automatically.
changes.latency_impact: Parallel fan-out keeps typical completion under 10 seconds; browser offline path completes in 2–3 seconds with an explicit unavailable marker. Progress acknowledgement is sub-second.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making redaction, provenance, TTL, and source boundaries mandatory. No form submission or external sharing. Raw Mail/browser bodies remain on-device when feasible; relay receives only selected redacted excerpts.
depends_on: Implement mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect rather than schema-only stubs
Browser bridge online/reconnect and bounded authenticated extraction endpoint
A relay durable job schema with partial completion and deletion/retention controls
Existing /briefing, /research, /capture, pipeline audio, and job receipt primitives

changes.change: Add a deterministic duplex budget governor to the live WebSocket: reserve a minimum uplink budget for pendant capture, classify each 60 ms downlink frame by urgency, and when acknowledgements/loss exceed thresholds, stop enqueueing nonessential TTS frames, switch the transcoder to the negotiated fallback profile, and emit a signed session QoS event. On recovery, require 10 seconds of hysteresis before restoring 24 kHz. The relay should also attach a short continuity marker (sequence range and profile transition) so the pendant and Mac receipt can say exactly what was degraded.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant stops competing with the assistant's speech for the same constrained radio link. The owner hears a complete answer more often, and if a transition still occurs they get an honest, concise indication rather than unexplained silence or clipped speech.
changes.effort: Medium: relay scheduler/transcoder changes, firmware profile negotiation, deterministic contention tests, and a small dashboard panel. No new model training.
changes.risk: Bad thresholds could make speech sound lower quality too often or cause profile flapping; hysteresis, bounded profiles, and a simulated loss test recover safely. If the relay crashes, the current fixed 24 kHz path remains the fallback. Never discard uplink frames solely to improve downlink quality.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful API increase; modest relay CPU and a few QoS events per call. Firmware RAM about 1.5 KB for counters/profile state; no raw audio retention.
changes.latency_impact: Profile changes add at most one 60 ms frame and relay scheduling (<300 ms target); recovery waits for a 10-second stable window by design.
changes.security_impact: Encrypted audio path remains unchanged. QoS events carry sequence numbers/counters only, with rotating session IDs and short retention.
depends_on: pendant duplex_audio_congestion_guard skill
A negotiated Opus profile identifier shared by firmware and cloud-relay/opusTranscode.js
POST /pipeline/events accepting typed QoS events and durable audio receipts
An end-to-end half-duplex contention test harness

changes.change: For the wearable revision, separate radio/control from audio timing: retain the LTE-M modem but add a small audio companion (or an SoC with a hardware audio/DSP block and DMA) responsible for I2S capture/playback, Opus encode/decode buffering, and congestion counters. Give it independent 24 kHz playback timing and at least 256 KB audio-working RAM, while the modem MCU handles TLS and policy.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Full-quality speech will not collapse merely because the pendant is simultaneously encoding their voice, decoding a reply, and servicing the modem. It creates enough headroom for the adaptive path instead of making the owner choose between clarity and connectivity.
changes.effort: High and product-level: schematic/PCB/firmware port, power and RF validation, enclosure redesign, and a real wearable prototype rather than the current DK.
changes.risk: More components increase BOM, board area, and power; a new codec/DSP can introduce clock drift or driver bugs. Retain the current fixed-path firmware as a manufacturing test mode and run A/B field trials before switching default hardware.
changes.cost_impact: Rough prototype delta: approximately $8–$25 BOM depending on codec/MCU choice, plus board/NRE; likely 10–30 mW additional audio-domain power, offset by putting the companion to sleep between frames. No per-call API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Should reduce encode/decode contention and jitter; target <60 ms added buffering, with deterministic I2S clocks.
changes.security_impact: Audio remains inside the pendant's encrypted path; add secure boot/firmware signing for the companion and avoid exposing raw PCM over debug UART in production.
depends_on: Measured QoS traces from the current nRF9160 prototype
Negotiated adaptive Opus profiles and contention test results
Power-budget and enclosure study
Secure firmware-update chain covering both processors

changes.change: Add a cross-node duplex-audio congestion controller. The pendant periodically emits compact loss/jitter/queue telemetry; the relay combines it with WebSocket backpressure and transcoder load; the Mac bridge contributes current network/CPU availability when present. A shared controller then selects among 24-kHz wideband, 16-kHz speech, packet-duration/FEC presets, and brief downlink suppression, with hysteresis and an explicit reason in the call receipt. It must preserve the owner's speech first, recover to 24 kHz after a stable window, and never make the Mac microphone active.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: During simultaneous talking and agent playback, the owner currently loses about 7.8 seconds of speech. This would make conversations intelligible instead of silently dropping their words, while returning to the richer 24-kHz sound when the link recovers.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define a tiny telemetry frame and state machine in firmware, relay-side controller and Opus preset table, bridge health adapter, dashboard diagnostics, and end-to-end impairment tests.
changes.risk: A bad controller could oscillate quality or over-prioritize downlink. Use hysteresis, hard upper bounds, local pendant fallback, and a call receipt showing every mode change. If telemetry stops, fall back to conservative 16-kHz speech rather than disabling audio.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model/API cost; a few hundred bytes/minute of telemetry and modest relay CPU. Firmware RAM likely 4–8 kB for telemetry ring/state, plus test effort. No new per-call service expected.
changes.latency_impact: Telemetry adds under one frame of control delay; mode changes take roughly 0.5–2 seconds due to hysteresis. Conservative mode may add a small packetization delay but prevents multi-second speech loss.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry contains transport health only, not audio or transcript. Keep Mac network metrics local to the relay job, redact device identifiers in receipts, and retain mode history with existing short audio-job retention.
depends_on: A 24-kHz/16-kHz dual-mode codec path on the pendant and relay
A durable per-call audio telemetry/receipt schema
A bridge health endpoint that does not require microphone or screen access
An owner-visible audio quality preference (speech-first default)

changes.change: Add an interruption-aware deferred-job coordinator between /plan, /execute, /jobs, /routines, Calendar/Mail context, and the browser queue. It should persist eligibility rules (free calendar window, foreground/idle constraints, quiet hours), wake on context events or bounded polling, lease one job at a time, honor pendant cancellation, and attach the existing per-action receipts and undo links. This is scheduling/orchestration, not a new unrestricted executor and not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “when I’m free” once and trust that work will happen without interrupting a meeting or getting lost when the Mac/browser link briefly drops. They receive a clear staged/running/completed result rather than having to ask where the job went.
changes.effort: Medium-high: durable state schema and lease/retry worker, Mac context adapter, relay reconnect handling, and pendant cancel/status events; reuse existing jobs, routines, browser commands, and receipts.
changes.risk: A stale context could start during a newly begun meeting, or retries could duplicate browser steps. Mitigate with short-lived context freshness, idempotency keys, a single active lease, step-level receipts, and cancellation checked before every step. Recovery is cancel/undo where supported and an explicit failed receipt where it is not.
changes.cost_impact: Low background model/API cost; mostly deterministic polling and D1/local state. One cheap planner call per staged job plus occasional extraction calls.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement remains under 2 seconds; execution intentionally waits for the next eligible window. Context freshness adds at most one short poll interval.
changes.security_impact: No new access beyond existing Calendar/Mail AppleScript and browser sessions. Keep private context local/relay-minimized, TTL queued plans, and redact snippets in dashboard/pendant speech.
depends_on: Browser extension must reconnect and expose reliable command acknowledgements (currently live status reports browser online=false with 5 pending commands).
Implement the newly granted bounded mac_read_sources/mac_readonly_inspect surfaces; today they are schemas with no implementation.
Owner must manually enable Accessibility/Screen Recording if foreground/UI evidence is required; current /ops/status reports both false.

changes.change: Implement the two newly granted bounded read-only Mac tools rather than exposing schema-only stubs: mac_readonly_inspect should call a signed local helper for running apps, foreground app, browser tab metadata, accessibility state, UI snapshot, and allowlisted directory listings; mac_read_sources should use AppleScript/read-only EventKit/Mail queries for calendar and mail, enforce account_scope, redact by default, cap result sizes, and emit source timestamps plus receipts. Keep them separate from mac_run_actions and do not grant arbitrary shell access.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The assistant can currently act on the Mac but cannot reliably see what is open or read a bounded calendar/mail brief through the granted interfaces. Implementing these makes “what am I looking at?”, meeting preparation, and recovery from failed browser jobs dependable without scraping or mutating anything.
changes.effort: Medium: local helper adapters, permission/error normalization, redaction and tests for each source; browser tabs require extension bridge integration. UI snapshots remain unavailable until the owner grants Screen Recording/Accessibility to the correct binary.
changes.risk: Calendar/Mail queries could leak private content if scoping or redaction fails; mitigate with snippets-only defaults, strict size limits, account allowlists, audit receipts, and explicit unavailable states. UI inspection must never fall back to mouse or keystrokes. Recover by returning a typed permission/offline error, not guessed state.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost; bounded local reads are cheaper than model vision. Engineering cost is the main expense. UI snapshots may add local image storage/transport cost and should be opt-in.
changes.latency_impact: Typically 100–800 ms for app/tab/source metadata; UI snapshots may take 1–3 s and should be requested only when needed.
changes.security_impact: Read-only boundary materially reduces risk, but browser URLs/titles and mail/calendar snippets are sensitive. Keep data local where possible, redact by default, and attach provenance/TTL to every returned fact.
depends_on: mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources granted schemas need real implementations
A signed localhost helper with the existing bearer-token boundary
Owner TCC grants only for UI snapshot features; non-visual app/browser/source reads should work without them

changes.change: Implement a causal recovery ledger and fail-fast reconciler between the existing relay/Mac job and browser queues. On enqueue, assign one intentId and per-step idempotency key; persist edges intentId→jobId→actionId→commandId. On browser heartbeat/poll/result, reconcile each step into completed, failed-before-delivery, delivered-unknown, or completed-with-evidence. If status is offline, return immediately with a resumable checkpoint instead of waiting 45 seconds. On reconnect, replay only steps marked safe-to-retry, quarantine delivered-unknown writes, and emit a local recovery capsule through /capture containing the exact evidence and next action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection stops being a mystery: the pendant can say what definitely happened, what did not happen, and what needs review, without duplicate form submissions or a misleading failed receipt.
changes.effort: Medium: shared ledger schema, adapters in browserBridge/browserSessions and Mac job receipts, reconnect worker, tests for crash between delivery and result.
changes.risk: A ledger bug could incorrectly classify a mutation. Default ambiguous states to quarantine/no replay; preserve raw receipts and support manual retry. Existing jobs remain readable during migration.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible D1/local JSON storage and one cheap background reconciliation pass; no additional realtime calls.
changes.latency_impact: Offline browser actions fail in milliseconds rather than 45 seconds; reconnect adds one heartbeat cycle and bounded reconciliation.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability; store hashes/snippets and tab/session identifiers rather than full private page content in relay. Keep detailed evidence local unless explicitly shared.
depends_on: Browser extension reconnect/heartbeat must actually report online; currently /browser/status reports offline with 6 pending commands.
A durable runner/checkpoint implementation (chg-16bc5dee) should supply step boundaries, but this ledger remains useful if that runner is delayed.

changes.change: Add a deterministic recovery classifier before any LLM call. It consumes typed Mac/browser receipts and maps them to four states (done, not-started, failed, ambiguous) using idempotency keys, delivery timestamps, and before/after evidence; only ambiguous multi-step cases go to a background model, while the pendant receives a fixed short status template from the realtime tier.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an immediate, accurate answer after a disconnect and does not pay for an expensive model to interpret a simple receipt. More importantly, the system will not confidently hallucinate that a private browser action succeeded.
changes.effort: Small to medium: define receipt state machine, add tests for timeout/crash/reconnect orderings, and route only unresolved cases to background reconciliation.
changes.risk: A too-conservative classifier may say 'needs review' more often. That is preferable to duplicate or falsely reported actions; raw evidence and a retry path remain available.
changes.cost_impact: Usually near-zero model cost; background model only for genuinely ambiguous cases, reducing realtime tokens and repeated context transmission.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate (<200 ms) local classification; model-backed cases remain asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Reduces private page data sent to models because typed metadata is sufficient for most recovery decisions.
depends_on: Causal intentId/jobId/actionId/commandId links from the browser-harness recovery ledger.
Stable typed receipt fields from /jobs/:jobId/receipts and /browser/result/:commandId.

changes.change: Introduce a signed Context Capsule carried end-to-end with every request and artifact. The capsule contains an opaque profile ID, issuance/expiry, allowed surfaces, and a key version; the relay signs it, Mac and browser adapters verify it, and receipts/captures/briefings/memory writes inherit it automatically. Add a context firewall that rejects a job when its source capsule, active Mac project, browser session, or destination artifact disagree, while allowing an explicit owner-triggered reclassification that records both old and new context.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: “Work mode” becomes an enforceable privacy guarantee instead of a label in the prompt: a personal browser tab cannot accidentally feed a work briefing, and a work file cannot silently become part of personal memory.
changes.effort: Medium to high: shared capsule schema and signing, propagation through relay/Mac/browser APIs, context-aware memory projection, migration for existing untagged jobs, and dashboard diagnostics.
changes.risk: Existing jobs and third-party tabs may be untagged and get paused. Treat unknown as quarantined, provide a local labeling flow, and preserve all existing receipts; never auto-classify sensitive content.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny metadata overhead per request and receipt; no meaningful model cost. Key rotation and local capsule storage add minor implementation complexity.
changes.latency_impact: Milliseconds for signature verification and mismatch checks; no additional model round trip for normal actions.
changes.security_impact: Strongly reduces accidental cross-context disclosure, but requires secure key storage and careful handling of mode-switch events. The relay should retain only opaque IDs and audit hashes, not content.
depends_on: A durable owner-controlled work/personal mode source on the pendant or client.
Shared propagation hooks in relay, Mac job runner, browser sessions, context graph, and briefing/capture writers.
A migration policy for existing untagged sessions and artifacts.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface execution ledger and coordinator between existing /plan, /execute, browser command results, and job receipts. Every multi-step job gets a durable DAG of idempotent steps, a lease/heartbeat, required surface, input/output hashes, and monotonic sequence. A reconnecting browser or Mac claims only expired steps; a stale browser command is moved to dead-letter with its reason; completed steps are never replayed. Emit one normalized timeline to the dashboard and a compact pendant event. Keep payloads redacted and store full evidence only on the Mac when available.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the laptop sleeps, browser extension disappears, or a request times out, the owner can trust that work will resume once—not run twice—and can see exactly what happened without inspecting logs or guessing whether a form was submitted.
changes.effort: Medium: schema/migrations, coordinator state machine, browser and Mac adapters, retry tests, and dashboard timeline. No new model training.
changes.risk: A bad idempotency key could suppress a legitimate retry, while an overly short lease could cause duplicate work. Recover with explicit step fingerprints, conservative lease expiry, dead-letter/manual-retry controls, and receipt reconciliation before any mutation. Existing jobs should be imported as unknown/legacy rather than guessed complete.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/storage and heartbeat traffic; one cheap background reconciliation call only for ambiguous failures. No realtime-token increase during offline waits.
changes.latency_impact: Adds milliseconds to normal job dispatch; reconnect recovery is faster than today's repeated 20–45 second browser timeouts because stale commands are classified immediately.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability and prevents duplicate authenticated actions. Do not persist page bodies in relay; retain redacted snippets/hashes and local Mac evidence paths. Irreversible browser steps remain explicitly owner-confirmed.
depends_on: A stable idempotency-key convention shared by browser and Mac adapters
Receipt schema that includes requestId, stepId, and before/after evidence
A browser-side tab/session reattachment endpoint
A pendant event consumer for compact job-state notifications

changes.change: Add a durable Attention Envelope contract and queue between browser watches, Calendar/Mail briefs, relay scheduling, Mac context, and pendant delivery. Each item carries source/session provenance, normalized urgency, interruptibility requirements, quiet-window expiry, dedupe key, redaction class, and delivery state (parked, eligible, delivered, acknowledged). Re-evaluate eligibility when Mac foreground/calendar state changes; park items when browser heartbeat or Mac is offline; never replay a stale browser command without session affinity revalidation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets fewer disruptive alerts and fewer missed urgent changes. A queued item can survive leaving the Mac or losing Safari, then arrive as one concise, sourced sentence at a sensible moment instead of repeated stale notifications.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and D1/R2 persistence, triage worker, Mac context adapter, browser heartbeat integration, and pendant delivery acknowledgement; add replay/dedupe tests for offline and reconnect cases.
changes.risk: A bad urgency classifier could suppress something important or interrupt at a bad time. Recover with explicit urgent override, visible review queue, expiry notices, and a manual pendant button to flush parked items. Browser session loss must fail closed to parked, not retry blindly.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata cost; background model calls only when a new/changed item needs ranking. Audio generation and browser extraction dominate variable cost.
changes.latency_impact: Eligibility decisions become near-real-time after heartbeat/context events, typically sub-second locally and a few seconds through relay; scheduled source checks remain cadence-bound.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by storing redacted summaries and provenance instead of raw page/mail bodies, with per-item sensitivity and expiry. Do not mix unrelated authenticated sessions in one envelope.
depends_on: Implement the currently schema-only mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources grants
Browser stale-queue TTL/session revalidation (browser-extension’s pending proposal)
A pendant-local quiet/urgent state and acknowledgement event
Durable relay scheduler/queue rather than transient polling

changes.change: Revise the wearable prototype with a low-power haptic actuator and a fuel-gauge/charger monitor on I2C, while retaining the single button and LED as fallback. Expose battery percentage/health and a distinct short/long haptic vocabulary for parked-item, urgent-item, and acknowledgement events.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant could notify discreetly without opening a microphone or interrupting audio, and the system could avoid starting a delivery that will die during an LTE-M burst. The owner would get dependable quiet alerts and an honest battery warning instead of guessing from the LED.
changes.effort: Prototype-level board spin and enclosure iteration; add I2C drivers, power budgeting, haptic patterns, and relay capability fields. Validate coexistence with the single full-duplex I2S peripheral and LTE-M transmit peaks.
changes.risk: Haptic draw may shorten runtime and vibration may be missed or annoying. Keep patterns brief, add a firmware disable/quiet mode, and retain LED/button fallback. Fuel-gauge readings can drift; calibrate and report confidence rather than false precision.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$8 BOM increase for a coin vibration motor/LRA, driver, and gauge IC plus PCB/enclosure work; tens of milliamps only during short haptic pulses, negligible average draw if rate-limited.
changes.latency_impact: Local haptic acknowledgement can be under 100 ms; battery telemetry adds no conversational latency.
changes.security_impact: Battery and haptic state are non-sensitive. Do not transmit microphone or user content for these events.
depends_on: Attention Envelope integration and pendant-local quiet/urgent state
A firmware delivery queue that can operate through dropped LTE/WebSocket links

changes.change: Create a cellular-failover coordinator spanning the pendant modem, relay, and Mac network stack: authenticated USB/tether handshake, health-based Wi‑Fi loss detection, an explicit metered allowlist, browser polling suspension, relay tunnel quotas, and automatic teardown/recovery receipts. Treat the pendant as an emergency narrowband link, not a hotspot.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A Wi‑Fi outage would no longer strand essential work or force the owner to hunt for a hotspot, while nonessential browser traffic is prevented from consuming the pendant’s limited radio budget.
changes.effort: High: firmware networking and power work, a signed Mac Network Extension/helper, relay tunnel and quota enforcement, and an end-to-end recovery test across sleep, reconnect, and modem loss.
changes.risk: A routing bug could leak traffic, drain the battery, or create an unexpectedly expensive cellular bill. Fail closed when authentication or policy is unavailable, show a prominent metered-mode indicator, cap bytes/time, and record a receipt for every activation and teardown.
changes.cost_impact: No per-request model spend; ongoing cost is cellular data and modest relay egress. Firmware may need a better USB/network-capable board and additional power-management components.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a few seconds only during failover; once active, LTE-M latency and throughput are materially worse than Wi‑Fi, so the coordinator must defer large transfers.
changes.security_impact: Adds a new network boundary and therefore requires device-bound keys, signed policy, encrypted tunnel, least-privilege routing, and no unrestricted LAN access. The owner must be able to disable it physically.
depends_on: USB/network-capable pendant hardware or firmware transport
Mac Network Extension/helper implementation
Relay tunnel and quota service
Browser metered-mode cooperation

changes.change: Add a cross-surface intent coordinator between the relay, Mac job runner, and browser bridge. It should compile one user intent into typed steps, assign each step an idempotency key and device-epoch lease, persist checkpoints, reject stale claims, and merge Mac receipts plus browser typed results into one causal timeline. On reconnect it retries only steps declared safe-to-replay and emits an explicit blocked state for uncertain mutations.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped Wi‑Fi link or sleeping laptop would no longer leave the owner wondering whether a page was changed twice, a file was written, or a form was submitted. They get one honest answer and safe continuation when devices return.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay state machine and schema, Mac/browser adapters, failure-injection tests across reconnect and duplicate delivery, plus dashboard timeline.
changes.risk: A bad idempotency classification could replay a mutation or skip useful work. Default unknown steps to blocked; preserve raw receipts and allow manual reconciliation. Recover by replaying from the last durable checkpoint, never by guessing from a timeout.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing API cost; deterministic state transitions dominate. Occasional background summarization is a few thousand tokens per recovery. Small durable KV/D1/R2 growth from receipts and checkpoints.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local lease/checkpoint overhead; reconnect reconciliation typically seconds. No added latency to ordinary single-step Mac actions once bypassed as already-complete.
changes.security_impact: Requires strict account-scoped intent records and opaque step IDs; never copy browser cookies or private page bodies into pendant audio. Encrypt or redact receipt payloads and expire detailed evidence separately from status.
depends_on: Implement the durable browser runner and stale-device lease/epoch handling
Expose a stable Mac job/receipt correlation ID on POST /execute and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
Implement the missing read-only Mac inspection tool if foreground/browser context is needed for safe step selection

changes.change: Create a contradiction-aware evidence graph rather than a flat action log. Normalize Mac receipts, browser observations, relay delivery events, and device liveness into immutable claims with source, timestamp, causal parent, confidence, and supersession rules; derive explicit states such as confirmed, unverified, contradicted, and resolved.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner would know exactly when the system is uncertain instead of receiving a confident but wrong 'done'. They could resume work after a crash without duplicating a submission, and later inspect why the system reached its conclusion.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema, ingestion adapters for existing Mac/browser/relay records, conflict rules, retention/redaction policy, and a small protected timeline UI.
changes.risk: Incorrect normalization could create false conflicts or hide a real one. Keep raw source records immutable, expose both claims side by side, and default unresolved conflicts to non-action rather than silently choosing a winner.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and compute cost; deterministic graph updates are cheap. A small background model call may be used only to phrase a human-readable explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible for ordinary actions; conflict derivation should complete in under a second after each receipt, with verification reads adding network latency only when needed.
changes.security_impact: Evidence may contain private URLs, filenames, and snippets. Enforce per-owner encryption and field-level redaction; pendant output should contain only minimal labels and no sensitive content by default.
depends_on: A shared typed claim schema across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant events
Stable causal IDs on Mac job receipts and browser command results
Read-only verification adapters for authenticated browser state and Mac state
A protected dashboard/timeline surface for raw evidence and resolution actions

changes.change: Add a lease-and-checkpoint coordinator between the existing relay jobs, Mac /plan+/execute, and browser command queue. Each workflow step gets a stable stepId and lease expiry; the Mac and browser must acknowledge the same stepId with a typed receipt or explicit unknown result. On reconnect, reconcile receipts before issuing any new command, quarantine the seven currently pending browser commands if their device epoch is stale, and expose a compact causal timeline to /jobs/:jobId/receipts. This is wiring and failure semantics between existing components, not another generic durable job runner.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped Wi‑Fi link or sleeping browser would no longer make the owner wonder whether something happened twice. They get one truthful timeline and safe continuation from the last confirmed step, while stale browser commands cannot unexpectedly execute after reconnect.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared schema, relay state transitions, Mac acknowledgement hook, browser device-epoch handling, migration/tests for existing jobs.
changes.risk: A too-short lease can mark a slow action unknown and pause work unnecessarily; a too-long lease delays recovery. Recover by explicit unknown state and manual resume. Existing FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged; this adds receipts and quarantine, not a confirmation gate.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost on successful steps; small D1 storage increase for step receipts and hashes. Background reconciliation may use an inexpensive model only for ambiguous failures.
changes.latency_impact: One local receipt write per step; reconnect recovery adds a few seconds to reconcile before resuming.
changes.security_impact: Store hashes and redacted metadata rather than page bodies by default. Do not replay unknown mutating steps without an owner-directed resume. Device epochs prevent old browser sessions from consuming new commands.
depends_on: Browser extension reconnect heartbeat/device epoch
Mac executor emitting durable step acknowledgements
Relay job schema that supports per-step state and idempotency keys

changes.change: Introduce a single-use, expiring approval nonce bound to a redacted critical-field snapshot and source identities (browser tab/session or Mac file/app). Before any final browser or Mac mutation, the executor must re-read those fields and atomically consume the nonce; any mismatch, stale device epoch, or expiry changes the result to invalidated rather than executing. Relay receipts should record invalidated, regenerated, and consumed states so an old queued command cannot revive.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Prepared work stays trustworthy while the owner is away. They will never approve yesterday's form, an old price, or a changed recipient by accident, and they get a clear explanation when regeneration is needed.
changes.effort: Medium: shared escrow schema, atomic relay check, small Mac/browser preflight adapters, and migration tests for queued commands.
changes.risk: Overly broad critical-field selection could invalidate harmless changes and annoy the owner; recover by showing the changed fields and offering regenerate. A relay outage should fail closed for final mutations but preserve the draft locally for later.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal storage and one extra typed preflight per final action; no additional realtime-model usage in the normal path.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly one network round trip (target under 3 seconds) immediately before the final mutation.
changes.security_impact: Improves replay resistance and limits authorization to the exact artifact and context the owner reviewed. Redacted snapshots reduce private-data exposure; nonce consumption must be atomic and never logged with secret contents.
depends_on: A shared escrow/approval record across relay, Mac, and browser
Typed critical-field extraction from each source
Final-action adapters that can reject an invalid nonce

changes.change: Implement a Browser Bridge circuit-breaker and reconciliation worker between the existing command queue and job receipts. On each heartbeat, classify the bridge as online, stale, or offline; assign every command a creation time, TTL, idempotency key, session/tab binding, and mutation class; persist a state machine queued→leased→acknowledged→completed/failed/quarantined. When the bridge returns, automatically retry only expired-safe read steps whose binding and request hash are unchanged, quarantine all mutating steps, and emit one compact interruption receipt listing what ran, what did not, and why. Reconcile the current seven pending commands on startup rather than replaying them blindly.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets honest recovery after closing a laptop or losing Safari: no duplicate form submissions, no silent dropped research, and a single pendant-ready answer to “did that happen?” even after a restart.
changes.effort: Medium: a persistent worker, schema migration, queue leases, and tests for crash/reconnect races; no new model is needed. Requires wiring the existing local browser queue, /browser/status heartbeat, /browser/poll, result callbacks, and job receipts.
changes.risk: A false stale classification could quarantine a harmless read or leave work unfinished; recovery is explicit retry from the receipt. The critical safety rule is never auto-replay a mutation after an uncertain disconnect. Existing commands need a one-time migration with unknown status marked quarantined, not completed.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible compute/storage; one small receipt per command and occasional inexpensive background triage call only for ambiguous failures.
changes.latency_impact: Heartbeat remains lightweight; reconnect reconciliation completes within seconds for reads and intentionally pauses mutations until the owner asks.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing replay. Keep private page content and session tokens on the Mac/relay; receipts should store hashes and minimal snippets, with configurable redaction.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner persistence (chg-16bc5dee is still open; router/backends exist but runner does not)
Typed browser action/result schema with idempotency and tab affinity (parts of chg-14accc01 exist, but need queue integration)
Browser extension heartbeat/poll endpoint remaining available

changes.change: Create a Mac-resident private-data diode for authenticated browser work. It accepts a natural-language question, executes only read operations in bound private tabs, maps results into a typed schema (e.g. price, date, status, count), strips free text and identifiers by default, and emits a signed disclosure envelope containing only approved fields, provenance hashes, freshness, and a human-readable disclosure manifest. The relay rejects any payload outside that schema; the owner can approve a one-field expansion from the pendant, producing a new envelope rather than exposing the page.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for comparisons, eligibility checks, or summaries across private accounts without handing an AI service their whole logged-in pages. The owner gets the benefit of the hive's reach while retaining a clear, inspectable privacy boundary.
changes.effort: High: a local policy/extraction service, browser field provenance, envelope signing and schema validation at the relay, redaction tests, and a pendant disclosure UI/audio format. This is a new privacy architecture, not a planner prompt.
changes.risk: Incorrect extraction could produce a wrong derived answer; every value must retain source URL, timestamp, selector/hash, and confidence so the owner can inspect it. A schema bug could leak data, so default-deny validation, fuzz tests, payload size limits, and immediate intermediate deletion are required. If uncertain, return 'could not safely derive' rather than raw text.
changes.cost_impact: Small local CPU/storage cost; typically one cheaper synthesis call over a tiny derived payload, with no cloud cost for raw page data. Engineering cost is substantial because the boundary must be security-reviewed.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a local transformation step, roughly seconds; avoids uploading large pages and can be faster for multi-page comparisons once typed extractors exist.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves privacy by making raw authenticated DOM and credentials non-exportable. It introduces signing keys and a policy engine that become high-value targets; store keys in the Mac keychain, rotate them, and audit every envelope and field expansion.
depends_on: A browser result format with field-level provenance and sensitivity labels
A Mac-local policy broker able to inspect authenticated tabs without returning whole-page content
Relay-side schema enforcement and signature verification
A pendant disclosure receipt and explicit field-expansion interaction

changes.change: Add a live reachability-aware planner preflight that queries /ops/status and /browser/status before selecting an execution path. For each browser intent, classify it as public-read (may fall back to Mac Safari/Chrome AppleScript or direct web retrieval), authenticated-session (queue until the extension is online), or browser mutation (queue and preserve session affinity). Return the chosen path and blocker reason in the plan and receipt, rather than attempting a 45-second browser timeout.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A spoken request will fail quickly and intelligibly instead of hanging, and public information can still be delivered when the browser extension is asleep. Authenticated work will wait safely rather than being rerun or accidentally performed in the wrong session.
changes.effort: Medium: planner preflight, intent classification, bounded fallback executor, and receipt fields; no new model tier required.
changes.risk: Misclassification could send a public read through the wrong browser or queue work unnecessarily. Default uncertain cases to queue/no action; retain the original command and idempotency key so recovery is deterministic.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one or two local status reads per browser request. No extra model call for deterministic classification.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for status checks; avoids 45-second dead waits when the bridge is offline.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by forbidding authenticated fallback outside the paired browser session and making session affinity explicit. Public-page fallback still needs URL allowlisting and evidence capture.
depends_on: Browser bridge must expose a stable online/heartbeat state and session identity (already represented by /browser/status and /browser/sessions).
Planner must attach an idempotency key to queued browser intents.
For authenticated recovery, durable queue and pendant status events are still needed.

changes.change: Implement a reconnect-safe browser work capsule and release protocol between the existing command queue and job receipts. At enqueue, persist a capsule per step containing request/idempotency key, session+tab affinity, read/write class, URL/title/DOM fingerprint, and a redacted evidence pointer. On browser heartbeat, require a fresh tab identity and fingerprint; automatically release only idempotent reads/navigation, mark all mutations quarantined, and emit one deduplicated pipeline event plus a pendant-sized receipt. Expired or mismatched capsules are discarded with an explicit reason instead of replayed.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the browser bridge goes offline, the owner gets a truthful one-sentence status and later receives the safe result without duplicated clicks or submissions. A stale logged-in tab can never silently consume an old command after reconnect.
changes.effort: Medium: queue schema and state machine, heartbeat response fields, browser extension handshake, receipt/event integration, and a small dashboard queue. Add crash/restart tests for offline, timeout, reconnect-to-different-tab, and mutation quarantine.
changes.risk: A false fingerprint mismatch may leave safe work waiting; recover with a visible Retry after revalidation. A bug in classification could release a mutation, so default unknown actions to quarantine and log every release decision. Do not delete current pending commands until their capsules are migrated.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and polling overhead; one short background classification per multi-step job at most. No additional realtime calls except optional spoken alert/TTS.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one heartbeat/fingerprint round trip before resuming, typically under 1–2 seconds; prevents 45-second browser timeout loops by failing fast when offline.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding commands to a tab/session and retaining redacted evidence only. Authenticated content remains on the Mac/approved relay path; no credentials are persisted. Mutations remain owner-reviewed.
depends_on: chg-14accc01 request IDs/tab affinity/typed results must be completed as the queue substrate
browser-extension reconnect and Safari handshake
a durable job runner (chg-16bc5dee)
pipeline event/audio delivery for the pendant receipt

changes.change: Add a read-only Safari fallback adapter for browser status and page capture when the extension is offline: use the already-granted Safari automation channel to enumerate windows/tabs, read URL/title and selected visible text, and return a typed source capsule. Mark the result as safari-automation (not extension) with lower confidence, never expose cookies, and refuse all form filling, clicks, navigation, or submissions through this fallback. When the extension reconnects, reconcile by tab URL/title before merging evidence.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A disconnected browser extension would no longer turn every logged-in question into a dead end. The Mac could still answer a read-only question or preserve a page snapshot, while the stronger browser session resumes later for actions.
changes.effort: Medium: implement a narrow AppleScript adapter, typed redaction/size limits, source labeling, and reconciliation tests against extension tab IDs. Keep it separate from FULL_CONTROL computer actions.
changes.risk: Safari may return incomplete or stale text, or a dialog may block automation. Surface source and timestamp, fail closed on ambiguous tab identity, and never use this path for mutations. If Safari automation is revoked, report unavailable rather than falling back to UI scraping.
changes.cost_impact: Near-zero API cost; local AppleScript only. Small CPU/token cost for text extraction and redaction.
changes.latency_impact: Fast local read (roughly 1–3 seconds), avoiding a 45-second extension timeout; extension reconnect still adds its own handshake.
changes.security_impact: Read-only authenticated content stays on the Mac; no credentials or cookies leave Safari. Because this bypasses the extension, audit every read with tab URL, timestamp, and redacted excerpt hash.
depends_on: Safari automation grant already present in /ops/status
reconnect-safe browser work capsule proposed above
a typed page-capture route or extension-compatible source-capsule schema

changes.change: Create a three-way draft synchronization protocol spanning Mac and browser rather than treating each action result as a replacement string. Assign every draft a stable draftId and immutable base revision; record agent revision and owner revision separately, with per-field hashes for browser forms and byte/line ranges for local files. Before any write, compare both descendants to the base, emit a conflict event when they diverge, and expose a resolution token that applies only the selected fields. Expire drafts and securely erase versions after a short retention window.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can edit while the agent works without losing their changes or having stale text silently enter a private form. They get a precise choice instead of a vague failure or a full restart.
changes.effort: Medium-high: local file/editor watchers for supported apps, browser field identity extraction, encrypted short-lived version storage, three-way merge tests, and a small conflict UI/pendant protocol.
changes.risk: Some editors or dynamic forms will not expose stable identifiers; fall back to whole-document conflict and preserve both copies. A merge bug could alter wording, so unresolved prose conflicts must remain untouched and require explicit field-level choice.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and compute; conflict summaries may incur a small background-model call. No realtime call unless the owner asks for a spoken explanation.
changes.latency_impact: Normal writes add a local hash check under 100 ms; conflict detection should be seconds, with no browser submission until resolution.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing stale writes. Full drafts stay on the Mac/browser path with encryption and TTL; relay receives hashes, metadata, and redacted summaries unless the owner explicitly requests content sharing.
depends_on: browser bridge returning stable tab/session and form-field identifiers
Mac editor/file change observation without requiring Accessibility for supported applications
durable encrypted draft/version store
pendant and dashboard resolution UI

changes.change: Replace browserBridge's single 45-second waitForBrowserResult with a leased, event-driven job state machine. On dispatch, persist commandId/action idempotency key/session id and a short lease; emit queued/dispatched/acknowledged/completed/abandoned events; renew the lease on extension heartbeat; on reconnect reconcile command receipts before retrying. Expire commands without a live lease and mark sessions detached when lastSeenAt is older than the lease window. Expose non-blocking GET job progress and a bounded stream for the planner.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A browser action will stop hanging for 45 seconds and then possibly replay after the owner has moved on. The owner gets immediate, truthful progress and can safely resume only unapplied work when the bridge returns.
changes.effort: Medium: browserBridge queue/state persistence, heartbeat endpoint, reconciliation tests across restart and reconnect, and planner polling/stream wiring.
changes.risk: A lease that is too short could abandon a slow but valid page load; use separate dispatch and execution deadlines and preserve the receipt for late completion. A reconnect race could duplicate a mutation; content-addressed idempotency keys and receipt reconciliation must win before retry. Recovery is to surface abandoned state and require a new explicit resume command.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and request overhead; one heartbeat per active browser job. Reduces wasted model calls and repeated 45-second waits.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate queued/failed status; read actions resume within one heartbeat after reconnect. Slow pages still honor a bounded execution deadline.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing stale authenticated commands from executing after an unattended reconnect. Keep private-page payloads on the Safari bridge; persist only hashes, ids, status, and minimal metadata in relay storage.
depends_on: chg-14accc01's existing request IDs/idempotency keys and typed receipts
chg-16bc5dee's existing backend selection; do not fail over owner-private Safari sessions to public relay
A browser extension heartbeat/reconnect signal

changes.change: Add a resumable 24 kHz playback protocol: the relay sends a signed manifest and fixed-size audio chunks; the nRF9160 acknowledges the highest fully verified chunk plus sample offset; on link loss it writes only unplayed/partial chunks to the existing microSD failure buffer, and on reconnect requests a range by content hash. The Mac pipeline must publish the manifest once and never synthesize again for a resume.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A long answer remains continuous across elevator rides, dead zones, and reconnects. The owner does not hear repeats, lose the end of a briefing, or wait for a second TTS render.
changes.effort: Medium: protocol/schema shared by firmware and relay, state-machine changes in playback and pipeline upload, plus an interruption test harness. No new model work.
changes.risk: Power loss or a corrupt checkpoint could skip or repeat a small boundary; recover by replaying the last acknowledged chunk and validating hashes. Stale manifests must be rejected by device nonce/content hash. Existing SD failure-buffer semantics must remain unchanged.
changes.cost_impact: No additional inference cost. Small D1 metadata and request overhead; SD writes only on failure. RAM impact should stay bounded by one manifest plus one/two audio chunks, not whole-response buffering.
changes.latency_impact: No change to first-byte playback; reconnect adds one manifest/range request, target under 2 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Requires authenticated device-bound manifests, per-chunk integrity hashes, and expiry/lease checks so an old response cannot be resumed by another session.
depends_on: 24 kHz audio path emits stable chunk boundaries and a content hash
Relay audio routes persist response object references long enough for a resume lease
Pendant firmware exposes playback position and durable checkpoint storage

changes.change: Replace the prototype's single LED-only notification path with a low-power coin/LRA haptic actuator plus a tri-color LED and a GPIO-capable button controller. Define three short patterns (urgent, informational, waiting) and a long-press local quiet toggle; expose a battery-safe driver and persist only alert ID/state, not content.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can recognize and control important events discreetly in a meeting or outdoors, without taking out a phone or listening to unsolicited speech. Different patterns make the alert actionable even when the screen and audio are unavailable.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium hardware revision and firmware driver work: enclosure/PCB change, power characterization, pattern state machine, and relay event integration. Existing dev-kit firmware can prototype the protocol before a product board spin.
changes.risk: Added vibration and LED draw may reduce battery life; mitigate with duty-cycle limits, a battery threshold, and a local quiet mode. A failed actuator must degrade to LED/audio and never block normal command delivery.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $3–$8 added BOM at low volume; roughly 5–30 mA while vibrating and negligible idle current, subject to actuator choice. No model/API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement is immediate; cellular delivery remains the dominant delay.
changes.security_impact: Patterns must encode only coarse urgency, never secret text. Persist opaque event IDs and timestamps; do not log sensitive alert payloads on the pendant.
depends_on: Relay normalized alert schema and subscription policy
Pendant firmware event acknowledgement and offline queue protocol
Battery/power budget validation on the final wearable enclosure

changes.change: Add a cross-surface event ledger and focus-state lease in the relay. Each incoming alert or completion event gets a stable event ID, source (pendant/Mac/browser), sensitivity class, urgency, focus-block ID, and delivery acknowledgments. The relay exposes a compact delta feed; Mac and browser adapters report applied notification state and restore tokens. On focus end, a worker joins undelivered deltas with Calendar/Mail/browser citations, emits one digest, and marks each item delivered or unavailable. Expire leases and held payloads automatically, and make replay idempotent.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can press one pendant control to get uninterrupted work without losing important things, even if the Mac or browser disconnects. They get one trustworthy catch-up instead of duplicate alerts, silent loss, or a permanently altered notification setting.
changes.effort: Medium-high: new D1 schema/state machine, relay endpoints, Mac notification adapter, browser event adapter, and pendant start/stop/replay protocol; add fault-injection tests for disconnects and duplicate delivery.
changes.risk: A stale lease could suppress an urgent event or fail to restore the prior notification state. Mitigate with hard lease expiry, emergency bypass rules, visible active-state feedback on the pendant, restore tokens, and a recovery sweep that replays anything unacknowledged. If the digest worker fails, retain the queue and report its unavailable state rather than dropping data.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and worker cost; one inexpensive digest inference per focus block, plus optional TTS. No continuous realtime model use.
changes.latency_impact: State changes and suppression deltas are sub-second when online; reconnect replay is bounded by the next heartbeat. Digest generation is asynchronous and should complete within 10 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive content remains on the Mac by default; the relay holds IDs and redacted snippets only, encrypted with short retention. Every digest item carries provenance and a reason for inclusion. Focus state is scoped to the owner's authenticated devices.
depends_on: A pendant-side focus start/stop event and offline persistence skill
A relay-held alert queue with TTL and urgency policy
Mac notification-state read/restore adapter (AppleScript where possible)
Browser watch/event adapter that can pause and resume cleanly

changes.change: Add a resumable decision-packet coordinator above the existing Mac jobs and browser sessions. It should create packetId/resume token, persist a state machine (captured → collecting → synthesized → review-ready), append immutable evidence references and action receipts, checkpoint after every surface, and expose GET status plus a compact completion event. On restart it resumes only unfinished steps; on privacy expiry it tombstones source material while retaining a redacted receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: If the owner leaves Wi‑Fi, closes the lid, or is interrupted, they can return to the same answer instead of repeating the request or guessing what changed. Every recommendation has a source and the exact draft/action state is visible on the Mac.
changes.effort: Medium-high: coordinator, durable store, adapters for browser and Mac job receipts, resume protocol, and a small workspace renderer.
changes.risk: A stale packet could act on changed information. Every packet needs freshness timestamps, invalidation on source/session loss, and a visible 're-check required' state. Recovery is replay from the last checkpoint; no mutation is auto-replayed.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage; background synthesis costs a few slower-model calls per packet. Reconciliation after restart may repeat only the failed step.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement stays realtime; first useful packet usually 30–90 seconds, with no blocking of the pendant conversation.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive extracts remain local or encrypted; relay stores hashes and minimum snippets. Resume tokens must be unguessable and revocable; destructive actions remain drafts until owner confirmation.
depends_on: Durable browser job runner (chg-16bc5dee is still missing persistence/retry/result stream)
A packet-aware relay event/result route
Atomic Mac workspace bundle writer
Existing Mac job receipts and browser session affinity

changes.change: Add a bridge-health lease and dead-letter watchdog, distinct from the command queue: treat a heartbeat with tabId/windowId null, missing browserName, or an old lastSeenAt as degraded even when online=true; stop claiming queued commands, mark the existing 9 pending commands as quarantined with their request IDs, and require a fresh tab-bound heartbeat epoch before replaying only idempotent reads. Surface a single repair action in the dashboard and a concise pendant notification.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Prevents a disconnected or reloaded browser extension from silently executing stale private-page commands later, while making the current 'online but no tab' state understandable and recoverable instead of leaving work hanging.
changes.effort: Medium: heartbeat validation, command lease/dead-letter state, replay classification, dashboard status, and a small relay notification adapter.
changes.risk: A false degraded state could delay a legitimate read; recover by accepting a fresh tab-bound heartbeat and allowing explicit replay from the dashboard. Never delete quarantined commands automatically; retain receipts and audit history.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local JSON records per command and one periodic watchdog invocation.
changes.latency_impact: Adds no delay to healthy commands; degraded detection occurs at heartbeat/lease expiry, with recovery in one heartbeat interval.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by preventing stale commands from being applied to a different authenticated tab or account. Quarantined payloads should be redacted in dashboard/pendant views and retained under existing private-session policy.
depends_on: A heartbeat payload that includes a monotonically increasing bridge epoch and bound tab/window identity
Typed idempotency classification for browser commands (read-only versus mutation)
A dead-letter/quarantine record and dashboard repair/replay control
An explicit relay notification route for degraded browser state

changes.change: Introduce a four-party, one-task authorization envelope: the pendant signs an owner confirmation containing target origin/account label, normalized action hash, allowed field scope, expiry, and nonce; the relay forwards only that envelope; the Mac bridge asks the browser extension to attest the bound tab's origin and account label; execution receipts include matching hashes and a redacted before/after diff. Reject any tab, account, origin, or action mismatch and invalidate the nonce after one use.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can safely say “use my work account for this” and know which signed-in account acted, without handing credentials to the AI or wondering whether a stale tab performed the wrong change.
changes.effort: High: protocol design, pendant signing/secure storage, browser extension account-identity attestation, Mac/relay verification, receipt schema, and recovery for browser reloads or clock skew.
changes.risk: Pairing loss or extension updates could invalidate authorization; recover with an explicit re-pair flow and never silently fall back to an unbound session. An account label could itself be sensitive, so redact it in relay logs and expose only a user-chosen alias.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible per-task API cost; engineering and secure-key storage are the main cost. Requires a small key record on the pendant and short-lived records in relay/bridge storage.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local attestation round trip, typically 100–500 ms on a healthy link; no model latency on execution.
changes.security_impact: Materially reduces confused-deputy and stale-tab risk while preserving the owner's maximum-access policy. It does not block ordinary unscoped local actions, only account-scoped browser work lacking a valid envelope.
depends_on: A pendant signing/key-storage primitive with rotation and recovery
Browser extension support for origin plus signed-in account identity attestation
Relay and Mac verification libraries with nonce replay protection
Redacted proof receipts and dashboard rendering

changes.change: Add a privacy-aware circuit breaker and queue reconciler between the existing browser routes: before dispatch, label each step public or authenticated; when /browser/status is offline, immediately divert only public steps to /research, persist private steps with idempotency keys and a resumable cursor, stop retry storms, and publish one pendant-readable state transition. On heartbeat, reconcile pending command IDs against job receipts, expire commands whose tab/session is stale, and resume only read-only steps automatically; keep mutations paused for explicit owner review.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A disconnected extension should not make the owner wait, lose work, or accidentally replay a form submission. They receive partial useful results now and a clear, trustworthy list of private work waiting for Safari.
changes.effort: Medium: dispatcher state machine, step classification, durable queue schema, receipt reconciliation, and tests for offline/online transitions.
changes.risk: Misclassification could leak a private URL to public research or leave a safe read stuck. Default unknown to private, retain original step, and provide an inspectable queue with manual retry/cancel. Idempotency prevents duplicate mutations.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for health checks; modest D1/local storage growth for cursors, classifications, and receipts.
changes.latency_impact: Removes current ~45-second browser timeout from the voice path; adds sub-second classification and background reconciliation.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by making private-by-default routing explicit and preventing authenticated payloads from reaching public fallback; mutation replay remains paused.
depends_on: chg-16bc5dee durable browser job runner
chg-14accc01 request IDs/idempotency/tab affinity
browser extension heartbeat implementation
working read-only Mac source/inspection tools

changes.change: Add a reconnect watchdog and stale-command quarantine for the browser bridge. On every heartbeat transition offline→online, atomically inspect pending commands, expire entries past TTL, mark attempts with a stable idempotency key, replay only commands whose tab/session preconditions still match, and emit one aggregate receipt for skipped/failed items. If the extension stays offline, surface a single actionable alert rather than allowing an unbounded queue (currently 9 pending commands).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops seeing repeated opaque browser failures and does not accidentally get old commands replayed against a different tab. When Safari/Chrome returns, useful work resumes once, stale work is clearly discarded, and the pendant can say exactly what was recovered.
changes.effort: Medium: bridge heartbeat state machine, durable command metadata and TTL migration, atomic claim/replay, aggregate receipt, and a small dashboard status panel; test crash/reconnect races.
changes.risk: A command may be incorrectly judged stale or its tab may have changed. Recover by defaulting to quarantine (not replay), showing the reason and original URL/title, and offering explicit retry. Existing pending commands need a one-time migration with conservative expiry.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; small D1/local JSON metadata and a few heartbeat writes. No new external data beyond existing command payloads.
changes.latency_impact: Heartbeat processing adds under 100 ms; reconnect replay begins within one poll interval and avoids 45-second timeout failures.
changes.security_impact: Keep tab/session binding and bearer authorization; never replay irreversible browser actions automatically. Quarantine records should redact page content and expire.
depends_on: Browser command records need createdAt, TTL, tab/session preconditions, and idempotency key
Extension must reliably report heartbeat transitions and command results
Receipt/journal schema must support aggregate recovery outcomes

changes.change: Add a cross-surface causal observation ledger, distinct from ordinary memory: every Mac inspection, browser extraction, pendant event, and execution receipt gets a device clock, relay receive time, sequence/nonce, and parent observation ID. Plans carry a compact precondition vector; execution compares it against fresh observations and returns stale/conflict rather than replaying. Persist only hashes and typed facts by default, with source pointers for local evidence.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says 'do that' after switching tabs, closing a laptop, or reconnecting the pendant, the system can know whether 'that' still refers to the same thing. It prevents duplicate or stale actions while preserving a human-readable explanation of what changed.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared event schema, append-only bounded ledger, adapters in relay/pipeline, Mac jobs, and browser commands; add crash/reconnect and duplicate-delivery tests.
changes.risk: Clock skew and missed heartbeats can create false conflicts; use monotonic per-device sequence numbers and treat uncertainty as review-needed, not success. Metadata itself can reveal activity, so hash sensitive payloads and enforce TTL.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and negligible model cost; deterministic comparison handles most events. Background summarization only for conflict explanations.
changes.latency_impact: Under 100 ms for local vector comparison; reconnect reconciliation adds one inspection round trip (typically <2 s) before mutation.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety without introducing approval gates. No raw audio or credentials in the ledger; retain only minimal typed metadata and encrypted local evidence references.
depends_on: Implementations of mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources
Typed browser command/job receipts with request IDs
Relay delivery with idempotency and reconnect handling

changes.change: Create a local attention broker between Mac Notification Center, browser-extension events, Calendar, and the pendant pipeline. It should maintain an encrypted, append-only held-item queue keyed by opaque IDs; apply deterministic urgency policy locally; emit only category/urgency over /pipeline/events; restore or summarize items when the attention window closes; and expose an audit record with source, reason, and disposition. This is the missing connective layer, not another briefing routine.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets uninterrupted meetings and focus time without losing notifications or having them silently discarded. When free, they receive one concise digest with the urgent items first and can see exactly why anything was held or escalated.
changes.effort: High: macOS notification integration, browser event adapter, queue durability/recovery, policy UI, Calendar-driven state transitions, and pendant haptic/audio states. Test crash, reboot, duplicate event, and offline cases.
changes.risk: A misclassification could delay an important alert; provide emergency allowlists, a physical pendant override, expiry-based escalation, and a visible held-count indicator. If the broker crashes, fail open for urgent/VIP sources and preserve queued metadata. Never delete source notifications.
changes.cost_impact: Small local storage/process overhead; low model spend because ranking is mostly rules. Engineering cost is concentrated in private notification APIs and browser event normalization.
changes.latency_impact: Local known-policy decisions <300 ms; ambiguous ranking can be asynchronous. Reconnection may briefly show a held-count badge before the digest is ready.
changes.security_impact: Raw notification content remains on-device; relay sees opaque IDs and urgency labels. Encrypt the queue at rest, TTL old content, and require explicit opt-in for each source and browser profile.
depends_on: A supported Mac Notification Center read/hold/restore adapter
Browser-extension notification event protocol
Shared attention-window state and local policy store
Pendant urgency/override event support
Existing pipeline event and briefing consumers

changes.change: Add a closed-loop AudioQoS session shared by pendant firmware, Cloudflare relay, and Mac audio pipeline. The pendant emits compact 1-second counters (uplink loss, jitter, queue depth, playout underruns); relay computes a mode (normal, uplink-protect, recovery) and sends a signed mode update; Mac TTS packetizer and relay Opus transcode honor that mode. In uplink-protect, cap/reshape downlink and reserve modem budget for microphone packets; in recovery, refill the jitter buffer gradually. Record the mode and counters in the existing pipeline event/receipt stream so each call can be diagnosed without retaining speech.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner speaks while the agent replies, their words will no longer vanish for several seconds, and a degraded connection will recover gracefully instead of producing silence or a late burst of audio. The owner also gets an honest explanation in a completion receipt when quality was reduced.
changes.effort: Medium-high: a firmware telemetry packet and state machine, relay session state and packet scheduler, Mac/Opus packetizer changes, plus an automated contention test. This is a focused vertical slice rather than a new surface.
changes.risk: A bad mode update could starve replies or cause oscillation. Use monotonic sequence numbers, hysteresis (minimum 2 seconds per mode), a 5-second local timeout to return to normal, and retain the current static 24 kHz path as fallback. Recovery is automatic on reconnect.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model calls. A few dozen bytes/sec of telemetry and small relay memory per active call; adaptive mode should reduce LTE airtime during contention. Engineering/test cost is the dominant cost.
changes.latency_impact: Telemetry/control under 1 second; at most one 60 ms codec frame to change mode, with up to 120 ms intentional jitter buffering during recovery.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry contains transport statistics only. Authenticate mode updates to the paired pendant; do not upload raw microphone samples beyond the existing audio path, and keep diagnostic counters under the existing audio-retention policy.
depends_on: Pendant firmware support for loss/jitter/queue counters and a local fallback mode
Relay scheduler and Opus profile negotiation
Mac TTS/Opus packetizer that can honor a per-session audio mode
A contention/fault-injection harness covering simultaneous uplink and downlink

changes.change: Insert a fail-closed privacy firewall between the browser bridge and every research/realtime request. Each extraction returns a redacted payload plus a signed manifest containing policy version, source tab/session, withheld categories, byte counts, and a hash of the original region map; the relay accepts the payload only when the manifest attests that raw DOM, screenshots, form values, and clipboard data were not included. Keep the original and region map on the Mac, expose a local review/rollback endpoint, and emit the manifest hash into the existing job and pipeline receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for help on a logged-in page without trusting an invisible promise. They receive a concrete, reviewable statement of what was blocked, and a policy failure cannot silently turn into secret exfiltration.
changes.effort: High: extension interception plus Mac-local classifier, signed request schema, relay rejection path, and adversarial tests for secrets hidden in attributes, screenshots, accessibility trees, and copied text.
changes.risk: False positives may make answers less complete; false negatives are unacceptable. Fail closed on classifier uncertainty, maintain a user-editable allowlist of non-sensitive fields, and provide a local-only re-run after policy changes. Recovery never retries with the raw page.
changes.cost_impact: No additional model calls on the normal path; Mac CPU and test-maintenance cost are significant, with small relay storage for manifests. Data egress decreases.
changes.latency_impact: Typically 100–300 ms local processing; complex pages may add up to 1 second. No network round trip is added for policy decisions.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves confidentiality only if cryptographic attestation is verified server-side and keys never leave the Mac. A compromised extension remains an explicit threat requiring code signing and version pinning.
depends_on: Browser bridge interception before /research and realtime submission
Mac-local secret classifier and durable policy store
Relay schema validation that rejects unredacted or unattested payloads
Receipt/dashboard rendering for redaction manifests

changes.change: Add an execution-policy reconciliation check to the pipeline event writer. Before emitting “Waiting for your approval,” read the effective executor mode and action policy; in FULL_CONTROL_MODE emit “Executing under owner’s maximum-access policy” (or a real failure), and attach the exact policy version to the job receipt. Alert when pipeline metadata and executor behavior disagree.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently hears/ sees an approval gate for a shell-backed news task even though the configured Mac policy says no gates run in FULL_CONTROL_MODE. That makes it impossible to know whether a task is waiting, running, or stuck, and can leave routine work silently incomplete.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: centralize policy lookup in pipelineTrace/orchestrator, add a consistency assertion and regression tests for plan→execute→TTS flows.
changes.risk: A strict assertion could mark old jobs unhealthy; recover by treating it as an observability warning and preserving execution. No user data needs to leave the Mac.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local policy lookup and a few receipt bytes per job.
changes.latency_impact: Under 5 ms in the local pipeline.
changes.security_impact: Improves audit accuracy without adding a confirmation gate or reducing the owner’s explicitly chosen maximum access.
depends_on: A single authoritative effective-policy endpoint or in-process policy object shared by executor.js and pipelineTrace.js
Receipt schema support for policyVersion/effectiveMode

changes.change: Make action execution reachability-aware without adding a confirmation gate: consume the existing read-only /observe result before ui_* actions; when synthesized input is not accepted, automatically downgrade those steps to an AppleScript/accessibility-free equivalent when one exists, otherwise return `not_reached` (not success) with the exact TCC cause. Keep non-UI actions executing normally.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Right now the Mac reports ui_click/type_text/press_keys as successful while doing nothing because AI Pendant Agent is not trusted by Accessibility. This would stop false completion claims and still let Calendar, Mail, Finder, Safari, and other AppleScript-capable work continue.
changes.effort: Medium: add a reachability preflight and fallback map in computerControl/executor, plus receipt status and tests for trusted and untrusted hosts.
changes.risk: Some AppleScript fallbacks may target the wrong document; restrict fallback to named-app scripts with explicit object IDs and mark ambiguous cases not_reached. Existing maximum-access behavior is preserved.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local observation/cache lookup per UI batch.
changes.latency_impact: Typically 10–100 ms for cached reachability; no added delay for non-UI actions.
changes.security_impact: No new privilege or data egress. It makes the existing TCC boundary visible rather than pretending it was crossed. Screen Recording remains unnecessary for non-vision fallbacks.
depends_on: /observe or an equivalent cached inputReachability state
A typed receipt status distinguishing executed, failed, and not_reached
AppleScript adapters for the small set of supported named-app operations

changes.change: Make the briefing source adapter perform a live per-source authorization probe and normalize errors before composing the brief. If Calendar/Mail automation is actually available, read through the bounded mac_read_sources path; if it is unavailable, distinguish TCC denial from timeout, stale grant cache, and empty data.
