Include a source-health receipt (checkedAt, method, result) in the briefing and suppress the misleading generic 'needs an Automation grant' message when the cached and live states disagree.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current workday brief says Calendar and Mail were not read because an Automation grant is needed, while /ops/status reports both grants as available. The owner needs a truthful brief, not a false missing-permission warning or silent omission.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: adapter preflight, error taxonomy, and receipt fields; add tests for grant-cache disagreement and empty inbox/calendar.
changes.risk: A probe could trigger an unwanted permission prompt if implemented with the wrong API; use the existing bounded read source adapter and never open UI. On failure, retain the current conservative omission and explain the exact reason.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one local read/preflight per briefing. No new cloud storage beyond a few status fields.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms per source, parallelized.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by keeping reads bounded and making source health explicit; do not store message bodies in the health receipt.
depends_on: Use the granted mac_read_sources implementation rather than the legacy briefing.js AppleScript path
A typed source-health result shared by /briefing and /briefing/latest

changes.change: Introduce a signed, expiring Continuity Capsule contract as the sole handoff object between pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. The capsule must carry a redacted transcript, decisions, unresolved questions, source/provenance references, pending action DAG, session ownership, and attachment descriptors (tab IDs/file bookmarks), with per-field sensitivity and a monotonic revision. Each surface acknowledges the same capsule revision and appends receipts instead of copying context into separate prompts. A return handoff produces a delta, not a second summary.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can switch from speaking to working without losing the exact thread or accidentally acting on stale context. They can see what the system knows, what is unresolved, and what changed while they were away, then continue on either device as one conversation.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: define and validate the schema, encrypted storage and expiry, redaction, revision conflict handling, and adapters for relay sessions, Mac jobs, browser tabs, and pendant playback.
changes.risk: A malformed or stale capsule could attach the wrong private tab or cause context confusion. Require paired-device identity, origin/session checks, revision matching, automatic expiry, and a visible mismatch state that refuses attachment rather than guessing.
changes.cost_impact: Small metadata/storage cost; summarization cost falls over time because deltas replace repeated full-context prompts. No page bodies or raw audio need be duplicated.
changes.latency_impact: Initial handoff adds a small serialization step; subsequent turns should be faster because only capsule deltas and relevant fields are sent.
changes.security_impact: Improves data minimization and auditability, but creates a concentrated sensitive object. Encrypt at rest and in transit, field-level redact by default, use short TTLs, and allow pendant gesture to expire or redact it.
depends_on: Relay session ownership and resume semantics
Typed browser attachment descriptors with session/origin validation
Mac workbench renderer and receipt integration
Pendant resume/expire interaction

changes.change: Add a local meeting-marker protocol using the existing single button: double-press emits ENTER_MEETING, long-press emits LEAVE_MEETING, and a short press during the active capsule starts/stops a tiny follow-up memo buffer. Persist only an event ID, monotonic timestamps, and encrypted compressed audio chunks in a bounded ring; on reconnect send an idempotent capsule event with sequence numbers, then delete acknowledged chunks.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can mark the moment without touching the Mac or trusting a fragile network connection, and can leave a thought immediately after a meeting while walking away. If the link drops, the handoff is not lost or duplicated.
changes.effort: Medium firmware plus relay protocol work; test button debounce, reconnect, duplicate delivery, and flash wear on the prototype before committing product hardware.
changes.risk: False enter/leave gestures and ring overflow. Recover by LED/haptic confirmation, an undo gesture within a few seconds, explicit overflow indication, and server-side sequence deduplication. Never auto-send captured content to third parties.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; flash writes and occasional LTE-M transfer increase battery use modestly. On the current prototype, budget about 20–35 kB RAM for one compressed chunk plus protocol buffers, and reserve flash for a bounded queue; product hardware should include secure storage and ideally a second tactile control.
changes.latency_impact: Local marker acknowledgement is sub-second; upload is deferred when radio is unavailable and should not block playback or button handling.
changes.security_impact: Encrypt queued audio at rest and bind capsule uploads to the device identity; expose retention and deletion state in the dashboard. Do not log raw audio in UART diagnostics.
depends_on: A relay meeting-capsule endpoint with idempotent event sequencing
An audio codec/queue contract compatible with the owner's 24 kHz superwideband path
A Mac/browser evidence collector that can attach sources to the same capsule

changes.change: Add a resumable-handoff envelope shared by the pendant, Mac harness, and browser extension. It should contain an owner label, source surface, tab/file identifier, URL or path, excerpt hash, semantic text anchor, optional character/scroll range, project context, created/expiry timestamps, and a reopen result. On reopen, validate the source identity and anchor hash; if content moved, present the nearest cited match for review instead of guessing.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can reliably stop reading or editing on one surface and resume later at the same place, without hunting through tabs, files, or memory. It turns a fleeting “I need to come back to this” moment into a dependable physical-to-desktop handoff.
changes.effort: Medium integration work across the browser extension, Mac read-only inspection, relay storage, and pendant command protocol; substantial testing is needed for document edits, closed tabs, renamed files, and expired links.
changes.risk: A stale anchor could reopen the wrong content, or a sensitive excerpt could persist too long. Use identity/hash validation, bounded retention, explicit stale-state errors, encryption, and a one-command delete-all control. Never fall back to an unverified location.
changes.cost_impact: Low API and storage cost: typically a few KB per handoff, with model calls optional and background-priced. No meaningful pendant RAM increase if the envelope remains server-side and only IDs/status are cached locally.
changes.latency_impact: Capture is immediate locally; synchronization can be asynchronous. Reopen adds one validation round trip, targeted at under five seconds.
changes.security_impact: This creates a new sensitive-data store, so encrypt excerpts, minimize retention, redact credentials, scope records to the owner, and include a complete audit trail of capture and reopen operations.
depends_on: A browser extension message for selected/semantic content and stable anchors
A Mac adapter exposing foreground document or selection metadata without requiring the Mac microphone
A durable relay record and pendant lookup/delete protocol

changes.change: Add a local plan-validity envelope around every /execute job: capture a redacted state fingerprint (foreground app, running-app set, browser online/session IDs, relevant path existence, and a monotonically increasing machine-context version) at plan time; before each mutating step compare it, mark the job stale on mismatch, and enqueue a background replan rather than executing stale coordinates. Add explicit deferred_until / wake_condition / quiet-hours fields and a bounded browser-offline backoff that expires old commands with receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tasks handed off from the pendant will stop acting on yesterday’s screen or a different document. The owner can keep working uninterrupted and receive a truthful “deferred, replanned, completed, or expired” result instead of a silent failure or wrong-app action.
changes.effort: Medium: local state fingerprint module, job schema migration, scheduler/backoff loop, and receipt/dashboard fields; no new model is needed for the common case.
changes.risk: A false mismatch can defer a task unnecessarily; recover by allowing a ‘run now’ command and recording the compared fields. A missed mismatch is mitigated by checking before every mutating step, not only at job start. Browser commands must be idempotent or expire rather than replay blindly.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local JSON/D1 writes and periodic inspection. Background replans add a small text-model call only on actual drift.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds per step for local comparison; deferred work starts at the next wake boundary rather than immediately.
changes.security_impact: Keep raw URLs, file paths, and window titles local; relay receives only state class and receipt IDs. Fingerprints need TTL and deletion with the job.
depends_on: The existing /execute job tracker and receipts
A scheduler capable of wake conditions and bounded retries
A relay event mapping job receipts to pendant notifications
Browser bridge heartbeat/offline status (currently browser is offline with 9 pending commands)

changes.change: Create an end-to-end audio acceptance harness that propagates one testRunId from pendant diagnostic frames through relay Opus/transcode and pipeline events into a Mac-collected receipt. The harness should run fixed fixtures (silence, speech-shaped noise, bidirectional contention), align uplink/downlink timestamps, calculate packet loss/jitter/decode CPU/resampler underruns and a conservative MOS proxy, then publish a signed pass/fail artifact with raw audio omitted by default. Add a regression threshold so a firmware or relay change cannot claim 24 kHz support without passing both idle and contention cases.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They get a trustworthy answer to “does this work?” and early warning when an update makes calls lose speech or sound narrowband. It directly addresses the measured contention failure instead of hiding it behind a nominal sample-rate label.
changes.effort: Medium: firmware diagnostic event format, relay trace aggregation, a Node/Python-style fixture runner, and a small dashboard receipt view. No new model training required.
changes.risk: Bad clock alignment or overly strict thresholds could produce false failures; recover with a calibration fixture and versioned thresholds. Never treat synthetic-test success as proof that real speech is safe; label the result accordingly.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one short synthetic run and small metadata receipt. Storage drops substantially if raw audio is not retained.
changes.latency_impact: Adds no production call latency. A test run takes roughly 2–5 minutes.
changes.security_impact: Synthetic fixtures by default, no Mac microphone, redacted identifiers, signed receipts, and TTL deletion for any optional captured samples.
depends_on: A pendant diagnostic event/fixture mode
Relay correlation IDs and per-packet telemetry
A defined 24 kHz acceptance threshold and clock calibration

changes.change: Add a cross-node execution ledger shared by relay, Mac bridge, and browser extension. Each requested task gets a durable taskId and ordered step records with idempotency key, expected origin/URL fingerprint, lease owner, lease expiry, and terminal state (applied, not_applied, unknown). The relay grants one short lease at a time; the extension heartbeat renews only while the same session/tab is present; POST /browser/result/:commandId atomically closes the step. On reconnect, reconcile pending commands against the ledger and quarantine unknown writes instead of replaying them. Surface the ledger through the existing /jobs and receipts APIs so the pendant can say exactly where the task stopped.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped browser connection would stop being a source of duplicate submissions, repeated purchases, or uncertainty. The owner could safely say "resume" and receive a precise completion report rather than guessing whether the last action happened.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema and atomic state transitions in relay D1, Mac bridge adapters, extension heartbeat/result changes, plus crash/reconnect tests for timeout at every step boundary.
changes.risk: A false page fingerprint could pause a harmless task or, worse, permit a mismatched page. Default to quarantine on mismatch; recovery is manual resume after a fresh inspection. Ledger corruption should leave steps paused, never replayed.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and event overhead; one small D1 write per step and occasional heartbeat. No additional model call is required for retries.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–150 ms per step for lease/receipt persistence; resume waits for the next heartbeat (target under 10 s).
changes.security_impact: Improves security by binding writes to origin/session/page state and limiting replay. Relay must not store page bodies or credentials; encrypt or hash fingerprints and redact receipt text.
depends_on: chg-16bc5dee durable browser runner remains unimplemented
browser-extension offline-queue reconciler / stale-command pause
A result contract that can report unknown after a timeout

changes.change: Attach a compact, signed environment capsule to every server-to-Mac plan: machine-context revision, browser session/tab identity and heartbeat age, active project/session, and the plan's allowed origin/app targets. Before each mutating step, the Mac bridge compares the capsule to a fresh read-only snapshot; on drift it pauses and returns a structured stale-plan receipt (what changed, which step was withheld), while read-only observations may continue. Keep the capsule as hashes and IDs rather than page text. This is observability and correctness, not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Plans would stop acting on yesterday's browser tab, a different account, or a changed project after the owner has resumed work. The owner gets a clear "paused because the page/account changed" explanation instead of a silent wrong edit.
changes.effort: Medium: add revision counters to machine/browser state, snapshot-and-compare middleware in POST /execute and browser dispatch, and stale-plan receipts in the existing job journal.
changes.risk: Over-sensitive revisions could pause harmless tasks during normal tab title changes; compare only security-relevant fields (origin, session, tab ID, app target) and allow explicit rebase. If the snapshot cannot be read, fail closed for writes and report uncertainty.
changes.cost_impact: Tiny: hashes and a few metadata fields per plan/step; no extra model calls.
changes.latency_impact: One local snapshot comparison per mutating step, target under 100 ms; no perceptible delay for reads.
changes.security_impact: Reduces confused-deputy and cross-account writes by binding execution to the observed session and origin. Do not put cookies, page bodies, or secrets in the capsule.
depends_on: GET /machine-context and POST /machine-context/refresh
GET /browser/status and POST /browser/heartbeat
POST /execute and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts
A real implementation of the granted read-only Mac inspection/source tools or equivalent local snapshot route

changes.change: Add a browser-device lease and command-reconciliation layer. Treat a heartbeat as valid only when it carries a fresh device epoch plus a real tab/window identity and capability hash; mark the current home-chrome lease stale when tabId/tabUrl/tabCount are null or the heartbeat expires. Move commands claimed by that lease into a quarantined state (never execute them on a later device by accident), then requeue them with the same idempotency key only after a new valid heartbeat. Emit one durable reconciliation record per command with claimed lease, quarantine reason, retry count, and final disposition, and expose a compact status endpoint for the pendant/Mac planner. This is the missing control plane beneath the still-unbuilt durable browser runner—not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops seeing 45-second hangs and silent duplicate browser actions. If Safari/Chrome sleeps or a dialog blocks it, the pendant can say “paused, 9 commands preserved; resumed at 2:14” and continue safely when the real tab returns, rather than treating a ghost device as online.
changes.effort: Medium: browser bridge heartbeat schema and lease store, queue state transition/reconciliation endpoint, planner notification adapter, and restart tests.
changes.risk: A too-strict heartbeat could pause valid work; recover by allowing an explicit device re-announce and operator-visible requeue reason. Never auto-fail private work to the public relay, which cannot hold the owner’s login session.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local JSON writes per heartbeat and command transition.
changes.latency_impact: Heartbeats remain cheap; failed commands return a fast paused/quarantined result instead of waiting 45 seconds. Resume adds only one heartbeat interval.
changes.security_impact: Improves session safety: stale leases cannot execute, idempotency keys prevent replay, and private URLs/results stay on the authenticated browser path.
depends_on: chg-14accc01’s existing request IDs/idempotency/tab affinity (progressive polling remains unfinished)
chg-16bc5dee’s durable browser runner and result stream
browser extension must emit a real tab-bearing heartbeat

changes.change: Make execution routing liveness-aware before invoking the expensive realtime tier: consult the browser lease/status and Mac bridge readiness, classify each planned step as ready, wait-for-device, or blocked, and hand wait-for-device work to a durable background lane with a bounded exponential retry schedule. Realtime should answer immediately with the classified state and receipt ID, not sit on a 45-second browser wait. When readiness changes, send only the delta back to the planner and pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Requests feel immediate and honest: “I can do this when Chrome reconnects” replaces a long silence, while the owner’s battery and attention are not spent on repeated failed attempts. They also get one completion message rather than multiple duplicate failure notices.
changes.effort: Medium: a preflight classifier, routing metadata in job records, background wake/retry trigger, and a small event-to-pendant adapter.
changes.risk: A readiness check can be briefly stale; the executor still verifies the lease immediately before each action and records any mismatch. If the background lane is unavailable, the task remains visibly paused rather than being discarded.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces GPT realtime usage and browser timeout work; background classification can use a low-cost model or deterministic rules. Storage/event costs are small.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement under 1–2 seconds; successful work is unchanged, unavailable work waits without blocking the conversation.
changes.security_impact: No additional page data needs to leave the Mac. Routing sees only readiness, origin (private/public), and task metadata; private pages remain pinned to the authenticated browser.
depends_on: Browser lease/quarantine change proposed this round
GET /routing and GET /ops/status
GET /browser/status and POST /browser/heartbeat
POST /jobs and GET /jobs/:jobId
POST /pipeline/events

changes.change: Add an explicit interruption contract to every delegated task: quiet/until-time, urgent-only, or conversational. Compile that contract once at task creation, propagate it through relay, Mac jobs, browser commands, and receipts, and collapse all retries/reconnects into one owner-visible state machine. At completion, materialize a review packet containing outcome, evidence links, failures, and recommended next action; deliver it through the pendant only when the contract permits, otherwise expose it at the next attention window.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can delegate real work without being nagged, lose neither failures nor completions, and review one trustworthy packet instead of reconstructing a task from scattered spoken alerts, browser tabs, and Mac logs.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared task contract schema, event severity/deduplication, packet renderer, and attention-window integration across relay and Mac.
changes.risk: Incorrect severity could delay an important alert. Recover with a persistent dashboard badge, an always-available “what’s waiting?” query, and a hard upper bound after which a quiet task becomes a review item rather than an unspoken failure.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and event cost; cheaper background synthesis replaces repeated realtime narration. No new per-task realtime call unless escalation occurs.
changes.latency_impact: Delegation acknowledgement remains near-instant; routine narration is suppressed, while urgent events are pushed promptly and completion packets are ready at the next review point.
changes.security_impact: Contracts and packet metadata may cross the relay, but private evidence remains local or redacted until explicitly requested. The contract controls delivery timing, not authorization to perform actions.
depends_on: Durable task identity shared by relay, Mac jobs, and browser commands
A typed event severity/deduplication stream
Calendar/foreground/pendant attention-window signals
Existing action receipts and evidence capsules

changes.change: Add an ingress validator and causal state machine for Mac jobs. Reject empty action lists before creating a job; attach one correlation ID from pendant request through /execute, browser command, receipt, and spoken response; record terminal reason codes (offline, stale, timeout, permission, no-op) and reconcile orphaned browser commands into the same timeline. Expose a compact incident view in the dashboard and a machine-readable status endpoint.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently sees failed jobs with empty commands and nine browser commands stranded separately from their originating requests. This would make the system tell one truthful story—what was requested, what device was unavailable, whether anything changed, and whether retry is safe—rather than making the owner debug the harness.
changes.effort: Medium: shared request envelope, ingress validation, job/command linkage, reason-code taxonomy, dashboard grouping, and regression fixtures for offline/timeout/retry paths.
changes.risk: A stricter validator could reject malformed plans that used to limp through; preserve a compatibility path for legacy callers and add tests. Correlation metadata must never include page contents or secrets.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API/storage overhead; saves expensive model retries by eliminating no-op and duplicate execution attempts.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-millisecond validation; no added latency to valid actions. Dashboard aggregation can be asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Improves auditability without adding access. Keep URLs/DOM snippets redacted by default and use opaque IDs in relay speech.
depends_on: Browser queue and receipt linkage from chg-14accc01 should be reused rather than replaced
The existing /jobs, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, /journal, and /browser/result/:commandId data stores need a shared correlation field
mac_readonly_inspect implementation remains desirable for verifying local recovery, but this change does not depend on it

changes.change: Implement a cross-surface Focus Lease protocol, not another briefing: FocusLease {leaseId, owner, startedAt, expiresAt, priorMacNotificationState, deliveryPolicy, queuedEventIds, version}. The relay is authoritative for lease state; pendant start/stop events are idempotent and can queue offline. Mac applies the lease through a non-Accessibility notification/Focus integration, reports applied/restored receipts, and reconciles after reconnect. Browser watchers publish only normalized severity events; the relay deduplicates them and releases a single catch-up bundle on restore. Expiry, crash, and duplicate button presses must converge to the saved prior state.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: One press creates a dependable, temporary interruption boundary across the devices the owner already uses, and one short catch-up replaces a pile of notifications. It remains safe if the Mac sleeps, the radio drops, or the owner forgets to end focus.
changes.effort: Medium: protocol and relay state machine, Mac Focus adapter and restore tests, browser event adapter, pendant event persistence, plus dashboard visibility.
changes.risk: A stale lease could suppress an important alert or fail to restore notifications. Use a hard maximum TTL, urgent bypass rules, visible pendant expiry indication, persisted prior-state snapshots, and a reconciliation job. If state is uncertain, restore notifications rather than keep them muted.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/compute; roughly <$0.001 per transition. Background catch-up summarization is the only model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second relay state change; 1–2 seconds for Mac apply/restore; no impact on ordinary conversation.
changes.security_impact: Lease metadata and event IDs may leave the Mac; page content stays local unless explicitly requested. Treat notification titles/snippets as sensitive, redact by default, and delete queued events at lease expiry plus retention window.
depends_on: A real pendant offline event/LED skill (offline_attention_window_toggle is still pending)
A relay-side lease endpoint and reconnect reconciliation
A Mac Focus adapter that works without Accessibility permission
Browser watcher output in a typed severity/event schema

changes.change: Add a durable notification mailbox on the pendant for typed external receipts. It stores at most 8 compact records (receipt ID, coarse state, timestamp, retry count), renders three distinct haptic patterns, acknowledges delivery to the relay, survives a dropped link, and exposes a single-button 'latest status' request. It must never store transcript text or page content, and must coalesce duplicate receipt IDs.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Long-running work can finish without the owner staring at the Mac or listening continuously; the pendant quietly tells them whether to continue walking, check something, or review a failure.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium firmware change plus relay protocol and integration tests; requires validating haptic actuator timing and flash wear limits on the actual pendant.
changes.risk: A missed or repeated vibration could cause confusion. Use sequence numbers, a bounded mailbox, explicit delivery acknowledgements, a periodic expiry, and a neutral pattern when state is unknown.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost. Firmware power impact is limited to short haptic pulses and occasional radio packets; no new hardware assumed until the pendant actuator spec is verified.
changes.latency_impact: Terminal receipt to haptic target under 2 seconds while connected; queued delivery on reconnect.
changes.security_impact: Only coarse status leaves the Mac. No transcript, notification title, URL, or file name is stored on the pendant.
depends_on: A shared terminal receipt taxonomy across Mac jobs and browser commands
Relay-to-pendant notification delivery and acknowledgement route
Actual pendant haptic actuator/storage limits and offline event queue implementation

changes.change: Add a cross-surface browser-queue reconciler in the Mac planner: correlate each pending browser command with its local jobId, journal/receipt, tab/session lease, and last heartbeat; classify it as runnable, duplicate, orphaned, or stalled. A command with no live tab, an expired lease, or a high attempt count must be quarantined (not replayed), emit one durable diagnostic event, and expose a resume/ discard operation. Reconcile after every browser heartbeat and before any new browser action, then surface a compact Mac review item and, when appropriate, a pendant alert. Keep the existing owner policy of maximum access: this is observability and replay prevention, not an approval gate.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops getting silent duplicate clicks or 45-second hangs after Safari/Chrome closes. They receive one clear explanation—what was attempted, whether it changed anything, and whether it can safely resume—instead of the system repeatedly acting on a stale private tab.
changes.effort: Medium: a small persistent ledger and state machine in local-agent, adapters for /browser/status, /browser/poll, /browser/result/:commandId, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and journal events, plus dashboard/briefing presentation and tests for restart/heartbeat races.
changes.risk: Incorrect classification could quarantine a valid long-running read or discard a command whose result is merely delayed. Preserve the raw command and receipt, use lease expiry plus attempt/time thresholds rather than attempts alone, and make resume/discard explicit operations. Recovery is replay from the preserved command only after a fresh tab/session binding.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one lightweight ledger write per heartbeat/command and bounded diagnostic context. No extra model call unless generating the human summary.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds before a browser action; removes the current worst-case 45-second blocking wait for commands that can never complete.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by preventing stale authenticated commands from replaying into a different tab. Store opaque session/tab IDs and hashes, not page contents; redact URLs in pendant alerts.
depends_on: chg-14accc01's request IDs/idempotency and resumable polling (currently missing progress/resume implementation)
chg-16bc5dee's durable browser job runner (router exists, persistence/retry/result stream still missing)
A browser heartbeat that reports active tab/session identity rather than online=true with tabId=null

changes.change: Add a commitment-risk and recovery transaction layer that consumes timestamped Calendar/Mail/browser observations, maintains a state machine (planned → at-risk → missed → recovery-pending → chosen → executed), and emits an option envelope rather than an action. Each envelope contains 2–3 ranked recovery plans with evidence IDs, affected apps, exact proposed changes, and an opaque selection token. The pendant can select an option; the Mac then materializes drafts/previews, executes only the selected reversible bundle, and records per-step receipts plus a compensating plan.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an immediate, concrete way out of a missed obligation instead of another passive summary: choose the least damaging recovery plan from the pendant, with the Mac preparing the exact drafts and schedule changes for review.
changes.effort: High: new durable state and evidence schema, cross-source diffing, option ranking, pendant option-selection messages, transactional multi-app planner, and receipt/compensation handling.
changes.risk: A false positive could cause stressful alerts or propose an inappropriate message. Require confidence and quiet hours, suppress duplicate alerts, preserve drafts only, and make every mutation a separate explicit execution step. If execution partially fails, leave a discrepancy card with receipts rather than guessing.
changes.cost_impact: Low-to-moderate background model cost only on state transitions; storage and deterministic conflict analysis dominate routine operation. No additional realtime model call beyond the short alert/selection exchange.
changes.latency_impact: Detection depends on source polling, but once an at-risk transition is observed, option generation should complete in 1–2 minutes; pendant acknowledgement remains sub-second.
changes.security_impact: The option envelope sent to the pendant contains opaque IDs and short redacted labels, never private message bodies or portal content. Evidence and drafts remain on the Mac/relay under existing authenticated scope; execution logs record app and field changes.
depends_on: A durable commitment lifecycle and cross-source observation diff store
A pendant protocol for presenting/selecting opaque option IDs
A transactional multi-app action bundle with per-step receipts and compensating recovery
Reliable authenticated browser observation with tab/session continuity

changes.change: Make the audio contract genuinely symmetric at 24 kHz: capture 24 kHz from the microphone (or oversample at 48 kHz and decimate), encode 24 kHz Opus uplink, and advertise the negotiated sample rate in the pipeline handshake. Keep the current 24 kHz decoder for downlink, but add bounded jitter buffering and a relay pass-through mode so the relay does not silently transcode 16 kHz speech back into 24 kHz. Measure encode+decode CPU, heap high-water, packet loss, and glass-to-glass latency in a hardware-in-the-loop fixture; refuse the mode and fall back to 16 kHz before audio underruns if the budget is exceeded.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's voice and the assistant's reply would stop being upsampled on one direction: meeting mode, voice notes, and ordinary conversation would sound noticeably more natural and intelligible, especially for names and consonants. A negotiated fallback means a weak link becomes lower fidelity rather than a broken conversation.
changes.effort: Medium-to-high: firmware microphone clock/driver and Opus application mode, relay negotiation/transcode changes, bridge clock validation, and a repeatable HIL latency/packet-loss test. The current nRF9160 prototype has only 211,608 B app RAM and both encode/decode already consume about 87% of one core, so profiling must precede enabling it by default; the eventual product board may need a codec/DSP or faster MCU.
changes.risk: 24 kHz capture can exhaust CPU, increase radio bitrate and battery drain, or expose clock drift between the nRF9160 and ESP32. Recover by capability negotiation, a watchdog on underrun, and automatic 16 kHz fallback; retain diagnostic counters rather than dropping the session.
changes.cost_impact: No incremental API cost for codec changes; 24 kHz Opus likely increases radio airtime and energy roughly in proportion to bitrate. Hardware cost is TBD, but a production audio codec/DSP or faster MCU may add roughly $3–$10 BOM and tens of mW compared with this development kit.
changes.latency_impact: Potentially +10–30 ms from larger capture/codec work unless frames stay bounded; target under 250 ms glass-to-glass and measure p50/p95. Fallback must happen within one failed negotiation/underrun window.
changes.security_impact: Audio remains encrypted in transit; higher-fidelity raw audio increases sensitivity and should use the existing short-retention/deletion policy. Do not persist PCM on the pendant or relay except bounded diagnostic samples with explicit opt-in.
depends_on: A pipeline handshake carrying sample rate/codec/bitrate and a relay pass-through path
The pending audio-path diagnostic/HIL fixture and offline delivery retry behavior
A production hardware decision if nRF9160 CPU headroom cannot meet simultaneous encode/decode
An end-to-end 24 kHz capture test using the actual microphone clock rather than resampling a 16 kHz source

changes.change: Replace the prototype nRF9160-plus-ESP32 audio split with a production pendant audio front end: a low-power 24/48 kHz codec or DSP with hardware sample-rate conversion, a small secure ring-buffer SRAM, and a shared clock exposed to the modem MCU. Keep the nRF9160 for LTE-M/NB-IoT control and negotiation, but move Opus pre/post-processing and jitter-buffer servicing off the 64 MHz application core. Add a physical recording-status indicator driven independently of firmware task load.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They would get natural, stable 24 kHz speech without the pendant becoming hot, stuttering, or dying quickly, and the recording indicator would remain trustworthy even if the network or application task is wedged. It makes long conversations and meeting handoffs dependable rather than a lab-only mode.
changes.effort: High: select codec/DSP and PMIC, redesign the board and clock tree, update Zephyr drivers and the ESP32 bridge contract, validate RF coexistence and acoustic performance, and manufacture a small pilot. This is intentionally a product redesign rather than a software workaround for the development kit.
changes.risk: New clock domains can introduce drift, RF noise, boot failures, or a more difficult firmware update path. Recover with a bypass path to the existing I2S wiring, a hardware watchdog, signed dual-image firmware, and a 16 kHz compatibility mode. Validate on a pilot batch before replacing the prototype fleet.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $5–$15 additional BOM depending on codec/DSP, SRAM, PMIC, and indicator choices, plus one-time board/NRE cost; active audio power should fall versus spending most of the nRF9160 core on codec work, though idle BOM power rises slightly.
changes.latency_impact: Hardware buffering should reduce codec CPU contention and make p95 latency more predictable; target under 50 ms local audio buffering and under 250 ms glass-to-glass. Clock conversion must be bounded and measurable.
changes.security_impact: A hardware ring buffer must be volatile by default and zeroized on stop; do not add persistent raw-audio storage. The independent indicator must be fail-safe—if capture power is enabled, it should indicate capture even when the main MCU is unresponsive.
depends_on: A measured 24 kHz end-to-end audio contract and HIL test vector
A product-board decision replacing the explicitly provisional Nordic development kit
Relay negotiation for codec/sample-rate capability and a bridge firmware protocol version
A hardware privacy-indicator review with the owner

changes.change: Add a cross-surface causal event ledger. Every spoken request, relay event, browser command, Mac job, and pendant delivery receives a correlation ID, parent ID, origin surface, intended effect, sensitivity, and terminal outcome. The relay maintains a lease per correlation ID so reconnects cannot duplicate a reminder or action; Mac and browser receipts append typed evidence, and the pendant can ask 'what happened to that?' and get the same timeline. Expire abandoned leases and expose a compact redacted timeline in the dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one trustworthy answer about whether a request was heard, queued, acted on, or failed, instead of duplicate Mac actions, repeated browser submissions, or a pendant saying 'done' when a surface was offline. It also makes recovery after Wi‑Fi loss understandable without exposing raw private content.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define the event/receipt schema, add correlation propagation to relay, browser and Mac adapters, persist an append-only or compacted ledger, and add reconciliation tests for retries and reconnects.
changes.risk: A schema or clock mismatch could make work appear stuck or incorrectly completed. Recover by treating terminal receipts as immutable, using monotonic sequence numbers per job, and providing a replay/reconcile worker. Never infer success from a timeout.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 storage and negligible compute; compact old entries and retain only hashes/metadata by default. One additional receipt write per cross-surface step; no model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Usually under 20 ms per event write; reconciliation is asynchronous. A first response can be acknowledged before the ledger is fully compacted.
changes.security_impact: The ledger is a sensitive activity trail. Store redacted metadata by default, encrypt it, scope reads to the owner/session, and hash or omit URLs, snippets, file names, and message contents unless explicitly requested. Correlation IDs must be unguessable.
depends_on: Existing Mac job receipts and undo routes
Browser command queue request IDs and tab/session affinity
A relay durable job/event store
A typed pendant delivery acknowledgment path

changes.change: Add an offline-queue circuit breaker and stale-command reconciler. When browser/status reports offline or a command exceeds its deadline, stop issuing retries, atomically mark the command blocked_on_surface with the last heartbeat and reason, and expose a single resumable queue entry. On the next heartbeat, revalidate tab/session affinity and page identity before replaying only idempotent reads; discard or require a new explicit plan for writes. Also alert the relay/pendant once, not once per retry.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current Mac has an offline browser bridge with 10 pending commands, and prior navigation jobs can wait 45 seconds before failing. This change prevents invisible backlogs, duplicate browser work, and repeated false 'working' status. The owner gets one honest message—browser unavailable, N items held—and automatic safe recovery when the extension returns.
changes.effort: Medium: implement heartbeat-aware queue state transitions, deadlines, deduplication, typed read/write replay rules, and a small reconciliation worker plus tests for disconnect/reconnect and stale tabs.
changes.risk: A false offline signal could delay a harmless read, or a tab may change between disconnect and reconnect. Recover by expiring leases, rechecking URL/title/session IDs, and requiring a fresh plan for any mutation. Keep held commands inspectable and cancellable.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; a few D1/local queue writes and one heartbeat check per interval. Reduces wasted browser action retries and their associated latency.
changes.latency_impact: Failures become fast (seconds rather than 45-second timeouts); safe reads resume within one heartbeat plus validation. Writes never replay automatically.
changes.security_impact: Do not retain page bodies in the held queue. Store only command type, redacted session/tab identifiers, deadline, and reason. Encrypt queue records and ensure stale authenticated commands cannot replay against a different tab.
depends_on: Existing GET /browser/status and POST /browser/heartbeat
Browser command queue with request IDs, idempotency keys, and tab/session affinity
Existing Mac job receipts and cancellation/status routes
A relay notification path for one deduplicated surface-health event

changes.change: Add a resumable, manifest-driven playback protocol for generated speech. The relay publishes an authenticated manifest containing Opus 24 kHz/60 ms frame count, SHA-256, duration, and expiry; the nRF9160 fetches frames in small windows, decodes into a bounded jitter buffer, persists only the next frame cursor and manifest ID, and ACKs the highest contiguous frame. On reconnect it resumes from that cursor, validates the final hash, and emits explicit started/paused/completed/corrupt/expired events. Keep microSD as the existing failure buffer only, not routine audio storage.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped bridge or LTE connection no longer forces the owner to restart a briefing or wonder whether it played. Scheduled audio becomes trustworthy while preserving the owner's rule that the pendant should not routinely fill its SD card with recordings.
changes.effort: Medium-high: relay manifest/range endpoints and transcode validation, firmware Opus frame windowing/cursor persistence/events, and Mac dashboard receipt display. Test modem loss, reboot, duplicate frames, expired URLs, and PCM/Opus mismatch.
changes.risk: A corrupt cursor or interrupted SD write could skip or repeat a frame; recover by replaying the last acknowledged frame and treating the manifest as idempotent. Decoder timing or RAM pressure could cause underruns; use a 3–5-frame buffer, measure heap, and fall back to whole-object download when the manifest is unsupported.
changes.cost_impact: No additional LLM cost. Minor D1/R2 metadata and egress overhead; bandwidth is approximately the encoded audio size. Firmware uses a few KB of RAM for frame metadata/buffer; playback decode is about 25.4 ms per 60 ms frame on the measured 64 MHz core, materially below the simultaneous encode+decode prototype load.
changes.latency_impact: First audio can remain under 2 seconds; reconnect resumes in about one frame window rather than re-rendering. Hash validation adds only end-of-item time.
changes.security_impact: Signed, short-lived frame URLs and device/session binding prevent cross-account audio access. Manifest hashes detect tampering or stale PCM. Expiry and deletion must follow the existing 30-day audio-retention policy.
depends_on: A single canonical relay contract for Opus rather than the currently observed PCM payload at relay_result
Durable relay playback state and typed pipeline events
A small firmware update that can persist a cursor without violating the microSD failure-buffer policy

changes.change: Add a reachability-aware execution envelope spanning relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge. Before dispatch, stamp each action with surface, session/tab affinity, idempotency key, and a short lease. The Mac agent must consult live /ops/status and /observe: accessibility-dependent UI actions become explicitly blocked/unverified when uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false (never successful receipts), while AppleScript/read-only actions remain eligible. Browser commands queued while offline are quarantined as stale after the lease, not replayed blindly; on heartbeat they are resumed only if their idempotency key and tab/session still match. Emit one durable state transition (planned → dispatched → verified/blocked/expired) to the relay so the pendant can say exactly what happened and what needs reconnecting.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing 'done' when nothing happened, avoids ten old browser commands firing at once after reconnect, and gets a concise pendant notification naming the one blocked prerequisite. Safe read-only work can still proceed through AppleScript even when GUI input or Safari is unavailable.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared action envelope/schema, status preflight, browser queue lease/quarantine, relay state projection, and migration of receipts; add fault-injection tests for disconnect/reconnect and stale tabs.
changes.risk: A conservative status check could mark an action blocked during a transient probe failure, and lease expiry could leave work pending. Recover by retaining the plan and idempotency key, exposing explicit retry/resume, and never deleting the user's requested work. Existing maximum-access policy remains unchanged; this adds truthfulness/observability, not an approval gate.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local JSON state writes per action and one reconnect notification. Engineering/storage cost is the dominant cost.
changes.latency_impact: ~100–300 ms for status/lease checks; no extra model call. Reconnect may delay work until a heartbeat and verification arrives.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety against stale authenticated-tab replay and false success. Preserve URL/tab metadata minimization and do not transmit page content in status events; idempotency keys must not contain secrets.
depends_on: A shared action-envelope contract between /execute, browser command queue, and relay job records
A browser heartbeat/reconnect handler that reports tab/session identity
A verified distinction between read-only AppleScript and accessibility-dependent UI actions
Relay durable job-state projection and pendant notification path

changes.change: Create a cross-surface postcondition-and-witness layer, not another action queue. Every planned multi-surface job must carry declarative assertions such as file hash changed, app state contains a named value, or a browser session's specific DOM region equals an expected normalized value. After execution, independent adapters collect fresh witnesses from the Mac agent and authenticated browser, attach timestamps/tab IDs/file identities, and classify each assertion as verified, contradicted, or unknown. The relay stores the compact assertion result and the pendant speaks only the delta; action receipts remain evidence of attempted steps, never proof of the final state.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for an outcome and know whether it is true across the places that matter, even when a UI action was swallowed or a browser disconnected. Partial completion becomes visible without blindly repeating a payment, submission, message, or file mutation.
changes.effort: High: define a small assertion language, implement Mac and browser witness adapters, bind observations to job/session identity, add freshness and conflict handling, and test non-idempotent failures. This is deliberately separate from the existing executor and receipt/undo mechanisms.
changes.risk: A witness can be stale, ambiguous, or unavailable; incorrectly declaring success is worse than declaring unknown. Require source timestamps and identity binding, use an explicit unknown state, expire assertions, and make repair a separate reviewed plan. No automatic retry of irreversible effects.
changes.cost_impact: Small deterministic compute and local/relay storage cost per assertion; background model cost only when normalizing conflicting textual/page evidence. Data volume can be kept low with hashes, normalized fields, and cited snippets.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds for independent postcondition reads after an action; complex browser pages may continue in background. Initial acknowledgment remains immediate.
changes.security_impact: Witnesses must be scoped to the initiating job and redact page content, email bodies, and secrets. Do not copy full authenticated DOMs to the relay; retain local evidence references and short hashes where possible.
depends_on: A shared postcondition schema between /plan and /execute
Independent read-only Mac and browser inspection adapters
Relay persistence for assertion results and expiry
Pendant phrasing for verified/contradicted/unknown outcomes
Existing job receipts, journal records, and browser session identity

changes.change: Add an attention-envelope and durable attention-queue protocol between event ingestion and delivery. Each item has eventId, source, observedAt, freshness deadline, urgency/reason, sensitivity, required surface, quiet-policy result, browser command epoch, dedupe key, capsule URL/snippet hash, and state {queued,snoozed,delivered,acknowledged,expired,blocked}. Accept availability transitions from pendant and Mac, re-evaluate only on meaningful transitions, and emit one delivery receipt plus an owner-visible explanation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one calm, trustworthy place for things that need attention instead of duplicate voice alerts and stale browser findings. They can understand why something was held back and recover missed items after reconnecting.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema, D1/R2 queue and lease worker, event reducer, relay delivery adapter, and dashboard endpoint; add contract tests for offline tabs, meeting quiet mode, reconnect, duplicate events, and expiry.
changes.risk: A bad urgency rule could delay something important or spam the owner. Recover with conservative defaults (urgent safety/security events may break quiet mode; everything else queues), visible reason codes, expiry warnings, and replayable event logs. Do not mutate external systems.
changes.cost_impact: Low background storage/compute; roughly one small D1 row and occasional R2 capsule per item. Cheap model only for ambiguous ranking; no new realtime call for routine queue operations.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second state re-evaluation and seconds-to-minutes for background extraction; reconnect delivery is immediate once a lease is acquired.
changes.security_impact: Private snippets remain encrypted/local where possible; source permissions and sensitivity travel with the envelope. Browser session tokens never enter the capsule. Dashboard and acknowledgment endpoints require bearer auth.
depends_on: Browser extension typed liveness states and command epoch
Pendant availability/acknowledge event skill
Working implementations of mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect
A relay durable queue/receipt store

changes.change: Add a cross-surface intent-claim coordinator for every owner request. Normalize the request into an intentId, then let relay, Mac, and browser workers advertise capabilities and acquire short leases on individual subtasks (read, draft, execute, deliver). Claims include dependency edges, idempotency key, cancellation epoch, and expected side effects; a coordinator prevents two surfaces from acting on the same intent, merges receipts into one causal timeline, and reassigns only expired or explicitly cancelled leases. A pendant interruption or reconnect advances the cancellation epoch rather than starting a duplicate run.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say one thing naturally while several surfaces work, without getting duplicate drafts, two browser submissions, repeated notifications, or a Mac action racing a browser action. If a laptop sleeps or the browser disconnects, work resumes safely and the owner receives one coherent result instead of conflicting reports.
changes.effort: High: intent normalization, lease store, dependency-aware scheduler, cross-surface receipt correlation, cancellation/reassignment protocol, and failure-injection tests for reconnects, duplicate voice turns, stale browser epochs, and Mac sleep.
changes.risk: A lease bug could strand work or incorrectly suppress a needed action. Recover with short bounded leases, visible pending/blocked states, deterministic idempotency keys, append-only receipts, and a manual retry that starts a new intent generation. It must coordinate execution, not silently authorize high-impact actions.
changes.cost_impact: Low persistent storage and queue compute; cheap model only for ambiguous intent decomposition. Avoids duplicate model/browser/Mac work, likely reducing cost overall.
changes.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for claim acquisition; parallel subtasks remain parallel. Recovery waits for lease expiry unless a cancellation/reconnect event arrives.
changes.security_impact: Claims carry capability and sensitivity labels but never session secrets. Workers receive only their subtask's minimum context. Every external mutation remains attributable to one intent generation and one surface receipt.
depends_on: A shared intentId/idempotency-key format across relay jobs, POST /execute, browser command queue, and pendant events
A durable lease/claim store and event stream
Receipt correlation that can link GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts with browser and Mac results
Explicit cancellation/reconnect epochs from the browser extension and pendant

changes.change: Add an execution-truth reconciler between POST /execute, the job/action receipt writer, and POST /pipeline/events. On every action, derive the displayed state from the actual executor result and FULL_CONTROL_MODE, not from the planner's generic risk message. Emit a typed lifecycle (accepted, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled) with jobId/actionId, executor, and undoability; suppress or rewrite legacy 'Waiting for your approval' events when fullControlMode=true and no gate exists. Reconcile orphaned processing pipeline runs on bridge restart from the durable job/receipt store, and attribute each receipt to deterministic/background/planner/realtime tier.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently hears a false approval prompt even though their chosen policy is maximum access and the action path executes without approval; this makes them unsure whether a task ran. A single truthful spoken/dashboard status would prevent duplicate commands and make completion receipts trustworthy. It also turns the observed 112 unattributed jobs into an actionable history instead of an unexplained cost/latency bill.
changes.effort: Moderate: shared event schema, replay/reconciliation worker, migration for legacy pipeline events, and tests covering execute success/failure, bridge restart, and policy modes.
changes.risk: A bad reconciliation could mark an action complete twice or hide a real failure. Use monotonic event sequence numbers, durable jobId/actionId keys, and retain raw legacy events for diagnostics; never execute during reconciliation. Recovery is replay from pendant-jobs.json and actionReceipts.
changes.cost_impact: No model calls; a few hundred bytes of metadata per action and one low-rate background reconciliation pass. Saves planner spend by preventing duplicate retries caused by phantom waiting states.
changes.latency_impact: Less than 50 ms local bookkeeping on execution; reconnect reconciliation completes in the background. Spoken status can arrive immediately from deterministic events.
changes.security_impact: No new data access. Receipts should contain action type and redacted outcome only; keep command text/page content out of relay events. Existing owner policy remains unchanged—this fixes reporting, not authorization.
depends_on: A canonical actionId/jobId correlation persisted by the executor and relay
A versioned pipeline event schema with monotonic sequence numbers
A small read-only reconciliation worker over GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and GET /pipeline

changes.change: Add a browser-bridge liveness watchdog and queue quarantine layer, distinct from the command protocol itself. Track each device heartbeat lease and each command claim lease; when the lease expires, atomically move processing commands to `orphaned` (not immediately runnable), stop claiming new commands while the device is offline, and mark sessions whose lastUsedAt exceeds a configurable TTL as stale. On reconnection, require a fresh heartbeat and device/session identity before offering quarantined commands; replay only idempotent commands with the original request/idempotency key, while non-idempotent commands remain held for review. Emit one durable incident/receipt linking the command, attempts, last heartbeat, and reason, and let the pendant/relay announce a compact “browser bridge offline; N queued, M held” status rather than timing out for 45 seconds.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Today a dead or stale browser bridge can leave ten commands queued and a command stuck `processing` for hours with 18 attempts, while a browser action burns ~45 seconds before failing. The owner would get an honest immediate status, no accidental duplicate navigation/form action after reconnect, and automatic continuation of safe reads when the browser returns.
changes.effort: Medium: browserBridge queue state machine plus a small periodic reaper/lease table, session TTL handling, and relay-facing status projection; add crash/reconnect integration tests for offline, duplicate poll, and reconnect cases.
changes.risk: A too-short lease could quarantine a slow but healthy tab; use heartbeat-derived TTL with generous grace and an explicit operator replay endpoint. A crash between state transition and receipt write must be recovered by an idempotent transaction. Never auto-replay submit/click/form mutations.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small D1/local state record per lease and occasional watchdog work. Reduces wasted planner/bridge retries and 45-second timeout traffic.
changes.latency_impact: Offline browser requests fail/status-return in milliseconds instead of waiting for bridge timeout. Healthy polling adds only a lease check; safe queued reads resume after one fresh heartbeat.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety for authenticated sessions by preventing stale-tab actions and cross-device claims. Persist only command metadata, not page contents; bind leases to extension/device and session identity.
depends_on: A heartbeat payload must include a stable extension/device identity and server-observed lease timestamp.
Existing request IDs/idempotency keys and typed action results from the browser queue work must be retained.
Relay/pendant needs a read-only bridge-health status projection and compact notification path.

changes.change: Add an accessibility-aware execution truth layer (observability, not an approval gate). Before and after every ui_* / synthesized-input action, attach the latest `/observe` inputReachability and accessibility probe to the receipt. If eventsPost=false or uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false, label the action `unverified_no_input_path` rather than `ok`, preserve the requested action and failure reason, and automatically suggest/route an equivalent AppleScript or high-level action when the target app is in the granted Automation list. For actions with no equivalent, report “not executed” immediately instead of claiming success. Expose a compact capability matrix per app (automation available, accessibility available, screen recording available) so faculty-action can choose a truthful route.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Right now the Mac reports that clicks, typing, and keypresses succeeded while doing nothing because AI Pendant Agent lacks Accessibility; the owner can be told a false success and lose trust. This change makes receipts honest and still lets Calendar, Mail, Notes, Finder, Safari, Chrome, and other already-authorized apps work through AppleScript without waiting for a manual TCC fix.
changes.effort: Medium: enrich executor receipts and journal derivation, add an action-equivalence registry for common app intents, and add tests with accessibility trusted/untrusted and secure-input states.
changes.risk: An app may accept an AppleScript command but produce an unexpected UI result; retain before/after app-level evidence and mark semantic completion separately from dispatch. Some actions genuinely require Accessibility and must remain unexecuted/unverified until the owner grants it.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful model/API cost; a small local probe and receipt metadata per action.
changes.latency_impact: Adds a local probe (sub-second). High-level AppleScript fallback can be faster than a no-op UI loop.
changes.security_impact: Does not broaden permissions. It makes existing Automation grants explicit and avoids silently pretending input reached the screen; receipt metadata should omit page contents and secrets.
depends_on: Keep `/observe` read-only and make its inputReachability result available to executor receipts.
Preserve the owner’s maximum-capability policy: this is truthful classification and fallback, not a confirmation or refusal policy.
Accessibility/Screen Recording remain owner-installed TCC grants for vision/UI tasks; no server-side substitute exists.

changes.change: Create an ephemeral-private data lane spanning browser extraction, relay speech, and pendant playback. A request creates a short-lived handoff ID bound to the authenticated tab and owner device, returns only one bounded field plus source metadata, streams it to the pendant, and then performs an atomic purge of extracted text, generated audio, research/session references, and temporary receipts. The purge receipt retains only hashes, timestamps, domain, byte counts, and success/failure—not the sensitive value. Make this lane separate from ordinary `/research` briefings so it cannot accidentally enter durable briefings, memory, or the conversation transcript.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could ask for one private fact while moving around—such as a deadline or balance—and hear it once without creating a durable copy of the page or forcing a full authenticated-page summary. Today the component routes exist independently, but there is no trustworthy boundary proving the sensitive handoff was erased.
changes.effort: Medium-high: define a volatile handoff record and lifecycle across the Mac bridge and relay, add streaming playback acknowledgement and crash cleanup, then test relay loss, pendant disconnect, duplicate requests, and purge verification.
changes.risk: A crash or logging path could retain the value; use memory-only buffers where possible, scrub structured logs, encrypt any unavoidable short-lived relay storage, and run a TTL sweeper. Delivery acknowledgement must not imply purge success; report those separately. Never permit credentials or one-time codes through the ordinary path.
changes.cost_impact: Small per-request relay/storage overhead and one short TTS turn; lower than a full research run. Cleanup metadata is tiny and contains no page content.
changes.latency_impact: One bounded extraction plus streaming audio, target 2–3 seconds; purge occurs immediately after playback acknowledgement and has a hard TTL fallback.
changes.security_impact: Adds a strict data-minimization boundary and auditable deletion without weakening browser authentication. It requires an explicit owner privacy policy for whether selected text may transit the relay.
depends_on: A browser command that supports bounded semantic extraction from the current authenticated tab.
Relay/pendant playback acknowledgement and a volatile audio queue.
A purge-capable handoff store and log scrubber; ordinary research/session persistence must be bypassed.
A privacy classifier that refuses credentials and one-time secrets by default.

changes.change: Add a cross-surface reachability/truth layer for every Mac or browser job. Before dispatch, snapshot /observe, /ops/status, and /browser/status; after each action, attach the corresponding receipt plus post-state and classify the outcome as verified, completed-but-unverified, queued-offline, or failed. Relay should never speak 'done' for UI actions when uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false, and should automatically resume queued browser work after a heartbeat/reconnect using the existing stable action IDs. Persist a compact evidence capsule (jobId, surface, timestamps, state deltas, reason) and expose it to the pendant and dashboard.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently gets false confidence: UI actions report success while Accessibility=false, and browser work can sit in a queue while the extension is offline. They would hear the truth immediately—'queued until Chrome reconnects' or 'completed and verified'—and returning to the Mac would resume without duplicate clicks.
changes.effort: Medium: a relay/result schema, pre/post probes in the Mac bridge, reconnect worker, and pendant phrasing tests; no new model training.
changes.risk: A stale probe could label a real action incorrectly, or reconnect could replay an action if its ID mapping is wrong. Recover with conservative 'unverified' status, content-addressed action IDs, and the existing receipts/undo history; never infer success from an executor HTTP 200 alone.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few hundred bytes of D1/R2 metadata per action. Background reconciliation can use a cheap model or no model.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–300 ms for local pre/post probes; offline work returns immediately as queued instead of blocking 45 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Evidence capsules must redact page text, mail contents, secrets, and shell arguments by default; retain only hashes, app/URL origin, and state labels unless the owner asks for detail.
depends_on: Accessibility or screen recording remains optional; without it the system must honestly stay in unverified mode
The existing action receipts/undo implementation
The browser command queue and heartbeat endpoint
A relay-to-pendant result delivery path

changes.change: Add a durable cross-surface task capsule and lease protocol. Every relay-issued goal gets a capsule containing ordered step IDs, surface ownership (pendant/relay/Mac/browser), idempotency key, precondition snapshot hash, lease expiry, and receipt links. The Mac and browser bridge atomically claim one step, heartbeat it, and return a typed result; on disconnect the relay marks the lease abandoned, freezes dependent steps, and hands the capsule to the next available surface for reconciliation instead of replaying the whole plan.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A request such as “find the invoice in Safari, save it on my Mac, and tell me on the pendant” would survive a browser crash or dropped voice link without losing place or repeating a download, email draft, or other side effect. The owner gets one truthful status and one recovery report instead of conflicting “done” and timeout messages.
changes.effort: Medium-high: shared D1/local JSON schema, atomic claim/lease transitions, adapters in browser bridge and Mac executor, and receipt correlation tests across reconnects.
changes.risk: A bad precondition hash could pause harmless work or, worse, allow a duplicate if a client loses its receipt. Recover with conservative lease expiry, append-only receipts, duplicate-result reconciliation, and manual resume for any unknown mutation. Do not infer completion from lastSeenAt alone.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible inference cost; small D1/local storage and heartbeat traffic increase. No new paid model calls in the normal path.
changes.latency_impact: Adds one local ledger write and claim check per step (tens of milliseconds); reconnect recovery waits for bounded health confirmation rather than immediately retrying.
changes.security_impact: Capsules should carry opaque identifiers and redacted hashes by default; sensitive page text remains on the owning Mac/browser session. Cross-surface messages need authenticated pairing and scope-limited session IDs.
depends_on: Browser bridge heartbeat/result endpoints must expose a stable command lease and actual tab/session identity
Mac receipts need a shared idempotency key and step ID rather than only per-action receipt IDs
Relay durable job records need a capsule pointer and explicit abandoned/reconciled states

changes.change: Replace the single browser online boolean with a state panel showing transport health, extension heartbeat age, active tab/session identity, oldest pending command age, lease owner/attempt count, and a clear “safe to resume / quarantined / owner action needed” state. Detect and visibly flag contradictions such as /browser/status offline while /ops/status says online, rather than presenting online:true.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When browser work fails, the owner can immediately see whether Chrome/Safari is closed, the extension is not polling, a page is blocked, or a command is stuck. They can recover the right thing instead of repeatedly asking the pendant to retry and risking duplicate actions.
changes.effort: Small-medium: derive health states from existing endpoints, add stale/contradiction rules, and link each queued item to its receipt and cancel/quarantine action.
changes.risk: An overly sensitive indicator could create noise during normal tab transitions. Use hysteresis (three heartbeats and a 15-second grace period) and preserve raw timestamps for diagnosis.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; a few local/relay reads and negligible dashboard storage.
changes.latency_impact: Status refresh every 5–15 seconds; no impact on action execution.
changes.security_impact: Show URLs/titles only on the local Mac dashboard; relay-facing telemetry should redact them and expose opaque session IDs.
depends_on: GET /browser/status
GET /browser/poll
GET /ops/status
POST /browser/heartbeat
GET /browser/sessions
GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts

changes.change: Add an owner-visible ephemeral-context mode spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. Before a task begins, the system creates a declared data boundary (which tabs, files, calendar range, and mail scope may be read); each surface emits signed provenance receipts; when the task ends or the owner says “forget this,” relay copies, browser extraction buffers, and Mac temporary artifacts are cryptographically shredded or expired, while retaining only a redacted outcome and an auditable deletion receipt.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could safely ask for help with a sensitive logged-in page or document and know exactly what was consulted, what left the Mac, and what was erased afterward. Today privacy depends on scattered redaction and retention behavior that the wearer cannot inspect or control from the pendant.
changes.effort: High: define a cross-surface data-boundary manifest, add provenance/deletion receipts to browser and Mac jobs, implement relay-side encrypted ephemeral storage with expiry, and expose a simple pendant review/forget interaction.
changes.risk: Deletion cannot retract data already copied by an external website or a model provider, and a crash could leave a temporary local artifact. Mitigate by defaulting to local extraction, minimizing outbound payloads, encrypting per-task keys, short TTLs, crash-startup garbage collection, and clearly reporting deletion limits.
changes.cost_impact: Small storage and key-management overhead; lower model cost when local extraction avoids sending full pages. No recurring inference cost outside the task.
changes.latency_impact: A few hundred milliseconds to establish the manifest and finalize deletion; no meaningful impact to ordinary read-only tasks.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves least-privilege and auditability, but requires careful key isolation and authenticated pairing. Raw sensitive content must never be logged in receipts or relay telemetry.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface task identity shared by relay, Mac, and browser
Browser extraction and Mac read actions must return provenance without raw content in logs
Relay durable storage needs per-task TTL and deletion receipts
Pendant needs a local confirmation/review affordance for scope and forget

changes.change: Replace the prototype 15,625-Hz I2S microphone path with a production audio front end that captures 24 kHz (preferably 32 kHz I2S/PDM with hardware decimation), and ship a coordinated 24-kHz Opus profile end to end: pendant capture/encode, relay transcode and congestion control, and ESP32 playback. Add a tiny local jitter/packet-loss telemetry record (sequence gaps, encode/decode time, queue depth) that the pendant sends as compact events; have the Mac planner collect those receipts during calls and write a dated diagnostic bundle in ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace. Keep a negotiated fallback to the current 16-kHz uplink/24-kHz downlink profile when LTE-M budget is insufficient.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely wideband speech instead of a 24-kHz playback path fed by narrowband capture, while the system automatically falls back rather than dropping speech. When quality is poor, the Mac can explain whether the cause was radio contention, codec CPU, or playback buffering instead of making the owner guess.
changes.effort: High: select and validate a 24/32-kHz low-power microphone and clocking; firmware DMA/Opus profile and RAM/CPU measurements; relay negotiation and bitrate/QoS changes; Mac receipt collector and regression fixtures across radio contention and reconnects.
changes.risk: A higher-rate uplink can worsen the already measured half-duplex LTE-M contention (388 uplink packets lost during simultaneous speech), and the current nRF9160 CPU is already ~87% utilized when encode and decode run together. Recover with negotiated fallback, bounded queues, and watchdog-triggered profile downgrade; never make the new mode mandatory until packet-loss and latency thresholds pass.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype API cost is negligible; relay compute/storage rises modestly with larger audio packets and telemetry. Hardware estimate: roughly $3–$10 incremental microphone/clock/analog-front-end BOM, with a small continuous power increase (validate against the final battery target).
changes.latency_impact: Potentially +10–30 ms from larger frames/queues under contention; target <150 ms mouth-to-ear in wideband mode and immediate downgrade when queue age or loss exceeds threshold.
changes.security_impact: Diagnostic bundles must contain timing and counters only, not PCM/audio or transcript; store locally with the existing workspace permissions and honor the existing audio retention/deletion policy.
depends_on: A firmware/relay negotiated audio-profile protocol (24-kHz wideband versus current fallback)
A real packet-loss/queue telemetry event schema on POST /pipeline/events
A Mac read-only diagnostic collector or receipt endpoint; current mac_readonly_inspect cannot read call telemetry
Owner hardware acceptance target for speech quality, battery life, and maximum tolerable latency

changes.change: Add a non-blocking action-schema compatibility layer at the POST /plan and POST /execute boundary. Normalize aliases (open_app.appName→app, run_shell.command nested or top-level, run_applescript.script nested or top-level, browser_navigate.url) into one canonical internal action shape; preserve the original payload, emit a schemaVersion, and return a typed preflight diagnostic for unknown/missing fields. Record normalization and executor result in the existing receipt/journal without introducing approval gates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently experiences silent-looking failures and may retry the same request: live jobs show run_shell, AppleScript, app launch, and browser navigation actions failing because planner and executor disagree about field names. This makes ordinary requests complete reliably instead of leaving half-finished desktop work or duplicate retries.
changes.effort: Small-to-medium: shared validator/normalizer, adapters for existing action types, contract tests against /plan→/execute and browser bridge, plus dashboard display of the canonical action and diagnostic.
changes.risk: An overly permissive alias could reinterpret malformed input. Mitigate by requiring exactly one canonical value after normalization, marking ambiguous payloads as invalid (diagnostic only), and retaining the original action for debugging. Recovery is straightforward: receipts preserve both forms and the adapter can be disabled by schema version.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful model cost; a few milliseconds and small journal overhead per action. Prevented retries likely reduce API and Mac-agent spend.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 ms validation/normalization before execution; no extra model round trip.
changes.security_impact: No access expansion and no gates. Preserve existing bearer/session authorization; never log secrets from command text or page content, only field presence and action type.
depends_on: A single canonical action-type schema shared by planner, browser bridge, and executor
Receipt/journal storage already present in actionReceipt
Contract tests or a replay fixture for the 24 observed failures and repeated browser-navigation failures

changes.change: Introduce a signed capability/schema handshake between the relay planner, Mac executor, and browser bridge at session start and whenever an executor reconnects. Each surface publishes its supported action types, required fields, aliases, result envelopes, and schema version; the planner compiles actions against that negotiated contract rather than assuming a hard-coded shape.
