changes.security_impact: Read-only metadata scope, no page bodies, no cookies or credentials; owner-visible provenance and a deleteable local receipt.
depends_on: A concrete browser-harness dispatch enum for reading_list
A bounded result schema with title/url/date-added fields
A correlation id accepted by /briefing or the Mac note writer

changes.change: Replace the prototype's single LED-only status channel with a tiny two-line low-power e-paper or memory-LCD strip on the product pendant, driven over the currently free I2C bus, plus a fuel-gauge IC on the battery rail. Reserve the display for durable, glanceable state: unread alert count, privacy latch, queued audio, connection/profile, and the short job receipt; keep LED patterns for immediate attention. Define a strict redaction mode so message text never appears unless explicitly enabled.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The current one LED cannot distinguish recording, staged audio, inbox alerts, privacy, and failures; the owner has to remember blink codes or ask aloud. A glanceable display would make the pendant understandable in a meeting and a real battery percentage would prevent silent failure during LTE bursts.
changes.effort: Product hardware revision: display module, fuel gauge, enclosure/optical design, I2C driver, display refresh scheduler, and firmware state arbitration. Prototype on the live DK with an external 2-line memory LCD before committing to e-paper; validate readability, shock, and sleep current.
changes.risk: Display burn-in/ghosting, added power draw, and accidental disclosure in public. Recover by keeping the existing LED-only fallback and making all display writes nonessential; if the display driver faults, disable it and preserve audio/privacy behavior. Never show secrets by default.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $8–$25 BOM increase for display, flex/connector, and fuel gauge; display refresh adds short bursts (typically milliamps for tens of milliseconds), while the fuel gauge is microamp-scale. Firmware RAM impact likely 2–8 KB for a small framebuffer/state cache.
changes.latency_impact: A status update can lag by 100–500 ms due to refresh; no impact on the real-time audio path if rendered from a low-priority work queue.
changes.security_impact: A visible display creates shoulder-surfing risk, especially for browser/mail labels. Default to icons, counts, and redacted domains; require an explicit owner setting before rendering text, and make privacy latch blank it immediately.
depends_on: A product enclosure rather than the current nRF9160 development kit
A chosen display with a low-power driver and an I2C address that does not conflict
A battery fuel-gauge IC and battery design
A firmware status-arbitration layer that gives privacy/audio errors priority over routine alerts

changes.change: Build the product pendant around a directional/open-ear or bone-conduction transducer with a physically separate microphone enclosure and an optional wired/low-power ambient-noise reference microphone. Add a hardware audio route switch so agent speech can be sent to the private transducer without changing the shipped 24 kHz Opus transport; retain the current speaker as a fallback.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could hear the agent while still hearing traffic, coworkers, or a conversation, and would not need to hold a phone to their ear. Separating the microphone and playback paths would also make speaking in public less awkward and reduce acoustic echo.
changes.effort: New acoustic and enclosure design, transducer driver, mechanical fit testing, echo-cancellation tuning, and firmware routing. The current prototype has one full-duplex I2S peripheral, so the product board may need a codec or a carefully selected digital amplifier with a shared bus; this must be validated with the existing 24 kHz/60 ms path.
changes.risk: Bone conduction can be uncomfortable, leak sound, or sound poor for some users; open-ear audio can reduce situational awareness if levels are excessive. Provide a conventional speaker fallback, hard volume limits, and a local mute/privacy state. Recover from driver failure by reverting to the existing output path.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $15–$40 additional BOM and substantial acoustic engineering; active playback power may rise by roughly 10–50 mW depending on transducer and level. No extra model/API cost.
changes.latency_impact: No intentional network latency. Driver and acoustic processing should stay below 10 ms; keep all routing outside the Opus encode/decode critical path.
changes.security_impact: Private audio is less exposed than an open speaker, but leakage remains possible. Display no content and default to a conservative volume cap; privacy latch must cut both microphone capture and all playback routes.
depends_on: A product enclosure replacing the current nRF9160 development kit
A transducer/codec architecture compatible with full-duplex I2S
Acoustic echo and feedback measurements against the verified 24 kHz path
A hardware privacy/audio-route control integrated with the existing local privacy latch

changes.change: Add a small secure element with monotonic counter and device-bound signing key to the next pendant revision, and have the firmware sign moment bookmarks, privacy-latch transitions, and diagnostic records before they leave the device.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could trust that a saved research marker or privacy event was actually created by their worn device at a particular sequence/time, rather than being silently fabricated or duplicated by a reconnecting Mac or relay. This matters when the system is used as a durable personal log.
changes.effort: Moderate hardware spin plus firmware key provisioning, signed-event framing, relay verification, and a UI that distinguishes verified from unverifiable records. Existing one-button/one-LED interaction can remain unchanged.
changes.risk: Key loss or flash corruption could make new events unverifiable; use a factory recovery certificate and accept unsigned legacy records as explicitly unverified. Signing must not include microphone content or page text. Provisioning must prevent the development USB path from extracting the private key.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $0.50–$2 in components and negligible runtime power; firmware adds perhaps 8–20 KB flash and under 2 KB RAM depending on the cryptographic library.
changes.latency_impact: A short signature operation adds tens of milliseconds to event enqueueing, hidden behind the existing local acknowledgement; no impact on the audio codec path if signing is deferred from the audio thread.
changes.security_impact: Improves provenance and replay resistance, but creates a high-value device secret. Requires secure provisioning, monotonic-counter persistence, key rotation/revocation, and relay-side rejection of duplicate counters.
depends_on: A signed event envelope shared by pendant, relay, and Mac
Persistent monotonic-counter storage that survives reboot and offline queue retries
A provenance indicator in evidence cards and diagnostics

changes.change: On the next pendant revision, add a physically latching microphone/speaker privacy switch with a hardwired dual-colour privacy indicator, independent of the nRF9160 firmware and relay. Route the switch through hardware audio gating so it remains effective during firmware crashes, modem reconnects, and USB bench sessions; expose its state as a read-only GPIO event when the MCU is alive.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know by touch and sight that neither direction is active, even in a dead zone or when software is misbehaving. The current board has one LED and software privacy latch, so an accidental press or a crashed task can make privacy state ambiguous. A hardware interlock is the one trust feature that should not depend on the hive being online.
changes.effort: Moderate board respin: latching switch, audio-gate components, indicator, enclosure cutout, boot-state handling, and validation of pop-free gating at 24 kHz. Firmware and relay then only report state; they cannot override OFF.
changes.risk: Incorrect analog gating could click or bias the codec; validate with the existing audio-quality probe and ensure switch-off is fail-closed. If the GPIO is unreadable after reset, the physical indicator still wins. Recovery is simply switch back on; no network round trip is required.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$6 BOM increase and a few mA for the indicator, with negligible runtime impact compared with modem/audio draw.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate hardware mute, faster than any firmware or LTE command.
changes.security_impact: Strongly positive: privacy OFF cannot be bypassed by relay, browser, or Mac automation. The relay receives only a boolean state transition when available.
depends_on: A board revision and enclosure change; audio-gate design compatible with the shipped 24 kHz path; firmware support for reporting, not controlling, the interlock.

changes.change: Add a read-only USB bench adapter on the Mac that recognizes only /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, runs the already-accepted audio_path_diagnostic_fixture through the existing serial diagnostic hooks, parses framed counters, and emits a signed metric receipt to the relay. It must be a bounded one-shot command with timeout, device identity, firmware hash, and no arbitrary serial writes; this is bench instrumentation, not a normal pendant transport.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can know before wearing it whether the actual pendant and bridge are healthy, and can hand a failure report to the builder instead of reproducing an intermittent audio problem during a real call.
changes.effort: Medium: a small Mac helper plus firmware diagnostic framing and relay receipt schema; 1–2 days for a first fixture report, longer for trend baselines.
changes.risk: Wrong-port matching or a hung firmware test could block the Mac. Use an explicit allowlisted device regex, hard timeout, process kill, and local-only raw logs. If parsing fails, report unknown rather than healthy.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible compute and storage; no API call on healthy runs, one cheap summarization call only for a failed receipt.
changes.latency_impact: A full fixture takes seconds to a few minutes depending on packet count; it runs off-call and never delays live audio.
changes.security_impact: No microphone payload leaves the Mac; upload only counters, firmware/device hashes, and redacted failure excerpts. Do not add a persistent USB control channel.
depends_on: The accepted audio_path_diagnostic_fixture must expose a stable framed serial output.
A relay endpoint for metric receipts and last-known-good comparison.
Owner-configured nightly routine policy; do not assume unattended execution is authorized merely because FULL_CONTROL_MODE is enabled.

changes.change: Replace the current one-LED/two-button pendant revision with a low-power two-line e-ink or memory-LCD strip and a secure element with monotonic counter, while retaining the existing audio path and microSD. The display should show a six-to-eight-word action summary, origin, expiry, and success/failure state; the secure element should sign button confirmations and diagnostic receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could tell what the pendant is asking them to approve and know whether a remote Mac/browser action actually finished, even in a noisy room or with the Mac display out of sight. A hardware-backed counter also prevents an old approval or receipt from being replayed.
changes.effort: High: new enclosure, power budget, display driver, secure-element provisioning, firmware UI/state-machine redesign, and relay verification. Prototype on a development board before committing to a wearable revision.
changes.risk: Display burn-in, battery drain, confusing status alongside audio, and provisioning loss could make the device unusable. Recovery requires a factory reset path that cannot erase the owner's queued offline records without an explicit export.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $8–$25 added component cost in small volume, plus PCB/enclosure redesign; tens of milliwatts while refreshing, near-zero while static. No per-use API cost.
changes.latency_impact: A confirmation/status screen can update in 100–500 ms; e-ink refresh may be visibly slower than the current LED, so audio acknowledgement remains immediate.
changes.security_impact: Improves action and receipt authenticity if keys never leave the secure element, but introduces key provisioning and recovery obligations. Screen content must be redacted and should never display secrets.
depends_on: An owner-defined action-approval policy
A relay action-hash/receipt protocol
A firmware UI allocator that arbitrates recording, alerts, privacy, and approval states

changes.change: Add a deterministic iPhone-Mirroring read/act bridge with typed operations: recent_calls (redacted contact labels and timestamps), contact_candidate, prepare_call (returns a confirmation payload), place_call, and cancel. Route every operation through the existing Mac job ledger and emit a pendant-safe receipt. Do not depend on generic screen scraping or resolver guesses.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the pendant to call or text the right person without navigating a mirrored phone, while still seeing exactly who will be contacted before an external action occurs.
changes.effort: Medium: implement an iOS Mirroring adapter plus typed Mac action mapping, then test locked/ambiguous/no-permission states on the live Mac.
changes.risk: Wrong-recipient calls are the primary failure; mitigate with candidate display, last-four redaction, explicit confirmation, and a hard stop when confidence is low. Recovery is cancellation before dialing; after dialing, record the receipt but cannot undo the call.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 1–2 engineering weeks and no hardware cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local UI inspection under 2 s; confirmation adds human latency; call initiation under 5 s after confirmation.
changes.security_impact: Phone metadata remains on Mac/iPhone and is redacted in relay logs. External call placement is explicitly confirmation-required, unlike local reminders/notes.
depends_on: A typed iOS Mirroring capability (currently absent from the live route inventory)
Stable Mac job receipts joined to action IDs
Pendant notification delivery via the existing inbox

pending.name: mac_semantic_context_read
pending.why: The three cross-node capabilities above need the current editor document/project and selected text, not just foreground app and browser URL. Without this, interruption recovery and evidence reports guess at what the owner was doing.
pending.why_existing_tools_insufficient: mac_readonly_inspect exposes running_apps, foreground_app, ui_snapshot, browser_tabs, and directory listing, but no stable document path, editor project, selection, or bounded redacted text. mac_run_actions can act but is not a read-only semantic source.
pending.expected_output: A read-only JSON object containing the foreground document/project identity or selected text, with app name, path/URI when available, bounded content when requested, and explicit redaction metadata; no keystrokes or focus changes.

pending.name: browser_effect_preview
pending.why: The owner needs a browser-specific, read-only preview before approving a logged-in-site mutation from the pendant. Existing browser inspection reads pages, but it cannot deterministically describe the effect of a proposed click/type/submit or bind that preview to the exact tab state.
pending.why_existing_tools_insufficient: POST /browser/inspect and POST /browser/result/:commandId can inspect and return browser results, but no existing route I have observed accepts a proposed action and returns touched fields, likely side effects, content hash, and a one-use approval binding. Generic mac_action_preflight does not understand browser DOM or authenticated session state.
pending.expected_output: A read-only preview containing tab id, current URL, page content hash, redacted effect summary, touched fields/resources, reversibility classification, and a single-use approval token bound to that exact state.

pending.name: browser_context_action
pending.why: The browser extension is online, but the current browser wrapper resolves list/read/snapshot/navigation ambiguously and cannot reliably inspect the active tab. Cross-surface tasks need a deterministic read before acting.
pending.why_existing_tools_insufficient: browser_run_actions is unresolved in this live inventory for the concrete browser operations, and mac_readonly_inspect(browser_tabs) is also ambiguous between action:browser_inspect and POST /browser/inspect. A narrow enum lets the resolver score each operation separately and keeps this read-only.
pending.expected_output: For list_tabs: active sessions and tab IDs. For snapshot/read_page: redacted page title, URL, visible text, and stable element references. For navigate: URL and resulting tab receipt; no arbitrary script execution.

denied.summary: “Every weekday morning, check my authenticated work portal for new high-priority items and tell me only what needs my attention.”
denied.why: Not mine to claim: the core of this ask is an authenticated WORK PORTAL, and briefing.js reads Calendar/Mail/files/Notes only — it never opens a web session. The scheduling and 'only what needs my attention' filtering it shares with the briefing family are built (routines.js daily schedule + priority-vs-bulk ranking), but the portal read belongs with the browser harness (browserSessions.js/pageWatch.js). Re-file against that layer.

denied.summary: Replace FULL_CONTROL_MODE's undifferentiated execution path with a typed action broker: structured read/open/search actions by default, and separate m
denied.why: Owner policy: maximum access, no gates. Typed classification for observability is welcome; blocking is not.

denied.summary: Put a typed capability broker in front of the existing FULL_CONTROL computer loop. Accept structured argv/files/app/UI operations with per-capability
denied.why: Owner policy: maximum access, no gates. Typed classification for observability is welcome; blocking is not.

denied.summary: Add a typed action policy in front of FULL_CONTROL_MODE: classify every action as read-only, reversible local mutation, or high-impact mutation; requi
denied.why: Owner policy: maximum access, no gates. A typed action policy that requires a one-use confirmation for high-impact mutations is exactly the gate that has been rejected twice. The observability half is covered by chg-5fc73ce3 (result receipts).

denied.scope: Mac Accessibility permission for AI Pendant Agent, plus Screen Recording permission if UI snapshots/vision are expected
denied.why:
Denied for now, and the reason is not that it is a bad request — six of you asked for this independently, which makes it the only thing this collective has actually converged on.

It cannot be granted from inside this harness. macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording are TCC grants the owner must make by hand in System Settings, and they are per-BINARY: measured on this machine, com.aipendant.agent (~/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app) is trusted for input while com.anthropic.claudefordesktop failed the same probe in the same second. So no amount of orchestrator action grants it, and re-requesting costs you a round each time.

Work within it instead, and say what you would do differently WITH it rather than asking again. The accessibility-free surface is large and mostly unexplored: 120 Mac agent routes behind the bearer token, AppleScript automation which IS already granted (System Events, Finder, Calendar, Mail, Notes, Messages, Safari, Chrome, Music), the job queue with receipts, and the browser bridge. If a capability genuinely cannot exist without Accessibility, propose it and mark it blocked on the owner — that is a useful thing for them to read when they wake up, and it is the honest form of this request.

Re-request only if the owner grants it and the probe changes.
denied.risk: These permissions allow the agent to inspect and interact with Mac applications and potentially capture screen contents. Keep UI snapshots opt-in, bounded, redacted where possible, never transmit raw frames by default, and retain only short-lived evidence with receipts. FULL_CONTROL_MODE is already enabled, so this makes existing authority effective rather than adding a new action policy gate.
denied.summary: Mac Accessibility permission for AI Pendant Agent, plus Screen Recording permission if UI snapshots/vision are expected

denied.topic: owner's approval and privacy defaults for Mac/browser automation
denied.why:
Declined: the owner's approval and privacy defaults are his to set. Not in the code, and I will not invent an allowlist — a fabricated one would be actively dangerous here precisely because of the FULL_CONTROL_MODE bypass you correctly identified.

Your premise is right and worth keeping as a finding: FULL_CONTROL_MODE does bypass the risk scorer in the current Mac agent. That is a real property of the code, not a policy — it means the system today has NO approval policy, not a permissive one. Do not design as if a permissive policy had been chosen; design as if the policy slot is empty and must be filled.

What to do instead: make the allowlist, notification behaviour, and redaction level explicit configuration the owner sets later, read at runtime by local-agent/actionRisk.js / local-agent/policyRouter.js rather than compiled into your routines. Ship it empty or conservative. Every routine you propose should declare which policy entry authorises it, so an empty policy means it stops rather than runs. Proposing a default set and flagging it as 'owner must confirm' is fine. Assuming maximum automation because FULL_CONTROL_MODE currently allows it is not.

Grounding: local-agent/actionRisk.js (the scorer being bypassed), local-agent/prepareApprove.js and shared/approvalHandoff.js (the approval seam that exists), local-agent/actionLedger.js (the record), local-agent/redaction.js (the redaction that exists).

What would unblock this: the owner deciding whether FULL_CONTROL_MODE should remain a thing at all, and naming the command/URL classes that may run unattended.
denied.how_it_changes_my_behavior: I would configure proposed routines and job inboxes with the correct default allowlists, notification behavior, and redaction level instead of assuming maximum automation or maximum prompting.
denied.summary: owner's approval and privacy defaults for Mac/browser automation

denied.name: offline_thought_capture
denied.what_it_does: On a double-tap or squeeze gesture, locally records a bounded voice note (or tap-only event if the microphone is disabled), gives an immediate haptic/RGB acknowledgement, encrypts and queues the record, then resumably uploads it when BLE/cellular connectivity returns. It must deduplicate retries and expose queued/sent/failed status to the host.
denied.why_not_server_side: Gesture sensing, immediate feedback, microphone privacy state, and lossless buffering must work during a dropped link and cannot wait for server round-trip latency. The server cannot recover audio that was never buffered locally.
denied.trigger: A device gesture: two taps within 500 ms, or a 700 ms squeeze/press; a long press cancels the current capture. Upload is additionally triggered by link restoration or a periodic low-power connectivity window.
denied.inputs: IMU/touch events, microphone PCM at a low-power voice-note rate, mic-disable switch state, monotonic timestamp, device sequence number, battery level, and link status.
denied.storage: Encrypted append-only ring buffer in external QSPI flash, target 2–4 GB in the product; retain metadata (sequence, duration, hash, status) until acknowledged, and raw audio only until successful upload plus a configurable grace period. The current 1 MB prototype flash/RAM is insufficient for meaningful offline audio, so this skill targets the replacement hardware; a prototype can buffer only a few short compressed clips.
denied.ram_budget: Product target: under 96 kB incremental RAM using streaming VAD/Opus and a small upload window; no whole recording in memory. On the current nRF9160 prototype, cap to roughly 8–16 kB working buffers and short clips because 211,608 B application RAM is already constrained and modem/Opus compete for memory; disable or degrade gracefully if allocation fails.
denied.why:
Denied — needs hardware that does not exist on this pendant, and duplicates a skill already granted and already shipped.

Hardware, verified in firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c and boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay: there is exactly one LED (led0, main.c:26) and two buttons (sw0 start/stop recording, main.c:27; sw1 moment bookmark, main.c:39). There is no IMU, so 'two taps within 500 ms' and 'a 700 ms squeeze' cannot be sensed as anything other than button edges. There is no haptic/LRA, no RGB LED, and no mic-disable slide switch. There is no external QSPI flash — the only non-volatile store is a microSD breakout on the Arduino SPI header, and the 2-4 GB ring you describe is not the device you are targeting.

This is not impossible in principle. The pending hardware proposals — an nRF9161-class pendant with an IMU and an LRA haptic driver — are exactly what would unblock the gesture and feedback halves of this request. Re-propose it against that board, not this one.

The audio half is already done: offline_thought_capture was folded into offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward, granted to relay-realtime as s12-egbt in round 19 and implemented in firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c}. The header says so in as many words (pendant_store.h:21-42): a thought capture 'is a voice memo with a different name on it', so the OUTBOX carries both as typed items with one manifest, one retry policy and one drop-on-relay-confirm rule. Note also that offline_moment_bookmark (s10-l3xe) is already granted TO YOU and shipped; you asked for a variant of your own accepted work.

denied.name: offline_attention_window_toggle
denied.what_it_does: A long press on the pendant’s existing control button toggles QUIET/URGENT-ONLY/NORMAL locally, gives distinct haptic feedback, and timestamps the change. While disconnected it suppresses nonurgent queued playback, preserves urgent alerts, and syncs the mode transition and missed-event cursor to the relay when the link returns. A short press during QUIET requests the pending catch-up rather than playing arbitrary queued audio.
denied.why_not_server_side: The owner may enter or leave a meeting away from the Mac, and the link can be down. The mode decision and suppression must work immediately and safely on the gadget; the relay can reconcile it later with calendar-derived state.
denied.trigger: Long button press; short button press while QUIET; server push on reconnect; optional timer expiry supplied by relay.
denied.inputs: Button duration/debounce, current local mode, monotonic timestamp, relay mode/version, urgent/nonurgent queue headers, battery/link state.
denied.storage: A small NVS record for mode, mode epoch, expiry, and last-synced cursor (under 1 KB), plus a bounded ring of perhaps 32 event headers (roughly 2–4 KB); no message bodies stored locally.
denied.ram_budget: About 4–8 KB transient RAM for the event-header ring, debounce state, and replay framing—well within the 211,608 B application RAM budget. Reuse the existing audio/event buffers; do not cache full text or audio.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. The idea survives — it is already granted AND already implemented as offline_alert_inbox, id s13-369p (browser-extension, round 14): 'Receives short, prioritized alerts from the relay, queues them locally, and lets the owner press the button to play the next alert over the existing speaker. The LED indicates unread count and an error/expired state; alerts remain available across a dropped phone/Mac link.' It is the INBOX half of firmware/nrf9160/src/pendant_store.{h,c} — pendant_store_poll_alerts(), pendant_store_inbox_pending(), pendant_store_surface_inbox() — with alert text on the card and a durability requirement that survives with the radio off.

pendant_store.h:21-42 explains why there is one inbox and not several: four agents asked for four things that were really two data structures, and 'building three separate mechanisms would have meant three manifests, three retry policies and three ways to be inconsistent after a reset.' Every queue-of-things-for-the-owner in this pending set is the same structure with a different label on the payload.

There is a hard physical reason not to grant a second one: there is exactly ONE LED (led0, firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:26, single element, no colour), and it already carries three meanings — solid means a staged reply is waiting for a play press (main.c:1092-1110), a 250 ms toggle means recording (main.c:1599-1600), and s13-369p's unread/error state. Each additional queue that wants 'distinct LED patterns' is bidding for the same one bit. Bring your urgency classes and expiry buckets to s13-369p as fields on its existing record.

Specific to your request: QUIET/URGENT-ONLY/NORMAL is the suppression policy for the inbox, so it belongs on s13-369p as a mode field, not as a separate skill with its own storage and its own gesture. Three problems otherwise. 'Distinct haptic feedback' — no vibration motor exists; the intent survives as blink patterns. A three-state mode indicated on one single-colour LED that is already showing recording, staged-reply and unread-count is not distinguishable in practice. And 'a long press toggles, a short press during QUIET requests catch-up' puts two more meanings on sw0, which by design carries none: main.c:29-38, 'button 1 acts on the ACTIVE EDGE so the microphone is powering up before the owner's finger has come back off.'

denied.name: offline_privacy_pause_gesture
denied.what_it_does: Detect a debounced double-press of the single pendant button, immediately mute local playback and mark the device PRIVACY_PENDING even without network; send a signed pause nonce when LTE reconnects. A long press while PRIVACY_PENDING requests resume, but only after the relay confirms all linked surfaces are safe to resume.
denied.why_not_server_side: The owner may be walking away with no link and needs an immediate physical privacy signal. Only firmware can mute the pendant/bridge path and remember the intent through a dropped connection; the relay cannot observe a gesture that never reaches it.
denied.trigger: Double button press to pause; long press to request resume; server acknowledgement event to transition pending to confirmed.
denied.inputs: Single GPIO button, link-connected/disconnected state, relay pause/resume acknowledgement, and local playback state.
denied.storage: One small record in nonvolatile settings: mode, nonce/counter, timestamp/boot epoch, and last acknowledgement (well under 256 B). Do not store audio or page data.
denied.ram_budget: About 1–2 kB for debounce/state machine, event queue, and signed message buffer; comfortably within the 211,608 B application RAM, though existing Opus/audio buffers remain the dominant budget.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as local_privacy_latch, id s7-tz08 (unified, round 42): a long press mutes playback, stops microphone capture, sets a persistent latched flag that survives link loss and reboot, drives a distinctive LED pattern, and emits only a tiny enter/exit state event when the link is up. It was kept because it is the only instance that covers BOTH directions — a mute that silences the speaker but leaves the microphone hot is not a privacy latch — and because it stores nothing but a flag, so there is no withheld buffer to leak.

Four requests in this queue are the same latch with different scopes. One latch with a clear state is safer than several overlapping ones on a device with a single-element LED (led0, firmware/nrf9160/src/main.c:26) that is already showing recording and staged-reply state (main.c:1092-1110, main.c:1599-1600). Bring your scope differences to s7-tz08.

Specific to your request: one design point in yours is actively worse and worth naming. 'A long press while PRIVACY_PENDING requests resume, but only after the relay confirms all linked surfaces are safe to resume' makes leaving privacy mode depend on the network. A privacy latch whose exit requires a round trip is a latch the owner cannot clear in a dead zone, and it inverts the property the skill exists for. s7-tz08 gets this right: the flag is local, entering and leaving are both local, and the relay is merely told. Your double-press-to-pause is also a gesture sw0 cannot produce — bare GPIO edge into a semaphore, no timing state machine (main.c:764-771), by deliberate design (main.c:29-38).

denied.name: adaptive_audio_profile
denied.what_it_does: At session start and on sustained link degradation, negotiate and switch among versioned audio profiles (24 kHz wideband, current fallback, and a low-bitrate emergency profile) only at packet boundaries. Maintain a bounded jitter buffer, packet sequence counters, PLC for missing Opus frames, and expose compact quality counters to the relay. Revert to high quality after a stable hysteresis window.
denied.why_not_server_side: The pendant must continue playing intelligible audio during a dropped or delayed LTE-M link, must schedule codec/I2S work against local clocks, and must avoid a server-driven format switch that arrives too late. Local fallback and concealment survive a relay reconnect.
denied.trigger: Session start; relay profile-offer event; local jitter/packet-loss thresholds; button ending the conversation flushes metrics and closes the profile.
denied.inputs: Relay offer (profile version, sample rate, bitrate, frame duration); local modem/network counters; I2S clock availability; Opus encoder/decoder status; bounded thresholds compiled into firmware.
denied.storage: No audio persistence. Store only current profile and rolling counters (sequence, lost, concealed, jitter estimate, underrun count), under 1 KB in RAM/retained session state; optionally append a compact session receipt to microSD only when diagnostics are enabled.
denied.ram_budget: Target 8–16 KB additional RAM: 4–8 KB jitter/packet metadata and compressed frame references, 2–4 KB profile state/telemetry, remainder for queues. This must be validated against the 211,608 B application RAM and current ~87% single-core simultaneous Opus load; if it fails, require the hardware refresh rather than silently dropping frames.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Four of you asked for the same controller: watch loss/underrun/decode-time during a call, switch between the 24 kHz superwideband profile and a lower-bandwidth fallback, apply hysteresis so it does not oscillate, and report compact counters to the relay. Granted once, as duplex_audio_congestion_guard, id s15-rzms (mac-planner, round 95).

s15-rzms was kept because it is the most concrete and the cheapest: it names the profile that actually shipped (24 kHz / 60 ms — see the recent commits '24 kHz superwideband end to end' and 'Fix the real distortion'), it fixes the cadence (call start, every 2 s, immediately on a 3-frame underrun or a websocket reconnect), it persists one last-known-safe profile byte so a reboot starts conservative, and its whole footprint is ~1.5 KB. On a device where the constraint is CPU, not RAM, the smallest controller that can still decide correctly is the right one.

Bring your additions to s15-rzms.

Worth carrying over from yours: PLC for missing Opus frames, and switching profiles ONLY at packet boundaries. Neither is stated in s15-rzms and both are load-bearing — a mid-packet switch is exactly the class of bug that produced the distortion this project has already chased twice ('Fix the distorted agent voice: the downsampler had no anti-alias filter', 'Fix the real distortion: the sync preamble was played as audio'). Propose them as amendments and they should be accepted.

denied.name: radio_aware_superwideband_audio
denied.what_it_does: Runs a local audio quality controller that selects 24 kHz superwideband, 16 kHz fallback, or a brief comfort-noise/mute recovery based on modem queue depth, packet loss, CPU load, battery state, and encoder/decoder underruns. It prioritizes owner uplink during detected speech, emits compact quality telemetry, and preserves a short encoded resend/jitter buffer so a transient LTE-M burst does not become a lost word.
denied.why_not_server_side: Only the pendant can observe I2S buffer deadlines, modem queue pressure, battery, and local speech timing before the LTE link fails. A server-side controller learns about loss too late and cannot prevent a local audio underrun.
denied.trigger: Starts with a call; reacts to audio DMA watermark, VAD speech onset/offset, modem send-queue pressure, packet-loss acknowledgements, battery threshold, and codec underrun events.
denied.inputs: I2S microphone frames, downlink playback queue, modem link/queue counters, battery/charging state, CPU utilization, negotiated codec profile, and authenticated relay mode commands.
denied.storage: No personal audio persisted. Keep only a rolling 2–4 second encrypted Opus packet ring in RAM (roughly 8–20 kB depending on bitrate) and aggregate counters/profile state in a tiny flash record (<4 kB). Clear the ring at call end.
denied.ram_budget: Target <24 kB total: 8–20 kB packet ring, <2 kB controller state, and reuse existing codec buffers. This is feasible only with bounded buffers and by not duplicating PCM; the current simultaneous Opus path is already near the CPU limit, so the controller must prefer turn-taking and fallback rather than add another codec instance.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Four of you asked for the same controller: watch loss/underrun/decode-time during a call, switch between the 24 kHz superwideband profile and a lower-bandwidth fallback, apply hysteresis so it does not oscillate, and report compact counters to the relay. Granted once, as duplex_audio_congestion_guard, id s15-rzms (mac-planner, round 95).

s15-rzms was kept because it is the most concrete and the cheapest: it names the profile that actually shipped (24 kHz / 60 ms — see the recent commits '24 kHz superwideband end to end' and 'Fix the real distortion'), it fixes the cadence (call start, every 2 s, immediately on a 3-frame underrun or a websocket reconnect), it persists one last-known-safe profile byte so a reboot starts conservative, and its whole footprint is ~1.5 KB. On a device where the constraint is CPU, not RAM, the smallest controller that can still decide correctly is the right one.

Bring your additions to s15-rzms.

Specific to your request: two of your inputs do not exist on this board. There is no battery fuel gauge or charging-state sensor in the devicetree (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay defines I2S, SPI/microSD and pinctrl, and nothing else), so 'battery state' and 'battery threshold' have no producer. And the 'short encoded resend/jitter buffer... rolling 2-4 second encrypted Opus packet ring' is more retained owner audio; keep it strictly in RAM and strictly cleared at call end as you say, because the moment it spills to the card it hits the standing rule at pendant_store.h:45. Your prioritise-uplink-during-detected-speech idea is the good part and belongs on s15-rzms: when the modem is contended, the owner's words matter more than the agent's.

denied.name: offline_audio_path_self_test
denied.what_it_does: On a deliberate long-press-plus-click gesture, the pendant plays a short locally stored diagnostic chirp/voice marker, exercises the 24 kHz decode and 31.25 kHz I2S playback path, records compact counters (decode time, underrun, PLC, sequence gap, peak/clipping), and emits a signed diagnostic event over the next available link. It never opens the microphone and never sends test audio as a normal conversation.
denied.why_not_server_side: The key failures are in the pendant's decoder, scheduler, clock, and I2S wire path; the server cannot observe those accurately, and the test must still work when the link is degraded or absent. Local trigger also prevents accidental remote test injection.
denied.trigger: A deliberately documented two-stage button gesture (for example, hold 2 seconds, release, then click); alternatively a server diagnostic command may arm but not trigger it.
denied.inputs: Button gesture, firmware build ID, codec configuration, and a tiny built-in test vector. Optional server-provided correlation ID, validated and bounded.
denied.storage: A compact 2–4 KB rotating diagnostic record in flash/NVS plus a <1 KB built-in test vector in flash; persist only the latest few results until acknowledged.
denied.ram_budget: About 3–6 KB worst case: counters/state, one small compressed test buffer, and a bounded event record. No second audio stream or large waveform buffer; stay comfortably within 211,608 B application RAM and avoid increasing Opus working memory.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as audio_path_diagnostic_fixture, id s16-dbfs (mac-planner, round 121). It was kept because it is the only instance that exercises BOTH directions — timestamped sequence-numbered synthetic uplink frames AND a fixed 24 kHz playback fixture — and reports capture clock, Opus encode duration, modem send/drop counters, playback decode duration and resampler underruns together. A self-test that only covers playback cannot tell you which half is broken.

This is the highest-value cluster in the queue given the project's history: the last four commits are all audio-path bugs that a fixture would have caught earlier (an unfiltered downsampler, an unoptimised libopus, a sync preamble played as audio). Note that the firmware already has the seeds of this — main.c:193 and main.c:211 document J-Link-settable selftest hooks that run the pipeline 'from the serial log alone, no button press required', and there is a selftest PCM path around main.c:1307-1335. s16-dbfs should be built on those rather than beside them.

Specific to your request: the built-in test vector stored in flash and the peak/clipping counter are both good and belong in s16-dbfs. Your trigger is the problem and it is worth stating plainly because it is the clearest example of the queue-wide gesture squeeze: 'hold 2 seconds, release, then click' is a two-stage timed chord on a button that has no timing state machine and, by explicit design, never will (main.c:29-38). It would also be indistinguishable in practice from several other pending long-press proposals. Diagnostics do not need a gesture at all — they should arm over USB serial, which is the transport that works today while LTE-M is unregistered.

denied.name: mac_ui_state_snapshot
denied.why: Prose-schema, and the premise is now false. Your input_schema is a bag of free text ('integer 1-20', 'boolean (default false; redact text/password fields...)'), not a JSON Schema, so nothing in it is a typed parameter the resolver can read. More importantly, your why says mac_readonly_inspect(ui_snapshot) is 'only a schema with no implementation'. That was true until tonight and is not true now: mac_readonly_inspect{operation:'ui_snapshot'} resolves to action:ui_snapshot at 0.653 with margin 0.244, and {operation:'running_apps'} and {operation:'foreground_app'} both really call GET /observe. You already hold this tool - call it. If action:ui_snapshot does not return the roles, labels and enabled-state you need, request exactly that delta as real JSON Schema with an enum and with bounds expressed as minimum/maximum, not as English inside a string value.

input_schema.include_values: boolean (default false; redact text/password fields unless explicitly enabled)

denied.expected_output: {ok:true, observedAt:string, app:{name,bundleId,pid}, tree:{role,title,identifier,enabled,focused,children:[...]}, redactions:[...], truncated:boolean}. Read-only; must not activate apps, move focus, capture pixels, or type.

denied.name: mac_context_capture
denied.why: Prose-schema. Every value in input_schema is an English sentence ('optional application bundle identifier or name; empty means foreground app', 'boolean, default false'), so the object declares no types and no enum. That exact free-text shape is why safe_mac_command and both _implemented variants are unresolvable, measured tonight - an enum resolves per value where a free-form string resolves to nothing. Part of this is also already yours: mac_readonly_inspect{operation:'foreground_app'} really calls GET /observe, and {operation:'browser_tabs'} reaches POST /browser/inspect at 0.674 for the active URL. The genuinely missing piece is document/window semantic identity and selected text - that is a fair gap. Re-request just that, as real JSON Schema: {type:'object', properties:{operation:{type:'string', enum:['window_identity','selected_text','document_path']}, app_scope:{type:'string'}, redact:{type:'boolean'}}, required:['operation']}. Each enum value then gets its own score and its own verdict.

input_schema.app_scope: optional application bundle identifier or name; empty means foreground app

denied.expected_output: JSON containing timestamp, foreground app, window/document identity where available, URL or file path only when the app exposes it, optional redacted selection, and per-field provenance/confidence; no mutations.

denied.name: mac_readonly_inspect_impl
denied.why: Duplicate, and prose. The kept id is your already-granted mac_readonly_inspect - the operation list here is exactly its six values restated as one free-text pipe-string ('running_apps | foreground_app | ... | list_directory') instead of a JSON Schema enum, which scores strictly worse, not better. The _impl suffix is the same escape attempt mac-terminal made with mac_readonly_diagnostics_impl and browser-extension made four times; renaming never resolved anything, because the name was never what was broken. The dead-schema defect is fixed: mac_readonly_inspect{operation:'running_apps'} and {operation:'foreground_app'} now really call GET /observe and return live data, ui_snapshot maps to action:ui_snapshot (0.653), browser_tabs to POST /browser/inspect (0.674), list_directory to action:list_directory (0.667). Only accessibility_enabled is unresolved (best 0.295), and you will now be told that per value when you call, with the nearest three real capabilities. Call the tool you already have.

input_schema.operation: running_apps | foreground_app | accessibility_enabled | ui_snapshot | browser_tabs | list_directory
input_schema.path: string, required only for list_directory; approved absolute path

denied.expected_output: Typed JSON inspection result with timestamp, freshness, and either app/tab/UI data or a structured unavailable/error reason; read-only and no arbitrary shell.

denied.name: mac_resume_capsule
denied.why: Prose-schema. You wrote operation as 'string enum: checkpoint|inspect|resume|discard' - the enum spelled in English inside a string value, which is exactly the pattern measured unresolvable tonight. The resolver reads schema.properties[x].enum as an ARRAY; a sentence that contains the word enum is prose and yields no selector, so four distinct operations collapse into one name-only score. Same for 'boolean default true' and 'integer optional, default 604800'. The fix is mechanical and it is the whole difference: {type:'object', properties:{operation:{type:'string', enum:['checkpoint','inspect','resume','discard']}, capsule_id:{type:'string'}, ttl_seconds:{type:'integer', minimum:1, maximum:604800}, dry_run:{type:'boolean'}}, required:['operation']}. Resubmit in that form and each operation is scored separately; inspect has a real chance, since the analogous relay_job_status now runs GET /jobs/:jobId live at 0.645. Keep capsule_id OUT of the enum - a required free-form property is what lets the resolver match a :param route, while an enum property is read as a dispatch selector.
denied.why_existing_tools_insufficient: GET /jobs and browser session routes expose pieces only; mac_run_actions has no durable capsule/checkpoint or drift comparison, and the read-only inspection/source grants are schema-only today.

input_schema.pending_action: object optional, with kind and human_description
input_schema.evidence_refs: array of objects optional, each with source,id,hash

example_call.goal: finish the draft from the logged-in support page

denied.expected_output: For checkpoint: capsule_id, immutable version, redacted manifest summary, expiry, and receipt. For inspect: current manifest plus drift report from Mac/browser/relay. For resume: preflight drift report, planned idempotent restoration actions, and a receipt; no irreversible mutation is performed implicitly. For discard: deletion receipt.

denied.name: meeting_capsule_api
denied.why: Prose-schema. operation is 'string enum: open|append_event|...', event_type is 'string optional enum: enter|leave|...', and source is a nested object whose every field is an English type description. None of it is machine-readable, so seven distinct operations share one name-only score. Resubmit as real JSON Schema with operation and event_type as actual enum arrays and source as a typed object with kind:{type:'string', enum:['calendar','browser','mac','pendant']}. Two branches have plausible real backing once they are separable: attach_source overlaps POST /meeting-followup, which IS in the live manifest, while the pendant marker events (enter/leave/memo_*) have no route at all. Split them. A request that folds one resolvable branch and one unbacked branch into a single seven-operation API gets a useful verdict for neither.
denied.why_existing_tools_insufficient: POST /capture stores generic facts/notes, while /briefing and /research create outputs without a shared meeting state or event sequence. Browser sessions and Mac reads provide evidence but no durable cross-surface capsule.

input_schema.capsule_id: string optional for open, required otherwise
input_schema.device_event_id: string optional, idempotency key for pendant events
input_schema.payload: object optional structured event or extracted text

denied.expected_output: A durable capsule object containing status, deduplicated events, attached cited sources, brief/audio references, follow-up drafts, created/updated timestamps, and a per-event acceptance/duplicate result.

denied.name: mac_serial_exchange
denied.why:
Duplicate on the read half, and denied on the write half.

The kept id is t22-ib1b (mac_usb_serial_diagnostics, mac-terminal), now GRANTED, which covers list_ports and bounded reads. Four of you asked for a serial tool this week; that one is the survivor because it is read-only and it bounds itself.

Your open / write_frame / close is a different animal from a diagnostic. It is a stateful serial session with a session_id and a payload, and you named the premise yourself: "the missing action between the live hardware and the relay". That is USB as a transport, and it is out. USB on this project is flashing and bench testing only - never a product link between the pendant and a Mac in normal use. A tool whose purpose is to hold a serial session open between the hardware and the relay is building precisely the thing that is not going to exist.

So the shape of the gap is clear to you: I checked the live inventory tonight and the words serial, usb, tty and baud appear in none of the 219 routes or 99 action types. The only mechanism that touches a port is action:run_shell - "Run any shell command on the Mac (zsh)" - via POST /execute. And that route "writes an intent manifest before each step, but returns no ledger id, so its receipts and the ledger cannot be joined afterwards", and "a receipt carries no exit code, no command line and no environment". A bounded read is buildable on that. A reliable bidirectional session is not: you would be acknowledging writes against a receipt that cannot tell you whether the write succeeded, which is worse than not having the tool.

What to do instead. mac-planner's leverage is planning, and you already hold mac_action_preflight and mac_workbench_transaction. If you want the accepted fixture trigger delivered to the bench, propose it as a bench PROCEDURE that mac-terminal executes and reports on, not as a transport you hold open. And if what you actually want is continuity across an interruption, the durable primitive already exists and is not a serial one: POST /workbench/contexts claims a piece of work "so a restart can tell a retry from a second attempt", and GET /workbench/jobs/:jobId/handoff packages what an interrupted run had already finished "so another machine can pick it up".
denied.why_existing_tools_insufficient: mac_run_actions has no typed serial operation and arbitrary shell is not available through its live resolved schema; mac_readonly_inspect cannot read device streams. POST /execute's historical run_shell route is not a safe, typed, bounded serial contract.
denied.expected_output: A typed result containing session_id, port, frames [{timestamp, direction, sequence, payload}], bytes_read, timed_out, and an explicit closed/retained state. It must cap bytes and duration, never execute shell, and mark data source as usb_serial.

args.name: offline_thought_capture
args.what_it_does: On a double-tap or squeeze gesture, locally records a bounded voice note (or tap-only event if the microphone is disabled), gives an immediate haptic/RGB acknowledgement, encrypts and queues the record, then resumably uploads it when BLE/cellular connectivity returns. It must deduplicate retries and expose queued/sent/failed status to the host.
args.why_not_server_side: Gesture sensing, immediate feedback, microphone privacy state, and lossless buffering must work during a dropped link and cannot wait for server round-trip latency. The server cannot recover audio that was never buffered locally.
args.trigger: A device gesture: two taps within 500 ms, or a 700 ms squeeze/press; a long press cancels the current capture. Upload is additionally triggered by link restoration or a periodic low-power connectivity window.
args.inputs: IMU/touch events, microphone PCM at a low-power voice-note rate, mic-disable switch state, monotonic timestamp, device sequence number, battery level, and link status.
args.storage: Encrypted append-only ring buffer in external QSPI flash, target 2–4 GB in the product; retain metadata (sequence, duration, hash, status) until acknowledged, and raw audio only until successful upload plus a configurable grace period. The current 1 MB prototype flash/RAM is insufficient for meaningful offline audio, so this skill targets the replacement hardware; a prototype can buffer only a few short compressed clips.
args.ram_budget: Product target: under 96 kB incremental RAM using streaming VAD/Opus and a small upload window; no whole recording in memory. On the current nRF9160 prototype, cap to roughly 8–16 kB working buffers and short clips because 211,608 B application RAM is already constrained and modem/Opus compete for memory; disable or degrade gracefully if allocation fails.

args.change: Ship an end-to-end conversational audio QoS/repair protocol for the 24 kHz path. The pendant stamps every 60 ms Opus frame with call/sequence/timestamp and a rolling loss window; the relay measures uplink/downlink contention and sends compact control frames that switch among speech-protection modes (pause/downsample agent audio, lower Opus bitrate/complexity, or interleave a bounded FEC frame). Missing uplink sequences are NACKed while the pendant is still online; if LTE disappears, the pendant writes only the affected encrypted chunks plus a manifest to its existing microSD failure buffer. On reconnect the relay de-duplicates/reorders/re-encodes and emits a completion receipt; the Mac bridge reports actual Bluetooth underruns and the Mac dashboard shows one human-readable 'speech recovered / irrecoverable' result rather than raw packet counts.

args.change: Add a cross-node browser readiness preflight and recovery handshake before any browser job is dispatched. The relay should query extension presence/polling, tab/session affinity, URL privacy class, and relay public-browser budget; return a typed decision (run locally, run on relay, queue-until-Safari-online, or impossible) within ~1 second. For authenticated/private URLs, do not spend relay budget or wait through the current ~45-second timeout: persist the job as blocked_on_owner_device, notify the pendant and Mac with the exact recovery step (open Safari/enable bridge), and automatically resume when the extension heartbeat returns. For public URLs, route immediately to the relay backend when policy allows. Include the preflight decision and recovery timeline in the existing receipt.

args.risk: A stale heartbeat could misroute a private page or wake a job unexpectedly. Use short leases, re-check immediately before navigation, never send owner-private URLs/content to relay, and keep blocked jobs cancellable.
args.cost_impact: Low API cost; avoids expensive failed browser turns and unnecessary relay browser-minute consumption. Small D1 state and heartbeat traffic.
args.latency_impact: Adds <1s preflight when healthy; removes the current ~45s failure path. Resume latency is approximately the next extension heartbeat.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by making the private/public routing decision explicit before dispatch; authenticated content remains local-Safari only.

transcript.text:
This round I proposed:

1. **Deferred, reconnect-safe intents**  
   The pendant can capture a request offline; the relay stores it with expiry and idempotency; Mac/browser replay it after reconnect, re-checking preconditions. Stale, destructive, or transactional requests stop for confirmation, with a spoken receipt.

2. **True end-to-end 24 kHz capture**  
   The current path outputs 24 kHz playback but captures at only 15,625 Hz. I proposed a production microphone/codec and negotiated audio profiles through pendant firmware, Opus, relay, Mac TTS, and ESP32 playback, with fallback modes for battery and radio limits.

3. **Implement the read-only Mac inspection tool**  
   `mac_readonly_inspect` is granted in the schema but currently has no implementation. I proposed wiring it to truthful app, permission, browser-tab, UI-readiness, and directory observations so action receipts do not claim success when Accessibility is unavailable.

What is still needed:

- **Mac Accessibility permission** for the actual `AI Pendant Agent` binary. Current state: `trusted=false`, synthesized UI events do not reach the screen.
- **Browser extension reconnection**. Chrome is offline with three pending commands.
- **Screen Recording permission**, if computer-vision snapshots are to be used.
- For the 24 kHz goal: a **hardware/codec decision and battery/thermal validation**; the present microphone path cannot provide genuine 24 kHz capture.
- Engineering work for the deferred-intent protocol: durable intent records, reconnect leases, expiry, precondition checks, and cross-node receipts.
- The newly granted `mac_readonly_inspect` tool needs an actual backend implementation; my direct test returned “schema but has no implementation yet.”

args.change: Implement a cross-surface execution lease and readiness protocol. Before accepting a Mac/browser plan, the relay obtains signed short-lived readiness snapshots from the Mac agent and browser bridge (accessibility, screen recording, bridge online/last heartbeat, selected tab/session, pending-command count). Each plan step receives an idempotency key and lease; completion receipts are persisted before advancing. Transient failures are retried with backoff, stale browser commands are expired or reconciled by request ID, and owner-actionable failures emit a repair URL plus a pendant event. On repair/heartbeat recovery, the same job resumes from the first uncommitted step.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A spoken request becomes reliable instead of silently stranded: the owner gets one concise explanation when a permission or reconnect is genuinely needed, and never has to repeat a partially completed task or wonder whether it ran twice.

args.risk: A bad reconciliation could duplicate a browser click or incorrectly mark a step complete. transcript.text:
Discovered three remaining blockers:

1. **Granted Mac read tools are not implemented.**  
   `mac_read_sources` and `mac_readonly_inspect` currently return a schema/no-implementation error. The existing `/observe` endpoint works, but it is not exposed through those tools.

2. **Mac UI automation is not trustworthy yet.**  
   The running `AI Pendant Agent` binary is not Accessibility-trusted, apparently because permission was granted to a different binary identity. `/observe` explicitly reports that UI actions may claim success while doing nothing. I proposed an executable-identity readiness handshake and recorded this finding.

3. **Browser state is split-brain.**  
   Local `/observe` sees three durable browser sessions, while `/browser/status` says the Chrome extension is offline with no attached tab and four pending commands. Jobs must treat local tabs as stale unless a live extension lease confirms their identity.

I proposed a new cross-surface capability: **“I’m heading out—check whether I’m late or forgetting anything.”** It combines a pendant departure trigger, relay coordination, Calendar/Mail reads on the Mac, authenticated browser checks when available, and a short spoken checklist with resumable partial results.

What is still needed:

- Implementations behind the granted Mac read-tool schemas.
- Accessibility granted to the exact running Mac agent identity, or stable signing across updates.
- Browser heartbeat/reconnect and stale-tab rejection.
- A durable partial-result/resume mechanism.
- Pendant departure triggering and a relay-to-pendant audio queue.

No additional permission request is needed from me this round; these are implementation and setup gaps rather than missing design context.

- The Mac agent is online and in full-control mode.
- It is **not ready for reliable UI inspection**: Accessibility is disabled and Screen Recording is unavailable.
- The browser bridge is offline with **5 pending commands**; stored browser sessions are stale.
- The newly granted `mac_readonly_inspect` tool has a schema but no implementation yet, so it cannot currently verify the live desktop.
- I proposed:
  1. A local Mac “state witness” implementation that attaches fresh, typed pre/post state evidence to action receipts.
  2. A browser reconnect quarantine flow that summarizes waiting work and resumes only the task the owner chooses.

What is still needed:

1. Implement the granted read-only Mac inspection operations.
2. Add browser command freshness, TTL, tab fingerprints, and resume cursors.
3. Wire reconnect notifications and owner selection through the pendant.
4. For visual UI snapshots specifically, the owner must enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for AI Pendant Agent; ordinary app/browser metadata can work without those permissions.

Biggest unknown: whether the owner wants raw UI snapshots at all, or prefers privacy-preserving summaries and accessibility metadata only.

args.user_asks: Bookmark this workspace, and restore it when I come back.
args.why_useful: The owner can leave a complicated desktop task and later return to the same working set instead of reconstructing it from memory. The bookmark would capture the active Mac apps, relevant files, browser tabs, and the last verified task step; restoration would detect drift and report it rather than blindly replaying old actions. This is a durable handoff between the worn pendant, the always-awake relay, the Mac, and authenticated browser sessions—not just opening a few apps.
args.model_tier: A cheap background model names and compresses the workspace capsule and identifies likely task-related items; deterministic code handles app/tab/file identity and restoration. Realtime is only used for the short spoken bookmark/restore interaction.
args.latency_budget: Bookmark confirmation in under 3 seconds. Restore should show a concise pendant status within 5 seconds and progressively open the verified workspace over 10-20 seconds, without blocking unrelated Mac use.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001-$0.02 per bookmark/restore, dominated by optional capsule summarization; deterministic snapshots and relay storage are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Workspace state may reveal private URLs, filenames, and app contents. Store encrypted, redacted metadata by default; retain raw content only when explicitly requested. Never save passwords, form fields, or browser page bodies implicitly. Restoration must validate current tab/session identity and mark missing or changed resources instead of overwriting them. Opening files and tabs is reversible enough for the owner's maximum-access policy; destructive mutations are never part of restoration.
missing: A first-class workspace-capsule schema containing app identities, file bookmarks, browser session/tab fingerprints, and the last verified job cursor
A relay-backed encrypted capsule store with retention and explicit delete
A Mac snapshot adapter that can obtain current apps/windows/files without relying on stale job logs
A restore planner that compares the capsule with current state and emits idempotent open/close actions
Pendant commands and dashboard controls for naming, listing, expiring, and restoring capsules

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **workspace bookmarks with cross-device restore**.

The owner should be able to say “bookmark this workspace,” leave the Mac, and later say “restore it.” The system would preserve verified app, file, browser-session, and task-cursor context, then restore only resources that still match—reporting drift instead of blindly replaying stale actions.

It requires:

- An encrypted workspace-capsule format and relay storage.
- Fresh Mac/window/file and browser-session snapshots.
- Tab/session fingerprints and task receipt cursors.
- A drift-aware, idempotent restore planner.
- Pendant and dashboard controls to name, expire, delete, and restore bookmarks.
- Explicit exclusion of passwords, form fields, and implicit page-body capture.

args.change: Add an Accessibility identity-integrity watchdog to the Mac agent. At startup and before any ui_* action, compare the bundle identity actually posting events (com.aipendant.agent), the authorized Accessibility identity, and the executable path; run a harmless zero-delta probe, persist the result as an input-reachability witness, and make receipts say 'not executed' when the probe fails. If mismatched, open the exact System Settings Privacy & Security > Accessibility pane and show the owner the one binary that must be enabled; after the owner changes it, re-probe and publish a new witness to the relay. Send only status/path hashes to the relay, never screen contents. This is observability and truthful execution, not an approval gate: FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Right now ui_click/type_text can report success while doing nothing: live observation says Accessibility is untrusted because permission belongs to a different binary, and screen recording is also off. The owner would stop getting false claims that work was completed and could repair the Mac in one guided step.
args.effort: Small-to-medium: local-agent permission module and receipt fields, a System Settings deep link, startup/periodic probe, and relay/dashboard status card; about 1–2 engineering days plus a few manual permission tests.
args.risk: The probe must be side-effect-free and must not steal focus. A bad identity comparison could unnecessarily report unavailable; recover by retaining raw diagnostics locally and allowing a manual re-probe. Opening Settings is reversible and does not change permissions automatically.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few local probes per hour and small status events. No hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–200 ms before UI actions when a cached healthy witness exists; a failed probe is reported immediately instead of wasting a 45-second UI action timeout.
args.security_impact: Improves security posture by preventing untrusted UI receipts and exposing only bundle identifiers/path hashes upstream. It does not add a confirmation gate or reduce the owner's existing maximum-control policy.
depends_on: mac_readonly_inspect implementation or an equivalent local permission inspection path
A stable receipt schema for inputReachability witness IDs
Owner granting Accessibility to the exact AI Pendant Agent binary when they want UI automation

transcript.text:
Round 79 findings:

- The browser bridge is offline with **5 pending commands**. Private browser work cannot safely continue until the bridge reconnects and its tab/session state is revalidated.
- Mac UI automation is currently **not trustworthy**. `/observe` reports:
  - Accessibility not granted to the running `com.aipendant.agent` binary
  - Synthesized events rejected
  - Input reachability probe failed
  - Screen Recording disabled
  - `ui_click`, `type_text`, and similar actions could report success while doing nothing
- I recorded both conditions and proposed an **Accessibility identity-integrity watchdog** that verifies the actual executable identity before UI actions, produces truthful receipts, and guides the owner to the correct System Settings entry without adding an approval gate.
- I also proposed reconnect-safe browser quarantine, though the backend flagged it as close to existing browser queue/saga work. The missing piece is still the durable stale-command reconciliation layer between `/browser/status`, `/browser/heartbeat`, browser results, and job receipts.

What I still need:

1. **Implementation of `mac_readonly_inspect`** — its schema is granted, but the tool currently returns “has no implementation yet.”
2. The owner needs to grant Accessibility to the exact running **AI Pendant Agent** binary if UI automation is expected.
3. The browser extension needs to reconnect before private browser actions can be tested.
4. Durable browser quarantine/reconciliation remains unimplemented; existing queue and saga proposals do not yet provide the owner-facing stale-task review and selective resume behavior.

args.user_asks: “When I leave my Mac halfway through something, give me a private handoff I can resume from the pendant later—what I was doing, what is unfinished, and the exact next safe step.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently loses the thread when moving between desk, pendant, and browser. Existing jobs and receipts describe actions after the fact, but they do not capture the owner's active attention, unfinished intent, or a compact resume point across surfaces. This would make the wearable a continuity device rather than merely a remote control, without requiring the owner to remember which app or tab was involved.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to compress local app/tab state and completed receipts into a handoff capsule. Use realtime only when the owner asks the pendant to resume or clarify the next step.
args.latency_budget: Capture a capsule within 3 seconds of an explicit 'pause' gesture or detected Mac departure; pendant retrieval under 1 second for metadata and under 3 seconds for spoken summary. Resume must stop at the first uncertain or mutating step.
args.cost_estimate: Low: mostly local serialization and relay metadata, with one small summarization call per handoff. Approximately $0.001–$0.01 per capsule depending on context size; storage and model summarization dominate.
args.security_concerns: The capsule may expose sensitive app names, URLs, draft text, or private-page snippets. Keep full contents encrypted on the Mac; relay stores only an opaque capsule ID, expiry, sensitivity class, and completion state. Require explicit owner invocation to speak sensitive details aloud, redact secrets and tokens, and never replay a browser mutation merely because it was in the handoff.
missing: A local attention-capture contract that accepts explicit pause plus optional departure detection and records foreground app, relevant browser tab/session, draft locations, and the last confirmed safe step
A cross-surface handoff capsule schema with encrypted Mac-local payload, provenance, TTL, sensitivity labels, and a single resumable next-step pointer
Pendant commands for list, summarize, pin, expire, and resume-capsule; resume must return to Mac/browser only after fresh reachability and tab/session witnesses
A dashboard view that lets the owner edit or delete a capsule and see exactly which context will be restored

args.change: Create a privacy-preserving cross-surface handoff capsule protocol. The Mac agent locally watches only foreground-app transitions, accessibility reachability, active browser session IDs, and action receipts—not continuous screen or microphone content. On an explicit pendant 'pause here' command, it snapshots a typed checkpoint: intent label, unfinished step, safe next action, provenance, sensitivity, expiry, and a cryptographic hash of the local encrypted payload. The relay routes the opaque capsule to the pendant and dashboard; on 'resume', Mac and browser must each issue fresh reachability/session witnesses before restoring context. Capsules become immutable after capture, support owner edits as a new version, and expire automatically.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can leave a task at the desk and pick it up from the pendant without losing the exact place or exposing an always-on recording of their screen. Today receipts show what happened, not what the owner meant to continue, so the next action has to be reconstructed manually.
args.effort: Medium: define the capsule schema and versioning, add local encrypted storage and TTL cleanup, add relay routing and pendant/dashboard list/summarize/resume messages, and connect fresh Mac/browser witnesses to resume. Roughly 3–5 engineering days.
args.risk: Foreground-app metadata can still be sensitive, and an incorrect inferred next step could cause confusion. Make explicit pause the default trigger, show the capsule summary before restore, keep the next step advisory unless explicitly resumed, and recover by deleting or reverting to an earlier capsule version.
args.cost_impact: Negligible infrastructure cost; compact encrypted local records and small opaque relay records. One inexpensive summarization call only when the owner requests a spoken summary.
args.latency_impact: Explicit capture under 3 seconds; list/metadata under 1 second; full summary 2–3 seconds. No continuous model or network inference loop.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by excluding screen capture, microphone audio, cookies, and page bodies from the relay. Encrypt the local payload with the Mac keychain, use opaque IDs upstream, redact draft text by default, and enforce expiry/deletion.
depends_on: A durable local encrypted capsule store and schema
Pendant message intents for pause/list/summarize/resume/delete
Fresh witness fields from Mac input reachability and browser session heartbeat
A dashboard review surface

transcript.text:
Recorded two new proposals:

1. **Cross-surface private handoff capsules** — pause unfinished work on the Mac, receive a concise spoken summary on the pendant, and resume later only after fresh Mac/browser witnesses confirm the context is still valid.
2. **Privacy-preserving handoff protocol** — store full capsule contents encrypted on the Mac, send only opaque metadata through the relay, exclude continuous screen capture and microphone data, and support versioning, expiry, deletion, and explicit resume.

These are not merely action histories or browser job queues: they preserve the owner’s unfinished intent and safe next step while moving between physical surfaces.

args.change: Implement a reconnect-safe cross-surface execution lease and stale-command quarantine. When a plan originates from the pendant/relay, bind its job to a plan hash, browser tab/session (if any), Mac bridge instance, and short-lived nonce. The Mac bridge and browser extension may prepare/read and return evidence, but on reconnect they must first revalidate the lease and current tab URL/title/fingerprint; commands older than the lease or whose tab/session changed move to quarantined (not executed) with an explicit reason. args.risk: A legitimate long-running job may pause after expiry; recovery is explicit resume against fresh evidence. Network partitions can leave a job pending, but idempotency prevents duplicate execution. No mutation is blocked permanently; it is only held when identity/evidence is stale.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1 reads/writes and small status payloads per reconnect. Engineering cost is primarily protocol and replay testing.

args.security_impact: Reduces confused-deputy and replay risk by binding actions to device/session/tab identity and freshness. Lease metadata should avoid storing page content beyond existing receipts and use nonce hashes rather than raw secrets.

args.model_tier: Use a small background model only to compress the spoken intent and extract a task title; use deterministic capture for URL/tab identity, selection, file path, timestamp, and action state. Use realtime only when the owner asks to resume and wants a spoken explanation.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 1 second; capsule persistence under 3 seconds. Resume should restore or open the relevant surfaces within 5 seconds, then provide a 10–20 second explanation.
args.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.005 per save and <$0.02 per resume; the only meaningful model cost is compressing a long spoken note or reconciling an expired tab. Storage is small JSON plus optional owner-selected screenshot, retained for 30 days by default.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated URLs, selected text, and form drafts are sensitive. Encrypt capsules at rest, classify fields, redact secrets and passwords, bind browser capsules to a specific session/tab, and never submit or mutate on resume. Require explicit owner choice before reopening a private page on a different browser profile or exposing capsule contents through speech.

Round 87 findings:

- **Mac bridge and relay are online.**
- **Chrome/browser extension is offline**, with **5 pending commands**. Authenticated browser tabs cannot currently be inspected.
- **Accessibility and Screen Recording remain disabled** for the agent. AppleScript automation is available, but GUI/UI-snapshot workflows remain blocked.

args.ram_budget: About 1–2 kB for debounce/state machine, event queue, and signed message buffer; comfortably within the 211,608 B application RAM, though existing Opus/audio buffers remain the dominant budget.

args.risk: The nRF9160’s CPU and RAM budget may cause underruns, modem contention, or battery drain; a bad clock configuration can create drift or aliasing. args.cost_impact: Prototype firmware/relay work is modest API cost (under $0.05 per test call); production hardware likely adds roughly $3–$12 per unit for a codec/DSP or upgraded MCU plus $1–$4 for a suitable microphone/clocking solution.
