args.latency_impact: A 24 kHz Opus path can retain 40–60 ms frames; expect no material conversational latency increase if offloaded. On the current MCU, software-only operation risks 20–50 ms additional buffering and underruns, so it should not ship without measured headroom.
args.security_impact: No new content leaves the device beyond the existing encrypted audio stream, but audio diagnostics must report only rates, packet loss, and CPU occupancy—not raw audio. Capability negotiation should be authenticated so a peer cannot force an unsupported mode or exhaust battery.

args.why_useful_to_owner: After walking away, losing LTE, or saying “not now,” the owner can return to the exact unfinished work instead of explaining it again or risking duplicate actions. They see what is stale and what will reopen before anything is sent or submitted.

args.user_asks: “Stop everything and protect my data.” (A physical pendant gesture, even if the Mac screen is locked.)
args.why_useful: Today there is no single owner-controlled emergency stop spanning the wearable, relay, Mac executor, and authenticated browser. args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for the stop path: firmware and relay perform deterministic cancellation and revocation. Use a cheaper background model only afterward to summarize what was stopped and what could not be stopped; realtime may speak the short confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Pendant-to-relay stop acknowledgement under 1 second when connected; queued commands must be rejected immediately on reconnect. Mac/browser revocation and cancellation receipts should arrive within 5 seconds, with honest per-job status if an external mutation already completed.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for the emergency path; a short post-incident summary is typically under $0.01. Main engineering cost is reliable distributed cancellation, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The gesture must be hard to trigger accidentally but work without an open microphone. Use a deliberate long-press plus button/LED confirmation, TLS-authenticated device nonce, replay protection, and a local audible/vibration confirmation. The stop operation should cancel pending work, revoke browser command leases, terminate active Mac jobs where possible, pause new execution, and mark already-completed external actions as completed rather than falsely claiming rollback. It must not pretend that sent email, submitted forms, or other irreversible effects were undone.

args.change: Introduce a signed, short-lived global execution lease with an epoch counter. Every Mac and browser action must carry the current epoch and check it before each step; a pendant emergency gesture increments the epoch, cancels queued jobs, invalidates browser command leases, and causes workers to stop at the next safe boundary. Persist a per-action terminal receipt (prevented, interrupted, completed, or unknown) and require an explicit re-enable operation to issue a new epoch.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a real emergency brake across all automation surfaces, including work already handed off to a background worker. They can stop the system from the pendant and later know exactly what did and did not happen, instead of guessing whether a command is still running.
args.effort: High distributed-systems work: relay lease authority, worker checks, pendant envelope/reconnect handling, cancellation adapters, race-condition tests, and dashboard incident history.
args.risk: A network partition may prevent immediate cancellation on an offline Mac, and stopping mid-step may leave a partial local mutation. Use bounded check intervals, local deny-new-work state, idempotency keys, explicit unknown outcomes, and never claim rollback of an external action. Recovery is a new epoch plus deliberate re-enable.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful model cost; small durable relay state and one tiny control message per job step. No hardware cost if the existing button/LED is used, though a production pendant should add haptic confirmation.
args.latency_impact: Adds a sub-100 ms local lease check per action and typically under 1 second over the live link; offline surfaces can only enforce stop when reachable.
args.security_impact: This becomes a high-value control channel: authenticate the pendant, bind it to the owner, rotate keys, reject replays, audit every epoch change, and keep the emergency gesture local/offline-capable.

transcript.text:
Proposed a new cross-surface capability: **“I’m switching tasks—make me a handoff packet.”**

It would:

- Capture bounded Calendar/Mail context through `mac_read_sources`
- Capture the current authenticated browser tab with provenance
- Include relevant Mac job/context state
- Redact secrets and label every observation with source, timestamp, hash, and TTL
- Save Markdown + JSON atomically under `~/AI-Pendant-Workspace/handoffs/`
- Queue a short spoken summary to the pendant
- Continue asynchronously if a source is slow or offline, clearly marking gaps

I also proposed the missing **Context Handoff Job protocol** connecting relay, browser, and Mac planner with durable IDs, retries, evidence manifests, redaction, and retention controls.

What I still need:

1. **Implementation of `mac_readonly_inspect`** — it is granted but currently returns “schema but has no implementation,” including for `browser_tabs` and `running_apps`.
2. A browser-bridge operation for bounded current-tab extraction with URL/tab provenance.
3. A durable relay job/audio-queue endpoint for asynchronous handoff completion.
4. An atomic local packet writer and retention/delete policy.

No additional owner permission is needed for this read-only workflow.

args.user_asks: “Are my plans still valid?”
args.why_useful: Today the owner must manually compare Calendar, recent Mail, and authenticated browser pages when reservations, meetings, deliveries, or appointments change. This capability would detect contradictions across those sources, explain exactly what disagrees, identify the most reliable/latest evidence, and prepare a reviewable correction plan without silently changing anything.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the short question and spoken result. A cheaper background model performs source comparison, date/entity normalization, contradiction classification, and evidence ranking.
args.latency_budget: Speak an acknowledgement within 1 second; return an answer within 10–20 seconds. If a browser source is unavailable, return a partial result with the missing source explicitly named.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.08 per investigation, dominated by reading and comparing authenticated page text and generating the evidence-backed explanation.
args.security_concerns: Read-only unless the owner separately asks to change a calendar event or draft a reply. Restrict browser reads to explicitly bound sessions/pages, redact credentials and secret-mode memory, keep evidence snippets minimal, and attach source URLs/timestamps. Any proposed correction must show before/after values and require the owner's existing confirmation policy before sending or mutating.
missing: A durable cross-source contradiction record keyed by normalized person/event/reservation and observation time
Common entity/date normalization and source-precedence rules shared by Calendar, Mail, and browser extraction
A browser extraction result containing bounded text, semantic fields, URL, tab identity, and observedAt timestamp

transcript.text:
Round 95 findings:

- The current pendant already decodes 24 kHz/60 ms playback, but simultaneous encode/decode consumes about 87% of one Cortex-M33 core.
- LTE-M duplex contention is the larger immediate problem: the measured path lost about 7.8 seconds of uplink while the assistant was speaking.
- The Mac bridge is online, but browser extension is offline with five pending commands. Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable; no new permission is needed for the audio work.

I proposed and queued:

1. **Pendant congestion guard** — local packet-loss, underrun, queue-depth, and decode-timing counters; conservative fallback profile with hysteresis. Queued device skill `s15-rzms`, estimated at ~1.5 KB RAM.
2. **Relay duplex budget governor** — reserve uplink capacity, reduce or pause nonessential downlink TTS under contention, restore 24 kHz only after 10 seconds of stability, and emit sequence-numbered QoS receipts.
3. **Next hardware revision** — add a dedicated audio companion/DSP or audio-capable SoC. The current nRF9160 prototype has too little CPU headroom for robust full-quality duplex operation.

What is still needed to ship this:

- A negotiated Opus profile contract between firmware and `cloud-relay/opusTranscode.js`.
- Relay-side scheduling and typed QoS events through `/pipeline/events`.
- A contention test harness reproducing the measured packet-loss case.
- Dashboard/receipt support showing when audio quality degraded, what sequence range was affected, and when it recovered.
- For a production wearable, hardware validation of a separate audio-processing path.

No further tool or permission request is necessary this round; the remaining gaps are implementation and hardware validation.

result.summary: “When I ask you to do something that takes time, keep working after I leave and tell me exactly what happened when it’s done.”

args.user_asks: “Do this when I’m free”: stage the browser/Mac work now, wait for a real interruption-safe gap, then carry it out and tell me on the pendant exactly what happened; let me cancel it with one button press.
args.why_useful: Long tasks would stop competing with meetings and active work. The pendant supplies the owner’s intent and cancellation; relay keeps the request alive; Calendar/Mail and Mac foreground state identify a safe gap; the browser bridge performs logged-in steps; receipts return to the pendant. This is more useful than either an immediate automation or a generic overnight job.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap background planner to decompose and poll the queued task; use realtime only for the initial voice exchange, spoken status, and cancellation. Use a stronger planner only when the browser task is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge and stage within 2 seconds. Gap evaluation every 2–5 minutes (or on Calendar/foreground events); start within 30 seconds of a qualifying gap. Pendant cancellation should take under 1 second. No microphone needs to remain open.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per request depending on decomposition; polling and gap checks should be deterministic or use a cheap model. Browser extraction and receipts dominate compute, not voice.
args.security_concerns: Private calendar/mail snippets and authenticated page data leave the Mac only as compact task context and cited results. Store the queued plan encrypted with a TTL and bind browser work to a named tab/session. Do not submit irreversible browser actions unless the owner explicitly included submission; always retain before/after receipts. A physical pendant cancel must win over queued execution.
missing: A durable deferred-job state machine with a next-eligible-time and cancellation token, distinct from the existing immediate jobs queue

A Mac context event/periodic sampler that reports Calendar busy/free, foreground app, idle/active state, and a freshness timestamp without Accessibility (AppleScript can cover Calendar/foreground where possible)
Browser bridge online/reconnect and a queue consumer that can resume a named authenticated tab after a dropped link
Pendant firmware/server protocol for one-button cancel and concise queued/running/completed/error tones
A dashboard view for staged jobs, eligibility reason, TTL, and receipts

args.change: Add an interruption-aware deferred-job coordinator between /plan, /execute, /jobs, /routines, Calendar/Mail context, and the browser queue. It should persist eligibility rules (free calendar window, foreground/idle constraints, quiet hours), wake on context events or bounded polling, lease one job at a time, honor pendant cancellation, and attach the existing per-action receipts and undo links. This is scheduling/orchestration, not a new unrestricted executor and not an approval gate.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “when I’m free” once and trust that work will happen without interrupting a meeting or getting lost when the Mac/browser link briefly drops. They receive a clear staged/running/completed result rather than having to ask where the job went.
args.effort: Medium-high: durable state schema and lease/retry worker, Mac context adapter, relay reconnect handling, and pendant cancel/status events; reuse existing jobs, routines, browser commands, and receipts.
args.risk: A stale context could start during a newly begun meeting, or retries could duplicate browser steps. Mitigate with short-lived context freshness, idempotency keys, a single active lease, step-level receipts, and cancellation checked before every step. Recovery is cancel/undo where supported and an explicit failed receipt where it is not.
args.cost_impact: Low background model/API cost; mostly deterministic polling and D1/local state. One cheap planner call per staged job plus occasional extraction calls.
args.latency_impact: Immediate acknowledgement remains under 2 seconds; execution intentionally waits for the next eligible window. Context freshness adds at most one short poll interval.
args.security_impact: No new access beyond existing Calendar/Mail AppleScript and browser sessions. Keep private context local/relay-minimized, TTL queued plans, and redact snippets in dashboard/pendant speech.

Round 97 findings:

- The pendant is still a prototype nRF9160 DK with one button/LED and 211 KB application RAM, so cancellation/status signaling must remain very small and local.

I recorded two new items:

1. **“Do this when I’m free”** — stage work, wait for a safe Calendar/foreground/idle window, execute through Mac/browser, and report completion or cancellation on the pendant.
2. **Interruption-aware deferred-job coordinator** — durable eligibility rules, leases, retries, pendant cancellation, browser reconnect handling, and existing job receipts/undo integration.

What I still need for that capability:

1. A durable deferred-job state machine and worker, distinct from the immediate `/jobs` queue.
2. Implementations for bounded Calendar/Mail reads and read-only Mac context inspection.
3. Browser extension reconnection and reliable command acknowledgements.
4. Pendant protocol support for queued/running/completed/error states and one-button cancellation.
5. A dashboard showing eligibility, TTL, current lease, and receipts.
6. If UI-state or vision evidence is required, the owner must manually enable Accessibility and Screen Recording for **AI Pendant Agent**. I will not re-request those permissions from the orchestrator.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving the Mac—package this exactly so I can resume it from the pendant later.” Preserve the current Mac app/document state, authenticated browser tabs, unsent drafts, evidence, and next safe step; let me ask the pendant what is waiting and resume or abandon it when I return.
args.why_useful: Today a task is split across a browser session, Mac files/apps, and conversation history; walking away loses the working set or forces the owner to reconstruct it. A resumable handoff would make the pendant a true continuation of the Mac rather than a separate voice endpoint. It is specifically a state-preservation and restoration capability, not a generic background job or page watch.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to summarize and validate the handoff capsule. Use realtime only when the owner asks the pendant for status or gives resume/abandon commands. Use a stronger model only to resolve conflicting state during restoration.
args.latency_budget: Create a capsule in under 5 seconds after the owner says to leave. Pendant status should answer in under 2 seconds. Restore should begin within 10 seconds of returning the Mac, with a clear partial-restore report.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.003–$0.02 per handoff, dominated by optional document/browser summarization. Deterministic file manifests, app identifiers, tab metadata, and action receipts should avoid model calls.
args.security_concerns: Capsules may contain private file paths, authenticated tab identifiers, drafts, and snippets. Encrypt them, keep the default retention short, bind browser data to the original session, exclude passwords/tokens and full page bodies unless explicitly requested, and provide a physical pendant abandon/delete command. Restoration must never silently send, submit, or delete anything.
missing: A cross-surface handoff-capsule schema with typed state, provenance, sensitivity labels, expiry, and a resumable step pointer
Mac snapshot/restore adapters for open documents, app context, unsaved draft locations, and the active project without requiring Accessibility for the basic tier
Browser extension export/import of tab/session identity and staged form state without exporting credentials
Relay storage and synchronization for encrypted capsules plus pendant-sized status summaries
A restoration reconciler that detects changed files/tabs and presents conflicts instead of replaying stale actions
A user-facing dashboard and pendant commands for list, resume, fork, abandon, and securely erase

args.user_asks: “Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser, show me exactly what private data will leave each device, what will stay local, and let me say ‘redact that’ or ‘local only.’ Then proceed with the least-data version and give me a receipt afterward.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has maximum-control automation but no intelligible, per-task data boundary. This would let them use powerful cross-device actions without needing to understand prompts, tokens, browser sessions, or relay internals. It is a live privacy contract spanning the pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—not merely an execution confirmation.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic typed accounting for paths, snippets, tab origins, and payload sizes. Use a cheap model to phrase the summary for speech; realtime is only needed for the owner’s short redact/local-only replies.
args.latency_budget: Generate the data-flow preview in under 2 seconds for ordinary tasks. Apply redaction before any network submission. Final receipt should be available within 3 seconds of task completion.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.005 per task because accounting is deterministic; model cost is only the short spoken explanation. Storage cost is small for hashed receipts and policy decisions.
args.security_concerns: The preview itself must not reveal the sensitive data it is describing. Use category labels, hashes, lengths, and destination names by default, with optional local-only reveal. Enforce the selected policy at every handoff, not just at planning time; fail closed if a new field appears. Keep the policy decision and receipt tamper-evident but avoid retaining raw content.
missing: A typed end-to-end data-flow ledger attached to every plan, browser command, Mac action, and relay message
A preflight transformation layer that can remove fields, replace values with local summaries, or force a computation to remain on the Mac
A small pendant interaction protocol for redact, local-only, allow-once, and revoke-current-task
Browser and Mac adapters that report actual outbound fields rather than only intended actions
Tamper-evident receipts showing destinations, categories, byte counts, and policy decisions
A dashboard view that lets the owner inspect and revoke standing data policies

args.user_asks: “If that multi-step task partly failed, figure out exactly what changed, what did not, and repair only the missing pieces—without repeating anything that already happened.”
args.why_useful: Cross-surface work can succeed in one place and fail in another: a file may be created while a browser update times out, or a draft may be staged while its evidence fetch fails. Today the owner must manually inspect every surface and risks duplicate actions. A bounded reconciliation mode would make failures recoverable rather than opaque.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic receipt/state comparison first; use a cheap background model to classify discrepancies and generate a repair plan. Realtime is only for announcing the failure and accepting “repair,” “leave it,” or “discard.”
args.latency_budget: Report partial failure within 3 seconds of detection. Produce a repair plan within 10 seconds for ordinary jobs; execute only the missing idempotent steps after the owner’s command.
args.cost_estimate: Low: receipts and hashes dominate, with roughly $0.002–$0.01 for discrepancy classification. Avoid re-running expensive browser extraction when prior evidence remains valid.
args.security_concerns: Never infer success from a timeout. Preserve before/after evidence, use idempotency keys, and treat unknown outcomes as requiring reconciliation. Repair plans must exclude irreversible steps unless explicitly reissued. Keep sensitive evidence local or hashed in relay receipts.
missing: A cross-surface transaction journal with per-step preconditions, postconditions, idempotency keys, and unknown-outcome status
State probes for Mac files/apps and browser pages that can verify postconditions without replaying actions
A reconciliation planner that computes the minimal missing-step set and detects conflicting external changes
A durable repair lease and retry budget shared by Mac and browser workers
Pendant and dashboard controls for inspect, repair, abandon, and export the failure receipt

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Cross-device resumable handoff** — preserve the exact Mac/browser working state so the owner can leave and resume from the pendant.
2. **Per-task data-flow control** — show what private data would leave each device, support “redact” or “local only,” and issue a tamper-evident receipt.
3. **Partial-failure reconciliation** — determine exactly which steps completed and repair only missing steps, avoiding duplicate actions.

They require new cross-surface state protocols, typed provenance and postcondition checks, durable encrypted capsules/receipts, browser and Mac state probes, and pendant controls for resume, redact, repair, or abandon.

args.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” while I’m looking at a page, capture the page and my spoken note as a sourced, searchable research card; later I can ask the pendant what I saved and have the Mac reopen the exact source.
args.why_useful: This turns an ephemeral browser tab plus a two-second pendant utterance into durable memory with provenance. It works across the surfaces: the browser has the authenticated page, the pendant supplies intent while away from the keyboard, the relay keeps the request alive, and the Mac creates/reopens a human-readable artifact. It is materially safer than an unsourced memory because every claim points back to URL, tab, timestamp, and excerpt.
args.model_tier: Realtime tier only parses the short capture command and acknowledges it. A cheaper background model normalizes the note, extracts a short title/topics, deduplicates against existing cards, and generates a citation-preserving summary. Retrieval is semantic plus exact-topic matching; no model call if the user asks for a title/URL lookup.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pendant within 500 ms, enqueue capture in under 2 s, and finish the card in 5–15 s. Retrieval should return the top cards in under 2 s and open the chosen source on the Mac in another 1–3 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per capture depending on page length and summarization; retrieval usually under $0.001. Dominant costs are extracting long authenticated pages and background summarization, so cap captured text and hash unchanged excerpts.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page content and the spoken note leave the browser/Mac only to the owner's relay and memory store; redact secrets and form fields before persistence. Store URL, title, excerpt hash, and source timestamp by default, with full text opt-in. Never submit forms or alter the page. Reopening a private URL must preserve its browser session and should fail closed if the session is gone. The pendant acknowledgement should not read the captured page aloud in public.

args.user_asks: Tell me before my important logged-in browser sessions expire or get signed out, and when I’m back at the Mac, open only the affected sign-in pages so I can restore them without exposing page contents.
args.why_useful: Silent session expiry is a recurring failure mode for every authenticated workflow: a morning brief can look empty, a form can be half-filled, or a watch can stop silently. This gives the owner an actionable warning from the pendant while keeping private page contents out of the alert, then uses the Mac only for the narrowly scoped recovery step.
args.model_tier: No expensive model for detection: a deterministic browser heartbeat/session-state classifier runs on the relay or extension. Use the realtime tier only to understand a spoken request such as “which account needs attention?” and a cheap background model to rank urgency from session age and scheduled watches.
args.latency_budget: Heartbeat every 5–15 minutes with <1 s relay processing; alert within one heartbeat of an auth transition. On request, enumerate affected sessions in <2 s; Mac opens the recovery pages in 1–3 s.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; roughly a few thousand lightweight heartbeat events per month. The dominant cost is relay/browser storage and any optional notification audio, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Transmit only state (session ID, origin, auth-needed/healthy, last-seen), never cookies, tokens, DOM text, screenshots, or typed credentials. Keep an allowlist of origins and let the owner pause monitoring from the pendant. Never auto-enter credentials or submit MFA; opening a sign-in page is the maximum automatic action. Expiry records should have short retention and be deletable.

Durable per-origin watch policy with quiet hours and a last-alert fingerprint to prevent repeated alerts

args.security_concerns: Evidence must remain account-scoped and redact private page contents in pendant audio. Never retry an uncertain mutation automatically. args.security_impact: Evidence may contain private URLs, filenames, and snippets. Enforce per-owner encryption and field-level redaction; pendant output should contain only minimal labels and no sensitive content by default.

A cross-surface transaction would make long tasks trustworthy: the relay coordinates checkpoints, the Mac records durable receipts, the browser contributes tab-scoped evidence, and the pendant gives a compact status/resume control even after disconnection.
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for checkpoint reconciliation and retry planning; reserve realtime for the owner's spoken request and a short exception/resume conversation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; checkpoint updates within 5 seconds of each action; retries can run in the background. Never block the owner waiting for a whole workflow.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly 1–3 background model calls per failed or resumed task; normal successful steps use typed receipts and no model call. Dominant cost is only reconciliation of ambiguous outcomes.
args.security_concerns: The coordinator must never replay a non-idempotent browser submit or Mac mutation merely because a receipt is missing. Persist a step idempotency key, precondition/evidence hash, and outcome (completed/unknown/skipped); quarantine unknown steps for review. Private URLs, snippets, and action receipts leave the Mac only when needed for the relay's task record; redact by default. Pendant resume/status should reveal only task labels, not page contents. Existing maximum-access policy means this is observability and safe replay—not a new approval gate.
missing: A durable cross-surface saga/job schema with step IDs, idempotency keys, preconditions, evidence hashes, and explicit unknown outcomes
A relay coordinator that leases work to Mac/browser and reconciles receipts after reconnect
A pendant status/resume command and offline-safe cancellation marker
Browser stale-command quarantine and a Mac-to-relay receipt acknowledgement protocol

args.change: Add a lease-and-checkpoint coordinator between the existing relay jobs, Mac /plan+/execute, and browser command queue. On reconnect, reconcile receipts before issuing any new command, quarantine the seven currently pending browser commands if their device epoch is stale, and expose a compact causal timeline to /jobs/:jobId/receipts. This is wiring and failure semantics between existing components, not another generic durable job runner.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped Wi‑Fi link or sleeping browser would no longer make the owner wonder whether something happened twice. They get one truthful timeline and safe continuation from the last confirmed step, while stale browser commands cannot unexpectedly execute after reconnect.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema, relay state transitions, Mac acknowledgement hook, browser device-epoch handling, migration/tests for existing jobs.
args.risk: A too-short lease can mark a slow action unknown and pause work unnecessarily; a too-long lease delays recovery. Recover by explicit unknown state and manual resume. Existing FULL_CONTROL_MODE remains unchanged; this adds receipts and quarantine, not a confirmation gate.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost on successful steps; small D1 storage increase for step receipts and hashes. Background reconciliation may use an inexpensive model only for ambiguous failures.
args.latency_impact: One local receipt write per step; reconnect recovery adds a few seconds to reconcile before resuming.
args.security_impact: Store hashes and redacted metadata rather than page bodies by default. Do not replay unknown mutating steps without an owner-directed resume. Device epochs prevent old browser sessions from consuming new commands.

This capability turns preparation into time-bounded escrow: the relay records the relevant facts, the browser and Mac re-check them immediately before the final action, and the pendant reports a concise change alert. A stale approval cannot silently authorize a different price, recipient, appointment, or document.
args.model_tier: Use a low-cost background model to identify which fields are approval-critical and compare before/after evidence; use realtime only to tell the owner what changed and ask whether to regenerate the preparation.
args.latency_budget: Preparation can be asynchronous. The final freshness check should complete within 3–5 seconds; if it fails, stop and notify rather than retrying blindly.

args.security_concerns: Never retain full private pages or message bodies when hashes and selected fields suffice. Scope each escrow to a specific account, tab/session, file, recipient, and expiry. args.change: Introduce a single-use, expiring approval nonce bound to a redacted critical-field snapshot and source identities (browser tab/session or Mac file/app). args.risk: Overly broad critical-field selection could invalidate harmless changes and annoy the owner; recover by showing the changed fields and offering regenerate. A relay outage should fail closed for final mutations but preserve the draft locally for later.
args.cost_impact: Minimal storage and one extra typed preflight per final action; no additional realtime-model usage in the normal path.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly one network round trip (target under 3 seconds) immediately before the final mutation.
args.security_impact: Improves replay resistance and limits authorization to the exact artifact and context the owner reviewed. Redacted snapshots reduce private-data exposure; nonce consumption must be atomic and never logged with secret contents.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets honest recovery after closing a laptop or losing Safari: no duplicate form submissions, no silent dropped research, and a single pendant-ready answer to “did that happen?” even after a restart.
args.effort: Medium: a persistent worker, schema migration, queue leases, and tests for crash/reconnect races; no new model is needed. Requires wiring the existing local browser queue, /browser/status heartbeat, /browser/poll, result callbacks, and job receipts.
args.risk: A false stale classification could quarantine a harmless read or leave work unfinished; recovery is explicit retry from the receipt. args.cost_impact: Negligible compute/storage; one small receipt per command and occasional inexpensive background triage call only for ambiguous failures.
args.latency_impact: Heartbeat remains lightweight; reconnect reconciliation completes within seconds for reads and intentionally pauses mutations until the owner asks.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing replay. Keep private page content and session tokens on the Mac/relay; receipts should store hashes and minimal snippets, with configurable redaction.

A lost presence signal must fail closed for mutating browser actions, while read-only actions may be cancelled or retained—not silently run. The pendant’s explicit resume phrase should be bound to the same job/session and a displayed action hash.

args.user_asks: Use my private accounts to answer a question, but never send the private page or raw personal data off my Mac—give me only the minimum derived result and show me exactly what was disclosed.
args.why_useful: The owner could get genuinely useful cross-site answers today only by exposing whole private pages to a general model or by doing the comparison manually. A local privacy boundary would let the pendant ask questions over logged-in data while keeping credentials, page contents, and unnecessary personal fields on the Mac.
args.model_tier: Use a small local Mac model or deterministic extraction for filtering and aggregation; use the cheaper background model for synthesis over the redacted derived dataset. Realtime is reserved for the final short spoken answer.
args.latency_budget: Local extraction and redaction under 10 seconds for a handful of pages; synthesis under 15 seconds. If the query requires broad browsing or an uncertain field mapping, pause and ask rather than widening disclosure.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.02 per request, dominated by one background synthesis call; local filtering and hashing are effectively free. No cloud token cost for raw page content because it never leaves the Mac.
args.security_concerns: The Mac must treat authenticated browser DOM and credentials as private. A non-bypassable data diode should allow only typed aggregates, boolean predicates, ranges, and owner-approved snippets to cross into the relay. Every outbound field needs a reason, sensitivity label, provenance, and hash; the pendant should announce the disclosure summary. No automatic submission, message send, or account mutation. Encrypt the local intermediate and expire it after the answer.
missing: A Mac-local privacy broker that can query authenticated tabs, transform raw DOM into a typed derived dataset, and enforce an allowlisted outbound schema.
A browser extraction protocol with field-level provenance and sensitivity labels rather than whole-page text results.
Relay/model routing that rejects payloads containing raw private fields and accepts only the signed derived-result envelope.
A pendant disclosure receipt and a way for the owner to approve expanding one field when the derived answer is insufficient.

args.change: Create a Mac-resident private-data diode for authenticated browser work. It accepts a natural-language question, executes only read operations in bound private tabs, maps results into a typed schema (e.g. price, date, status, count), strips free text and identifiers by default, and emits a signed disclosure envelope containing only approved fields, provenance hashes, freshness, and a human-readable disclosure manifest. The relay rejects any payload outside that schema; the owner can approve a one-field expansion from the pendant, producing a new envelope rather than exposing the page.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for comparisons, eligibility checks, or summaries across private accounts without handing an AI service their whole logged-in pages. The owner gets the benefit of the hive's reach while retaining a clear, inspectable privacy boundary.
args.effort: High: a local policy/extraction service, browser field provenance, envelope signing and schema validation at the relay, redaction tests, and a pendant disclosure UI/audio format. This is a new privacy architecture, not a planner prompt.
args.risk: Incorrect extraction could produce a wrong derived answer; every value must retain source URL, timestamp, selector/hash, and confidence so the owner can inspect it. A schema bug could leak data, so default-deny validation, fuzz tests, payload size limits, and immediate intermediate deletion are required. If uncertain, return 'could not safely derive' rather than raw text.
args.cost_impact: Small local CPU/storage cost; typically one cheaper synthesis call over a tiny derived payload, with no cloud cost for raw page data. Engineering cost is substantial because the boundary must be security-reviewed.
args.latency_impact: Adds a local transformation step, roughly seconds; avoids uploading large pages and can be faster for multi-page comparisons once typed extractors exist.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves privacy by making raw authenticated DOM and credentials non-exportable. It introduces signing keys and a policy engine that become high-value targets; store keys in the Mac keychain, rotate them, and audit every envelope and field expansion.
depends_on: A browser result format with field-level provenance and sensitivity labels
A Mac-local policy broker able to inspect authenticated tabs without returning whole-page content
Relay-side schema enforcement and signature verification
A pendant disclosure receipt and explicit field-expansion interaction

args.user_asks: “If you start something on my Mac and the browser or connection drops, keep track of it and continue safely when it comes back—tell me what finished, what did not, and what you need from me.”
args.why_useful: Today a browser command can sit in a pending queue or fail after a 45-second timeout while the owner receives no durable, cross-device explanation. This capability turns a disconnected multi-surface task into a resumable handoff: the relay/pendant can acknowledge the interruption, the Mac can preserve receipts and checkpoints, and the browser can resume only the uncompleted steps once its extension is healthy. It is beyond a generic durable job runner because it reconciles Mac receipts, browser tab/session identity, and pendant-delivery state, preventing duplicate submissions after reconnect.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background worker/state machine for heartbeat monitoring, checkpoint reconciliation, retry classification, and delivery; use the realtime tier only for the owner's short spoken request and an urgent interruption notice. Escalate to the stronger planner only when a failed step is ambiguous or the page has materially changed.
args.latency_budget: A reconnect should be noticed within 10–20 seconds of browser heartbeat recovery; deterministic reconciliation should take under 2 seconds. Pendant interruption/complete notices should be queued for offline delivery and spoken on next contact. No polling or model call is needed while all surfaces are healthy.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per task, dominated by occasional background model recovery for ambiguous page changes; healthy tasks use only D1/R2/worker operations. TTS/audio delivery is the secondary cost when a notice is actually spoken.
args.security_concerns: Persist only task IDs, step receipts, tab/session IDs, URL hashes, and minimal redacted evidence; never copy page secrets into the pendant queue. Resume must require an idempotency key and verify the same tab/session plus a precondition (URL/title/semantic fingerprint) before any browser write. A changed page becomes paused and asks the owner; no automatic retries of submit/send/purchase steps. The owner can ask the pendant for status and cancel, while existing maximum-control policy remains unchanged.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint record linking each Mac action receipt to its browser command and pendant delivery acknowledgment.
A reconnect coordinator that consumes browser heartbeat changes, reconciles pending commands against receipts, and distinguishes safe read/retry steps from non-repeatable writes.

An explicit browser precondition/fingerprint check and idempotency key carried through /browser/poll and /browser/result before resuming.

args.user_asks: “When I’m in a focus block or meeting, keep interruptions out of my way, but collect anything important and give me one short catch-up when it ends.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is the one surface that can start or end a focus block without the owner touching the Mac, while the relay can hold alerts during a dropped link, the Mac can change local notification state and collect Calendar/Mail context, and the browser can stop surfacing non-urgent page-watch changes. Existing routines and briefings do not provide a shared interruption contract or a single end-of-block digest.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a small background model to classify queued events by urgency and deduplicate them. Use the realtime tier only for the pendant's start/end acknowledgment and when the owner explicitly asks for an interruption. Generate the end digest with a cheaper batch model, grounded in collected source snippets.
args.latency_budget: Start/stop acknowledgment under 1 second when connected; if offline, persist the state locally and replay it on reconnect. Suppression decisions are immediate and rule-based. End-of-block digest in under 10 seconds, with no need to wait on every source if one is unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.01 per focus block: mostly event storage and one small digest call. TTS costs only for the final spoken catch-up. No model call is made for routine low-priority events.
args.security_concerns: The relay stores event metadata and redacted snippets with a user-configurable retention window; sensitive mail/browser bodies stay on the Mac unless explicitly included. Urgency classification must show source links and why an item was held. Emergency/allowlisted senders, alarms, and explicit owner interrupts bypass suppression. Never alter or send messages; this is notification control and summarization only.
missing: A shared focus-state lease with owner/device origin, start/end time, timezone, and offline replay semantics.
A relay-side held-event queue with urgency/allowlist rules and deduplication across Mail, Calendar, browser watches, and Mac jobs.
Mac/browser adapters that apply and restore notification suppression without losing the prior user state.
An end-of-block reconciliation job that cites every surfaced item and reports anything that could not be inspected.

args.change: Add a cross-surface event ledger and focus-state lease in the relay. Each incoming alert or completion event gets a stable event ID, source (pendant/Mac/browser), sensitivity class, urgency, focus-block ID, and delivery acknowledgments. The relay exposes a compact delta feed; Mac and browser adapters report applied notification state and restore tokens. On focus end, a worker joins undelivered deltas with Calendar/Mail/browser citations, emits one digest, and marks each item delivered or unavailable. Expire leases and held payloads automatically, and make replay idempotent.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can press one pendant control to get uninterrupted work without losing important things, even if the Mac or browser disconnects. They get one trustworthy catch-up instead of duplicate alerts, silent loss, or a permanently altered notification setting.
args.effort: Medium-high: new D1 schema/state machine, relay endpoints, Mac notification adapter, browser event adapter, and pendant start/stop/replay protocol; add fault-injection tests for disconnects and duplicate delivery.
args.risk: A stale lease could suppress an urgent event or fail to restore the prior notification state. Mitigate with hard lease expiry, emergency bypass rules, visible active-state feedback on the pendant, restore tokens, and a recovery sweep that replays anything unacknowledged. If the digest worker fails, retain the queue and report its unavailable state rather than dropping data.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and worker cost; one inexpensive digest inference per focus block, plus optional TTS. No continuous realtime model use.
args.latency_impact: State changes and suppression deltas are sub-second when online; reconnect replay is bounded by the next heartbeat. Digest generation is asynchronous and should complete within 10 seconds.
args.security_impact: Sensitive content remains on the Mac by default; the relay holds IDs and redacted snippets only, encrypted with short retention. Every digest item carries provenance and a reason for inclusion. Focus state is scoped to the owner's authenticated devices.
depends_on: A pendant-side focus start/stop event and offline persistence skill
A relay-held alert queue with TTL and urgency policy
Mac notification-state read/restore adapter (AppleScript where possible)
Browser watch/event adapter that can pause and resume cleanly

args.user_asks: If I ask you to do something while my Mac or browser is offline, remember the intent, wait for the right device to reconnect, then carry it out safely and tell me exactly what happened — without losing it or doing it twice.
args.why_useful: Today the pendant can hear an intent while the browser is offline and the Mac may reconnect later, but there is no owner-visible, cross-node reconciliation contract. This would turn intermittent connectivity into a dependable assistant: one request ID, durable pending state, deduplication, conflict detection, and a short spoken result when the action is finally applied. It is specifically multi-node: pendant captures intent, relay persists and arbitrates, Mac/browser execute, and the pendant reports the receipt.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to normalize the spoken request and clarify ambiguity; use a cheap background model (or deterministic rules) to reconcile queued intents, device capabilities, and receipts after reconnect.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgment under 1 second offline; reconnect reconciliation within 10 seconds of a device heartbeat; spoken completion within 3 seconds after receipt. No waiting loop on the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per request, dominated by optional normalization/reconciliation; most retries, dedupe, and receipt matching should be deterministic. Small durable relay storage per intent and receipt.
args.security_concerns: The relay must store only a minimized intent capsule, not page contents or secrets, with encryption, expiry, and device-scoped bearer authorization. Never replay destructive actions (send mail, delete, purchase) from an offline capsule without a fresh owner confirmation; reversible/read-only actions may replay according to owner policy. Surface conflicts such as changed URLs, stale files, or changed calendar state instead of guessing. Dashboard must expose cancel/expire and the full action/receipt chain.

This makes the hive reliable across disconnections: the wearable captures the request, the always-on relay preserves it, the Mac/browser reevaluate current state, and the owner gets a concise spoken receipt or a clear conflict to resolve.

args.security_concerns: The relay must store encrypted intent capsules, not raw microphone audio; bind each capsule to owner/session and a nonce; never replay a send/delete/purchase without the owner's existing confirmation policy. Browser credentials stay in the extension, Mac data stays local. Show source tabs, timestamps, and before/after evidence in the dashboard and spoken receipt.

Expose the same observation ID to /plan and /execute so a plan can declare which fresh observation it was based on.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The assistant can currently act on the Mac but cannot reliably see whether the right app/tab is open or whether the world changed between planning and execution. args.user_asks: “Let me have a normal conversation through the pendant even when the connection is busy—keep my speech from disappearing, and keep replies understandable.”
args.why_useful: The live trace proves 24 kHz TTS is being rendered and accepted (75,734-byte PCM), but the measured LTE-M link drops about 7.8 seconds of uplink when 24 kbps downlink overlaps it. This capability turns the current demo into a conversation that remains usable under the exact condition the owner will encounter.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the conversational turn; deterministic firmware/relay control for congestion decisions; no planner-tier model call.
args.latency_budget: Add no more than one 20–40 ms control interval. Keep audio playout under 120 ms of additional buffering; a codec-mode change may take one frame (60 ms).
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost. Relay CPU/storage rises modestly for packet statistics and short Opus transcode buffers; LTE data may fall because the adaptive mode lowers bitrate during contention.
args.security_concerns: Only transport quality metrics, codec mode, and packet sequence numbers leave the pendant; never audio-derived content. Persist no speech beyond existing retention. No confirmation is needed because this changes transport quality, not an external side effect.
missing: Firmware telemetry for sequence gaps, jitter-buffer depth, modem send-queue occupancy, and button/turn state
A relay codec-negotiation and prioritization state machine that can lower uplink bitrate or pause nonessential downlink frames without dropping speech
Mac TTS output packetization that can emit a negotiated Opus profile instead of always uploading a large 24 kHz PCM blob
An end-to-end fault-injection test that overlaps owner speech and reply audio and verifies bounded loss/recovery

args.change: Add a closed-loop AudioQoS session shared by pendant firmware, Cloudflare relay, and Mac audio pipeline. The pendant emits compact 1-second counters (uplink loss, jitter, queue depth, playout underruns); relay computes a mode (normal, uplink-protect, recovery) and sends a signed mode update; Mac TTS packetizer and relay Opus transcode honor that mode. In uplink-protect, cap/reshape downlink and reserve modem budget for microphone packets; in recovery, refill the jitter buffer gradually. Record the mode and counters in the existing pipeline event/receipt stream so each call can be diagnosed without retaining speech.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner speaks while the agent replies, their words will no longer vanish for several seconds, and a degraded connection will recover gracefully instead of producing silence or a late burst of audio. The owner also gets an honest explanation in a completion receipt when quality was reduced.
args.effort: Medium-high: a firmware telemetry packet and state machine, relay session state and packet scheduler, Mac/Opus packetizer changes, plus an automated contention test. This is a focused vertical slice rather than a new surface.
args.risk: A bad mode update could starve replies or cause oscillation. Use monotonic sequence numbers, hysteresis (minimum 2 seconds per mode), a 5-second local timeout to return to normal, and retain the current static 24 kHz path as fallback. Recovery is automatic on reconnect.
args.cost_impact: No additional model calls. A few dozen bytes/sec of telemetry and small relay memory per active call; adaptive mode should reduce LTE airtime during contention. Engineering/test cost is the dominant cost.
args.latency_impact: Telemetry/control under 1 second; at most one 60 ms codec frame to change mode, with up to 120 ms intentional jitter buffering during recovery.
args.security_impact: Telemetry contains transport statistics only. Authenticate mode updates to the paired pendant; do not upload raw microphone samples beyond the existing audio path, and keep diagnostic counters under the existing audio-retention policy.
depends_on: Pendant firmware support for loss/jitter/queue counters and a local fallback mode
Relay scheduler and Opus profile negotiation
Mac TTS/Opus packetizer that can honor a per-session audio mode
A contention/fault-injection harness covering simultaneous uplink and downlink

args.latency_budget: Local scan and redaction under 300 ms for a normal page; at most 1 second added before the spoken answer. Never upload the original page as a fallback when the scanner is uncertain.
args.cost_estimate: No required realtime-model increase; modest Mac CPU for DOM classification and a small relay/database cost for hashed redaction receipts. The dominant engineering cost is testing false negatives against real authenticated sites.
args.security_concerns: The original DOM, screenshots, and secret values must remain on the Mac. Send only redacted text plus field-type counts and salted hashes of region identifiers. Treat uncertainty as deny-and-report, not allow. Make policy version, withheld categories, and source URL visible in a local receipt; require explicit owner configuration to permit any category.

args.change: Insert a fail-closed privacy firewall between the browser bridge and every research/realtime request. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for help on a logged-in page without trusting an invisible promise. They receive a concrete, reviewable statement of what was blocked, and a policy failure cannot silently turn into secret exfiltration.
args.effort: High: extension interception plus Mac-local classifier, signed request schema, relay rejection path, and adversarial tests for secrets hidden in attributes, screenshots, accessibility trees, and copied text.
args.risk: False positives may make answers less complete; false negatives are unacceptable. Fail closed on classifier uncertainty, maintain a user-editable allowlist of non-sensitive fields, and provide a local-only re-run after policy changes. Recovery never retries with the raw page.
args.cost_impact: No additional model calls on the normal path; Mac CPU and test-maintenance cost are significant, with small relay storage for manifests. Data egress decreases.
args.latency_impact: Typically 100–300 ms local processing; complex pages may add up to 1 second. No network round trip is added for policy decisions.

transcript.text:
Round 117 findings:

- `/browser/status` reports the bridge offline with **9 pending commands**.
- Browser jobs can wait roughly **45 seconds** before failing, and stale commands remain queued.
- `/observe` reports the foreground app as Claude and confirms that synthesized UI input currently **does not reach the screen**: Accessibility is not trusted for the running AI Pendant Agent binary.
- The pipeline has emitted “Waiting for your approval” even though `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` is configured to run without approval gates. This is a state-reporting inconsistency.

I recorded three new proposals:

1. **Connectivity-aware browser task continuation**  
   Immediately tell the owner whether a task is queued, waiting for the browser, resumed, or abandoned; checkpoint authenticated steps; quarantine stale commands; resume only after a fresh tab/session check.

2. **Execution-policy reconciliation**  
   Make pipeline events use the actual executor policy, so the system cannot claim approval is required when the task is running under maximum-access mode.

3. **Reachability-aware Mac actions**  
   Before UI actions, consume `/observe`; use AppleScript fallbacks where safe, or return `not_reached` rather than falsely reporting success when Accessibility is unavailable.

What I still need:

- **Browser bridge recovery or an explicit queue-drain/quarantine implementation.** The current offline queue is the most urgent operational gap.
- A single authoritative **effective execution-policy/version** exposed to both the executor and pipeline recorder.
- A typed receipt state for **executed / failed / not_reached**, plus AppleScript adapters for common named-app operations.
- If reliable GUI automation is required, the owner must manually grant Accessibility to the exact running binary `/Users/evanliu/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app`; this cannot be granted from the harness.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving the Mac. Save exactly where I am, and when I come back—or ask from the pendant—put me back into that work without losing anything.”
args.why_useful: Today a Mac task is tied to the machine’s transient UI state. After sleep, a crash, or moving away, the owner must reconstruct the work manually. This would create a crash-safe, privacy-preserving continuation capsule: what was open, the relevant browser tabs, selected document locations, unsaved draft identity, and the last confirmed action. The pendant could give a short spoken ‘you were here’ summary, while the Mac could restore the workspace and detect conflicts before touching files or tabs.
args.model_tier: Use a local deterministic checkpoint builder for app/window/tab/document metadata and hashes. Use a cheaper background model to summarize and reconcile checkpoints. Use realtime only for the pendant’s short retrieval request and spoken summary; use vision only for apps whose state cannot be represented through AppleScript or structured inspection.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint in under 2 seconds when the owner presses a pendant button or says a leave-taking phrase. Spoken recall in under 3 seconds from the relay. Workspace restoration in under 10 seconds, with any conflict surfaced before mutation.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for capture and restore; one small background summarization call per checkpoint or only when requested. Storage is small encrypted metadata plus optional local-only document hashes. Vision fallback is the dominant cost and should be exceptional.
args.security_concerns: Never upload document contents, passwords, cookies, or page secrets. Store sensitive locators and browser session identifiers only on the Mac; relay receives an opaque capsule ID and redacted summary. Restore must be conflict-aware: if a file, tab, or draft changed since capture, open a comparison instead of overwriting. Provide retention expiry and one-button deletion from the pendant/dashboard.

Physical pendant proximity becomes a presence signal: the relay may prepare work while the owner is away, but restoration or sensitive continuation waits until the pendant is nearby and the Mac verifies the same paired device.
args.model_tier: No realtime reasoning is needed for proximity verification. Use firmware and local Mac cryptographic checks for the common path; use a background model only to explain why a capsule is waiting or summarize what will resume.
args.latency_budget: Presence verification under 1 second when the pendant arrives; resume notification under 3 seconds. Remote preparation remains asynchronous and must not block on the pendant.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost. Requires a small BLE presence protocol and key storage; relay storage remains opaque identifiers and status only.
args.security_concerns: Use rotating authenticated BLE challenges, not RSSI alone, and bind keys to the pendant and local Mac. Do not treat proximity as approval for irreversible actions; it only unlocks restoration of a previously prepared context. Revocation, lost-pendant reset, replay protection, and a local-only fallback are mandatory. Browser cookies and page contents remain on the Mac.

Per-capsule sensitivity classes and a local resume policy
Mac secure key storage and pairing/revocation UI
Relay support for prepare-while-away versus resume-when-present states

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Crash-safe cross-device work capsules**  
   Save the owner’s exact Mac/browser work context and let the pendant recall or restore it later, with conflict detection so changed files or tabs are never overwritten.

2. **Pendant-presence-gated sensitive work**  
   Let the Mac prepare private work while the owner is away, but require authenticated physical pendant proximity before restoring sensitive context. This would use rotating BLE challenges rather than trusting RSSI or relay connectivity.

Both require new connective infrastructure rather than merely exposing today’s routes: capsule schema and conflict handling, browser context export, relay state, authenticated pendant–Mac presence, key revocation, and local privacy boundaries.

args.user_asks: “Verify my pendant’s 24 kHz audio path end to end, including while I’m speaking over the agent, and tell me whether it passes.”
args.why_useful: The current prototype claims 24 kHz playback but measured LTE-M contention drops about 7.8 seconds of uplink speech. The owner needs an objective go/no-go result, not another codec setting: a repeatable test can distinguish codec quality, resampling defects, and half-duplex congestion before they rely on the pendant.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for test planning and report generation; reserve realtime only if the owner is actively listening to the test call.
args.latency_budget: A scheduled or on-demand run may take 2–5 minutes. The spoken result should be one short sentence plus a link to the detailed receipt.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.05 per run; dominated by one short controlled realtime audio session and storage of telemetry, not reasoning.
args.security_concerns: Use synthetic prompts/test tones by default and redact transcript/audio payloads. Do not open the Mac microphone. Require explicit opt-in before recording real speech; retain only aggregate packet loss, jitter, decode underruns, and MOS proxy, with automatic deletion.
missing: A firmware diagnostic mode that emits timestamped sequence-marked uplink frames and accepts a known playback fixture without opening the microphone.
Relay-side per-call telemetry correlating sequence gaps, LTE-M retransmits, Opus decode time, and resampler underruns in one trace.
A deterministic contention scenario that makes the agent speak while the pendant uplinks, plus pass/fail thresholds for intelligibility and loss.

args.change: Create an end-to-end audio acceptance harness that propagates one testRunId from pendant diagnostic frames through relay Opus/transcode and pipeline events into a Mac-collected receipt. The harness should run fixed fixtures (silence, speech-shaped noise, bidirectional contention), align uplink/downlink timestamps, calculate packet loss/jitter/decode CPU/resampler underruns and a conservative MOS proxy, then publish a signed pass/fail artifact with raw audio omitted by default. Add a regression threshold so a firmware or relay change cannot claim 24 kHz support without passing both idle and contention cases.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They get a trustworthy answer to “does this work?” and early warning when an update makes calls lose speech or sound narrowband. It directly addresses the measured contention failure instead of hiding it behind a nominal sample-rate label.
args.effort: Medium: firmware diagnostic event format, relay trace aggregation, a Node/Python-style fixture runner, and a small dashboard receipt view. No new model training required.
args.risk: Bad clock alignment or overly strict thresholds could produce false failures; recover with a calibration fixture and versioned thresholds. Never treat synthetic-test success as proof that real speech is safe; label the result accordingly.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one short synthetic run and small metadata receipt. Storage drops substantially if raw audio is not retained.
args.latency_impact: Adds no production call latency. A test run takes roughly 2–5 minutes.
args.security_impact: Synthetic fixtures by default, no Mac microphone, redacted identifiers, signed receipts, and TTL deletion for any optional captured samples.

args.inputs: Fixture profile ID, run nonce, requested contention level, and optional start/stop command. No raw microphone input.
args.storage: No persistent audio. A compact 256-byte rolling diagnostic record in RAM and one final event of roughly 1–2 kB sent upstream; discard after acknowledgement.
args.ram_budget: About 2–4 kB for counters, timestamps, and the fixture state machine, plus reuse of existing Opus buffers; well below the 211,608 B application RAM, but must be measured against the current ~87% single-core encode+decode load.

args.user_asks: “Let me have a genuinely natural, full-duplex 24 kHz conversation from the pendant—even when the agent is speaking—without my speech disappearing or the audio silently falling back to narrowband.”
args.why_useful: Today’s measured LTE-M link is half-duplex in practice and simultaneous 16 kbps uplink plus 24 kbps downlink drops about 7.8 seconds of speech. A quality test can diagnose that, but it cannot make the owner’s everyday conversations reliable. This capability requires making the wearable’s transport and audio hardware sufficient for the experience rather than merely labeling the prototype superwideband.
args.model_tier: Realtime model for the live conversation; a small background controller should handle codec/transport negotiation and quality telemetry so the expensive model is not used for transport decisions.
args.latency_budget: Under 150 ms conversational one-way latency in good coverage; under 300 ms during adaptation. Any mode change should be under one frame and audible only as a brief, intelligible status cue.
args.cost_estimate: Realtime inference cost is unchanged for ordinary speech. Hardware redesign is the dominant cost: roughly $15–35 per prototype unit for a stronger cellular/audio subsystem, plus engineering and certification; modest additional relay telemetry storage.
args.security_concerns: Audio remains encrypted end to end. Quality adaptation must not upload raw diagnostic samples by default. The pendant should indicate degraded or buffered mode, and the owner should be able to disable recording/telemetry independently of conversation.
missing: A product-class wearable architecture with a dedicated audio DSP or second core so Opus encode/decode does not consume ~87% of the current single core.

A cellular transport with reliable simultaneous uplink/downlink capacity above the current LTE-M contention point, or a designed Wi-Fi/Bluetooth-to-phone fallback that is seamless and explicitly indicated.
A jitter buffer and packet-priority scheduler that protects owner speech over agent playback without creating an unbounded delay.

args.user_asks: "Continue that web task when my browser comes back, without repeating anything or losing where you got to."
args.why_useful: Today nine queued browser commands can sit behind an offline extension, while a retry can duplicate clicks or form edits. This would let the pendant accept a long-running authenticated task, pause it safely when the browser disappears, resume from the last verified step when the extension returns, and report exactly what was completed versus skipped. It needs all four surfaces: the pendant captures the request and speaks a compact status; the relay owns the durable lease and wakes on heartbeats; the Mac bridge executes owner-private browser steps; the browser extension returns step receipts and page evidence.
args.model_tier: background for planning/retry classification; realtime only for the owner's initial request and status questions
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; checkpoint each browser step within 2 seconds; resume within 10 seconds of a healthy heartbeat. Never burn a retry on a stale/offline session.
args.cost_estimate: Low per task: one short background planning call plus small receipt/status events; dominant cost is authenticated page extraction, not the lease protocol.
args.security_concerns: Private page text and cookies remain in the browser/Mac lane; relay stores only an opaque job, step hashes, timestamps, and redacted receipts. A resume must verify extension/session identity, URL/origin, and a page-state fingerprint before any write. Never replay a non-idempotent click/type step; mark it unknown and ask the owner. Destructive sends/purchases remain explicitly owner-confirmed even under maximum-access policy.
missing: A durable cross-node job record with step leases and idempotency keys (not merely a pending command queue)
Extension heartbeat carrying session identity and current tab/page fingerprint
Receipt protocol distinguishing applied, not-applied, and unknown after timeout
Resume/reconcile worker wired from relay to Mac bridge and browser result stream

args.change: Add a cross-node execution ledger shared by relay, Mac bridge, and browser extension. Each requested task gets a durable taskId and ordered step records with idempotency key, expected origin/URL fingerprint, lease owner, lease expiry, and terminal state (applied, not_applied, unknown). The relay grants one short lease at a time; the extension heartbeat renews only while the same session/tab is present; POST /browser/result/:commandId atomically closes the step. On reconnect, reconcile pending commands against the ledger and quarantine unknown writes instead of replaying them. Surface the ledger through the existing /jobs and receipts APIs so the pendant can say exactly where the task stopped.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped browser connection would stop being a source of duplicate submissions, repeated purchases, or uncertainty. The owner could safely say "resume" and receive a precise completion report rather than guessing whether the last action happened.
args.effort: Medium-high: schema and atomic state transitions in relay D1, Mac bridge adapters, extension heartbeat/result changes, plus crash/reconnect tests for timeout at every step boundary.
args.risk: A false page fingerprint could pause a harmless task or, worse, permit a mismatched page. Default to quarantine on mismatch; recovery is manual resume after a fresh inspection. Ledger corruption should leave steps paused, never replayed.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and event overhead; one small D1 write per step and occasional heartbeat. No additional model call is required for retries.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 50–150 ms per step for lease/receipt persistence; resume waits for the next heartbeat (target under 10 s).
args.security_impact: Improves security by binding writes to origin/session/page state and limiting replay. Relay must not store page bodies or credentials; encrypt or hash fingerprints and redact receipt text.

1. **Cross-node execution ledger** — durable task IDs, step leases, idempotency keys, page/session fingerprints, and `applied / not-applied / unknown` receipts. This would let the owner safely say “resume that web task” without duplicate clicks or uncertain form submissions.

2. **Staleness-bound execution capsules** — bind every Mac/browser plan to the observed origin, account/session, tab, app target, and machine-context revision. If those change, pause with a precise stale-plan receipt instead of acting on the wrong page or account.

What I still need:

- A real implementation of the read-only Mac inspection and Calendar/Mail tools.
- Browser heartbeat and result-stream implementation sufficient to reconcile the 9 queued commands.
- Durable browser job execution with crash-safe step state.
- Owner-side TCC grants for Accessibility and Screen Recording if UI automation or vision is desired; these cannot be granted from this harness.

I did not re-request previously denied permissions or tools.

args.cost_estimate: Low: metadata/event diffs dominate; one small summarization call per away interval. No page-body upload is needed for intervals with no relevant changes.
args.security_concerns: Departure and return signals are sensitive. Keep raw browser URLs, mail subjects, and calendar details on the Mac unless explicitly requested; relay stores encrypted checkpoint IDs and redacted summaries. Never reopen tabs, send messages, or modify tasks automatically. Require an explicit spoken command before reading private details aloud in public, and provide a pendant privacy gesture to suppress playback.

transcript.text:
Round 126 findings:

- **Mac agent and relay are online.**
- **Browser extension is offline** with **9 pending commands**, so authenticated browser work is currently unreliable.
- **Accessibility and Screen Recording remain disabled**; computer-use vision is unavailable.
- Calendar, Mail, Notes, and System Events automation permissions are available, so scripted non-UI reads can work.
- The newly granted `mac_read_sources` and `mac_readonly_inspect` tools are **schemas only**, not implemented yet.

I proposed a new cross-surface **Focus Lease**: a pendant button starts a temporary focus window, the relay coordinates it, the Mac applies and restores notification state, browser changes are ranked into urgent versus queued events, and the pendant delivers one catch-up summary afterward.

What I still need:

1. A real pendant-side offline focus-toggle skill.
2. Relay-side lease state with expiry, reconnect recovery, and deduplication.
3. A Mac Focus adapter that snapshots and restores the prior state.
4. Browser reconnection and typed severity events.
5. Implementations—not just schemas—for bounded Mac source reads and read-only inspection.
6. Manual owner action for Accessibility/Screen Recording only if UI vision is required.

args.user_asks: “Continue this on my Mac.” — hand the current pendant conversation to the Mac as a private, one-time continuation: open the relevant app or authenticated browser tab, place a concise task capsule where I can see it, and let me say “back” to return the result to the pendant.
args.why_useful: Today the owner must repeat the task, find the right app or tab, and reconstruct context when moving from voice to desktop. This creates a secure handoff between the device that heard the intent and the machine that can show and edit the work, without dumping the entire conversation into a document or exposing unrelated private context.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the short handoff acknowledgement and return command. A cheaper background model compiles the minimal task capsule and extracts the final result; deterministic code handles token expiry, app/tab targeting, and receipts.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff within 500 ms; Mac opens the target within 3 seconds; return a result within 2 seconds after the owner says “back,” excluding long-running work.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.002–$0.02 per handoff, dominated by capsule compilation and result summarization; transport, routing, and local file/UI actions are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Use a single-use, short-lived handoff token bound to the paired pendant and Mac session. Send only the selected task capsule, never the raw transcript by default. Do not copy secrets into clipboard or files; redact sensitive entities and show the capsule destination. Browser actions remain read/draft-only unless separately requested, and the handoff expires if the Mac does not accept it.
missing: A relay handoff protocol that issues one-time capability tokens and tracks accepted/completed/expired states
A compact context-capsule compiler with explicit source references and redaction
A Mac receiver that resolves the capsule into an app, file, or authenticated browser tab and reports a typed receipt
A pendant return event that fetches the result without reopening the microphone
A dashboard view showing active handoffs and allowing revocation

args.user_asks: “Let me know silently when it’s done.” — after I hand a long Mac or browser task to you, give the pendant a distinct haptic pattern for completed, needs-attention, or failed, and let a button press replay a one-sentence status.
args.why_useful: The owner should not need to keep checking the Mac or open the microphone while walking, in a meeting, or listening to something else. A tactile receipt turns asynchronous work into an ambient signal, while keeping potentially sensitive content off the pendant speaker until explicitly requested.
args.model_tier: No realtime model is needed for completion classification. Deterministic receipt mapping handles completed/attention/failed; a cheaper background model produces the optional one-sentence spoken status.
args.latency_budget: Haptic notification within 2 seconds of a terminal receipt; button status replay begins within 500 ms.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.001 per event; almost entirely device and relay computation, with optional status summarization costing a fraction of a cent.
args.security_concerns: Haptics reveal only a coarse state, not task content. Do not speak sensitive details without the explicit replay press. Bind notifications to the paired device, deduplicate receipt IDs, and expire stale notifications so a later owner does not receive misleading signals.
missing: Pendant firmware haptic pattern queue with persistence across link loss and bounded flash use
Relay subscription that converts Mac/browser terminal receipts into device notifications
A stable receipt taxonomy shared by /jobs receipts, browser results, and failures
A button event to request the latest status and a delivery acknowledgement

args.change: Add a durable notification mailbox on the pendant for typed external receipts. It stores at most 8 compact records (receipt ID, coarse state, timestamp, retry count), renders three distinct haptic patterns, acknowledges delivery to the relay, survives a dropped link, and exposes a single-button 'latest status' request. It must never store transcript text or page content, and must coalesce duplicate receipt IDs.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Long-running work can finish without the owner staring at the Mac or listening continuously; the pendant quietly tells them whether to continue walking, check something, or review a failure.
args.effort: Small-to-medium firmware change plus relay protocol and integration tests; requires validating haptic actuator timing and flash wear limits on the actual pendant.
args.risk: A missed or repeated vibration could cause confusion. Use sequence numbers, a bounded mailbox, explicit delivery acknowledgements, a periodic expiry, and a neutral pattern when state is unknown.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost. Firmware power impact is limited to short haptic pulses and occasional radio packets; no new hardware assumed until the pendant actuator spec is verified.
args.latency_impact: Terminal receipt to haptic target under 2 seconds while connected; queued delivery on reconnect.
args.security_impact: Only coarse status leaves the Mac. No transcript, notification title, URL, or file name is stored on the pendant.
depends_on: A shared terminal receipt taxonomy across Mac jobs and browser commands
Relay-to-pendant notification delivery and acknowledgement route
Actual pendant haptic actuator/storage limits and offline event queue implementation
