args.user_asks: When I ask “what am I on the hook for today?”, gather my Calendar and Mail plus the logged-in pages I have open, identify commitments, deadlines, and conflicts, and leave me a sourced review board with a short spoken summary and suggested next actions—never send, submit, or reschedule anything.
args.why_useful: This turns scattered obligations into one actionable view: a meeting promise in Mail, a due date in a private portal, and a calendar collision are linked as one item rather than three separate alerts. The Mac leaves an auditable board the owner can review later, while the pendant gives only the highest-priority exceptions.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for extraction, deduplication, deadline/conflict reasoning, and board generation; reserve realtime only for the spoken request and a brief answer. Use no realtime context replay for the overnight/background work.
args.latency_budget: Spoken acknowledgement under 1 second; initial answer in 10–20 seconds when browser is healthy. If private tabs are unavailable, say so immediately and complete Calendar/Mail-only results rather than hanging. Background board can finish asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: One background text invocation per request plus bounded authenticated-page extraction; dominant cost is browser page reads and context, not the short realtime acknowledgement. TTS is a few seconds of generated PCM and should be cached with the board.
args.security_concerns: Calendar/Mail and logged-in page contents leave the Mac only as scoped extracts; redact message bodies by default and retain source URLs, timestamps, and snippets rather than whole pages. Never submit forms or send mail. Browser session IDs and tab URLs must be kept out of the pendant transcript; require explicit owner action later for any mutation.
missing: A durable cross-source commitment schema (source, evidence snippet, due timestamp, owner, confidence, status, conflict links) and deduplication pass
The durable browser job runner and resumable result stream for private-page reads; current router/backends exist but jobs do not survive restart
A review-board writer that atomically creates/updates one dated folder with a brief, evidence manifest, and draft suggestions
A healthy authenticated browser tab/heartbeat; current browser status is online but has no active tab and nine pending commands

args.finding: The browser extension reports online with no active tab and 9 pending commands, while GET /browser/poll repeatedly returns command browser_fc12217f-842e-4751-8697-c6c71706bd52 in processing, claimed by home-chrome, with 17 attempts. This is an orphan/stuck command state, not merely an offline heartbeat.
args.evidence: GET /browser/status => online=true, tabId=null, pendingCommands=9; GET /browser/poll => same command status=processing, claimedBy=home-chrome, attempts=17.

args.change: Add a cross-surface browser-queue reconciler in the Mac planner: correlate each pending browser command with its local jobId, journal/receipt, tab/session lease, and last heartbeat; classify it as runnable, duplicate, orphaned, or stalled. A command with no live tab, an expired lease, or a high attempt count must be quarantined (not replayed), emit one durable diagnostic event, and expose a resume/ discard operation. Reconcile after every browser heartbeat and before any new browser action, then surface a compact Mac review item and, when appropriate, a pendant alert. Keep the existing owner policy of maximum access: this is observability and replay prevention, not an approval gate.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops getting silent duplicate clicks or 45-second hangs after Safari/Chrome closes. They receive one clear explanation—what was attempted, whether it changed anything, and whether it can safely resume—instead of the system repeatedly acting on a stale private tab.
args.effort: Medium: a small persistent ledger and state machine in local-agent, adapters for /browser/status, /browser/poll, /browser/result/:commandId, /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and journal events, plus dashboard/briefing presentation and tests for restart/heartbeat races.
args.risk: Incorrect classification could quarantine a valid long-running read or discard a command whose result is merely delayed. Preserve the raw command and receipt, use lease expiry plus attempt/time thresholds rather than attempts alone, and make resume/discard explicit operations. Recovery is replay from the preserved command only after a fresh tab/session binding.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one lightweight ledger write per heartbeat/command and bounded diagnostic context. No extra model call unless generating the human summary.
args.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds before a browser action; removes the current worst-case 45-second blocking wait for commands that can never complete.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by preventing stale authenticated commands from replaying into a different tab. Store opaque session/tab IDs and hashes, not page contents; redact URLs in pendant alerts.
depends_on: chg-14accc01's request IDs/idempotency and resumable polling (currently missing progress/resume implementation)
chg-16bc5dee's durable browser job runner (router exists, persistence/retry/result stream still missing)
A browser heartbeat that reports active tab/session identity rather than online=true with tabId=null

args.user_asks: When I miss or am about to miss a commitment, tell me what is at risk, find the smallest set of recovery options across my Calendar, Mail, and logged-in work pages, and prepare a choice card on my Mac with draft messages and proposed times—then let me choose one from the pendant. Never send, submit, or reschedule without my explicit choice.
args.why_useful: Today the system can summarize sources, but it cannot connect a slipping commitment to concrete, evidence-backed recovery choices. This would turn “I’m late” into a calm decision: what can be moved, who needs a draft notice, what deadline is hard, and which option causes the least downstream damage.
args.model_tier: Use a background model for monitoring, commitment extraction, dependency analysis, and generating alternatives. Use the realtime tier only for the pendant’s brief alert and the owner’s selection. Use a cheap deterministic rules layer for time arithmetic, conflict checks, and redaction.
args.latency_budget: A risk alert should reach the pendant within 30 seconds of a detected change or missed start. A choice card should appear on the Mac within 1–2 minutes; selecting an option should acknowledge in under 1 second and queue the selected plan for explicit execution.
args.cost_estimate: Periodic checks are mostly deterministic and low-cost; one background model call only when a commitment changes or crosses a risk threshold. Browser extraction and authenticated session availability dominate cost and latency; spoken alerts are short cached audio.
args.security_concerns: Private calendar, mail, and portal evidence must remain scoped to the relevant commitment, with source snippets and timestamps rather than whole-page retention. Drafts must be visibly marked unsent. No browser form submission, email send, or calendar mutation may happen from the alert alone; the chosen option must produce a human-readable before/after plan and a second explicit execution request.
missing: A commitment lifecycle model with planned, at-risk, missed, recovered, and dismissed states, including evidence and dependency edges
A cross-surface change detector that compares Calendar/Mail/browser observations over time instead of only answering on demand
A choice-card renderer and pendant selection protocol that carries an opaque option ID back to the Mac without replaying private content
A transactional action bundle that can execute a selected multi-app recovery plan and return per-step receipts or restore the prior draft state

args.change: Add a commitment-risk and recovery transaction layer that consumes timestamped Calendar/Mail/browser observations, maintains a state machine (planned → at-risk → missed → recovery-pending → chosen → executed), and emits an option envelope rather than an action. Each envelope contains 2–3 ranked recovery plans with evidence IDs, affected apps, exact proposed changes, and an opaque selection token. The pendant can select an option; the Mac then materializes drafts/previews, executes only the selected reversible bundle, and records per-step receipts plus a compensating plan.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an immediate, concrete way out of a missed obligation instead of another passive summary: choose the least damaging recovery plan from the pendant, with the Mac preparing the exact drafts and schedule changes for review.
args.effort: High: new durable state and evidence schema, cross-source diffing, option ranking, pendant option-selection messages, transactional multi-app planner, and receipt/compensation handling.
args.risk: A false positive could cause stressful alerts or propose an inappropriate message. Require confidence and quiet hours, suppress duplicate alerts, preserve drafts only, and make every mutation a separate explicit execution step. If execution partially fails, leave a discrepancy card with receipts rather than guessing.
args.cost_impact: Low-to-moderate background model cost only on state transitions; storage and deterministic conflict analysis dominate routine operation. No additional realtime model call beyond the short alert/selection exchange.
args.latency_impact: Detection depends on source polling, but once an at-risk transition is observed, option generation should complete in 1–2 minutes; pendant acknowledgement remains sub-second.
args.security_impact: The option envelope sent to the pendant contains opaque IDs and short redacted labels, never private message bodies or portal content. Evidence and drafts remain on the Mac/relay under existing authenticated scope; execution logs record app and field changes.
depends_on: A durable commitment lifecycle and cross-source observation diff store
A pendant protocol for presenting/selecting opaque option IDs
A transactional multi-app action bundle with per-step receipts and compensating recovery
Reliable authenticated browser observation with tab/session continuity

args.user_asks: “Start meeting mode.”
args.why_useful: With one pendant press or spoken command, the hive should recognize the current/next meeting, quietly assemble the agenda and relevant mail/calendar context, keep a live 24 kHz audio sidecar while the owner talks, and after the meeting leave a cited recap with decisions, open questions, and draft follow-ups—never sending anything automatically. The pendant supplies an immediate, hands-free trigger and audio; the Mac knows which meeting app/window is active and can read Calendar/Mail; the browser bridge can inspect the authenticated agenda or project tab; the relay keeps the session alive and delivers the recap when the Mac or pendant link briefly drops.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the live turn-taking/audio control; use a cheaper background model for agenda extraction, transcript cleanup, decision/action-item synthesis, and draft generation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the pendant trigger in under 300 ms, select the meeting context in under 2 s, and keep audio playout below 250 ms end-to-end. Post-meeting recap can take 1–3 minutes and should be resumable.
args.cost_estimate: One realtime session plus roughly 2–5 minutes of background transcription/synthesis; dominant cost is live audio tokens, so only the meeting interval should use realtime and the recap should use the slower tier.
args.security_concerns: Calendar/Mail and authenticated browser content leave the Mac only as redacted, cited excerpts; raw audio/transcript needs explicit retention (default delete after recap). Never submit/send a draft. Starting capture must be an explicit button or spoken command with a clear LED/audio acknowledgment; meeting mode must show an obvious active indicator.
missing: A meeting-context correlator joining the next Calendar event to the foreground Mac app and optionally an authenticated browser tab
A session-scoped audio/transcript capsule that survives a dropped Mac link and supports resumable post-meeting processing
A citation-preserving recap/draft artifact written to the owner's AI-Pendant-Workspace with a dashboard review state
A true 24 kHz capture/uplink path: current pendant capture is 15,625 Hz and 16 kHz Opus uplink even though playback decodes 24 kHz

args.change: Make the audio contract genuinely symmetric at 24 kHz: capture 24 kHz from the microphone (or oversample at 48 kHz and decimate), encode 24 kHz Opus uplink, and advertise the negotiated sample rate in the pipeline handshake. Keep the current 24 kHz decoder for downlink, but add bounded jitter buffering and a relay pass-through mode so the relay does not silently transcode 16 kHz speech back into 24 kHz. Measure encode+decode CPU, heap high-water, packet loss, and glass-to-glass latency in a hardware-in-the-loop fixture; refuse the mode and fall back to 16 kHz before audio underruns if the budget is exceeded.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner's voice and the assistant's reply would stop being upsampled on one direction: meeting mode, voice notes, and ordinary conversation would sound noticeably more natural and intelligible, especially for names and consonants. A negotiated fallback means a weak link becomes lower fidelity rather than a broken conversation.
args.effort: Medium-to-high: firmware microphone clock/driver and Opus application mode, relay negotiation/transcode changes, bridge clock validation, and a repeatable HIL latency/packet-loss test. The current nRF9160 prototype has only 211,608 B app RAM and both encode/decode already consume about 87% of one core, so profiling must precede enabling it by default; the eventual product board may need a codec/DSP or faster MCU.
args.risk: 24 kHz capture can exhaust CPU, increase radio bitrate and battery drain, or expose clock drift between the nRF9160 and ESP32. Recover by capability negotiation, a watchdog on underrun, and automatic 16 kHz fallback; retain diagnostic counters rather than dropping the session.
args.cost_impact: No incremental API cost for codec changes; 24 kHz Opus likely increases radio airtime and energy roughly in proportion to bitrate. Hardware cost is TBD, but a production audio codec/DSP or faster MCU may add roughly $3–$10 BOM and tens of mW compared with this development kit.
args.latency_impact: Potentially +10–30 ms from larger capture/codec work unless frames stay bounded; target under 250 ms glass-to-glass and measure p50/p95. Fallback must happen within one failed negotiation/underrun window.
args.security_impact: Audio remains encrypted in transit; higher-fidelity raw audio increases sensitivity and should use the existing short-retention/deletion policy. Do not persist PCM on the pendant or relay except bounded diagnostic samples with explicit opt-in.
depends_on: A pipeline handshake carrying sample rate/codec/bitrate and a relay pass-through path
The pending audio-path diagnostic/HIL fixture and offline delivery retry behavior
A production hardware decision if nRF9160 CPU headroom cannot meet simultaneous encode/decode
An end-to-end 24 kHz capture test using the actual microphone clock rather than resampling a 16 kHz source

args.user_asks: “Move this conversation to my Mac.”
args.why_useful: The owner should be able to begin a thought hands-free on the pendant and continue it at the desk without repeating the request or losing the assistant's working context. The pendant marks the exact turn and provides a short spoken acknowledgment; the relay seals a resumable conversation capsule; the Mac opens the relevant workspace, browser tab, or draft and presents the same pending decision; the owner can then type, inspect sources, or continue by voice. When they leave the desk, a single pendant press should hand the unfinished state back, including what was already done and what remains.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the handoff acknowledgment and any continuing live speech. Use a cheaper background model to compress the conversation capsule, select relevant files/tabs, and generate the Mac-side continuation view.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 300 ms, persist the capsule before replying, and have the Mac workspace ready within 3 seconds. Returning to the pendant should require only a short state summary, not a full replay.
args.cost_estimate: One small realtime turn per handoff; background compression and workspace selection should be a low-cost model. Storage is a small encrypted capsule plus references, so the dominant cost is not storage but repeated context if the capsule is not compact.
args.security_concerns: The capsule may contain private speech, authenticated URLs, and draft text. Encrypt it, retain it only until the task is completed or for a user-configurable short TTL, and redact secrets from dashboard previews. Opening a file or tab is reversible; sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting must remain an explicit separate action. The owner must see which Mac surfaces will be opened before the handoff executes.
missing: A versioned, encrypted handoff-capsule format with turn boundary, task state, completed actions, pending decisions, source references, and expiry
A relay-to-Mac handoff route with idempotency and acknowledgement, plus a Mac-to-pendant resume route
A workspace resolver that maps capsule references to an existing Mac file/tab without leaking authenticated page contents into the relay log
A dashboard/menubar continuation card showing capsule provenance and allowing discard or resume

args.change: Replace the prototype nRF9160-plus-ESP32 audio split with a production pendant audio front end: a low-power 24/48 kHz codec or DSP with hardware sample-rate conversion, a small secure ring-buffer SRAM, and a shared clock exposed to the modem MCU. Keep the nRF9160 for LTE-M/NB-IoT control and negotiation, but move Opus pre/post-processing and jitter-buffer servicing off the 64 MHz application core. Add a physical recording-status indicator driven independently of firmware task load.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They would get natural, stable 24 kHz speech without the pendant becoming hot, stuttering, or dying quickly, and the recording indicator would remain trustworthy even if the network or application task is wedged. It makes long conversations and meeting handoffs dependable rather than a lab-only mode.
args.effort: High: select codec/DSP and PMIC, redesign the board and clock tree, update Zephyr drivers and the ESP32 bridge contract, validate RF coexistence and acoustic performance, and manufacture a small pilot. This is intentionally a product redesign rather than a software workaround for the development kit.
args.risk: New clock domains can introduce drift, RF noise, boot failures, or a more difficult firmware update path. Recover with a bypass path to the existing I2S wiring, a hardware watchdog, signed dual-image firmware, and a 16 kHz compatibility mode. Validate on a pilot batch before replacing the prototype fleet.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $5–$15 additional BOM depending on codec/DSP, SRAM, PMIC, and indicator choices, plus one-time board/NRE cost; active audio power should fall versus spending most of the nRF9160 core on codec work, though idle BOM power rises slightly.
args.latency_impact: Hardware buffering should reduce codec CPU contention and make p95 latency more predictable; target under 50 ms local audio buffering and under 250 ms glass-to-glass. Clock conversion must be bounded and measurable.
args.security_impact: A hardware ring buffer must be volatile by default and zeroized on stop; do not add persistent raw-audio storage. The independent indicator must be fail-safe—if capture power is enabled, it should indicate capture even when the main MCU is unresponsive.
depends_on: A measured 24 kHz end-to-end audio contract and HIL test vector
A product-board decision replacing the explicitly provisional Nordic development kit
Relay negotiation for codec/sample-rate capability and a bridge firmware protocol version
A hardware privacy-indicator review with the owner

args.risk: A schema or clock mismatch could make work appear stuck or incorrectly completed. Recover by treating terminal receipts as immutable, using monotonic sequence numbers per job, and providing a replay/reconcile worker. Never infer success from a timeout.
args.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 storage and negligible compute; compact old entries and retain only hashes/metadata by default. One additional receipt write per cross-surface step; no model cost.
args.latency_impact: Usually under 20 ms per event write; reconciliation is asynchronous. A first response can be acknowledged before the ledger is fully compacted.
args.security_impact: The ledger is a sensitive activity trail. Store redacted metadata by default, encrypt it, scope reads to the owner/session, and hash or omit URLs, snippets, file names, and message contents unless explicitly requested. Correlation IDs must be unguessable.

args.subject: 24 kHz path gap observed
args.body: Live /pipeline shows TTS 24k PCM upload accepted (75.7 KiB), but pendant spec decodes Opus 24k/60ms and relay retention 30d. Is transport currently PCM or Opus? Please confirm before I propose end-to-end packetized/resumable path.

args.user_asks: “Play my queued briefings on the pendant, and keep going from where I left off if the connection drops.”
args.why_useful: The current pipeline can render 24 kHz mono PCM and mark it waiting, but the wearable's actual decoder is Opus at 24 kHz in 60 ms frames. An interrupted download or format mismatch can strand an otherwise completed briefing. This would make long briefings and scheduled audio dependable: the owner hears each item once, can pause/resume, and does not need to repeat the request after LTE or bridge loss.
args.model_tier: Background/scheduled work uses a cheaper model only to rank and label queued audio; no expensive realtime reasoning is needed during playback. Realtime is used only when the owner interrupts or asks a follow-up. The pendant firmware handles packet timing locally.
args.latency_budget: Start playback within 2 seconds when a complete object is available; resume within 1 second after link recovery. Upload/render can remain asynchronous. A 60 ms jitter buffer and at least 3 acknowledged frames should mask normal LTE variability.
args.cost_estimate: Small per-briefing relay/storage cost; roughly one TTS render plus Opus transcode, dominated by audio duration and R2 egress. No extra LLM call for ordinary playback. Receipts and resume metadata are tiny D1 records.
args.security_concerns: Audio may contain private calendar/mail content. Bind each manifest and frame request to the owner's authenticated device/session, use short-lived signed URLs, encrypt in transit, and delete audio plus manifests according to the existing retention policy. Never synthesize or enqueue a new spoken response from a stale or unverified job. Playback is safe without confirmation; generating a briefing that reads private sources still follows their source permissions.
missing: A canonical Opus 24 kHz/60 ms object format and manifest (codec, sequence count, duration, hash, loudness metadata) instead of accepting ambiguous PCM at relay_result
Resumable range/frame fetch with per-frame acknowledgements, idempotency keys, and a durable pendant playback cursor that survives reboot
A relay-side transcode/validation step that rejects mismatched sample rate/codec before advertising 'waiting for the pendant'
A Mac/relay fallback policy: if the pendant is offline, retain the item and expose queued/started/paused/completed state rather than replaying it
Firmware implementation within the nRF9160 CPU/RAM budget, including jitter buffer, cursor persistence, and an explicit cancel/skip gesture

args.change: Add a resumable, manifest-driven playback protocol for generated speech. The relay publishes an authenticated manifest containing Opus 24 kHz/60 ms frame count, SHA-256, duration, and expiry; the nRF9160 fetches frames in small windows, decodes into a bounded jitter buffer, persists only the next frame cursor and manifest ID, and ACKs the highest contiguous frame. On reconnect it resumes from that cursor, validates the final hash, and emits explicit started/paused/completed/corrupt/expired events. Keep microSD as the existing failure buffer only, not routine audio storage.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped bridge or LTE connection no longer forces the owner to restart a briefing or wonder whether it played. Scheduled audio becomes trustworthy while preserving the owner's rule that the pendant should not routinely fill its SD card with recordings.
args.effort: Medium-high: relay manifest/range endpoints and transcode validation, firmware Opus frame windowing/cursor persistence/events, and Mac dashboard receipt display. Test modem loss, reboot, duplicate frames, expired URLs, and PCM/Opus mismatch.
args.risk: A corrupt cursor or interrupted SD write could skip or repeat a frame; recover by replaying the last acknowledged frame and treating the manifest as idempotent. Decoder timing or RAM pressure could cause underruns; use a 3–5-frame buffer, measure heap, and fall back to whole-object download when the manifest is unsupported.
args.cost_impact: No additional LLM cost. Minor D1/R2 metadata and egress overhead; bandwidth is approximately the encoded audio size. Firmware uses a few KB of RAM for frame metadata/buffer; playback decode is about 25.4 ms per 60 ms frame on the measured 64 MHz core, materially below the simultaneous encode+decode prototype load.
args.latency_impact: First audio can remain under 2 seconds; reconnect resumes in about one frame window rather than re-rendering. Hash validation adds only end-of-item time.
args.security_impact: Signed, short-lived frame URLs and device/session binding prevent cross-account audio access. Manifest hashes detect tampering or stale PCM. Expiry and deletion must follow the existing 30-day audio-retention policy.
depends_on: A single canonical relay contract for Opus rather than the currently observed PCM payload at relay_result
Durable relay playback state and typed pipeline events
A small firmware update that can persist a cursor without violating the microSD failure-buffer policy

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.finding: Relay pipeline currently reports TTS as 24 kHz mono PCM and uploads pcmBytes to the relay, while pendant hardware specification requires Opus decode at 24 kHz/60 ms frames. The end-to-end 24 kHz path is therefore not yet proven as the device's native packet format.
args.evidence: GET /ops/status reports textToSpeech='macOS say (24 kHz PCM)'; GET /pipeline run job_309f5663... has TTS done format=s16le sampleRate=24000 and relay_result meta pcmBytes=75734; pendant spec reports playback='Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames'.

transcript.text:
I found one important remaining gap: the live relay path currently produces and uploads **24 kHz PCM**, while the pendant is specified to receive **24 kHz Opus in 60 ms frames**. The sample pipeline completed successfully, but it does not yet prove native pendant playback.

I proposed an end-to-end resumable playback protocol with:

- Canonical Opus manifests and frame hashes
- Frame-window downloads and acknowledgements
- Resume-after-LTE/bridge-drop behavior
- Persistent playback cursors across reboot
- Explicit started/paused/completed/corrupt events
- SD-card use only as the existing failure buffer

What is still needed:

1. Relay-side Opus transcode/validation and resumable frame endpoints.
2. Pendant firmware support for jitter buffering, cursor persistence, ACKs, and hash validation.
3. A device integration test covering drop, reconnect, reboot, duplicate frames, expiry, and corrupted audio.
4. Dashboard/briefing state showing whether an item is queued, playing, paused, completed, or failed.

The Mac bridge and relay are online, but browser automation remains offline with 10 queued commands; that is separate from the audio work. Accessibility and Screen Recording are still disabled, so GUI-based testing remains blocked, although the audio protocol itself does not require those permissions.

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘put this in front of me,’ use the pendant to hand the conversation to my Mac: open the relevant document or logged-in page, place the exact cited passage and next action in a review note, and tell me when the handoff is ready.”
args.why_useful: Today the pendant can converse and the Mac can act, but the owner must manually explain the handoff, find the source again, and reconstruct what was decided. This creates a physical-to-desktop continuation: a short spoken request becomes a bounded, source-linked workspace waiting on the Mac without losing the conversational context or silently submitting anything.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to recognize the handoff intent and capture the owner's short clarification. Use a cheaper background model to resolve citations, select the target app/page, and format the review note. The Mac executor performs deterministic opening and note-writing actions.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge on the pendant within 500 ms, create a handoff capsule within 3 seconds, and stage the Mac workspace within 8 seconds when the required app/session is available. If a private browser session is unavailable, leave a clearly marked pending capsule rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: One small background-model call per handoff, plus negligible relay/D1 storage and normal Mac/browser operations. No vision call is needed when an existing URL, file path, or cited source locator is available; vision is an optional fallback only.
args.security_concerns: The capsule may contain private mail, calendar, or logged-in webpage content. Encrypt it in transit, bind it to the paired pendant and Mac session, redact secrets by default, and retain it briefly. Opening a page and creating a note are reversible; sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting anything must remain outside the handoff and require the owner's existing confirmation policy. Show source URL/path, timestamp, and quoted hash in the note so stale content is visible.
missing: A cross-surface handoff capsule schema carrying conversation ID, source citations, quoted text hash, target surface, requested next action, freshness deadline, and sensitivity
A relay-to-Mac delivery/acknowledgement channel with idempotency and expiry, distinct from ordinary action jobs
A provenance-aware Mac staging operation that can open a file/page and create a review note without treating the note as an instruction to submit
Browser-session reattachment and freshness verification before placing authenticated content in the capsule
Pendant feedback states for accepted, waiting-for-Mac, ready, stale, and failed handoffs

args.user_asks: “When I walk away from my Mac, pause anything private and put my browser work into a safe state; when I come back wearing the pendant, restore only what I was actively using.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is continuously with the owner and can provide a stronger presence signal than a Mac timer. This would prevent private mail, account pages, or spoken audio from remaining exposed during an unexpected interruption, while preserving the exact working state instead of forcing a full restart. It is a coordinated physical-presence feature that neither the pendant nor Mac can safely provide alone.
args.model_tier: No LLM is needed for presence transitions. Use deterministic firmware/relay state machines; a cheap background model may classify which open work is resumable after return. Realtime is reserved for an explicit spoken override.
args.latency_budget: Pause or mute within 2 seconds of confirmed departure and secure browser state within 5 seconds. Resume only after a stable return signal for 3–5 seconds, avoiding flapping at the edge of radio range.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; small relay state and event traffic. Hardware cost depends on presence signal: approximately $2–5 for a BLE-capable companion/proximity design if the current radio cannot provide sufficiently reliable proximity, with modest battery impact.
args.security_concerns: A proximity token must not become an unlock credential by itself. Use encrypted rotating challenge-response, require the already-paired pendant and Mac identity, and let the owner choose whether return restores tabs, unmutes audio, or only displays a summary. Never auto-submit or send anything. Departure should redact or lock sensitive content, not delete it.
missing: A signed, debounced pendant-presence signal with explicit departed/returned confidence and replay protection
Mac privacy actions that can mute pendant playback, lock or blur selected windows, and snapshot browser session state without destructive mutation
Browser extension support for freezing authenticated tabs and restoring only the owner-approved active set
A durable cross-surface state machine with crash recovery and an owner-visible audit trail
A first-run policy UI defining which apps/pages/audio may pause, hide, or restore

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **“Put this in front of me” handoff** — the pendant transfers a cited conversation or webpage to a source-linked Mac review workspace, with freshness and provenance preserved.
2. **Pendant presence privacy state** — walking away pauses or protects sensitive Mac/browser/audio activity; returning restores only owner-approved active work.

Both require new cross-surface protocols, not just wiring existing routes together: signed handoff capsules, provenance and expiry, reliable pendant presence signals, browser-session freeze/restore, Mac privacy actions, and crash-safe state machines.

Before dispatch, stamp each action with surface, session/tab affinity, idempotency key, and a short lease. The Mac agent must consult live /ops/status and /observe: accessibility-dependent UI actions become explicitly blocked/unverified when uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false (never successful receipts), while AppleScript/read-only actions remain eligible. Recover by retaining the plan and idempotency key, exposing explicit retry/resume, and never deleting the user's requested work. Existing maximum-access policy remains unchanged; this adds truthfulness/observability, not an approval gate.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local JSON state writes per action and one reconnect notification. Engineering/storage cost is the dominant cost.
args.latency_impact: ~100–300 ms for status/lease checks; no extra model call. Reconnect may delay work until a heartbeat and verification arrives.
args.security_impact: Improves safety against stale authenticated-tab replay and false success. Preserve URL/tab metadata minimization and do not transmit page content in status events; idempotency keys must not contain secrets.

A browser heartbeat/reconnect handler that reports tab/session identity

transcript.text:
Round 131 produced one new integration proposal: a **reachability-aware execution envelope** spanning the relay, Mac agent, and browser bridge.

It would:

- Preflight `/ops/status` and `/observe` before dispatching actions.
- Mark Accessibility-dependent UI actions as **blocked/unverified**, rather than successful, when macOS input cannot reach the screen.
- Give browser commands short leases and idempotency keys.
- Quarantine the 10 commands currently queued while the browser extension is offline, preventing an unsafe burst on reconnect.
- Resume work only when the same tab/session is confirmed.

Live state confirms this is needed:

- Mac bridge: online, but `ready=false`.
- Accessibility: not trusted for the running AI Pendant Agent binary.
- Screen Recording: unavailable.
- `/observe`: UI actions currently report success while doing nothing.

What is still needed from the owner is not another server permission:

1. Grant **Accessibility** to the exact running binary:

3. Re-enable or reconnect the AI Pendant Browser Bridge extension when browser actions are needed.

Until then, AppleScript/read-only Mac operations can still be trusted, but GUI input and browser execution should be reported as unavailable rather than completed.

args.user_asks: “Make sure that actually happened everywhere I asked, and tell me if anything is out of sync.” After an action spanning my Mac and a logged-in browser, reconcile the intended end state against independent observations, identify partial completion or conflicting state, and prepare the smallest repair plan without silently retrying.
args.why_useful: Today a receipt can say an action completed even when Mac input never reached the screen, while browser commands can remain queued against a private session. The owner needs an end-state guarantee, not merely an execution log: one answer showing which surfaces agree, which do not, and what repair would change.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the owner's live request and concise spoken status; use a cheaper background model for reconciliation, evidence comparison, and repair-plan generation. Use deterministic checks before any model interpretation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the request within 1 second; perform quick local checks within 5 seconds. Allow background reconciliation to continue after the conversation and notify the pendant when evidence converges or a repair decision is needed.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one low-cost background text-model invocation plus deterministic Mac/browser reads; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per reconciliation depending on page evidence size. Realtime cost is limited to the initial request and final short status.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and local application state must stay scoped to the requested job and be minimized in relay events. Never replay a stale browser mutation merely because the intended state is absent; distinguish unknown from false and require explicit owner confirmation for a repair that could duplicate an external side effect. Store hashes and provenance rather than full sensitive content where possible.
missing: A cross-surface end-state assertion schema that describes the intended result independently of the action list
Independent postcondition readers for Mac files/apps and browser DOM/session state
Receipt-to-observation reconciliation with confidence, freshness, and conflict states
A repair planner that understands non-idempotent external effects and produces a reviewable diff
Relay and pendant notification support for partial, conflicting, and finally-verified outcomes

args.change: Create a cross-surface postcondition-and-witness layer, not another action queue. Every planned multi-surface job must carry declarative assertions such as file hash changed, app state contains a named value, or a browser session's specific DOM region equals an expected normalized value. After execution, independent adapters collect fresh witnesses from the Mac agent and authenticated browser, attach timestamps/tab IDs/file identities, and classify each assertion as verified, contradicted, or unknown. The relay stores the compact assertion result and the pendant speaks only the delta; action receipts remain evidence of attempted steps, never proof of the final state.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask for an outcome and know whether it is true across the places that matter, even when a UI action was swallowed or a browser disconnected. Partial completion becomes visible without blindly repeating a payment, submission, message, or file mutation.
args.effort: High: define a small assertion language, implement Mac and browser witness adapters, bind observations to job/session identity, add freshness and conflict handling, and test non-idempotent failures. This is deliberately separate from the existing executor and receipt/undo mechanisms.
args.risk: A witness can be stale, ambiguous, or unavailable; incorrectly declaring success is worse than declaring unknown. Require source timestamps and identity binding, use an explicit unknown state, expire assertions, and make repair a separate reviewed plan. No automatic retry of irreversible effects.
args.cost_impact: Small deterministic compute and local/relay storage cost per assertion; background model cost only when normalizing conflicting textual/page evidence. Data volume can be kept low with hashes, normalized fields, and cited snippets.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 1–5 seconds for independent postcondition reads after an action; complex browser pages may continue in background. Initial acknowledgment remains immediate.
args.security_impact: Witnesses must be scoped to the initiating job and redact page content, email bodies, and secrets. Do not copy full authenticated DOMs to the relay; retain local evidence references and short hashes where possible.
depends_on: A shared postcondition schema between /plan and /execute
Independent read-only Mac and browser inspection adapters
Relay persistence for assertion results and expiry
Pendant phrasing for verified/contradicted/unknown outcomes
Existing job receipts, journal records, and browser session identity

args.user_asks: Don't interrupt me at the wrong time. Collect anything urgent from my pendant, Mac, calendar/mail, and logged-in browser, decide whether it can wait, and deliver it through the right surface when I'm actually available. If I miss it, leave one sourced, expiring queue item I can acknowledge later.
args.why_useful: Current briefs and page watches can find information but cannot arbitrate attention across surfaces. This would prevent stale browser alerts during meetings, avoid repeated spoken interruptions, and preserve one auditable handoff from discovery to delivery and acknowledgment.
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model for event normalization, deduplication, urgency scoring, and capsule composition; realtime tier only for the brief spoken handoff or a live follow-up question.
args.latency_budget: Event ingestion under 5 seconds; quiet-mode decisions under 1 second; spoken handoff under 2 seconds after an availability event; background reconciliation can take minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per event batch using a cheap model; realtime cost only when the owner answers or requests explanation. Dominant cost is browser extraction and repeated context, reduced by hashes and compact citations.
args.security_concerns: Calendar/mail/browser content is private and should remain local or authenticated relay paths; capsules must carry source URLs/snippet hashes, sensitivity labels, expiry, and delivery audit. Never infer urgency from an offline or unauthenticated browser. Require explicit owner action for any send/submit; acknowledgment is not approval to mutate external systems.
missing: A shared attention-state event schema (pendant availability, quiet hours, meeting/foreground state, browser health, urgency, expiry).
A relay-side durable attention queue with deduplication, leases, acknowledgment/snooze/expire, and exactly-once delivery receipts.
Pendant availability/quiet-mode events and a low-friction acknowledge/snooze gesture.
Mac read-only implementations (the granted mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources currently return schema-only errors) plus a foreground/meeting signal.
Browser liveness envelope and command epoch integration so stale/offline tabs cannot generate current alerts.
A dashboard view showing queued capsules, provenance, expiry, and delivery history.

args.change: Add an attention-envelope and durable attention-queue protocol between event ingestion and delivery. Each item has eventId, source, observedAt, freshness deadline, urgency/reason, sensitivity, required surface, quiet-policy result, browser command epoch, dedupe key, capsule URL/snippet hash, and state {queued,snoozed,delivered,acknowledged,expired,blocked}. Accept availability transitions from pendant and Mac, re-evaluate only on meaningful transitions, and emit one delivery receipt plus an owner-visible explanation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets one calm, trustworthy place for things that need attention instead of duplicate voice alerts and stale browser findings. They can understand why something was held back and recover missed items after reconnecting.
args.effort: Medium: shared schema, D1/R2 queue and lease worker, event reducer, relay delivery adapter, and dashboard endpoint; add contract tests for offline tabs, meeting quiet mode, reconnect, duplicate events, and expiry.
args.risk: A bad urgency rule could delay something important or spam the owner. Recover with conservative defaults (urgent safety/security events may break quiet mode; everything else queues), visible reason codes, expiry warnings, and replayable event logs. Do not mutate external systems.
args.cost_impact: Low background storage/compute; roughly one small D1 row and occasional R2 capsule per item. Cheap model only for ambiguous ranking; no new realtime call for routine queue operations.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second state re-evaluation and seconds-to-minutes for background extraction; reconnect delivery is immediate once a lease is acquired.
args.security_impact: Private snippets remain encrypted/local where possible; source permissions and sensitivity travel with the envelope. Browser session tokens never enter the capsule. Dashboard and acknowledgment endpoints require bearer auth.

Pendant availability/acknowledge event skill
Working implementations of mac_read_sources and mac_readonly_inspect
A relay durable queue/receipt store

args.change: Implement the granted read-only Mac inspection/source tools as a narrow AppleScript/NSWorkspace adapter instead of leaving schema-only stubs: running_apps and foreground_app from NSWorkspace; browser_tabs from Safari/Chrome AppleScript with URL/title/session timestamps; calendar_today/calendar_range and mail_unread/mail_recent through the already-authorized Calendar/Mail dictionaries; accessibility_enabled as a TCC status probe. Return a typed partial result with per-source permission/error, redaction, freshness, and no UI mutation. Do not depend on Accessibility or Screen Recording.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The system can finally know whether the Mac is in a meeting, what browser context is active, and what today's messages/events say without stealing focus or pretending an unavailable source is empty. That enables reliable briefs and the attention handoff while preserving the owner's current maximum-control policy.
args.effort: Medium: local adapter plus schema validation, timeout/isolation per app, and fixtures for Safari, Chrome, Calendar, Mail, no-app-running, and Automation-denied cases.
args.risk: AppleScript dictionaries and Automation grants vary by app/version; scripts may hang or expose more content than intended. Recover with strict 2–5 second timeouts, bounded item/snippet limits, default redaction, explicit unavailable status (never empty baseline), and process isolation. Screen Recording/Accessibility remain optional and reported honestly.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local CPU only. Small implementation and test burden.
args.latency_impact: ~100–500 ms for foreground/running apps; ~1–3 s for Calendar/Mail/browser reads, parallelized with per-source deadlines.
args.security_impact: Read-only by construction, account_scope required, snippets redacted by default, URLs and bodies excluded unless explicitly requested. Automation grants are used only for named apps; no arbitrary shell.
depends_on: Implementations behind mac_readonly_inspect and mac_read_sources
A stable typed result envelope consumed by relay attention decisions

args.user_asks: When I'm in a meeting or around other people, keep private browser, mail, and calendar details out of spoken responses. Tell me only that something needs attention, and put the details in a local Mac review panel until I explicitly unlock them.
args.why_useful: Timing/quiet-mode alone does not prevent accidental disclosure: a perfectly timed voice alert can still speak a subject line or account detail aloud. This creates a cross-surface privacy boundary while retaining useful awareness.
args.model_tier: Cheap/background classifier for sensitivity labels and meeting-state reconciliation; realtime model only produces a generic redacted sentence. No model should receive full content when a local rule can redact it.
args.latency_budget: Privacy decision must complete before any spoken payload (<100 ms after an event); local review panel can update within 2 seconds; unlock and detail retrieval may take 1–3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for rule-based redaction; <$0.005 only for ambiguous sensitivity classification. Main cost is local/browser extraction, not generation.
args.security_concerns: Sensitive payloads remain on the Mac or authenticated browser session; relay receives opaque item IDs, urgency, and redacted text by default. Meeting detection should use Calendar/foreground signals, not microphone capture. Explicit unlock is scoped, time-limited, and logged; never read full content aloud while privacy lock is active.
missing: A privacy-state contract shared by pendant, relay, and Mac (public, private, meeting, unlocked-until).
Local Mac review panel/API that can hold encrypted detail payloads and release them only after a deliberate unlock gesture.
Browser/Mail/Calendar sensitivity metadata and redaction before relay serialization.
A pendant privacy-lock and scoped unlock gesture that works offline and survives reconnect.

args.subject: New privacy boundary capability
args.body: Proposed meeting/private-room mode: Calendar + foreground/browser state drives a shared privacy-state; relay speaks only redacted urgency, details stay local Mac review panel until scoped unlock. Avoids accidental disclosure even when timing is right. Needs privacy-state contract, local encrypted panel, pendant unlock gesture.

args.change: Add a cross-surface intent-claim coordinator for every owner request. Normalize the request into an intentId, then let relay, Mac, and browser workers advertise capabilities and acquire short leases on individual subtasks (read, draft, execute, deliver). Claims include dependency edges, idempotency key, cancellation epoch, and expected side effects; a coordinator prevents two surfaces from acting on the same intent, merges receipts into one causal timeline, and reassigns only expired or explicitly cancelled leases. A pendant interruption or reconnect advances the cancellation epoch rather than starting a duplicate run.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say one thing naturally while several surfaces work, without getting duplicate drafts, two browser submissions, repeated notifications, or a Mac action racing a browser action. If a laptop sleeps or the browser disconnects, work resumes safely and the owner receives one coherent result instead of conflicting reports.
args.effort: High: intent normalization, lease store, dependency-aware scheduler, cross-surface receipt correlation, cancellation/reassignment protocol, and failure-injection tests for reconnects, duplicate voice turns, stale browser epochs, and Mac sleep.
args.risk: A lease bug could strand work or incorrectly suppress a needed action. Recover with short bounded leases, visible pending/blocked states, deterministic idempotency keys, append-only receipts, and a manual retry that starts a new intent generation. It must coordinate execution, not silently authorize high-impact actions.
args.cost_impact: Low persistent storage and queue compute; cheap model only for ambiguous intent decomposition. Avoids duplicate model/browser/Mac work, likely reducing cost overall.
args.latency_impact: Adds tens of milliseconds for claim acquisition; parallel subtasks remain parallel. Recovery waits for lease expiry unless a cancellation/reconnect event arrives.
args.security_impact: Claims carry capability and sensitivity labels but never session secrets. Workers receive only their subtask's minimum context. Every external mutation remains attributable to one intent generation and one surface receipt.
depends_on: A shared intentId/idempotency-key format across relay jobs, POST /execute, browser command queue, and pendant events
A durable lease/claim store and event stream
Receipt correlation that can link GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts with browser and Mac results
Explicit cancellation/reconnect epochs from the browser extension and pendant

transcript.text:
Recorded a new integration proposal: a **cross-surface intent-claim coordinator**.

It would let the relay, Mac, browser, and pendant divide one owner request into leased subtasks with shared intent IDs, idempotency keys, cancellation epochs, dependencies, and unified receipts. This would prevent duplicate drafts, competing actions, repeated notifications, and unsafe races when a device disconnects or reconnects.

It requires a durable claim/lease store, shared intent and receipt formats, dependency-aware scheduling, and explicit cancellation/reconnect epochs across surfaces.

args.user_asks: "When a browser-dependent task is waiting, keep it safely queued and tell me on the pendant exactly whether it is queued, stale, blocked, or completed; when Chrome reconnects, resume only still-valid steps and give me one completion receipt instead of replaying old commands."
args.why_useful: The live system currently has Chrome offline with 10 pending commands, while the Mac journal shows browser_navigate failed 9/9 times and 112/120 jobs lack tier attribution. Today the owner cannot distinguish a command that never reached Chrome from one that ran against an old tab, and reconnecting risks duplicate or stale actions. This makes the wearable/Mac/browser/relay combination dependable rather than silently accumulating work.
args.model_tier: Deterministic state machine and background model only for summarizing receipts; never spend the realtime tier on queue bookkeeping. Use the planner only if a resumed multi-step goal needs replanning after a tab or auth state changed.
args.latency_budget: Immediate pendant acknowledgement under 300 ms from relay state; reconnect reconciliation under 2 s for command metadata; browser execution remains bounded by the extension's normal response time. If offline, speak one short queued/stale sentence and do not pretend completion.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for state transitions and receipts; roughly 1–2k background tokens only when generating a human summary after a batch. Main cost is small durable metadata (command hash, tab/session binding, expiry, result cursor), under 10 KB per queued task.
args.security_concerns: Never persist page contents or cookies in the relay; persist only opaque session/tab ids, action hashes, timestamps, and typed outcome codes. Auth pages, CAPTCHA, changed origin, and missing tabs become blocked/stale and require a fresh owner request; do not auto-replay clicks or form submissions. Browser reads may proceed under the owner's existing preference, but sending/deleting/purchasing stays confirmation-required. The pendant should announce only status, not sensitive page text.
missing: A durable browser command state machine with leases, TTL, idempotency hash, tab/session fingerprint, and explicit queued/running/stale/blocked/completed outcomes
A reconnect handshake in the browser extension that reports current tabs and accepts only unexpired commands whose fingerprint still matches
Relay-to-pendant compact status events and a single cited completion receipt correlating browser result, Mac job, and relay job
A read-only reconciliation endpoint that can mark pending commands stale without executing them

args.change: Add an execution-truth reconciler between POST /execute, the job/action receipt writer, and POST /pipeline/events. On every action, derive the displayed state from the actual executor result and FULL_CONTROL_MODE, not from the planner's generic risk message. Emit a typed lifecycle (accepted, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled) with jobId/actionId, executor, and undoability; suppress or rewrite legacy 'Waiting for your approval' events when fullControlMode=true and no gate exists. Reconcile orphaned processing pipeline runs on bridge restart from the durable job/receipt store, and attribute each receipt to deterministic/background/planner/realtime tier.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner currently hears a false approval prompt even though their chosen policy is maximum access and the action path executes without approval; this makes them unsure whether a task ran. A single truthful spoken/dashboard status would prevent duplicate commands and make completion receipts trustworthy. It also turns the observed 112 unattributed jobs into an actionable history instead of an unexplained cost/latency bill.
args.effort: Moderate: shared event schema, replay/reconciliation worker, migration for legacy pipeline events, and tests covering execute success/failure, bridge restart, and policy modes.
args.risk: A bad reconciliation could mark an action complete twice or hide a real failure. Use monotonic event sequence numbers, durable jobId/actionId keys, and retain raw legacy events for diagnostics; never execute during reconciliation. Recovery is replay from pendant-jobs.json and actionReceipts.
args.cost_impact: No model calls; a few hundred bytes of metadata per action and one low-rate background reconciliation pass. Saves planner spend by preventing duplicate retries caused by phantom waiting states.
args.latency_impact: Less than 50 ms local bookkeeping on execution; reconnect reconciliation completes in the background. Spoken status can arrive immediately from deterministic events.
args.security_impact: No new data access. Receipts should contain action type and redacted outcome only; keep command text/page content out of relay events. Existing owner policy remains unchanged—this fixes reporting, not authorization.
depends_on: A canonical actionId/jobId correlation persisted by the executor and relay
A versioned pipeline event schema with monotonic sequence numbers
A small read-only reconciliation worker over GET /jobs, GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts, and GET /pipeline

args.user_asks: "When I'm in a meeting or presenting, keep the pendant and Mac quiet unless something is genuinely urgent; hold everything else, then give me one short catch-up when the meeting ends—without recording the meeting unless I explicitly press the button."
args.why_useful: Today Calendar, the Mac foreground state, relay delivery, and pendant output do not share a single interruptibility decision. The owner can be interrupted by routine mail/browser/job results at exactly the wrong moment, or miss them because each surface queues independently. This creates a real capability no one node can provide: calendar-aware, device-wide attention arbitration with a privacy-preserving meeting boundary.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy for meeting boundaries, urgency, quiet delivery, and queue coalescing; background model only to produce the post-meeting three-item digest. Realtime is reserved for an explicit spoken interruption or emergency alert.
args.latency_budget: Calendar/foreground changes reflected across surfaces within 1 second. Emergency alerts bypass within 300 ms; routine events are held. Post-meeting digest is ready within 5 seconds of the boundary, with no waiting on a large model call for the mode switch.
args.cost_estimate: Almost no model cost during meetings; one short background summarization call per meeting digest, typically 500–1,500 input tokens. Durable queue metadata is under 1 KB per event; audio recording remains zero unless the owner explicitly activates capture.
args.security_concerns: Calendar event titles and foreground-app names should be reduced to a local sensitivity class (meeting, presenting, private, free) before leaving the Mac. Never infer or transmit meeting audio; the relay receives only mode, urgency class, and opaque event ids. Emergency bypass must be configurable and auditable. Digest sources remain redacted by default and sending/deleting actions remain separate from notification.
missing: A shared interruptibility lease issued by the Mac/relay with start, end, reason class, and expiry, consumed by both pendant delivery and Mac/browser notifications
A deterministic urgency taxonomy and coalescer that turns held events into one bounded digest without silently dropping them
Calendar boundary and presentation detection using the already-authorized Calendar automation plus explicit owner button override; no microphone-based detection
A durable audit trail showing why an item was held, bypassed, delivered, or expired, and a recovery path for missed boundaries

args.user_asks: "For any answer or action, let me ask ‘what did you rely on?’ and hear a short source trail—what came from my Mac, browser, pendant, or the cloud, when it was observed, and what was inferred—without exposing page contents or secrets."
args.why_useful: The current system can execute across surfaces and produce receipts, but the owner cannot distinguish a fresh Calendar/Mail fact from a stale browser observation, a planner inference, or a relay-generated claim. A compact provenance trail would let them trust, correct, or retract an answer without reading raw logs or sending private page text to the cloud. This is a new epistemic capability, not another action gate or job-status screen.
args.model_tier: Deterministic provenance graph and freshness/confidence calculations; use a cheap background model only to verbalize the already-structured trail into one sentence. Never use the realtime tier merely to build provenance.
args.latency_budget: Attach provenance identifiers during execution with under 20 ms local overhead; answer a spoken ‘what did you rely on?’ query in under 500 ms from the durable graph. Raw evidence stays on the originating device; only the compact trail crosses surfaces.
args.cost_estimate: No per-turn model cost for capture or graph updates; roughly 200–600 tokens for an optional natural-language explanation. Storage is small: source id, timestamp, freshness, transform labels, and redacted hashes, under 2 KB per claim.
args.security_concerns: Store source classes, timestamps, redacted field names, and content hashes—not mail bodies, cookies, URLs with query secrets, or page text. Use per-owner encryption and expiry for sensitive provenance. The owner can delete a trail without deleting the underlying source. Clearly label inference and stale evidence; never claim a source was consulted when it was not.
missing: A claim-level provenance envelope propagated from Calendar/Mail/source reads and browser observations through planner, relay, TTS, and Mac action receipts
A privacy-preserving evidence registry with freshness/expiry, redacted hashes, and source-local retention
A compact pendant query/response protocol for ‘why do you think that?’ and ‘forget this evidence’
Dashboard visualization that joins claim ids to job/action/pipeline ids without revealing protected content

transcript.summary: Recorded two owner capabilities: calendar/presentation-aware device-wide interruption arbitration with explicit privacy-preserving meeting boundaries, and claim-level provenance so the owner can ask what each answer or action relied on without exposing secrets. args.change: Add a browser-bridge liveness watchdog and queue quarantine layer, distinct from the command protocol itself. Track each device heartbeat lease and each command claim lease; when the lease expires, atomically move processing commands to `orphaned` (not immediately runnable), stop claiming new commands while the device is offline, and mark sessions whose lastUsedAt exceeds a configurable TTL as stale. On reconnection, require a fresh heartbeat and device/session identity before offering quarantined commands; replay only idempotent commands with the original request/idempotency key, while non-idempotent commands remain held for review. Emit one durable incident/receipt linking the command, attempts, last heartbeat, and reason, and let the pendant/relay announce a compact “browser bridge offline; N queued, M held” status rather than timing out for 45 seconds.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Today a dead or stale browser bridge can leave ten commands queued and a command stuck `processing` for hours with 18 attempts, while a browser action burns ~45 seconds before failing. The owner would get an honest immediate status, no accidental duplicate navigation/form action after reconnect, and automatic continuation of safe reads when the browser returns.
args.effort: Medium: browserBridge queue state machine plus a small periodic reaper/lease table, session TTL handling, and relay-facing status projection; add crash/reconnect integration tests for offline, duplicate poll, and reconnect cases.
args.risk: A too-short lease could quarantine a slow but healthy tab; use heartbeat-derived TTL with generous grace and an explicit operator replay endpoint. A crash between state transition and receipt write must be recovered by an idempotent transaction. Never auto-replay submit/click/form mutations.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small D1/local state record per lease and occasional watchdog work. Reduces wasted planner/bridge retries and 45-second timeout traffic.
args.latency_impact: Offline browser requests fail/status-return in milliseconds instead of waiting for bridge timeout. Healthy polling adds only a lease check; safe queued reads resume after one fresh heartbeat.
args.security_impact: Improves safety for authenticated sessions by preventing stale-tab actions and cross-device claims. Persist only command metadata, not page contents; bind leases to extension/device and session identity.
depends_on: A heartbeat payload must include a stable extension/device identity and server-observed lease timestamp.
Existing request IDs/idempotency keys and typed action results from the browser queue work must be retained.
Relay/pendant needs a read-only bridge-health status projection and compact notification path.

args.change: Add an accessibility-aware execution truth layer (observability, not an approval gate). Before and after every ui_* / synthesized-input action, attach the latest `/observe` inputReachability and accessibility probe to the receipt. If eventsPost=false or uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false, label the action `unverified_no_input_path` rather than `ok`, preserve the requested action and failure reason, and automatically suggest/route an equivalent AppleScript or high-level action when the target app is in the granted Automation list. For actions with no equivalent, report “not executed” immediately instead of claiming success. Expose a compact capability matrix per app (automation available, accessibility available, screen recording available) so faculty-action can choose a truthful route.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Right now the Mac reports that clicks, typing, and keypresses succeeded while doing nothing because AI Pendant Agent lacks Accessibility; the owner can be told a false success and lose trust. This change makes receipts honest and still lets Calendar, Mail, Notes, Finder, Safari, Chrome, and other already-authorized apps work through AppleScript without waiting for a manual TCC fix.
args.effort: Medium: enrich executor receipts and journal derivation, add an action-equivalence registry for common app intents, and add tests with accessibility trusted/untrusted and secure-input states.
args.risk: An app may accept an AppleScript command but produce an unexpected UI result; retain before/after app-level evidence and mark semantic completion separately from dispatch. Some actions genuinely require Accessibility and must remain unexecuted/unverified until the owner grants it.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful model/API cost; a small local probe and receipt metadata per action.
args.latency_impact: Adds a local probe (sub-second). High-level AppleScript fallback can be faster than a no-op UI loop.
args.security_impact: Does not broaden permissions. It makes existing Automation grants explicit and avoids silently pretending input reached the screen; receipt metadata should omit page contents and secrets.
depends_on: Keep `/observe` read-only and make its inputReachability result available to executor receipts.
Preserve the owner’s maximum-capability policy: this is truthful classification and fallback, not a confirmation or refusal policy.
Accessibility/Screen Recording remain owner-installed TCC grants for vision/UI tasks; no server-side substitute exists.

args.user_asks: “Read the key number or sentence from the private page I’m looking at, say it to me once through the pendant, and forget it afterward.”
args.why_useful: Today the browser can hold an authenticated page and the pendant can speak, but there is no deliberate one-shot private handoff: the owner must expose the page to another surface, risk leaving sensitive text in durable research/session history, or read it themselves. This would let them retrieve a balance, deadline, tracking number, or short instruction hands-free while preserving a clear ephemeral boundary.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background/text extraction model for selecting the requested field and redacting surrounding content; use realtime only for the owner’s live request and one short spoken response. No model should summarize beyond the requested field.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds after the browser bridge responds; one browser read and one short TTS/audio delivery. If the bridge is unavailable, say so immediately rather than substituting a public or stale page.
args.cost_estimate: Typically a few cents or less per invocation; browser extraction and a short realtime/TTS turn dominate, with no need for a long context resend.
args.security_concerns: The browser extension must return only the requested semantic field, not a full page. Redact secrets by default, display the source tab/domain and capture time in the response metadata, keep the spoken payload in volatile memory/audio buffers only, and delete the associated capsule/session transcript immediately after successful delivery. Require an explicit spoken confirmation for values classified as authentication secrets, payment credentials, or one-time codes; never read those automatically. If audio is routed through the relay, the selected phrase leaves the Mac briefly, so the owner needs a privacy setting that permits or forbids relay transit.
missing: An ephemeral, non-persisting browser extraction contract with a field-size limit and source-domain receipt.
A relay audio delivery mode that acknowledges playback and then cryptographically/transactionally purges text, audio, and trace payloads.
A cross-surface privacy classification/redaction service that distinguishes ordinary private facts from credentials and one-time secrets.
A pendant response primitive for one-shot playback with no replay/history affordance.
A durable deletion receipt proving the handoff payload and derived audio were purged without retaining the sensitive value.

args.change: Create an ephemeral-private data lane spanning browser extraction, relay speech, and pendant playback. A request creates a short-lived handoff ID bound to the authenticated tab and owner device, returns only one bounded field plus source metadata, streams it to the pendant, and then performs an atomic purge of extracted text, generated audio, research/session references, and temporary receipts. The purge receipt retains only hashes, timestamps, domain, byte counts, and success/failure—not the sensitive value. Make this lane separate from ordinary `/research` briefings so it cannot accidentally enter durable briefings, memory, or the conversation transcript.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could ask for one private fact while moving around—such as a deadline or balance—and hear it once without creating a durable copy of the page or forcing a full authenticated-page summary. Today the component routes exist independently, but there is no trustworthy boundary proving the sensitive handoff was erased.
args.effort: Medium-high: define a volatile handoff record and lifecycle across the Mac bridge and relay, add streaming playback acknowledgement and crash cleanup, then test relay loss, pendant disconnect, duplicate requests, and purge verification.
args.risk: A crash or logging path could retain the value; use memory-only buffers where possible, scrub structured logs, encrypt any unavoidable short-lived relay storage, and run a TTL sweeper. Delivery acknowledgement must not imply purge success; report those separately. Never permit credentials or one-time codes through the ordinary path.
args.cost_impact: Small per-request relay/storage overhead and one short TTS turn; lower than a full research run. Cleanup metadata is tiny and contains no page content.
args.latency_impact: One bounded extraction plus streaming audio, target 2–3 seconds; purge occurs immediately after playback acknowledgement and has a hard TTL fallback.
args.security_impact: Adds a strict data-minimization boundary and auditable deletion without weakening browser authentication. It requires an explicit owner privacy policy for whether selected text may transit the relay.
depends_on: A browser command that supports bounded semantic extraction from the current authenticated tab.
Relay/pendant playback acknowledgement and a volatile audio queue.
A purge-capable handoff store and log scrubber; ordinary research/session persistence must be bypassed.
A privacy classifier that refuses credentials and one-time secrets by default.

args.why_useful_to_owner: A request such as “find the invoice in Safari, save it on my Mac, and tell me on the pendant” would survive a browser crash or dropped voice link without losing place or repeating a download, email draft, or other side effect. args.latency_impact: Adds one local ledger write and claim check per step (tens of milliseconds); reconnect recovery waits for bounded health confirmation rather than immediately retrying.

args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per pause/resume, dominated by one small background summarization call; calendar reads, local snapshots, and durable capsule storage are the main non-model costs.
args.security_concerns: Resume capsules may contain authenticated URLs, drafts, and local filenames. args.change: Add an owner-visible ephemeral-context mode spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. Before a task begins, the system creates a declared data boundary (which tabs, files, calendar range, and mail scope may be read); each surface emits signed provenance receipts; when the task ends or the owner says “forget this,” relay copies, browser extraction buffers, and Mac temporary artifacts are cryptographically shredded or expired, while retaining only a redacted outcome and an auditable deletion receipt.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could safely ask for help with a sensitive logged-in page or document and know exactly what was consulted, what left the Mac, and what was erased afterward. Today privacy depends on scattered redaction and retention behavior that the wearer cannot inspect or control from the pendant.
args.effort: High: define a cross-surface data-boundary manifest, add provenance/deletion receipts to browser and Mac jobs, implement relay-side encrypted ephemeral storage with expiry, and expose a simple pendant review/forget interaction.
args.risk: Deletion cannot retract data already copied by an external website or a model provider, and a crash could leave a temporary local artifact. Mitigate by defaulting to local extraction, minimizing outbound payloads, encrypting per-task keys, short TTLs, crash-startup garbage collection, and clearly reporting deletion limits.
args.cost_impact: Small storage and key-management overhead; lower model cost when local extraction avoids sending full pages. No recurring inference cost outside the task.
args.latency_impact: A few hundred milliseconds to establish the manifest and finalize deletion; no meaningful impact to ordinary read-only tasks.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves least-privilege and auditability, but requires careful key isolation and authenticated pairing. Raw sensitive content must never be logged in receipts or relay telemetry.

transcript.text:
Round 138 findings:

- **Browser bridge is offline** with **11 pending commands**, no attached tab, and stale session state. Relay and Mac bridge are reachable. The missing piece is a resumable, dependency-aware queue that quarantines stale browser leases and reports status on the pendant.
- **Playback is already 24 kHz**, but live input remains **15,625 Hz**. The current pipeline therefore is not genuinely superwideband end-to-end. The main remaining work is a new microphone/capture path, negotiated 24-kHz Opus profile, congestion fallback, and packet-loss telemetry.
- The Mac can already collect and write diagnostic bundles, but it still needs a typed call-telemetry source; current read-only inspection cannot access audio queue depth, codec timing, or packet gaps.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable for the Mac agent. AppleScript and non-visual automation work, but vision-driven GUI control remains blocked until the owner grants those macOS permissions manually.

I recorded two proposals: resilient browser-offline handoff and a negotiated wideband audio path. The most important things still needed are implementation of those two cross-surface protocols, plus an owner decision on acceptable wideband latency, battery draw, and quality degradation before fallback.

args.user_asks: When I say “save this for later” on the pendant, capture the thought, identify what I was looking at in the browser and what meeting or project it relates to, then create one private, cited Markdown note in my AI-Pendant-Workspace and tell me where it was saved. args.why_useful: The owner can speak an idea while walking away from the computer and later recover not just the words, but the page, project, and time context that make the idea useful. No single surface can do this: the pendant has the moment of capture, the relay can retain the intent, the browser has private page context, and the Mac has the durable workspace and local calendar/project data.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to detect the short capture command and acknowledge it. Use a cheaper background model to transcribe, resolve page/project context, generate the Markdown note, and produce the final receipt.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 1 second and persist the raw capsule immediately. Finalize within 10 seconds when all surfaces are online; otherwise tell the owner it is held and complete it within one browser/Mac heartbeat after recovery.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per capsule; transcription and context resolution dominate. Deterministic storage, file creation, retries, and receipts should not invoke a model.
args.security_concerns: Audio should be discarded after transcription unless the owner explicitly chooses retention. Browser content may contain secrets, so store only the minimum cited excerpt and URL, redact credentials and tokens, and never include private page text in spoken acknowledgements. Writing a note is permitted by the owner's current policy, but the file path and sources must be shown in the receipt.
