args.change: Add a low-power NFC tag plus a secure-element-backed pairing flow to the pendant enclosure, with the Mac agent presenting a one-time pairing nonce and the relay issuing a device-bound credential after an NFC tap. Keep the existing LTE/USB paths unchanged; NFC is only for physical proximity and bootstrap.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can move the pendant to a new Mac or recover from a reset by tapping it, rather than copying pairing codes or leaving a long-lived secret in a browser. It also gives the owner a clear physical signal that the wearable is paired to this nearby machine.
args.effort: Moderate hardware revision and firmware/relay work: NFC antenna/tag or reader integration, secure credential provisioning, Mac Core NFC/USB pairing helper, and recovery UX. Requires threat-model and manufacturing provisioning.
args.risk: A stolen pendant in proximity to an unlocked Mac could initiate pairing unless the Mac shows a nonce and the owner confirms with the existing button. Recover by revoking the device credential at the relay and requiring a fresh physical tap. Avoid NFC storage of the relay API key.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $2–$8 BOM increase depending on NFC controller and secure element; NFC power is near-zero in idle for a passive tag, with brief reader/provisioning power during pairing. No per-use model cost.
args.latency_impact: Pairing should complete in 5–15 seconds; no effect on live audio after pairing.
args.security_impact: Improves physical binding and credential rotation, but adds a proximity attack surface. Use ephemeral nonces, relay-side revocation, secure-element key generation, and explicit owner confirmation.
depends_on: A relay device-credential and revocation endpoint
A Mac pairing helper that can communicate with the connected pendant and display the nonce
Firmware support for NFC identity exchange and secure-element-backed key storage

args.subject: Three cross-node gaps this round
args.body: I’m proposing (1) USB tethered pendant relay while LTE unregistered, (2) interruption arbitration using foreground/calendar/browser state and pendant inbox, (3) one-button bookmark-to-context-to-action loop capturing current Mac/browser context and speaking confirmation. All combine surfaces; serial exchange + semantic selected text remain missing.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: When my pendant is plugged into my Mac, make it work as a full local relay: button events, bookmarks, diagnostics, and queued spoken replies should keep working even when LTE is unregistered, then reconcile cleanly when cellular returns.
args.why_useful: The pendant is physically usable today but currently loses its network-dependent value in exactly the state we can test now. This gives the owner one continuous wearable experience at home or at a desk, without changing button habits or creating duplicate events when LTE comes back.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for live turn arbitration; use a cheap background worker for deduplication/reconciliation and receipt generation.
args.latency_budget: Button/event acknowledgement under 250 ms over USB; staged reply playback start under 1 s; reconnect reconciliation within 10 s.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost: mostly local serial framing and relay event writes; occasional short realtime response dominates, roughly <$0.01 per event excluding audio generation.
args.security_concerns: USB serial grants the Mac access to wearable events and audio; keep the existing privacy latch authoritative, encrypt/authenticate the serial session, never upload diagnostic fixtures as owner audio, and log sequence-numbered receipts. Cellular and USB arrivals must be idempotent.
missing: mac_serial_exchange tool/route that can open the known USB serial device, frame messages, and report receipts
A relay-side transport adapter that treats USB as a second link without replaying LTE events
A deterministic per-device event id/ack reconciliation contract

args.user_asks: Don't speak over my meetings or presentations. If a pendant reply arrives while my calendar says I'm busy or the Mac is in a call, hold it, summarize urgency, and play it automatically at the first safe boundary or let me request it immediately.
args.why_useful: Today a generated reply can arrive at the worst possible moment, while a generic unread queue does not know whether the owner is presenting, in a call, or merely reading. This coordinates calendar, foreground/browser evidence, relay timing, and the pendant's existing inbox into a genuinely context-sensitive interruption policy.
args.model_tier: Cheap classifier/background worker for busy-state and urgency; realtime model only when the owner asks to hear or act on a held item.
args.latency_budget: Busy-state refresh within 2 s; no more than 300 ms added once a safe boundary is detected; immediate override begins within 1 s.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for calendar/foreground polling and metadata; <$0.01 only when a long held response needs summarization or speech regeneration.
args.security_concerns: Calendar titles, call state, and active tab metadata leave the Mac only as redacted policy facts (busy/free, app class, urgency); never transmit meeting content unless explicitly requested. A local privacy latch suppresses both microphone and playback.
missing: A Mac-side call/presentation detector that combines calendar state, foreground app and browser tab metadata
Relay policy fields for defer-until, urgency, expiry, and immediate-override
A safe-boundary event from Mac to relay and a playback lease so two surfaces cannot speak simultaneously

args.user_asks: When I short-press the pendant while looking at something on my Mac, save a private, timestamped context card containing the active app, browser tab, selected text or document path, and my bookmark label; later let me say 'do the thing I marked' and carry it out with a receipt.
args.why_useful: A moment bookmark currently records that something happened, but not what the owner was looking at. This turns a no-speech gesture into a reliable handoff from wearable attention to desktop action, useful when speaking would be awkward or the owner cannot stop to explain.
args.model_tier: No model for capture; cheap background extraction/redaction; realtime only to resolve the later spoken reference and plan ambiguous actions.
args.latency_budget: Card acknowledgement under 300 ms; context capture under 2 s; later retrieval and plan under 3 s before execution.
args.cost_estimate: Minimal storage and metadata cost; <$0.01–$0.03 for later language resolution, with action execution itself local.
args.security_concerns: Selected text and URLs can contain secrets. Redact password fields and token-like strings locally, encrypt cards at rest, expire by default, and require the owner's existing action policy for mutations. Never capture microphone audio unless the existing opt-in memo path is active.
missing: A real Mac semantic-context reader for selected text, document identity, and browser frame rather than only generic UI snapshots
A bookmark correlation protocol carrying the pendant event id into the Mac observation
A spoken-reference resolver and action receipt that can reopen the exact captured context without stale-tab surprises

args.user_asks: Run a pendant audio check from my Mac and tell me in one spoken sentence whether the microphone, uplink, downlink, and speaker path are healthy; if not, identify the failing segment and save a shareable diagnostic report.
args.why_useful: The existing fixture can measure the path, but today the owner has to interpret serial counters and logs. This turns a low-level test into a concrete go/no-go answer before a call, with evidence a maintainer can use instead of guessing whether a bad turn came from capture, radio, codec, or playback.
args.model_tier: Deterministic thresholds and report generation in background code; realtime model only to phrase the final short spoken verdict or answer a follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Start on explicit request; fixture and report within 15 s; spoken verdict within 2 s after receipt.
args.cost_estimate: No model call for healthy runs; <$0.01 for an exception summary. Local serial and report storage dominate, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The fixture must remain synthetic and never record microphone content. Reports should contain counters, firmware/build id, timestamps and hashes but no ambient audio, URLs, calendar data, or bearer tokens. Require explicit user initiation.
missing: A Mac serial command/receipt path to arm and collect audio_path_diagnostic_fixture while LTE is absent
A shared threshold schema that maps fixture counters to segment-level diagnoses
A relay spoken-verdict endpoint and durable report export

args.user_asks: After you change something in my browser on my behalf, tell me exactly what changed and give me a one-step way to undo it; for multi-page work, keep a before/after evidence bundle instead of just saying 'done'.
args.why_useful: A job receipt says an action completed but does not prove the resulting page state or make browser-side mutations easy to audit. This gives the owner a trustworthy spoken diff and a bounded recovery path across authenticated browser sessions, the Mac executor, and the pendant.
args.model_tier: Deterministic DOM/accessibility diff and URL/form-state capture first; cheap summarizer for the spoken sentence; realtime only for ambiguous follow-up or an undo request.
args.latency_budget: Capture before-state without delaying a simple action by more than 500 ms; after-state and receipt within 3 s; undo starts within 1 s.
args.cost_estimate: Low: local snapshots and hashes dominate storage; <$0.01 per multi-page summary, no model call for unchanged/read-only pages.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated pages may expose personal or financial data. Store redacted structural diffs and hashes by default, encrypt evidence, omit passwords/tokens, apply short retention, and never speak sensitive values aloud unless explicitly requested. Undo must target the exact session and page version, not blindly replay clicks.
missing: Browser bridge support for deterministic before/after snapshots and semantic mutation diffs
A mutation-specific inverse plan or browser transaction journal for actions that are not naturally reversible
Relay speech payload and pendant acknowledgement tied to the receipt id

args.change: Add a mutation journal around browser commands: capture a redacted structural before-state, command id/session/page version, after-state hash and a typed inverse descriptor when one exists; expose the compact diff and inverse token through the existing browser result and job receipt routes.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the agent changes an authenticated page, the owner can hear what actually changed and recover from the exact transaction instead of trusting an opaque 'done'.
args.effort: Medium: browser bridge snapshots, redaction, page-version checks, and inverse handlers for a small allowlisted set of mutations.
args.risk: Snapshots can leak page data and inverse handlers can be wrong on dynamic sites. Default to hashes/labels, short retention, refuse undo when page version changed, and keep the current action as completed if journaling fails.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and CPU; occasional small summarization call only when the owner requests a spoken diff.
args.latency_impact: Adds up to 300–500 ms before and 1–2 s after a mutating browser command.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates sensitive evidence; encrypt, redact secrets, scope by browser session, and never include bearer tokens or password fields.
depends_on: Browser bridge must expose stable page/session identifiers and a redacted structural snapshot
Owner-configured retention for evidence and inverse tokens

transcript.text:
This round I established three useful cross-surface capabilities:

1. **Context-sensitive interruption arbitration** — defer pendant replies during meetings, calls, or presentations and play them at the first safe boundary, while retaining an immediate override.
2. **Pendant bookmark-to-context action loop** — correlate a short pendant bookmark with the active Mac app, browser tab, selected text, or document, then let the owner later say “do the thing I marked.”
3. **Browser mutation evidence and recovery** — provide a spoken before/after diff and an exact undo path for browser changes, backed by a mutation journal and page-version checks.

I also recorded a browser-harness change to implement the journal using redacted structural snapshots, session/page identifiers, hashes, and typed inverse descriptors.

What I still need:

- **A working Mac USB-serial exchange capability.** The pendant is physically connected and testable, but I still cannot issue or receive serial frames from this harness. The pending `mac_serial_exchange` request remains unresolved.
- **Semantic Mac context capture:** selected text, document identity/path, and browser-frame identity. Current inspection is not sufficient for reliable bookmark-to-context actions.
- **Browser mutation journaling primitives:** deterministic before/after snapshots, redaction, stable page versions, and safe inverse operations.
- **Owner policy for evidence retention:** browser diffs and captured context may contain sensitive data, so retention and redaction defaults must be explicit rather than inferred.

The most valuable near-term capability is the interruption arbiter: it can be built from existing calendar, foreground-app, browser, relay, and pendant-inbox surfaces, without waiting for LTE registration.

args.user_asks: Why did you tell me that, and what exactly did you use? Give me a concise spoken provenance trail linking the pendant moment, Mac or browser evidence, relay reasoning, and the action receipt; let me inspect or revoke any source afterward.
args.why_useful: The owner currently receives answers and desktop actions without a unified, human-readable chain of evidence across nodes. A provenance trail would make the hive trustworthy: it distinguishes observed facts from inference, exposes stale or missing sources, and lets the owner revoke a captured browser or calendar source without deleting unrelated history.
args.model_tier: Deterministic event/provenance graph construction and source hashing; use a cheap summarizer for the spoken explanation, reserving realtime only for follow-up questions during an active conversation.
args.latency_budget: Attach provenance asynchronously without delaying ordinary responses; spoken explanation under 2 seconds for a small chain and under 5 seconds for a multi-node chain.
args.cost_estimate: Low storage and hashing overhead; typically <$0.01 for a generated spoken explanation, with no model call when the owner only opens the structured trace.
args.security_concerns: A provenance graph can itself reveal sensitive calendar titles, URLs, mail subjects, and voice-event timing. Store redacted typed facts plus encrypted source pointers, enforce per-source retention and revocation, never expose bearer tokens or raw audio, and require explicit owner intent before reading sensitive source details aloud.
missing: A cross-node provenance envelope with immutable event ids, timestamps, source classifications, confidence, and transformation links
Relay APIs to answer provenance queries and revoke or tombstone a specific source contribution without corrupting the resulting audit history
Mac/browser adapters that attach redacted evidence hashes and action receipts to the same envelope
A pendant response format for a short spoken explanation plus an optional dashboard detail view

args.user_asks: Before you act across my Mac and authenticated browser, tell me in one short spoken preview which resources will change, what cannot be undone, and what evidence will prove success; then let me say 'go' or revise the plan.
args.why_useful: The current Mac preflight does not cover browser-side effects or explain a single cross-node plan in owner language. A unified preview would let the owner understand a desktop-plus-browser action before it crosses an authenticated session, without requiring them to inspect technical receipts.
args.model_tier: Deterministic resource and reversibility classification first; cheap model for the short spoken rendering; realtime only for the owner's confirmation dialogue.
args.latency_budget: Preview under 2 seconds for ordinary plans; confirmation must bind to the exact plan hash and expire after 2 minutes.
args.cost_estimate: Low: local classification and hashing dominate; <$0.01 for a spoken preview, with no model cost for unchanged plan templates.
args.security_concerns: Previews must not leak page contents or secrets; use resource classes and redacted labels. Bind confirmation to plan hash, browser session, page version, and destination. Never treat a stale confirmation as authorization.
missing: Browser-side deterministic preflight with touched resources, reversibility, and exact plan hash
A relay-level cross-node plan composer joining Mac and browser actions
Pendant confirmation protocol and durable plan receipt that survives a dropped link
Dashboard rendering of the same preview and final evidence

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 6 of 7 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: mac_action_preflight. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: For a small set of actions I choose—such as sending a message, publishing, or placing an order—use a physical press on my pendant as the final proof that I am present, showing me the exact target and amount on the Mac first.
args.why_useful: A spoken confirmation can be triggered accidentally or become ambiguous while the owner is multitasking. A deliberate physical gesture on the worn device provides a distinct presence signal while the Mac/browser supplies the detailed preview, making high-consequence actions safer without requiring the owner to reach for the keyboard.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy and exact-plan hash binding; no model needed for authorization, with realtime used only to explain a rejected or expired approval.
args.latency_budget: The approval request should reach the pendant within 1 second; a button press should authorize or reject within 500 ms; approval expires after a short configurable interval.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost; implementation is protocol, firmware state, browser integration, and audit storage.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must not approve a changed plan or stale browser page. Bind approval to a cryptographic plan hash, target/session/page version, and expiry; show a compact LED/state code and speak details through the Mac or pendant; preserve a tamper-evident receipt. Owner must explicitly select which action classes use this mechanism.
missing: A firmware approval state machine using the existing button and LED without interfering with recording/bookmark semantics
Authenticated USB/LTE challenge-response between pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
Owner-configurable action classes and a browser/Mac enforcement hook that refuses execution without the matching physical approval

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 6 of 7 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: mac_action_preflight. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities the owner cannot have today:

1. **Cross-node provenance** — ask why the system said or did something and receive a redacted evidence chain across pendant, relay, Mac, browser, and receipts, with source revocation.
2. **Unified Mac/browser action preview** — hear exactly what will change, what is irreversible, and how success will be proven before approving a cross-node plan.
3. **Pendant physical approval for high-consequence actions** — bind a deliberate button press to an exact, expiring plan hash, target, browser session, and page version.

They require:

- A shared provenance envelope and query/revocation API.
- Browser-side deterministic preflight and mutation classification.
- A cross-node plan composer and plan-hash receipt.
- Authenticated pendant challenge-response and a firmware approval state machine.
- Explicit owner policy naming which actions require physical approval.
- Redacted, encrypted audit storage with configurable retention.

args.user_asks: “If I give you an instruction while I’m offline—‘when I’m back at my Mac, save this page to the project and remind me tomorrow’—remember the exact intent, then resume it later against the current browser and files without making me repeat myself.”
args.why_useful: Today the pendant can preserve a moment or voice memo, but it cannot preserve an actionable, target-bound instruction and safely finish it after the owner moves between dead zones, Mac, and authenticated browser sessions. This is the difference between recording what was said and carrying work across an interruption.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only parses the spoken instruction at capture time; a cheaper background model resolves references and checks whether the original target still exists when connectivity returns. Deterministic execution handles the final Mac/browser plan.
args.latency_budget: Offline capture acknowledgement under 300 ms; reconciliation within 10 s of link restoration; stale-target preview within 2 s before any mutation.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per deferred instruction, dominated by one short parse and later reference resolution; no cost while merely queued.
args.security_concerns: Persist the minimum structured intent, not ambient audio by default. Bind each instruction to an owner/device/session and an expiry. If the page, account, path, or requested effect changed, do not guess: speak the mismatch and require a new confirmation for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other irreversible action. Encrypt the pending intent locally and erase it after receipt or expiry.
missing: A new durable deferred-intent record distinct from the existing voice-memo/bookmark payloads, with target fingerprints, expiry, and idempotency key
Relay reconciliation that turns a queued intent into a current Mac/browser plan and reports stale-target conflicts
A resume executor that can atomically apply safe steps and return a spoken completion or conflict receipt

args.user_asks: “When I’m wearing the pendant and ask ‘what am I looking at?’, inspect the current Mac window and browser page, explain the important controls or error in one short spoken sentence, and include the exact place I can return to.”
args.why_useful: The pendant has no display, while the Mac has the visual and authenticated browser context. Today those surfaces can be inspected separately, but they do not produce a concise, location-preserving spoken explanation for a wearer who cannot stop to read the screen.
args.model_tier: A local/cheap vision model handles screenshot plus accessibility tree; realtime is reserved for the owner’s follow-up conversation. Browser DOM and URL extraction should be deterministic, with no model call when the page is simple.
args.latency_budget: Capture and answer in 3–6 s; URL/window identity returned with the sentence; stop immediately if the foreground app changes during capture.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 for a bounded screenshot/tree interpretation; local capture and speech delivery dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: Redact password fields, secure-input windows, and unrelated background apps before inference. Do not transmit the full screen by default: crop to the foreground window and send only the extracted explanation and return location after the turn. Authenticated page content must remain scoped to the owner’s active browser session.
missing: A stable semantic UI snapshot contract with roles, labels, selected state, and window identity (not just pixels)
A browser inspection result that returns the active tab’s title, URL, and bounded relevant DOM text without resolver ambiguity
A relay request/response envelope joining the Mac snapshot to one pendant spoken turn

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 4 of 5 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: mac_readonly_inspect. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

args.user_asks: “Read the useful parts of the authenticated page I’m on through the pendant while I’m away from the Mac; let me say ‘skip’, ‘go back’, or ‘bookmark this paragraph’, and stop when the page changes.”
args.why_useful: A browser session can reach pages the pendant cannot, and the pendant can deliver audio where the Mac cannot follow the owner. Today there is no durable, page-bound narration channel with spoken navigation and a bookmark tied to the exact paragraph, so the owner must remain at the screen.
args.model_tier: Cheap background extraction/chunking for the page; realtime handles only low-latency skip/back/bookmark commands. Use deterministic text extraction and sentence boundaries rather than repeatedly sending the whole page to the model.
args.latency_budget: Start playback within 3 s; skip/back response under 500 ms; page-change cancellation under 1 s; bookmark acknowledgement under 1 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per page depending on length, with caching by page revision so navigation costs almost nothing; audio bandwidth is the main ongoing cost.
args.security_concerns: Read only the active tab and bounded visible/article content, never hidden fields or other tabs. Detect URL/DOM revision and cancel on navigation. Store only a short redacted excerpt plus URL and paragraph locator for a bookmark; do not retain the full authenticated page.
missing: A page-to-speech stream with chunk IDs, sentence boundaries, and cancel-on-revision semantics
Low-latency pendant playback controls mapped to skip/back/bookmark events without confusing them with existing recording/bookmark button behavior
A browser content extractor that can identify a stable paragraph locator and return revision changes

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Offline deferred instructions** — capture an actionable command while disconnected, then safely resume it later on the Mac/browser with stale-target detection and confirmation for irreversible actions.
2. **Spoken screen and page explanation** — inspect the current Mac window and authenticated browser page, then explain the important content through the pendant with a return location.
3. **Hands-free authenticated page narration** — read the active page through the pendant with low-latency skip/back controls and paragraph-specific bookmarks.

All three require new cross-surface contracts rather than merely wiring existing routes: durable deferred-intent reconciliation, semantic UI/browser inspection, and page-revision-aware audio streaming.

args.subject: Novel Mac cross-node ideas
args.body: What owner-facing cross-node gaps are not in backlog? I'm targeting ambitious pendant+Mac+browser+relay workflows this round.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: When I say “finish this across my computer,” carry out the spoken task in the right authenticated browser tab and Mac app, then tell me exactly what changed and show me a proof receipt; if one critical detail is missing, ask only for that detail.
args.why_useful: Today the system can plan Mac actions and browser commands, but the owner has to trust that a multi-surface task actually finished. A single spoken request should become a coordinated browser+desktop transaction with a concise, auditable result instead of silent partial completion.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture intent and ask a single clarification; use a cheaper background planner to decompose and verify the workflow. Browser and Mac harnesses execute, while relay persists the receipt and pendant speaks the result.
args.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under 1 second; execution 5–30 seconds depending on browser and app; final receipt immediately after both surfaces report completion.
args.cost_estimate: One short realtime turn plus one background planning/verification call; roughly $0.01–$0.08 depending on task length. Browser/Mac I/O dominates latency, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents and local filenames may leave the device to the relay unless redacted. The owner must configure which domains/apps may run unattended; destructive sends/deletes need an explicit policy entry. Every step, touched resource, before/after hash or URL/title, and failure is retained in the receipt.
missing: A cross-surface transaction coordinator that can correlate browser command IDs and Mac action/job receipts, detect partial completion, and retry idempotently.
Browser result payloads with stable before/after evidence and an operation idempotency key.
Owner-configured action policy that is actually consulted by FULL_CONTROL_MODE.

args.user_asks: If my pendant is plugged into the Mac and cellular is unavailable, keep my conversation alive over the USB tether automatically; when LTE returns, hand the call back without making me repeat myself.
args.why_useful: The pendant is physically attached to this Mac today, while the LTE device is not registered. A dropped-radio conversation should degrade to a local tether rather than becoming a dead button. This would make the wearable useful indoors, in transit dead zones, and during radio outages.
args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for transport failover. Relay-realtime maintains the conversational session; a small deterministic bridge handles framed audio/control over USB and emits a compact state event. Realtime resumes only for the ongoing voice turn.
args.latency_budget: Failover detection under 500 ms and audio gap under 2 seconds; restoration to LTE in under 3 seconds with sequence continuity.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; persistent USB bridge and relay websocket are the dominant engineering/runtime resources. One small control event per transition.
args.security_concerns: USB serial must be authenticated and bound to the owner’s local bridge; do not expose a serial port as an arbitrary shell. Audio remains local-to-Mac until relay forwarding, with explicit link-state indicators and a hard local privacy latch. Reconnect must reject stale session tokens and replayed audio frames.
missing: A real serial transport adapter for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* with framed, authenticated audio/control messages; the requested mac_serial_exchange capability is still unavailable.
Relay session multiplexer that can switch transport while preserving conversation ID, Opus sequence numbers, and exactly-once control events.
A Mac bridge health/presence signal and a user-visible tethered-vs-LTE indicator.

args.user_asks: Undo the last thing you did across my Mac and browser, and tell me what could not be safely reversed.
args.why_useful: Current receipts can say what happened, but a failed multi-surface task can leave half a document, a moved file, and a changed web form. A spoken cross-surface undo would turn the system from an irreversible automation hazard into something the owner can recover from without hunting through apps.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic inverse-action planner over the recorded receipt; invoke realtime only if the inverse is ambiguous or an external side effect (send/purchase/delete) cannot be reversed. No model is needed for ordinary file staging, draft edits, or navigation rollback.
args.latency_budget: Receipt lookup and reversals in under 5 seconds for local/browser-state changes; external irreversible effects are reported immediately rather than pretending success.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model call; one cheap classifier/inverse lookup. Cost is dominated by browser/Mac operations and retention of before-state metadata.
args.security_concerns: Undo metadata can contain private page text, filenames, and form values, so encrypt and redact it. Never fabricate reversal: distinguish reverted, partially reverted, and irreversible. The owner must define whether browser history/navigation, drafts, file moves, and app edits are eligible; sent messages and purchases remain non-reversible.
missing: A shared inverse-operation ledger joining browser command IDs, Mac job receipts, and workbench transaction receipts.
Browser-side compensating actions and before-state snapshots for supported form/document operations.
A bounded retention policy and dashboard showing exactly which inverse steps will run.

args.user_asks: Research this for me, using both public sources and the sites I’m already signed into; save a cited decision memo on my Mac, and give me a 30-second spoken answer with the unresolved disagreements.
args.why_useful: Public web search alone misses the owner’s private dashboards and subscriptions, while browser automation alone does not produce a durable, cited artifact. This combines the relay’s research synthesis, authenticated browser sessions, and a local Mac memo so the owner gets both an answer now and something auditable later.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background research model for retrieval, deduplication, and citation extraction; use realtime only to clarify the question or speak the final short answer. Keep private authenticated-page extraction scoped to the requested domains.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; return a spoken provisional answer in 20–60 seconds; finish the cited memo in under 3 minutes, with progress available on the dashboard.
args.cost_estimate: One background retrieval/synthesis job plus optional realtime speech, roughly $0.03–$0.20 depending on source count. Browser fetches and page rendering dominate time.
args.security_concerns: Private subscription pages and account-specific data must stay scoped to the job and be redacted before any broad model call. Never mix sources across owners or silently quote paywalled content. The memo should include URLs, access time, confidence, and claims that could not be verified; saving locally is a write and must follow the owner’s policy.
missing: A research coordinator that can request bounded extracts from authenticated browser tabs and combine them with public web_search results.
A citation-preserving artifact writer that emits Markdown/PDF with source spans and hashes, not just a prose summary.
Browser command support for extracting structured text from the current authenticated page without exposing passwords or unrelated tabs.

args.finding: The live Mac agent currently reports Accessibility trusted, Screen Recording true, synthesized input events posting successfully, secure input false, and UI actions will reach the screen. AI Pendant Agent is foreground-capable even though Claude is the foreground app. This is a changed live fact relative to the earlier denied/grant context.
args.evidence: mac_readonly_inspect operation running_apps resolved to GET /observe at 2026-08-08T02:29:04.962Z and returned accessibility.trusted=true, screenRecording=true, eventsPost=true, inputReachability.status=verified.

transcript.text:
Round 192 produced three new owner-facing capabilities:

1. **Cross-surface task completion with proof receipts**  
   One spoken request can coordinate an authenticated browser tab and Mac app, then report exactly what changed, what failed, and which resources were touched.

2. **Cross-surface undo**  
   “Undo the last thing you did across my Mac and browser” reconstructs compensating actions from shared receipts and clearly distinguishes reverted, partially reverted, and irreversible effects.

3. **Authenticated research packets**  
   Combine public sources with bounded extracts from signed-in browser sessions, save a cited Markdown/PDF memo locally, and speak a short answer with unresolved disagreements.

I also tested the proposed USB-tethered conversation failover. It was rejected as a duplicate of an existing backlog capability, so I did not rephrase it.

A live observation changed an important assumption: the Mac currently reports **Accessibility trusted, Screen Recording enabled, synthesized input verified, and UI actions reaching the screen**. I recorded that finding.

What is still needed:

- A cross-surface coordinator joining browser command IDs, Mac job receipts, and workbench receipts.
- Idempotency keys and before/after evidence for browser operations.
- A browser extraction API that returns bounded structured text from the active authenticated page without passwords or unrelated tabs.
- Citation-preserving research artifact generation.
- A real inverse-operation ledger for cross-surface undo.
- An owner-configured policy that is actually consulted by `FULL_CONTROL_MODE`.
- The previously requested `mac_serial_exchange` capability remains unavailable; I did not re-request it.

args.user_asks: Take whatever I’m currently looking at on my Mac or in the active browser tab, and send it where I say — for example, “send this article to my notes,” “turn this selected paragraph into a reminder,” or “share this file with Alex.”
args.why_useful: The owner should not have to copy URLs, hunt for the selected text, or explain which window “this” means. The pendant supplies intent while the Mac establishes the exact foreground selection and the browser supplies authenticated context. This is a genuinely cross-node reference-resolution capability, not another generic automation macro.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to resolve the spoken destination and ambiguity. A small deterministic resolver obtains the active app, window, selection, URL, and file identity; a cheaper planner performs the requested transformation and dispatch.
args.latency_budget: Resolve “this” in under 1 second and confirm the target before any external send; complete local note/reminder actions within 5 seconds, with browser sharing actions reported when the site responds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn and one cheap classification call, approximately $0.005–$0.04. Mac/browser inspection and destination APIs dominate latency.
args.security_concerns: The active selection may contain secrets, credentials, or third-party personal data. Capture only the selected text or explicitly targeted file, redact passwords and secure-input fields, and show the exact source and destination in the spoken/dashboard receipt. Sending or sharing must be governed by an owner policy entry and must not silently broaden from selection to whole-page contents.
missing: A resolved Mac inspection operation for selected_text, window_identity, and document_path with stable source identifiers.
A browser extraction command that returns the active tab’s selected text and canonical URL without scraping unrelated tabs.
A typed source-reference object passed through relay planning so “this” cannot drift between inspection and execution.
Destination adapters for Notes, Reminders, email drafts, and authenticated browser share forms.

args.user_asks: For anything you tell me, let me ask “why?” and get the exact calendar event, email, browser page, or Mac file that caused the answer, including what was inferred versus directly observed.
args.why_useful: A spoken assistant becomes trustworthy when the owner can inspect the basis of an answer instead of accepting an opaque summary. This is especially valuable while walking: the pendant can speak a two-sentence provenance explanation, while the Mac dashboard opens the precise source and timestamp.
args.model_tier: No realtime model is needed to assemble provenance. Store structured source spans and inference labels during the original background job; use realtime only to summarize the trace aloud when asked.
args.latency_budget: Spoken “why?” response in under 2 seconds from the stored trace; opening the source on the Mac within 3 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible incremental model cost if provenance is captured during the original request. Storage and bounded source-span retention dominate.
args.security_concerns: Provenance can expose private mail, page contents, filenames, and other people’s data. Store redacted spans and source identifiers, enforce per-source retention, and refuse to read a source aloud when the owner’s privacy latch or secure-input state prohibits it.
missing: A provenance envelope required on every briefing, research, plan, and spoken response.
Stable source-span identifiers for Calendar/Mail, browser tabs, and local files that survive refreshes and edits.
A relay query that can retrieve and redact the trace for a pendant-sized spoken explanation.
Dashboard UI that highlights observed facts, inferred claims, and stale sources separately.

args.user_asks: Show me everything you sent or changed on my behalf today, grouped by recipient and app, with the exact final text or file and whether it was actually delivered.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has to search Mail, browser history, reminders, and local files separately to know what the assistant did. A single outbound ledger makes delegated work accountable and catches a mistaken or duplicated send before it becomes a surprise.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic event aggregation and hashes; no expensive model is required. Use realtime only to answer a spoken filter such as “only messages to work” or “what changed after lunch.”
args.latency_budget: Answer common queries from the ledger in under 2 seconds; source inspection or delivery verification may take up to 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost; bounded encrypted event storage and occasional browser/Mac verification are the main costs.
args.security_concerns: Outbound text, recipients, filenames, and destinations are highly sensitive. Encrypt the ledger locally, redact bodies by default on the pendant, support per-app retention, and clearly distinguish drafted, queued, submitted, and confirmed-delivered states. Never infer delivery merely from a click receipt.
missing: A normalized outbound-event schema spanning Mac actions, browser commands, reminders, notes, and relay messages.
Delivery-state callbacks from Mail and authenticated browser forms rather than only UI action success.
A retention/redaction policy and dashboard filters by time, recipient, app, and confidence.
A compact pendant query/summary path for voice-only audit questions.

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: 9 of 10 pieces you named are already known to this system. The rest are not in what anyone here has observed yet: mac_read_sources. That is not proof they do not exist — no agent has inventoried every surface — so check before treating them as the gap.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **“This” source resolution** — use the active Mac selection, document, or browser tab as the source for actions such as saving to Notes, creating a reminder, or sharing a file.
- **Ask “why?”** — trace spoken answers and actions to exact calendar events, emails, browser pages, or files, separating observed facts from inference.
- **Outbound accountability ledger** — show everything changed or sent today, grouped by app and recipient, with final content and confirmed delivery state.

The major changes required are shared source-reference and provenance schemas, bounded browser selection extraction, normalized Mac/browser action receipts, delivery callbacks rather than click-success assumptions, and owner-configurable retention/redaction policies.

args.subject: Avoid recent duplicates
args.body: Avoid offline bookmark/audio retry/congestion guard/diagnostic fixture (accepted), privacy latch/alert inbox, typed action broker/policy, readonly inspect/context capture, and generic USB-first local mode if it just repeats serial transport. Fresh angle: USB diagnostic fixture user flow is distinct only if it turns measurements into owner-facing pass/fail + repair plan across relay/pendant/Mac.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: When I leave a meeting, turn what happened into a ready-to-send follow-up: decisions, owners, deadlines, and the exact draft, using the meeting on my calendar, the document or browser tab I was looking at, and the bookmarks I made on the pendant.
args.why_useful: This closes the loop from a wearable moment marker to an actionable artifact instead of a transcript nobody revisits. It works only by joining pendant timing, Mac Calendar/Mail, the authenticated browser tab, and relay-side reasoning; the Mac alone cannot know the spoken/bookmarked moments or safely retain the browser session context.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to acknowledge a bookmark or a spoken 'wrap this meeting'; use a cheaper background model to reconcile calendar, browser and Mac sources, extract decisions, and draft. Escalate to realtime only when the owner asks for interactive edits.
args.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement under 1 s; first follow-up draft within 30 s of the wrap command; source collection is bounded to the active meeting window and one explicitly selected browser session.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01-$0.06 per meeting depending on audio/bookmark volume; background model tokens dominate, not the short acknowledgement.
args.security_concerns: Calendar titles, mail snippets, local documents and authenticated browser content leave the Mac only as redacted, source-scoped extracts. Never send the draft automatically; require an explicit owner command before any mail send. Expire raw excerpts after the draft and retain only cited source IDs and the owner's accepted edits.
missing: A serial/event bridge that exposes offline_moment_bookmark records to the relay while USB-attached
A meeting-window correlation service joining bookmark timestamps to Calendar events
A browser command to return the active tab's selected document context with explicit session scope
POST /meeting-followup implementation and a send-after-confirmation path

args.user_asks: Tell me when the thing I am about to do conflicts with my actual commitments—for example, when a browser deadline, an email promise, a local file, and my calendar disagree—and show me the smallest correction before I act.
args.why_useful: People lose trust when separate surfaces disagree. A cross-node consistency check catches stale dates, wrong time zones, duplicate commitments, and an outdated document while there is still time to fix them. The pendant gives a low-friction 'check this' trigger; the Mac and browser provide evidence that the relay cannot reach by itself.
args.model_tier: Background model performs structured extraction and contradiction ranking; realtime model only answers the owner's short query and reads the top conflict. Deterministic date/time and duplicate checks should run without an LLM.
args.latency_budget: Return a preliminary conflict scan in 3 s from bounded sources; stream deeper document/browser comparison within 15 s. Never block unrelated Mac use.
args.cost_estimate: $0.005-$0.03 per scan; most cost is document/browser text normalization and comparison, so cap each source and hash unchanged content.
args.security_concerns: Default to metadata, snippets, dates and hashes; do not upload whole documents or mail bodies unless the owner names the source. Authenticated browser pages must be session-scoped and never rendered into dashboard logs. A warning is read-only; changing a calendar event, file, or draft always becomes a separate explicit action.
missing: A typed cross-source evidence schema with provenance, timestamps, timezone and confidence
A browser read endpoint that returns bounded visible text/structured dates rather than screenshots alone
A relay trigger for a pendant bookmark plus current Mac foreground context
A conflict-ranking routine and a dashboard card with dismiss/snooze/correct actions

args.user_asks: I plugged the pendant into my Mac—run a complete audio and link check, tell me exactly what failed, and leave a one-page repair report I can send to you.
args.why_useful: The pendant is physically testable over USB today even though LTE registration is not. One command should exercise capture, Opus encode, serial transport, relay ingestion, decode and playback, then turn counters into an understandable pass/fail report instead of requiring firmware logs and expert interpretation.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic firmware thresholds and a cheap background model to explain the report; realtime is unnecessary except for a spoken result if the owner asks while wearing the pendant.
args.latency_budget: Start immediately and finish a normal fixture in 20 s; if a serial or relay stage stalls, stop after 5 s and report the exact stage rather than hanging.
args.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per run; the fixture and local parsing dominate, with almost no model tokens needed.
args.security_concerns: The fixture must use synthetic audio only and never open the microphone beyond the deliberate diagnostic mode. Serial output may contain identifiers, so redact device IDs in the dashboard and report. No network upload of raw PCM; send counters, sequence numbers, and hashes only.
missing: A resolved mac_serial_exchange tool for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
A USB session protocol that arms audio_path_diagnostic_fixture and correlates pendant, ESP32 bridge, Mac and relay clocks
A deterministic report generator with the shipped thresholds (alias rejection, codec CPU, mic drops, tx starvation, clipping and underruns)
A dashboard/download route for the signed repair report

args.change: Revise the next pendant revision to include a physical microphone power-cut switch with an independent sense line, plus a small LRA haptic driver. Keep the existing two-button/one-LED protocol as fallback, but make the cutoff electrically local so firmware, relay, Mac, and LTE cannot override it; expose switch state in the USB and relay status frames.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a privacy control they can verify by touch and a silent, unambiguous acknowledgement while moving. Today the pendant has no mic-disable switch, no vibration motor, and one LED overloaded with recording, inbox, and staged-reply meanings; software privacy alone cannot provide that confidence.
args.effort: Moderate hardware respin: switch, load switch or analog cutoff, sense GPIO, LRA and driver, enclosure change, firmware state/event integration, and privacy/audio acceptance tests.
args.risk: A bad cutoff implementation could leave the mic biased or create audio pops; default hardware state must be mic-off until firmware explicitly enables capture, and every transition needs a fixture test. If the haptic driver fails, LED/button behavior remains functional.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $3-$8 BOM increase in small volume, negligible average power when idle; brief haptic peaks require a regulated current path and may affect battery sizing on a future board.
args.latency_impact: Local cutoff is instantaneous; relay notification is best-effort and must not gate the local state.
args.security_impact: Strongly positive: an independent electrical path prevents compromised firmware, relay commands, or Mac automation from recording while the switch is off. Switch state should be reported as coarse state only, not tied to location or audio.
depends_on: A pendant board revision with one spare GPIO/ADC sense path and a power domain that can actually disconnect the microphone
Firmware integration with local_privacy_latch and existing audio-path diagnostics
Updated enclosure and a defined owner-visible haptic/LED state table

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.summary: Fresh work this round: (1) a cross-node meeting-to-follow-up flow that joins pendant bookmarks, Calendar/Mail, the active authenticated browser session, and a confirmed draft; (2) a commitment-conflict detector that compares bounded browser/Mac sources and warns before action; (3) a USB-connected pendant clinic that runs the synthetic audio fixture and produces a repair report; plus a hardware proposal for an independent physical mic cutoff and LRA haptic feedback. I also discovered live Mac state: Accessibility and Screen Recording are now trusted for AI Pendant Agent, input posting is verified, 18 apps are running, and three browser sessions exist. I told mac-terminal which accepted/duplicate ideas to avoid.
transcript.biggest_unknown: The missing resolved mac_serial_exchange capability remains the blocker for the USB clinic. transcript.text:
This round produced three new capabilities:

1. **USB fallback conversation — the most immediately useful**
   - Keep the pendant usable while plugged into the Mac even without LTE registration.
   - Stream microphone/audio through the Mac bridge into the existing relay pipeline.
   - Still needed: a real `mac_serial_exchange` capability, USB framing/handshake, and cable-loss cleanup.

2. **“What am I looking at?”**
   - Ask through the pendant and have the relay combine the utterance with the Mac’s foreground window, screen snapshot, and authenticated browser context.
   - Return one concise spoken answer, discarding the captured image afterward.
   - This is the strongest hive-native capability: the pendant hears and speaks, while only the Mac can see the owner’s current work.
   - Still needed: a stable resolved `ui_snapshot` operation, an ephemeral relay correlation route, and browser-field redaction.

3. **Spoken automation audit**
   - Ask, “What did the Mac agent change in the last hour?”
   - The pendant speaks a redacted summary of successful and failed Mac actions, touched files, tabs, and job receipts.
   - This is particularly important because `FULL_CONTROL_MODE` currently bypasses approval and risk classification.
   - Still needed: one append-only receipt schema across Mac, browser, and relay jobs, plus a query route that exposes only redacted resource summaries.

A useful live-state correction: the Mac now reports Accessibility **and Screen Recording granted**, synthesized input verified, and UI actions reaching the screen. That is newer than the earlier denied snapshot.

The main remaining blockers are therefore not permissions but:
- USB serial exchange for the physically connected pendant;
- resolving the ambiguous browser/UI inspection capability;
- unified, typed receipts for Mac and browser mutations;
- explicit owner-configurable redaction and unattended-action policy.

args.user_asks: When you tell me something through the pendant, let me ask 'why?' and hear the exact sources, timestamps, and uncertainty behind that answer.
args.why_useful: A short spoken answer is convenient but currently opaque. Provenance-on-demand would let the owner trust or challenge a briefing, browser summary, or Mac action without opening logs: the pendant asks, the relay traces the answer, and the Mac/browser provide the underlying evidence.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap structured provenance formatter; reserve realtime inference for the owner's follow-up question and only when evidence needs verbal compression.
args.latency_budget: Keep provenance records alongside every answer; return a two-sentence spoken explanation within 2 seconds, with an optional deeper written artifact in the workspace.
args.cost_estimate: Less than $0.005 per follow-up when source references are structured; storage and redaction are the main costs.
args.security_concerns: Source titles and URLs may expose private mail, work pages, or secrets. Speak only redacted labels by default, require an explicit request for full details, and preserve the original evidence locally rather than sending it back through the voice channel. Provenance must distinguish observed facts from model inference.
missing: A provenance envelope attached to relay answers, browser summaries, and Mac plans/actions
A durable local evidence bundle with source hashes, timestamps, and retention expiry
A relay query that resolves a spoken follow-up to the exact prior answer without replaying unrelated private context

args.user_asks: Before an agent sends, deletes, or buys something in my browser, let me approve it with one deliberate press on the pendant and hear exactly what will happen first.
args.why_useful: The owner wants automation but not invisible high-impact mutations. A physical confirmation channel is harder to trigger accidentally than a browser click and works while the Mac remains focused elsewhere. It restores meaningful control without turning ordinary reading or drafting into approval dialogs.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short spoken preview; policy evaluation and token matching should be deterministic and local to the relay/browser bridge.
args.latency_budget: Preview within 1 second; approval press accepted for 30 seconds; execution receipt within 3 seconds or explicit expiry/failure.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for structured actions; one short realtime response per high-impact approval.
args.security_concerns: A stolen or unattended pendant could authorize actions. Bind tokens to a specific action hash, browser session, account scope, and short expiry; invalidate on any page or amount change; never treat a generic button press as approval. Keep the owner's configurable policy authoritative.
missing: A relay-issued single-use approval-token route understood by the browser bridge
A browser-side action hash and preview protocol for send/delete/purchase operations
Firmware/bridge handling for a confirmation press without adding a new gesture or confusing the existing bookmark button

transcript.text:
Recorded two additional capabilities:

- **On-demand provenance:** ask “why?” after any spoken answer and receive its redacted sources, timestamps, evidence, and uncertainty.
- **Pendant approval for high-impact browser actions:** approve a specific send/delete/purchase action with a one-use, action-bound physical confirmation token.

The required changes are now captured in the proposals: provenance envelopes and evidence bundles, plus relay-issued approval tokens, browser action hashes, expiry, and pendant/bridge confirmation handling.

args.latency_budget: Read-back within 2 seconds of detecting a send/buy form; execute within 1 second after the physical press.

A common receipt envelope linking routine, pipeline, Mac job, and browser command IDs
A deterministic redaction-and-correlation worker

transcript.text:
This round produced three capabilities:

1. **Cross-source commitment checklist** — after the workday, extract likely commitments from Calendar, Mail, and opted-in browser sessions, with confidence and provenance beside every item. Nothing is sent or created without review.

2. **Authenticated work-portal attention digest** — scheduled, read-only checks of an explicitly allowed browser session, reporting only new urgent or blocked items while suppressing repeated bulk updates. This must be implemented in the browser-watch layer, not as a generic Mac briefing.

3. **One-command pendant/audio commissioning test** — run the existing bidirectional synthetic diagnostic fixture over USB, correlate pendant counters with relay pipeline telemetry, and produce a bug-reportable receipt identifying whether capture, transport, Opus, decoding, or playback failed.

Current live state:

- Mac bridge: online.
- Safari browser bridge: online with 9 tabs and no pending commands.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording: now granted to AI Pendant Agent.
- Relay: reachable.
- LTE pendant registration: still absent; USB tethering is the usable hardware path today.

What is still needed:

- **`mac_serial_exchange` or an equivalent allowlisted serial transport** for the nRF9160 and ESP32 USB devices. This remains the main blocker for actually exercising the hardware from the Mac.
- A typed browser-context read for authenticated portal sections, stable selectors, and per-section change hashes.
- Owner-configured portal origins, priority rules, retention, and redaction policy; these should not be invented by the agent.
- A durable cross-source checklist/evidence schema and review UI.
- Relay correlation and receipt generation for the USB audio diagnostic workflow.

args.user_asks: “Before each calendar event, assemble the exact preparation packet I need from the relevant mail, local files, and browser tabs, explain why each item was selected, and read me the three most important points through the pendant.”
args.why_useful: Today the sources are separately searchable, but the owner still has to decide which documents and tabs belong to a particular event. Event-linked retrieval would turn a calendar transition into useful preparation rather than a generic morning brief. It should preserve a reason and source for every included item so the owner can correct the association.
args.model_tier: A background model performs document/tab clustering and ranking; deterministic calendar matching, deduplication, and source citations do the rest. Realtime is only needed for spoken follow-up questions.
args.latency_budget: Begin 10 minutes before an event and produce an initial packet within 60 seconds; update incrementally if a relevant tab or mail arrives.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.12 per event, dominated by extracting and ranking text; local metadata matching is inexpensive.
args.security_concerns: Only the event's explicitly selected account and allowed folders/browser origins are searched. Exclude sensitive mail, passwords, and private tabs by policy. Show source citations and retention controls; never send or modify source documents.
missing: An event-scoped retrieval and association model that links Calendar attendees, subjects, projects, files, and browser sessions.
A bounded local-file content index with per-folder consent and redaction.
A browser extraction API that returns page text and stable source identifiers for opted-in tabs.
A pendant delivery queue that can replace or defer a packet when the owner is already in a call.

args.change: Add a cross-surface “quiet continuity” mode: when the owner begins a live pendant conversation, the relay snapshots the current Mac/browser work context and temporarily treats that context as the conversation's working set. If the owner says “that page,” “this file,” or “the thing I was doing,” the Mac and browser nodes resolve the reference against the snapshot rather than guessing from whatever is foreground later. End the mode on explicit stop or after a short idle timeout, and expose the captured context for deletion.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can speak naturally while moving between the pendant, Mac, and browser without repeating URLs, filenames, or project names. It makes the hive feel like one assistant instead of independent tools that lose the referent as soon as focus changes.
args.effort: Medium-high: define a time-bounded context lease, collect stable references from Mac/browser, and teach relay planning to resolve pronouns against it.
args.risk: A stale or sensitive page could be mistaken for the intended reference. Mitigate with visible context indicators, expiry, source citations, and a spoken clarification when multiple candidates match. Recover by deleting the lease and starting a fresh one.
args.cost_impact: Low storage cost; approximately $0.01–$0.05 per conversation for context extraction and occasional disambiguation.
args.latency_impact: Initial context capture under 2 seconds; reference resolution adds under 1 second when deterministic, with model fallback only for ambiguity.
args.security_impact: Potentially sensitive context crosses Mac/browser/relay. Default to metadata and short redacted excerpts, encrypt the lease, do not retain it after expiry, and honor per-app/domain exclusions.
depends_on: A relay context-lease schema and expiry semantics
Stable browser and Mac source identifiers
Owner-configured redaction and retention policy
A clarification path over the pendant when references are ambiguous

transcript.text:
Recorded three new items:

- **Event-linked preparation packets** assembled from relevant Mail, Calendar, local files, and browser tabs, with source citations and a three-point spoken summary.

The changes require event-scoped retrieval, project-switch detection, stable browser/Mac source identifiers, and an expiring cross-surface context lease.

args.user_asks: “I’m wearing the pendant and looking at something on my Mac—remember exactly what I’m looking at and turn it into a useful follow-up card.”
args.why_useful: A button bookmark currently remembers only a moment. This would bind that moment to the active app, browser URL/title, and a redacted screen context, so “that thing from earlier” becomes recoverable even when the pendant has no LTE. It is a genuinely cross-node memory handoff: pendant intent, Mac perception, browser session, relay ledger.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short spoken acknowledgement and intent; a cheaper background model extracts title, entities, and next action from the captured context.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 1 s; capture card within 5 s; background enrichment under 30 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per card depending on whether enrichment is invoked; Mac/browser capture and relay storage dominate latency, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Capture must default to URL/title plus a redacted accessibility snapshot, never raw screen or page body unless explicitly requested. Authenticated pages and tokens must be excluded. The card should show its sources and support deletion.
missing: A resolved USB-serial exchange path for the physically connected pendant when LTE is absent
A semantic Mac context operation for selected text/document identity; current ui_snapshot is not enough
A relay event schema that joins offline_moment_bookmark with a Mac/browser context receipt

args.user_asks: “From the pendant, draft a reply to the item I’m looking at, put it in the correct Mail or browser composer, and tell me what you prepared without sending it.”
args.why_useful: The owner can speak while away from the keyboard, while the browser extension supplies the authenticated page and the Mac planner places a draft in the right composer. This removes the painful context switch but preserves a hard non-send boundary. It works today for a pendant attached over USB even though the pendant is not LTE-registered.
args.model_tier: Realtime model parses the short command; background model drafts and checks tone/recipient/context; Mac execution is deterministic and does not need an expensive model.
args.latency_budget: Read current context and acknowledge in 1 s; draft visible in 5–10 s; never wait on a long autonomous loop.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.06 per draft, dominated by context extraction and generation; desktop/browser actions are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Never send, click final-submit, or expose full message bodies by default. Show recipient, quoted source, and exact draft in a local receipt. Require an explicit later user action for sending. Redact secrets and avoid drafting from pages marked private.
missing: A reliable pendant-to-Mac event transport while LTE is absent
Browser command metadata for composer identity and a typed no-submit stop condition
A local policy entry explicitly authorizing draft insertion but not send

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘handle this’ or press the bookmark button, make the smallest safe next step on my Mac, then tell me what happened and leave a resumable receipt.”
args.why_useful: This is the system’s highest-value behavior: the pendant captures intent at the moment of friction, perception identifies the real browser/app state, judgement chooses one bounded next step, and Mac action executes it with a receipt. If the link drops, the job remains resumable rather than silently disappearing. It turns the hive from a voice interface into an accountable action loop.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles intent and a brief spoken result; background/cheaper model performs state interpretation, planning, and summarization. Use the expensive tier only when ambiguity remains.
args.latency_budget: Spoken acknowledgement under 1 s; first action within 5 s; receipt within 15 s. Long tasks should stream status and be resumable.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.10 per action depending on visual/context reasoning; most simple actions should route to deterministic planners and cost near zero.
args.security_concerns: The current FULL_CONTROL_MODE has no effective approval gate. This capability therefore needs explicit owner policy classes, action receipts, touched-resource previews, and a kill/undo path. Never claim success without a receipt; redact page text and credentials from relay logs.
missing: A resolved pendant USB control path and offline event queue bridge
A policy-aware execution seam that observes but does not silently block owner-approved routines
A durable cross-node job/capsule protocol carrying intent, context hash, plan, action result, and resume token

args.change: Add a USB-local pendant gateway on the Mac bridge: accept bookmark, privacy, inbox, and audio-delivery status frames from /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*, timestamp them against Mac monotonic time, and forward them as authenticated relay events when online. Queue outbound acknowledgements locally with sequence numbers and replay them idempotently after reconnect. This is explicitly a local-mode path, not an LTE assumption.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant is physically wearable and connected today but unregistered with LTE. The owner should still be able to press the button, get a real acknowledgement, and have the Mac understand the event instead of losing the most useful wearable behavior in the exact environment available for testing.
args.effort: Medium: serial framing/parser, device identity handshake, replay ledger, and a small bridge daemon; then exercise existing firmware queues over USB.
args.risk: Malformed or stale frames could create duplicate bookmarks or replay an old privacy state. Use monotonic sequence numbers, device nonce, and idempotent event keys; expose a local reset command. Do not forward microphone payloads unless the existing privacy/recording state permits it.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 1–2 weeks engineering. No hardware cost or meaningful power increase while USB-powered.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement under 100 ms; relay forwarding is best-effort and does not block button feedback.
args.security_impact: USB serial is a privileged local channel. Authenticate the device handshake, bind events to the Mac session, and keep raw audio off the relay by default.
depends_on: A resolved mac_serial_exchange tool or equivalent implementation in the Mac bridge
A stable event envelope shared with offline_moment_bookmark and local_privacy_latch

args.change: Define a cross-surface Context Receipt object that every perception/action can emit: source surface, timestamp, URL/app/document identity, redaction class, content hash, and a short human-readable label. Make plans consume receipts rather than scraping fresh context ad hoc, and let the owner ask to reopen or delete a receipt.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner says “that one,” the system can prove which page, app, or document it meant and recover after a dropped link. It prevents the common failure where the Mac acts on a changed tab while the pendant conversation still refers to the old one.
args.effort: Medium: schema, relay persistence/TTL, browser and Mac adapters, and receipt display in job results.
args.risk: A receipt may outlive the sensitive page it describes. Default to hashes and labels, short TTLs, explicit source links, and deletion propagation; never persist credentials or full private page text.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and inference cost; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per receipt plus engineering time.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 200 ms to normal planning; avoids much slower re-observation and retries.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability but creates metadata. Encrypt at rest, redact by source, and make retention visible.
depends_on: A semantic Mac context operation for selected text/document identity
Browser command/result payloads carrying tab and frame identity
Durable relay job receipts

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Round 199 produced three capabilities and two stack changes:

- **Contextual pendant bookmarks:** bind a button bookmark to the active Mac app/browser tab and create a redacted, recoverable context card.
- **Pendant-initiated draft replies:** use the current browser or Mail context to prepare a draft without ever sending it.
- **Closed-loop “handle this”:** pendant intent → Mac/browser perception → bounded action → spoken result and resumable receipt.
- **USB-local pendant gateway:** make the physically connected pendant useful today despite absent LTE registration.
- **Cross-surface Context Receipts:** preserve source, timestamp, app/tab identity, redaction class, and content hash so “that one” remains unambiguous.

What I still need:

1. **A working USB serial exchange path** for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*`; the requested `mac_serial_exchange` remains unavailable. This is the largest immediate gap because the hardware is connected now.
2. **Semantic Mac context**, especially selected text, document identity, and stable window identity. `ui_snapshot` alone is insufficient.
3. **A shared durable receipt/event schema** joining pendant events, browser context, Mac actions, and relay jobs.
4. **Explicit owner-configured policy entries** for draft insertion, browser actions, and unattended routines. FULL_CONTROL_MODE currently has no effective approval gate.

The browser bridge is online with nine Safari tabs, currently focused on X, and the Mac bridge is online.

args.user_asks: “When my Mac wakes after being asleep or offline, restore the exact work state I was in: reopen the relevant apps and tabs, show me what changed while I was away, and ask me only about decisions that became stale.”
args.why_useful: Today a dropped bridge or sleep boundary breaks continuity: the owner must reconstruct which tabs, files, and pending actions mattered. This capability would make the Mac a durable second body for the pendant, with freshness checks instead of blindly replaying stale instructions.
args.model_tier: Background model builds the state delta and staleness explanations; realtime is used only if the owner asks from the pendant. Deterministic Mac actions reopen approved apps/tabs.
args.latency_budget: Detect bridge return within 10 s; produce a concise delta within 30 s; never auto-act on stale high-impact state.
args.cost_estimate: $0.005–$0.03 per wake/reconnect, mostly for summarizing changed state; local state hashing is effectively free.
args.security_concerns: Persist only encrypted app/tab identifiers and hashes, not page secrets. Never restore authenticated workflows that have changed materially without an explicit decision. Provide a one-command discard of the saved state.
missing: A durable cross-node state checkpoint distinct from individual job receipts
Browser tab change/version signals and Mac sleep/wake notifications
A stale-state decision protocol that can pause only the affected step while restoring safe context

args.user_asks: “Before I leave this Mac, make a private handoff package for tomorrow: the exact files and tabs I need, the unresolved questions, and a short spoken reminder when I next put on the pendant.”
args.why_useful: End-of-day context is currently scattered across tabs, files, mail, and memory. A handoff package would turn an arbitrary stopping point into a deliberate restart point, reducing the cost of resuming work without requiring the owner to write a status report.
args.model_tier: Cheaper background model extracts unresolved questions and summarizes only selected local sources; realtime speaks the reminder when requested or when the pendant reconnects.
args.latency_budget: Create in under 20 s for a normal work session; spoken reminder under 3 s after pendant connection.
args.cost_estimate: $0.01–$0.05 per package depending on document count; storage and local hashing dominate.
args.security_concerns: The package must be local-first and encrypted, with per-source inclusion shown before capture. Do not include whole documents or browser bodies by default. Expire reminders after a configurable date.
missing: A first-class encrypted handoff bundle format with source manifests
A Mac sleep/session boundary hook and browser tab snapshot versioning
A pendant notification payload that can reference the bundle without transmitting its contents

args.change: Add a local-first provenance and deletion ledger that tracks every derived fact, summary, reminder, and action back to its source surface and capture time. When a source is deleted or expires, automatically invalidate dependent summaries and notify the owner instead of leaving stale memory presented as truth.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner should never have to wonder why the assistant still believes something after the underlying email, tab, file, or bookmark was removed or changed. This would make long-lived personal memory trustworthy rather than merely persistent.
args.effort: High: dependency graph, source tombstones, expiry propagation across relay and Mac, and user-facing invalidation notices.
args.risk: Over-aggressive invalidation could erase useful history; preserve a user-approved archival snapshot separately from live memory and make every deletion reversible for a short window.
args.cost_impact: Low per-event API cost but meaningful engineering and encrypted storage overhead; background graph updates can use a cheap model.
args.latency_impact: No perceptible impact on ordinary actions; source-change propagation may take seconds to minutes.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by propagating deletion, but the dependency graph itself is sensitive. Keep raw content on the Mac where possible, send hashes and labels to the relay, and encrypt all provenance records.
depends_on: A shared Context Receipt or equivalent source identity
Change notifications from browser and Mac sources
Relay-side dependency storage and deletion propagation

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new proposals:

1. **Sleep/reconnect continuity:** restore the relevant Mac/browser state after wake, but detect stale context before resuming anything.
2. **Private end-of-day handoff packages:** save the exact work context, unresolved questions, and a concise reminder for the next pendant session.
3. **Provenance and deletion propagation:** invalidate derived summaries and reminders when their source email, file, tab, or bookmark changes or is deleted.

These require durable cross-node checkpoints, source/version notifications from Mac and browser, encrypted local-first storage, and relay-side dependency tracking.
